BLD-accept_changes.content:
A stop SHALL print `format_changes` of its changes — a line per kind and folder (`in <folder>`, `within <folder>`,
`from <folder> to <folder>`), each file under it — then `photos-cartographer <phase> <command> --accept-changes <code>`,
the code the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of those lines joined by newlines, and emit both as a `ChangesEvent`.
Every checking command takes `--accept-changes <code>`: where the code is that of the list the check would print, the
check adds to `photos-01-accepted-changes.json`, through `write_versioned_json` — the earlier file kept under `-NNN` —
an acceptance holding the code, phase, command, time, the record's id and each change with its entry as found, and the
command goes on; with any other code it stops as without one. A change equal to one an acceptance holds for the current
record's id stops nothing. A `photos-01-accepted-changes.json` that cannot be read stops the command, exit 2, and is
never written over. It lies in the control directory, so the archival package carries it. The console's Accept button
sends the same command with the code (`_accept_extra`), refusing a command that does not check.
BLD-accept_changes.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-accept_changes.title: Accepting a list of changes by its code

BLD-already_present_removed.content:
A photo already present SHALL be removed from photos by destination after the library's copy is fingerprinted again and
found to hold its content. Its bytes are compared with the workspace copy's first, on every path that removes one: a library file of the same fingerprint and other bytes blocks the photo, the plan's record carrying `library_match` (`bytes` or `pixels`) and, for a block, `same_picture` — the two paths and their sizes.

sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-already_present_removed.title: A photo already present is removed once the library's copy is checked

BLD-anchor_clustering.content:
`infer_anchor_proposal` SHALL cluster the candidates one by one in rank order — a precise one before an imprecise
one, a point before a segment, then the nearer, then by file and offset — each joining the first cluster whose offset
it agrees with, else starting one: a cluster's offset is that of its first and best-ranked candidate, never moved by
those that join it, so offsets are never chained beyond the spread. It proposes the cluster the most photos support; a
tie goes to the offset smaller in magnitude, then to the cluster started first. `groups` lists the clusters by photo
count, then magnitude, then signed offset, so where two tied clusters' offsets differ only in sign the first group may
be the other one than the proposal's.
BLD-anchor_clustering.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-anchor_clustering.title: How anchor offsets are clustered, and how a tie falls

BLD-anchor_matching.content:
For each photo holding its own position
({need}`BLD-own_position_test`) of a (camera group, destination, day) bucket, `frame_candidates` SHALL take, track by track, every point within `gpx_anchor_max_point_distance_meters` of it and every segment — two consecutive points of that track at most `gpx_anchor_max_segment_gap_seconds` apart — within `gpx_anchor_max_segment_distance_meters`, each at a time within `gpx_anchor_max_clock_error_seconds` of the photo's camera time read as UTC; a pass is an unbroken run of them along the track, passes of one track closer in time than `gpx_anchor_same_pass_max_seconds` being one; and keep each pass's best, a point before a segment, then the closest — dropped where a track of a better rank places a photo at its time by a point or between two (`BLD-track_placement`) — with `time_span_seconds` — the time from the first to the last match of the pass no farther than the best by `gpx_anchor_stay_distance_meters`. A candidate whose span exceeds `gpx_anchor_stay_max_seconds` agrees with any offset within that span, and the spread, of its own, and ranks after every other. `infer_anchor_proposal` clusters the candidates' offsets within the spread, `gpx_anchor_offset_spread_max_seconds`, and proposes the cluster the most photos support, a tie going to the smaller offset, its best-ranked candidate the representative; its confidence is `review_required` when a photo supports no pass of it, another cluster ties (`tied`), or its representative's span exceeds `gpx_anchor_stay_max_seconds` (`imprecise_seconds`), else `high` when another photo supports it or it is a point match, else `medium`. Only an agreed offset — no conflicting photo, no tie, not imprecise — applies itself, under `multi_anchor_auto_apply` or `single_anchor_auto_apply`; an imprecise one, accepted, takes effect as `gpx_anchor_imprecise`. The proposal names the photos no pass of which agrees (`conflicting_files`), and each cluster in `groups` with its photo count and a representative, its track file included; a `manual_offset_seconds` within the spread of a group's offset of a proposal that is not imprecise takes effect as `gpx_anchor_chosen`, which no drift check follows.
BLD-anchor_matching.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-anchor_matching.title: How anchors are matched and agreed

BLD-anchor_proposal_record.content:
A proposal from the camera's own GPS SHALL hold `anchors` — one per photo that matched a pass, the representative
first, then by rank: its candidate in the proposed cluster, else its own best — each with `proposal_id`
(`anchor-NNN`), `source_file`, `camera_source_naive_time`, `native_gps`, `gpx_match` (`match_type`, `gpx_file`,
`distance_m`, `segment_duration_seconds`) and `proposed_offset_seconds`; and `anchor_count`, how many photos matched a
pass, the count `multi_anchor_auto_apply` and `single_anchor_auto_apply` are read by ({need}`BLD-auto_apply_settings`).
A cell's `anchored_by` names the track files of the anchors within the spread of its offset
({need}`BLD-day_offset_kept`).

BLD-archive_manifest.content:
`geotag finalize` SHALL write `photos-26-complete-log.json` and the database snapshot `photos-26-geotag-ingest.db`, then
list every file of the control directory but the transient ones — locks, `.tmp-` files, SQLite's `-journal` files, the
plan memo `photos-00-plan-memo.db`, and any `*-archive.tar.gz` or its `-NNN` copy — with its SHA-256 and path in
`photos-26-archive-manifest.json`, recording the workspace's identity — the init run id prep wrote in the guard — with
the folder's name beside it, and the plan and execution ids, and archive those files and the manifest into
`photos-26-archive.tar.gz` in the control directory, by a temporary name and an atomic rename — writing nothing else,
and requiring a ready plan whose execution succeeded ({need}`BLD-finalize_preconditions`). Merge's re-seal does the same
into `photos-35-archive-manifest.json` and `photos-35-archive.tar.gz` ({need}`BLD-merge_success_sequence`).

BLD-artifact_numbering.content:
The numbered artifacts SHALL follow this scheme:

```text
0X  workspace infrastructure (phase-neutral): config, guard, live database
1X  prep-phase artifacts        (currently: 10 = prep plan, 11 = handoff, 15 = prep audit log + prep DB snapshot, 16 = prune record)
2X  geotag-phase artifacts        (currently: 21–26; 26 = complete log + geotag DB snapshot + archive manifest)
3X  merge-phase artifacts        (currently: 30 = merge plan, 31 = merge summary, 35 = merge log + fingerprint map + merge DB snapshot + archive manifest)
```

The first digit means only the producing phase. The second is a sequence number within the phase with no
further meaning: an absent number is not reserved, not headroom and not missing, and nothing is to be inferred from a
gap. Sibling end-of-phase records that differ only by extension MAY share a number — `photos-15-prep-log.json` and
`photos-15-prep-ingest.db` are both the end-of-prep record, one the human-readable log and one the database image;
likewise `photos-26-complete-log.json`, `photos-26-geotag-ingest.db` and `photos-26-archive-manifest.json`, and the
`photos-35` files. The full filename — number, name and
extension — is the identifier, never the number alone; `photos-0X-*` (and `1X`, `2X`, `3X`) names a band. The
bands are unrelated to the numbered media folders `0-sources`…`6-photos-by-dest`.
BLD-artifact_numbering.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media

BLD-artifact_numbering.title: An artifact's first digit names the phase that made it

`validate_config` SHALL check the configuration each time it is read: by prep as it seeds and reads it, by geotag and

A GPX self-anchor offset SHALL be set as `effective_time_anchor` with `decision_mode: "auto_resolved"` when its
anchors do not conflict and `camera_time_and_timezone_policy.multi_anchor_auto_apply` holds for two or more anchors,
or `single_anchor_auto_apply` for one — a phone's one anchor never ({need}`BLD-phone_offset_cell`); a destination's `inherited` timezone proposal is set as its
`effective_iana_timezone` likewise, a `config_default` one never; a `recorded_offset`, `timezone_naive` or `neighbour_day` offset proposal
becomes effective only with `accept_proposal: true`.

Prep's dry-run and execute SHALL refuse, before any change, a plan whose `blockers` list — where planning records every

BLD-by_dest_ops_refused.content:
Prep's plan SHALL hold no operation whose source or destination lies in `6-photos-by-dest`, its execute refusing a plan

BLD-cache_versions.content:
The workspace database's `meta` table SHALL hold `cache_schema_version` and `fingerprint_algorithm_version`, written by
each prep execute; prep's plan stops before reading the database when `cache_schema_version` is present and not this
build's.

BLD-camera_group_key.content:
The key SHALL be `camera_group_key`, computed by prep from the serial, make, model and owner fields and emitted in both
the handoff manifest and SQLite ({need}`BLD-metadata_extraction`); geotag consumes and classifies it
({need}`BLD-known_camera_group`).

BLD-camera_group_key_version.content:
The derivation of `camera_group_key` SHALL be versioned by `CAMERA_GROUP_KEY_VERSION`, recorded with each file's
metadata and in each plan's dependencies, and compared with the running code's: by prep's metadata freshness, by geotag's
plan against every file of the handoff, and by geotag's execute against its plan.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-camera_group_key_version.title: `CAMERA_GROUP_KEY_VERSION`

BLD-camera_identity_values.content:
Each identity field a file holds — `BodySerialNumber`, `CameraSerialNumber`, `InternalSerialNumber`, `SerialNumber`,
`Make`, `Model`, `OwnerName`, in that order — SHALL enter `camera_group_key` as its value's text with the blanks
around it stripped, the parts joined by `|`: a blank value is an empty part, so a file whose only identity fields are
blank has a key of empty parts (`""`, `"|"`, …), a camera group like any other; only a file holding none of them has
`NO_IDENTITY_KEY` (`unknown`) — and one whose only field reads `unknown`, which is then taken for a file naming no
camera ({need}`BLD-unidentified_files`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-camera_identity_values.title: Blank identity values

BLD-canonical_plan_paths.content:
The plan and decision artifacts SHALL be prep's `photos-10-prep-plan.json`, geotag's `photos-21`, `photos-22`,
`photos-23` and `photos-24`, and merge's `photos-30-merge-plan.json`, in `.photos-ingest/`: every phase's `plan` writes its file there,
`dry-run` and `execute` read it there, and no command takes a path flag for it.

BLD-carried_row.content:
Prep's plan SHALL carry a matched row whose fingerprint passes {need}`BLD-fingerprint_method` and whose metadata is
fresh as a `db_upsert` of it at the new path with the file's size, `mtime_ns` and inode; a matched stale row moves to
the new path in the planning's working state, where the freshness gate judges it as any row and the file's `db_upsert`
there is planned whatever it holds; each recognized move's `db_upsert` names the path it came from (`moved_from`), by
which prep's log finds the entry of a photo whose fingerprint changed with the move. The old path is left to the ghost
prunes; an unmatched row is a ghost, and its file is read as new.

BLD-case_rename_via.content:
A rename `plan_renames` plans whose new name differs from the current one only in case SHALL carry `via`: a
temporary name — the new name's stem with `.carto-case` before its extension, suffixed by `allocate_suffix` — free
among the destination's names and those planned. Execution moves the photo to it and then to the new name, each by a
no-clobber move and each name checked free first, so that a filesystem that ignores case, which holds the new name as
the photo's own, never refuses it nor overwrites anything; a photo found under `via` with its new name free is this
photo interrupted between the two, completed once it is seen to be the photo as planned.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-case_rename_via.title: A change of case alone goes by a temporary name

BLD-change_traced.content:
A change SHALL be traced from its decision record through the `depends_on` fingerprints ({need}`DEF-dependency_cascade`)
to the executable plan and the run's journal ({need}`BLD-prep_journal`; {need}`BLD-geotag_dependencies`,
{need}`BLD-geotag_execution`). Merge takes no decision; its placement is a fixed rule over recorded inputs, recorded the
same way ({need}`BLD-merge_journal_resume`, {need}`BLD-merge_records`).
BLD-change_traced.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-change_traced.title: How a change is traced to its decision

BLD-changed_fingerprint_mapped.content:
Merge's plan SHALL give a by-dest photo whose value taken again differs from the handoff's an `engine_mapping` — `was`
and `now`, each its `content_fingerprint` and `image_engine_version` — its `content_fingerprint` still the handoff's,
only where its path, size and modification time are those `photos-26-finalized-media.json` recorded, no other by-dest
photo holds its new value now, no file of the handoff held it, and no other by-dest photo's new value is its old; and
otherwise block it, naming why, together with a photo whose unchanged value its new value equals. A photo so mapped is
compared with the library's files — fingerprinted under the same version — by its new value: in the plan, at execute,
and when a later plan carries it forward and its place holds other bytes than those recorded as placed there
({need}`BLD-placed_bytes_journalled`).
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-changed_fingerprint_mapped.title: A changed fingerprint is mapped in the plan where it is one to one

BLD-changed_time_blocks.content:
The executable plan SHALL be `blocked` by a file with pinned values whose `DateTimeOriginal` and `OffsetTimeOriginal`
are neither the pinned pair — the true time the ledger keeps for it, where it keeps one
({need}`BLD-changed_time_kept_pinned`) — nor one the ledger records geotag writing, and whose question photos-21 holds no answer to
in effect ({need}`BLD-changed_time_question`), its blocker naming the file, the pair it holds, the last pair geotag wrote
to it — or that geotag wrote it no time — and its pinned pair; a file with no pin is not checked, and only those two
fields are compared.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-changed_time_blocks.title: A plan stops on a time changed since geotag wrote it

BLD-changed_time_kept.content:
A file whose answer in effect is `new`, or whose pin keeps a true time ({need}`BLD-changed_time_kept_pinned`), SHALL
be resolved from that pair's `DateTimeOriginal`, its recorded time, read by its destination's timezone
(`kept_true_time`) and by no cell's offset — a time the zone skips or repeats asked in `local_time_readings` as any
time the zone reads — its time write, that time with the zone's offset and its other time fields, planned as any
corrected time's.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-changed_time_kept.title: A time kept is resolved by its destination's zone

BLD-changed_time_kept_not_anchor.content:
A file resolved from a kept true time SHALL be left out, as a time geotag corrected is, of the photos its camera
group's offset cells are built from — anchors, fix times and recorded offsets — and of the drift check, of the photos
set against its destination's timezone, of the unreadable offset tags and of the question of files naming no camera.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-changed_time_kept_not_anchor.title: A time kept is left out of the clock's evidence

BLD-changed_time_kept_pinned.content:
The executable plan SHALL carry each kept pair, with its file's `content_fingerprint`, under `true_times_kept` by the
file's path, which execution writes into the file's pin in the original-values ledger as its `true_time` before any
write, while the file still holds that pair, the pinned own values staying — so every later plan resolves the file
from it, and asks nothing of the file holding it or a pair geotag wrote.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-changed_time_kept_pinned.title: A time kept is recorded beside the pin at execution

BLD-changed_time_kept_tag_noted.content:
Each `changed_times` cell whose `held_time` holds a time and an `OffsetTimeOriginal` that is an offset, and whose
destination's timezone gives another at that time — neither of its two, at a time it skips or repeats — SHALL hold
`offset_tag_disagrees`: `recorded_offset_seconds`, `timezone` and `timezone_offsets_seconds`; `geotag plan` warns of
each after writing photos-21. Kept, the time is read by the zone still.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-changed_time_kept_tag_noted.title: A kept time's offset tag that its zone does not give

BLD-changed_time_question.content:
Each file such a pair blocks SHALL be asked about in photos-21, in its destination's `changed_times` keyed by its path:
the cell names its `content_fingerprint`, its `held_time`, the last pair geotag wrote (`geotag_wrote`, or null) and its
`own_time` — the pinned pair, or the true time kept for it — and asks `user_decision.keep` — `new`, keep the time it holds, or `geotag`, take back geotag's —
with `answered_for`, the `held_time` it is given for. The answer is found again by the file's fingerprint and is in
effect (`effective_answer`) while `answered_for` is the pair the file holds, and, for `new`, while that pair holds a
time; another `keep`, or an answer with no `answered_for`, is a blocker; one given for another pair is
`stale_user_decision`. While a cell has no answer in effect it requires input, and photos-21 is not complete.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-changed_time_question.title: photos-21 asks of each changed time, by its photo

BLD-changed_time_restored_written.content:
A file whose answer in effect is `geotag` SHALL be planned as before the change — from its pinned values, or the true
time its pin keeps — its time write planned over the pair it holds as any write that differs from what a file holds.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-changed_time_restored_written.title: A time taken back is planned like any other

BLD-chosen_position.content:
An entry of `review_items` with `reason: "chosen_by_user"`, the `relative_path` of a photo `placed_photos` lists
({need}`BLD-placed_photos`) as placed by the tracks (`placed_by: "tracks"`) or the fallback (`placed_by:
"folder_fallback"`), and `manual_lat`/`manual_lon` — written by hand, or by the decision editor — SHALL be that photo's
decision: `classify_gps` gives it `manual_locked`, and photos-23 writes it back as a `manual_locked` review item, which
stays while its decision holds a position, found again by the photo's fingerprint whatever tracks or fallback come to
cover it; emptied, the photo is placed as before. An entry `chosen_by_user` whose path — or fingerprint — names no photo
of that destination, or one holding a position of its own, is a blocker naming it.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-chosen_position.title: A position chosen for a photo the tracks or the fallback place

BLD-clock_change_split.content:
For each `camera` day cell of photos not yet corrected, of a group not named in `several_bodies_groups`,
`clock_change_proposal` SHALL take the photos its GPX self-anchor anchors — else, with none, the readings of their
fixes' times — in the order of their true times: each anchor's camera time plus the offset of its match in the day's
consensus, the track time it matched; each reading's fix time. Where those photos do not already agree (the anchors
conflict or tie; the readings' offsets lie farther apart than `gpx_anchor_offset_spread_max_seconds`, their fix times
all different), it tries each place to cut them in two: a cut whose earlier and later photos each agree — a GPX
consensus over them with no conflicting photo, no tie and no stay; readings within the spread of each other, the first's
offset the run's — on offsets farther apart than the spread. Exactly one such cut, the first run's last true time — each
photo placed by its own run's consensus — a second or more before the second's first, is recorded on the day's cell
as `clock_change`: `evidence` (`gpx_self_anchor` or `gps_time`), `runs` — each `offset_seconds`, `photos`, and `first`
and `last` in true time (`source_file`, `camera_source_naive_time`, `real_utc`) — `unsettled`, and
`acceptance_tolerance_seconds`. A photo of the day that is a run's — anchored in it, or giving one of its readings — is
that run's part; another, at camera time t, could be the first part's where t plus the first run's offset is before
the second run's first true time, and the second's where t plus the second run's offset is after the first run's last:
one of the two, that part's; both or neither, it is listed in `unsettled` (`source_file`, `camera_source_naive_time`,
in camera-time order). The answer is the day cell's `user_decision.accept_clock_change`,
`accepted_change_offsets_seconds` (the runs' two offsets, in order) and `photo_parts` (an object giving a photo's
`source_file` its part, `1` or `2`), written on the cell only where a change is proposed or answered; not a boolean,
not two whole numbers, or not such an object, a blocker, as is an acceptance naming no offsets. Accepted while each
offset is within `gpx_anchor_decision_tolerance_seconds` of its run's, a `manual_offset_seconds` on the cell coming
first, and every `unsettled` photo given its part in `photo_parts` (else the cell asks), the day is split: the cell
holds `clock_change.effective_split` (`parts`, and `photo_parts`, the part of every photo of the day — its run's, the
one part that could take it, or the one it was given), its `effective_time_anchor` empty and asking nothing, and
beside it the parts `<key>#1` and `<key>#2`, each an offset cell built from its own photos as an acceptance of its
run's offset builds one — `gpx_anchor_accepted`, or `gps_time_accepted` — holding `clock_change_part` (`of`, `part`,
`photos`). An acceptance whose offsets are no longer the runs', or with no change proposed, is `stale_user_decision`
and splits nothing. A split day and its parts take no part in the offsets shared within a day
({need}`BLD-offset_shared_within_day`); `offset_cell_key` gives each photo of a split day the part its
`effective_split.photo_parts` names — one it names none, the day's cell, which offsets nothing.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-clock_change_split.title: A day split where the camera's clock changed

BLD-code_fingerprint.content:
The code's fingerprint, `code_fingerprint`, SHALL be the SHA-256 over the files of the `cartographer` package the
zipapp ships, as loaded — from the zipapp or a checkout, which agree — each one's path and bytes in path order. Prep's
plan records it as `code_fingerprint`, compared at execute and dry run after the plan's schema version and command and
before its operations; geotag's executable plan and merge's plan record it in their `depends_on`, a plan recording
another value or none stale at dry run and execute alike.
BLD-code_fingerprint.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-code_fingerprint.title: The code's fingerprint

BLD-collision_suffix.content:
An incoming photo whose name is taken by different content SHALL take, in the shared suffix convention
({need}`BLD-name_suffix`), the suffix one above the highest its name's root carries — the root its own name less any
`-NNN` it already carries — among the names in its library folder and those of every incoming photo bound for that
folder, passing over one taken there without regard to case; the library's own name keeps its bare form.
BLD-collision_suffix.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-collision_suffix.title: A different photo under a taken name takes the suffix above the highest

BLD-config_file.content:
The configuration SHALL be the JSON file `photos-00-config.json` in the workspace's control directory, `.photos-ingest/`,
which prep skips wholesale ({need}`BLD-prep_skip_set`) — never an in-code global.
BLD-config_file.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-config_file.title: The configuration is `photos-00-config.json`, in the control directory

BLD-config_fingerprints.content:
Two things SHALL be derived from the configuration: field-scoped fingerprints — the filename format, the camera-time and
timezone policy, the GPX thresholds, the camera-group-key version, the snapshot policy, the folder-name set, the
media-extension lists, and others — which drive staleness, the folder-set and media-extension fingerprints among the
dependencies of geotag's executable plan and of merge's plan; and one SHA-256 of the whole file, for integrity and
provenance, recorded in the archival manifest.

BLD-config_keys.content:
The areas SHALL be, at least: the `zfs` block and `snapshots_required` ({need}`BLD-snapshot_is_zfs`);
`camera_time_and_timezone_policy.device_groups`, with `phones` and `fixed_clock_cameras` ({need}`DEF-camera_group`), and
`several_bodies_groups` beside it ({need}`BLD-several_bodies_groups`);
`filename_timestamp_format` ({need}`BLD-filename_timestamp_format`); `gpx_root` and the GPX thresholds, such as `gpx_direct_match_max_seconds`,
`gpx_interpolation_max_gap_seconds` and `gpx_anchor_max_point_distance_meters` ({need}`DEF-tracks`), each read for one judgement only; the camera-time policy
flags, such as `single_anchor_auto_apply` and `multi_anchor_auto_apply` (geotag); `library_root`
(merge; {need}`DEF-library`) and `library_space_margin_percent` beside it ({need}`BLD-library_space`); `folders`, a role→name map of the numbered managed folders
`0-sources`…`6-photos-by-dest` ({need}`DEF-managed_folders`), whose code finds each folder by its role; and
`media_extensions`, mapping `image`, `raw` and `video` to lists of canonical extensions — lowercase, no leading dot
({need}`RUL-checked_extension_lists`). `CAMERA_GROUP_KEY_VERSION` is a code constant, never a configuration field.

Where `photos-30-merge-plan.json` is there and merge would read it as unreadable — it cannot be opened, does not parse as

BLD-contradicted_position.content:
A `camera` offset cell, of a group not named in `several_bodies_groups`, whose proposal is a precise GPX self-anchor and
whose effective source is `gpx_anchor_auto`, `gpx_anchor_accepted` or `gpx_anchor_chosen`, SHALL list, where the
anchors conflict or tie or the offset in effect is not the one proposed, in `positions_contradicted` the paths of its
photos holding their own position that matched a pass of the tracks and no pass of which agrees with the offset in
effect — within `gpx_anchor_offset_spread_max_seconds`, and the stay as well for a pass over
`gpx_anchor_stay_max_seconds` (`contradicted_frames`). Once photos-22 is complete, `contradicted_positions` gathers
them from the cells whose effective source is still one of those three; each is placed by the tracks at its resolved
time (`place_gps`), and where that place lies more than `gpx_anchor_max_point_distance_meters` from its own position,
photos-23 gives it a review item, `reason: "own_position_contradicted"`, `requires_user_input: false`, with
`own_position`, `proposed_position` (`lat`, `lon`, `method`, `gpx_file`) and `apart_meters`, its `user_decision`
`manual_lat` and `manual_lon`; where the tracks place it nowhere, its
destination's `gps_decisions.contradicted_without_track` lists it (`relative_path`, `content_fingerprint`). An item
whose earlier decision holds a position stays while it does, contradicted or not. A position set there replaces the
photo's own as `manual_locked`, its `metadata_gps_write` (`apply_manual`) carrying in `pre_state` the position it
replaces, which the log keeps ({need}`BLD-geotag_log_steps`).
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-contradicted_position.title: An own position the agreed offset contradicts

BLD-control_directory_contents.content:
The control records SHALL be these files in `.photos-ingest/` ({need}`DEF-archival_package` and {need}`DEF-workspace_database` for the archival and database ones):

```text
.photos-ingest/
  photos-00-config.json            workspace configuration (seeded by prep, BLD-config_file)
  photos-00-workspace.lock         the workspace lock: held by every run while it plans or executes (RUL-lock_through_the_run)
  photos-00-decision-editor.lock   the decision editor's lock: one editor at a time on a workspace
  photos-00-workspace-guard        workspace root sentinel: marks the workspace as INITIALIZED (written last by prep on init)
  photos-00-sealed.json            terminal/sealed marker, written by a successful merge ALONGSIDE the guard (a separate file, not a field inside the guard) — its presence seals the workspace (BLD-seal_marker)
  photos-00-ingest.db              SQLite identity/metadata cache + derived caches (live working DB, BLD-workspace_database)
  photos-00-plan-memo.db           prep-phase scratch: plan memo, what planning read of each media file (disposable, NOT part of the record)
  photos-01-accepted-changes.json  the changes to the workspace the user accepted, each by its code (BLD-accept_changes); an earlier one kept under -NNN
  photos-02-zone-table.json        the answer to whether to download the table of countries, and the copy downloaded (BLD-zone_table_question); an earlier one kept under -NNN
  photos-15-prep-ingest.db         prep-phase artifact: DB backup snapshot, end of prep (BLD-database_images)
  journal-*.json                   execution journals
  photos-10-prep-plan.json         prep-phase artifact: prep plan (written by `plan`, consumed by `dry-run`/`execute`; see "Canonical plan persistence" below)
  photos-11-handoff.json           prep-phase artifact: handoff manifest
  photos-15-prep-log.json          prep-phase artifact: end-of-prep audit log (BLD-prep_log_build)
  photos-16-prune-record.json      prep-phase artifact: what the latest deleting quarantine prune removed, and when (BLD-prune_record)
  photos-21-time-decisions.json    geotag-phase artifact
  photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json  geotag-phase artifact: GPS-drift validation gate (BLD-drift_validation)
  photos-23-gps-decisions.json     geotag-phase artifact
  photos-24-executable-plan.json   geotag-phase artifact
  photos-25-execution-summary.json geotag-phase artifact
  photos-26-complete-log.json      geotag-phase artifact: full transformation log (prep+geotag, at finalize, BLD-phase_logs)
  photos-26-geotag-ingest.db       geotag-phase artifact: DB backup snapshot, end of geotag (BLD-database_images)
  photos-26-finalized-media.json   geotag-phase artifact: each by-dest photo's size and mtime as finalize found it
  photos-26-archive-manifest.json  geotag-phase artifact: the archival package's manifest, at finalize (BLD-archive_manifest)
  photos-26-archive.tar.gz         geotag-phase artifact: the archival package, at finalize (BLD-archive_manifest)
  photos-30-merge-plan.json        merge-phase artifact: merge plan (written by `plan`, consumed by `dry-run`/`execute`)
  photos-31-merge-summary.json     merge-phase artifact: library-merge summary (BLD-merge_records)
  photos-35-merge-log.json         merge-phase artifact: full transformation log (prep+geotag+merge, BLD-phase_logs)
  photos-35-fingerprint-map.json   merge-phase artifact: each fingerprint another ImageMagick changed, old value to new (BLD-fingerprint_map)
  photos-35-merge-ingest.db        merge-phase artifact: DB backup snapshot, end of merge (BLD-database_images)
  photos-35-archive-manifest.json  merge-phase artifact: the re-sealed package's manifest, superseding photos-26's (BLD-merge_success_sequence)
  photos-35-archive.tar.gz         merge-phase artifact: the re-sealed archival package (BLD-merge_success_sequence)
  executed/<plan id>/              geotag: the decision records each executed plan ran against (BLD-history_kept)
  <artifact>-NNN.<ext>             a superseded plan or decision record, kept when it was replaced (BLD-plan_backups)
  gpx/                             gpx_root, when configured to live here (BLD-gpx_root)
```

The ids in it name the items that govern each entry.

BLD-coordinate_precision.content:
Geotag SHALL round a position it places between two track points or projects past an end to six decimal places of a
degree (about 0.1 m), and write a direct match's track point as the track gives it; a photo holds a position already
when its position marker is the one the write would carry and both its coordinates equal the position's to six
decimal places, and then no position is written ({need}`BLD-executable_plan`).

BLD-coordinate_precision.title: Coordinates to six decimal places

The costly caches SHALL be keyed on their own areas instead of the whole-file fingerprint: resolved UTC on the
time-policy subset ({need}`BLD-resolved_utc_fingerprint`), the renames on the filename-format fingerprint.

BLD-country_choice.content: A destination's `destination_timezone.user_decision.country` — the country it is in — SHALL hold an ISO 3166 code of `country_table` ({need}`BLD-country_table`) or be empty; another value is a blocker. The topmost country chosen above or at a destination is in effect there, recorded as `country`, with `country_from` where it was chosen above and `country_zones`. One chosen within it is written back empty, the cell holding `country_removed` (`country`, `because`, `country_there`) for that run, and `geotag plan` warns of each. A country of one timezone proposes it as `proposal_source: "country"`, taking effect like an inherited zone, over any zone from above. A country of several gives its own destination's zone to nothing within it and lets none through from above; within it a `manual_iana_timezone` that is none of `country_zones` is a blocker, and the configured default is proposed only where it is one. `photos-21-time-decisions.json` holds the table read as `countries`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-country_choice.title: The country a destination is in

BLD-country_table.content:
`zone_table(ws)` SHALL read `zone.tab` and `iso3166.tab` from where this Python reads its zones — `zoneinfo.TZPATH`,
then the `tzdata` package — as `source: "host"` where `zone.tab` is there; else the `copy` in the workspace's
`photos-02-zone-table.json` that `check_zone_table_text` still finds well formed, as `source: "web"`; else the copy in
the package's `zone_table/` (tzdata 2026c, from a Debian host's `/usr/share/zoneinfo`, with its `version`), as
`source: "bundled"`. `country_table` is its `countries`: every country of `zone.tab` holding a zone
`valid_iana_timezone` takes, named from `iso3166.tab` (its code where unnamed), with those zones, sorted; `sha256` is
the SHA-256 of `countries` as sorted JSON.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-country_table.title: The table of countries read

BLD-country_table_dependency.content:
`photos-24-executable-plan.json`'s `depends_on.country_table` SHALL be `{"source", "sha256"}` of the `zone_table` its
plan read, `revalidate_plan` holding the plan stale where the table read now differs in either.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-country_table_dependency.title: The plan names the table of countries it was made from

BLD-cross_fs_merge_only.content:
`_move_no_clobber` SHALL fall back to a cross-filesystem copy only when its caller passes `cross_fs=True`, which merge
alone does; for prep and geotag the `EXDEV` of a move across filesystems is raised as a failure.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-cross_fs_merge_only.title: Only merge's moves fall back to a copy

BLD-cross_fs_temp.content:
`_move_cross_fs_no_clobber` SHALL copy to a `.tmp-xdev-<random>.part` file in the destination directory, check it holds
the source's bytes — the same size, compared byte for byte — sync it, rename it into its place without overwriting, sync
the destination directory, and then remove the source.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-cross_fs_temp.title: The cross-filesystem copy

BLD-culled_raw_found.content:
At plan, after duplicates are set aside and before any name is checked, prep SHALL plan a `quarantine_move` of kind
`raw_culled` for each JPEG in `3-redundant-jpgs` whose `raw_fingerprint` in the prep log
({need}`BLD-set_aside_pair_recorded`) no file prep scanned holds — the inbox and `6-photos-by-dest` among them — and
which a workspace check found `deleted`: this run's, an earlier prep run's as `workspace_changes` of
`photos-15-prep-log.json` keeps it, or a geotag execution's as `photos-25-execution-summary.json` or a `-NNN` copy of it
keeps it ({need}`BLD-workspace_changes_logged`); a RAW moved out of the workspace is one, the check comparing only
the files inside it. The move carries the JPEG's `content_fingerprint`, and the RAW's
`raw_path` — the path the check found it deleted at — and `raw_fingerprint`, into the quarantine manifest; the JPEG's
entry in the prep log gains the step `raw_culled` with `from`, `to`, `raw_path` and `raw_fingerprint`, its `prep_path`
the quarantine path; and the execution's workspace record holds the JPEG in the quarantine like any file prep
quarantined.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-culled_raw_found.title: A culled RAW, found by its fingerprint

BLD-database_effects_one_transaction.content:
Execute SHALL apply the database effects of all its operations in one transaction, committed once every operation
has been carried out and checked, and rolled back where the run fails before that — the files being what the next
plan reads, the database is then as the earlier run left it.

BLD-database_images.content:
The images SHALL be `photos-15-prep-ingest.db`, written when prep writes its handoff and log;
`photos-26-geotag-ingest.db`, written by finalize with the complete log; and `photos-35-merge-ingest.db`, written when
merge succeeds, before it re-seals — each captured under the workspace lock by `VACUUM INTO` a `.tmp-` name in the
control directory, checked with `PRAGMA quick_check`, then renamed over the phase's earlier image.

BLD-database_ops.content:
Prep's plan SHALL refresh a stale database row with a `db_upsert`, and remove with a `db_remove` the row of a file gone
that no move explains and whose path no planned move fills again — that row is the move's to replace.

BLD-database_ops.title: The database is reconciled by planned operations

BLD-date_fallback_cell.content:
Each destination's entry in `photos-21-time-decisions.json`, a container's included, SHALL hold `date_fallback`:
`user_decision.date` — `""`, or `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD` in ASCII digits naming a day of the calendar, else a
blocker naming the destination and the value; `effective_date` — `date` as written, `filled`, the day it stands for as
`YYYY-MM-DD`, a month or day left out being `01`, and `set_at`, the destination it was written at — the one written
there, else, destinations being built parent first, its nearest ancestor's, else `null`; `inherited_from`, where an
ancestor has a date in effect, naming the nearest such, whether or not the destination writes its own;
`untimed_photos`, the paths of its photos whose `has_timestamp` is false, where it holds any; `requires_user_input`,
true where it lists one and has no `effective_date`, which leaves photos-21 incomplete; and `stale_user_decision`,
false. A photo whose `has_timestamp` is false is keyed `NO_IDENTITY_KEY` by `clock_group_key`, so in no group's offset
cell, drift check or class question; is resolved by `compute_resolved_utc` to its destination's `effective_date.filled`
at `00:00:00` read through the destination's zone, rule `date_fallback` — a midnight the zone skips or repeats asked as
{need}`BLD-local_time_readings` asks; is left by `classify_gps` and the tracks' window to its own position, the one set
for it or its folder's fallback, its review item's `tracks.reason` being `time_from_date_fallback`; and is written and
named by its resolved time as any photo is, its time write's `provenance` carrying `date_fallback` (`date`, `filled`,
`set_at`) and a `because` naming `photos-21 destinations.<set_at>.date_fallback`. A photo with a time of its own is
never given one. The values pinned at a photo's first write hold no time where it had none, so every later plan decides
it untimed again ({need}`BLD-decided_from_own_values`).
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-date_fallback_cell.title: The date fallback cell

BLD-day_folder_name.content: A day's folder SHALL be named `YYYY-MM-DD` from its recorded time's date, whatever `filename_timestamp_format` is.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-day_folder_name.title: A day's folder is named `YYYY-MM-DD`

BLD-day_offset_kept.content: A cell's dates SHALL be counted over all its group's photos in the destination, corrected ones included. A cell whose offset applied itself from the camera's own GPS (`gpx_anchor_auto`) records in `anchored_by` the track files of the anchors that agree with it, each with its SHA-256. A cell that would ask, its decision not given, takes the previous run's effective offset when that was `gpx_anchor_auto`, every file in its `anchored_by` is under `gpx_root` with that SHA-256, and no GPS proposal now made for it conflicts, ties, is imprecise or lies beyond `gpx_anchor_decision_tolerance_seconds` of it — as `decision_mode: "kept_from_earlier"`, `anchored_by` carried on; a cell whose photos are all corrected keeps its decision and its drift confirmation, the effective values derived again each run.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-day_offset_kept.title: A day's offset kept

BLD-decided_from_own_values.content:
Every plan SHALL decide about a photo from its own values, pinned before geotag first wrote to it
({need}`BLD-original_values_pinned`), so a withdrawn manual position is undone like any decision: the photo is placed
again, or geotag's position cleared; an
automatic position is recomputed, never rolled back.
BLD-decided_from_own_values.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-decided_from_own_values.title: Every plan decides from a photo's own values

BLD-decision_record_envelope.content:
`photos-21-time-decisions.json`, `photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json` and `photos-23-gps-decisions.json` SHALL each
carry `artifact_type`, `artifact_name`, `status` — `requires_user_input` or `complete` — `requires_user_input`, true
when any of its cells needs the user, `executable: false`, `depends_on`, and, when complete, `decision_mode`:
`no_op_or_auto_resolved` for photos-21 and photos-23, `no_op_or_confirmed` for photos-22. The `depends_on` of photos-21
holds the handoff's content fingerprint, `camera_time_policy_fingerprint` — over the whole
`camera_time_and_timezone_policy`, the camera groups' classes included — `gpx_fingerprint` and
`camera_group_key_version`. That of photos-23 holds `resolved_utc_cache_fingerprint`, `gpx_fingerprint`,
`gps_policy_fingerprint` — the SHA-256 of the nine placement settings of {need}`BLD-track_placement` as sorted JSON —
and `handoff`, the handoff's content fingerprint ({need}`BLD-handoff_content_fingerprint`).
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-decision_record_envelope.title: What every decision record carries

BLD-decision_records.content:
The decisions SHALL live in the `user_decision` fields of geotag's `photos-21`, `photos-22` and `photos-23`, each field
created by geotag and preserved across regeneration ({need}`RUL-decision_stage_writes_record`,
{need}`RUL-decision_kept`), the decision editor writing only those fields.

sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-decision_records.title: Where the decisions live

BLD-development_subfolder_case.content:
Geotag's and merge's preflights SHALL take a folder under `6-photos-by-dest` for a development subfolder when its name,
case folded, is one of `destination_distribution_subfolders`, case folded.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-development_subfolder_case.title: A development subfolder's name, case folded

BLD-drift_confirmation_tracks.content: A drift cell's `proposal` SHALL hold `tracks`, each track file its `track_segment` is drawn from with its SHA-256, by name, and the editor writes them with a confirmation as its `user_decision`'s `confirmed_against_tracks`. A confirmation takes effect only while every track it names is under `gpx_root` with the SHA-256 it names — naming none, only while `tracks` is empty; else the cell is `stale_user_decision`, its `user_decision` kept as written and taking no effect, and its `confirmed_tracks_changed` names the tracks no longer there with the SHA-256 named. Confirmed without a list of tracks, each a `gpx_file` and a `sha256`, a blocker.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-drift_confirmation_tracks.title: A drift confirmation names its tracks

BLD-drift_validation.content: Once photos-21 is complete, `geotag plan` SHALL write `photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json` with a cell for each offset cell whose effective source is `timezone_accepted`, `timezone_unconfirmed`, `recorded_offset_accepted`, `recorded_offset_unconfirmed`, `manual`, `gpx_anchor_imprecise`, `neighbour_day_accepted` or `neighbour_day_unconfirmed` and whose photos' resolved times lie within `drift_check_track_window_seconds` of track points, or, none lying there, whose photos' recorded times read as UTC do — whether or not a photo of the cell anchors on the tracks: its `proposal` holding `current_offset_seconds`, its source, the photos and that track segment; its `user_decision` `confirmed`, `corrected_offset_seconds` and `confirmed_offset_seconds`. A cell confirmed with `confirmed_offset_seconds` equal to its current offset takes effect as `gps_drift_validated` — the current offset when no correction is given, else the correction; confirmed against another offset it is `stale_user_decision` and takes no effect; confirmed naming none, a blocker. A `corrected_offset_seconds` or `confirmed_offset_seconds` that is written, the cell confirmed or not, is a whole number of seconds, else a blocker. Until every cell has taken effect, photos-23 and photos-24 are not written; then resolved UTC is computed again with the validated offsets, photos-21 left as it is. photos-22's `depends_on` holds photos-21's SHA-256, `gpx_fingerprint`, `camera_time_policy_fingerprint` and `camera_group_key_version`. A `timezone_unconfirmed`, `recorded_offset_unconfirmed` or `neighbour_day_unconfirmed` cell is always given its drift cell, whatever track lies by it. A phone's cell for its photos recording no offset is checked on those photos alone.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-drift_validation.title: The drift check

BLD-duplicate_evidence.title: The handoff names each duplicate's kept copy

BLD-editor_answers_every_question.content:
Each question geotag asks SHALL be a `user_decision` of a cell of its record, its fields documented in
`cartographer/editor/decision-json-reference.md`, which geotag reads whether the editor or a hand wrote it. The
editor loads and saves each by its kind: in photos-21, `timezone` (`destination_timezone`), `date` (`date_fallback`,
{need}`BLD-date_fallback_cell`), `offset` (a cell of
`camera_group_time_decisions`, a phone's among them, by its key — a day's split where its clock changed answered on the
day's cell, its parts never, and withdrawn there where geotag holds it stale, no change being proposed now), `reading` (an entry of `local_time_readings`, by
its photo's path), `changed` (an entry of `changed_times`, by its photo's path) and `unidentified`
(`unidentified_files`); in photos-22, `drift`; in photos-23, `fallback`, `review` and `chosen` (a photo of a
destination's `placed_photos`, by its path: written as its `chosen_by_user` review item, added where it has none —
{need}`BLD-chosen_position`);
in `photos-25-execution-summary.json`, which `geotag execute` reads, `fingerprint` (an entry of `fingerprint_mismatches`,
by its photo's path); and in the configuration a camera group's class, `camera` ({need}`BLD-editor_lists_new_camera_groups`),
and whether a camera group is several bodies, `bodies` ({need}`BLD-editor_marks_several_bodies`).
The editor writes each answer as geotag takes it, in each cell it is given for: where an offset cell lists
`conflicts_with`, a proposal the user takes there is written as `manual_offset_seconds`, the user's own offset, which
keeps its effect ({need}`RUL-chosen_offset_not_withheld`) — never as an acceptance, which geotag withholds there again;
and on a phone's day kept as it records itself, any other answer ends the keeping, which would outrank it
({need}`BLD-phone_offset_cell`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_answers_every_question.title: Every question is a decision field the editor answers

BLD-editor_checks_seal.content: `edit` SHALL refuse to serve a sealed workspace, with the same warning, its save writing nothing there.
BLD-editor_checks_seal.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_checks_seal.title: The editor checks the seal

BLD-editor_keeps_replaced_record.content:
Before it writes a record whose new bytes differ from those it loaded, the decision editor's save SHALL copy the record
to its next free `-NNN` sibling through `backup_existing_artifact`, the set-aside {need}`BLD-plan_backups` makes, so a
save's copies and a re-plan's are numbered as one series; a record whose bytes would not change is written with nothing
set aside. The configuration, written through `write_json_artifact`, keeps no copy, as merge's `init-library` keeps
none.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_keeps_replaced_record.title: The editor's save keeps the replaced record under `-NNN`

BLD-editor_lists_new_camera_groups.content:
The decision editor SHALL list, as `cameras`, each camera group of the handoff's photos under photos by destination that
`camera_time_and_timezone_policy.device_groups` lists in neither `phones` nor `fixed_clock_cameras`, or in both — the
groups geotag stops on, keyed as geotag keys them (`unclassified_camera_groups`) — with its photos' count and three of
their paths, and a `user_decision.device_class` it answers: `phones` or `fixed_clock_cameras`. Geotag's stop on such a
group still prints the two arrays, to paste in by hand.
BLD-editor_lists_new_camera_groups.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_lists_new_camera_groups.title: The editor lists the camera groups geotag stops on

BLD-editor_marks_several_bodies.content:
The decision editor SHALL list, as `cameras.bodies`, each camera group of the handoff's photos under photos by
destination that `device_groups` classes `fixed_clock_cameras` alone (`camera_groups_of_class`), with its photos' count,
three of their paths and `user_decision.several_bodies` — whether `several_bodies_groups` names it — never requiring
input; its save of one, `kind: "bodies"`, under the workspace lock and only while the configuration is the one it
loaded, by its SHA-256, puts the key into `camera_time_and_timezone_policy.several_bodies_groups` or takes it out,
refusing unless the group is still such a group of the photos, the answer a boolean, and the configuration then passes
the checks `load_config` makes, and writes the file again whole through `write_json_artifact`, every other setting
keeping its value.
BLD-editor_marks_several_bodies.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_marks_several_bodies.title: The editor names a camera group several bodies in the configuration

BLD-editor_save_locks.content:
The decision editor's save SHALL take the workspace lock for the time it writes, refusing at once while a run holds it;
the editor's display reads take none, each record being replaced whole. The editor is given, with each record it loads, the SHA-256 of its bytes, and sends them back with a save; under the lock the save compares them with the records on disk and checks that every edit names a decision its record holds, writing none of the records otherwise, and returns the hashes of what it leaves.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_save_locks.title: The editor's save takes the lock

BLD-editor_save_order.content:
The decision editor's save SHALL write, of the records it changes, `photos-21-time-decisions.json`,
`photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json`, `photos-23-gps-decisions.json`, `photos-25-execution-summary.json` and then
`photos-00-config.json`, in that order, each replaced atomically and synced to disk before the next is begun; a write
that fails ends the save there, the records before it written and those after it as they were.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_save_order.title: The order of the editor's save

BLD-editor_session_lock.content:
The decision editor SHALL take `photos-00-decision-editor.lock`, an exclusive lock taken without waiting that records
its owner, as `edit` opens a workspace, holding it until `edit` stops; the console's Edit tab takes it on its first
request for a workspace and holds it until the console stops. While another holds it, `edit` refuses to start and the
tab refuses to read or save. It is the editor's alone, apart from the workspace lock its saves take
({need}`BLD-editor_save_locks`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_session_lock.title: The editor's own lock, held for its session

BLD-editor_writes_device_groups.content:
The decision editor's save of a camera group's class SHALL, under the workspace lock and only while the configuration
is the one it loaded, by its SHA-256, put the group in the array named and take it out of the other, refusing unless the
group is still unclassed and the configuration then passes the checks `load_config` makes, and write the file again
whole through `write_json_artifact`, every other setting keeping its value.
BLD-editor_writes_device_groups.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_writes_device_groups.title: The editor writes a new camera group's class into `device_groups`

BLD-editor_zone_asking.content:
The editor SHALL show a timezone cell that requires input as settled once the decisions being edited give it a zone —
a `manual_iana_timezone` written there, a country of one timezone in effect there, or a zone reaching it from the
folders above as geotag passes one down ({need}`BLD-timezone_cell`, {need}`BLD-country_choice`) — and a container's,
once each destination of its `asked_for` is so settled, or it is given a zone itself.
Settled so, a cell whose photos then speak against the zone asks again on the next run.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_zone_asking.title: The editor's timezone questions, as the working decisions settle them

BLD-executable_plan.content: `photos-24-executable-plan.json` SHALL hold `status` — `ready`, or `blocked` with the plan's `blockers`, which `geotag plan` prints, exiting 2 — `executable`, `depends_on`, `plan_id` (the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of `depends_on`), `placement` — its photos counted as `native`, `matched`, `interpolated`, `extrapolated`, `manual_locked` or `manual_fallback` — and per destination its `operations`, `no_ops` (the photos it holds already as planned) and a `summary`. An operation is `metadata_time_write`, carrying the resolved time, its rule, offset and timezone, and the decision it followed; `metadata_gps_write`, its origin `apply_manual` — with the decision and the position it replaces — or `recompute_automated`, with the track file that placed it and the resolved time it was placed at; `gps_marker_write`, one that clears geotag's position carrying the position it removes; or `rename_no_clobber`. A write the photo already holds is not planned. A time is written as `DateTimeOriginal` with `OffsetTimeOriginal` as a sign, hours and minutes — an offset with seconds, as a zone's before it kept standard time, to the nearest minute — and its operation carries in `pre_state` the value each field it writes held and in `provenance` the field its time was read from.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-executable_plan.title: The executable plan

BLD-execution_summary.content: `photos-25-execution-summary.json` SHALL record the plan and execution ids, the SHA-256 of photos-24 and the dependencies it was validated against, counts per destination and in total, what was newly applied and what found satisfied, `failures` — each with its photo, operation id, operation `type` and the `error` that stopped it ({need}`BLD-write_failure_reason`) — `repeated_failures` ({need}`BLD-repeated_write_failure`) and blockers, `fingerprint_mismatches` — each with its expected and actual fingerprint and `user_decision.accept_fingerprint_change`, the one field a later execution reads — the snapshot, and run metadata apart; its `status` is `success`, `partial` (anything outstanding, a mismatch always), `failed` (nothing applied) or `rejected` (stopped before any change). An acceptance is read only from the summary of the same `plan_id` and holds for the `actual_fingerprint` it stands beside; a mismatch whose photo a later run of that plan finds still blocked is carried into the new summary as written. It is never a dependency.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-execution_summary.title: The execution summary

BLD-execution_summary_written.content:
`geotag execute` SHALL write `photos-25-execution-summary.json` only once its plan is revalidated and the records of
its earlier runs are read: when it has applied the plan, whatever the outcome, or, `rejected`, when a required snapshot
fails, carrying the fingerprint mismatches the summary it sets aside reports for the same plan. A refusal of the
preflight, a stale plan, a record that cannot be read or an interrupt writes none, the earlier summary left as it was;
an interrupted run's confirmations are in its journal.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-execution_summary_written.title: When the execution summary is written

BLD-exit_statuses.content:
Prep's plan, dry run, execute and `prune-quarantine`, and geotag's and merge's commands, SHALL exit 0 for a run that did what it was
asked; 1 for a workspace or a library found locked; 2 for a refusal — no control directory, the seal, a change in the
workspace no command made and none a person is expected to make, a workspace whose state no execution recorded (geotag's
and merge's), a record of accepted changes or of the answer about the table of countries it cannot read, a precondition,
a required tool absent, a plan missing, stale or failing its checks, a plan of prep's own it cannot read, a plan or
journal of merge's own it cannot read, a workspace database of another schema, a required snapshot not taken, a
prune's selection refused, and a plan, or a dry run, that reports a blocker; 3 for an execution that ended partial or failed — an operation failed, or
prep's log or handoff not written after its operations; and 130 for an interrupt. An error the build did not foresee
ends a command with 1, as Python ends it. Prep's execute or dry run with nothing to do ends 0. `merge init-library`
ends 0, 1 or 2 alike, and a phase named with no command prints what it does and ends 0.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-exit_statuses.title: The exit statuses

BLD-failed_fingerprint.content:
A fingerprint that could not be taken SHALL be recorded with the status `failed` and no value; prep's duplicate grouping
passes it over, its plan records a blocker for each such file outside `6-photos-by-dest`, and neither the workspace
database nor the plan memo offers it for reuse.
BLD-failed_fingerprint.section_name: 10. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
sections: 10. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-failed_fingerprint.title: A failed fingerprint is recorded as failed

BLD-failed_operation.content: Prep SHALL journal an operation that raised as `failed`, and stop.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-failed_operation.title: Prep's failed operation

BLD-fallback_placements_printed.content:
`geotag plan` SHALL print, for each destination whose folder fallback placed photos, how many, and whether the fallback
is its own or inherited, naming the destination it is inherited from — what photos-23 records as the destination's
`summary.automatic_folder_fallback` and its `folder_fallback`'s `fallback_source` and `inherited_from`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-fallback_placements_printed.title: What the fallback placed, printed and recorded

BLD-filename_format_zone_checked.content:
`validate_config` SHALL refuse a `filename_timestamp_format` that formats one time differently without a zone and with
a UTC offset of +05:30 — one holding `%z`, `%:z` or `%Z` — saying that prep names files from a time without a zone and
geotag from one with a zone; every phase reads the configuration through it before anything else.
BLD-filename_format_zone_checked.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-filename_format_zone_checked.title: A filename format reading a zone is refused

BLD-filename_timestamp_format.content:
The format SHALL be the configuration key `filename_timestamp_format`, default `"%Y-%m-%d--%H-%M-%S"`, which gives a
timestamp of the form `YYYY-MM-DD--HH-MM-SS`. Both phases read it; geotag's plans also depend on it through the
filename-format fingerprint ({need}`DEF-dependency_cascade`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-filename_timestamp_format.title: `filename_timestamp_format`

BLD-filesystem_trial.content:
`filesystem_lacks` SHALL make a folder of its own, `.photos-fs-trial-` and a random suffix, in the folder it is given,
and try in it, in order, each requirement asked: an exclusive non-blocking `flock` taken and let go; `os.replace` onto
a taken name; `_rename_no_clobber_same_fs` refusing a taken name, both files left as they were, and moving to a free
one; `fsync` of a file; `fsync` of the folder — returning the first that fails or raises, then removing its folder and
putting back the given folder's modification time. The workspace's are all five, tried in the control directory, or in
the workspace itself on a first prep run, before the control directory is made.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-filesystem_trial.title: The filesystem's requirements, tried on scratch files

BLD-finalize_checks_prep_log.content:
Geotag's finalize SHALL copy prep's log only when its bytes hash to the value {need}`BLD-prep_log_vouched` records, and
stop otherwise — the log missing or unreadable, or the handoff recording no hash, among the cases.
BLD-finalize_checks_prep_log.section_name: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-finalize_checks_prep_log.title: Finalize copies only the log the handoff vouches for

BLD-finalize_preconditions.content: `geotag finalize` SHALL refuse, writing nothing, unless `photos-24-executable-plan.json` is `ready`, `photos-25-execution-summary.json` is `success` for the same `plan_id`, every dependency of the plan but the handoff still holds — the handoff left out because prep, run after execute, records geotag's own writes and renames in it, and the tracks taken as the catalogue keeps them ({need}`BLD-track_window`) — and every photo under `6-photos-by-dest` is one of the plan's, at its final path, with the size and modification time the journal's `media_after` records for it, or the plan's `media_preconditions` for a photo the plan had nothing to do to — none of them holding no position ({need}`BLD-no_photo_unplaced`) — and every JPEG set aside in `3-redundant-jpgs` that the plan renames with its RAW ({need}`BLD-set_aside_renamed_with_raw`, {need}`BLD-set_aside_jpeg_catches_up`) is at its new name with the size and modification time `media_after` records for it. It prints the plan's `placement` and writes it into the archive manifest; the log gives each position from the tracks its `gpx_file` and `at_utc`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-finalize_preconditions.title: What finalize checks first

BLD-finalized_media.content:
`geotag finalize` SHALL write `photos-26-finalized-media.json`, giving each photo in photos by destination, under its
final path, its size and modification time; merge's preflight refuses when a photo still there differs from it, or the
record is missing.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-finalized_media.title: Each photo as finalize found it

BLD-fingerprint.content: A photo's fingerprint SHALL be ImageMagick's signature — a SHA-256 of the normalized pixel stream — of its one frame, or, of a file of several frames, the SHA-256 of every frame's signature, one to a line, in order, the same whichever of the two ways of running ImageMagick took it; a video's, the `ffmpeg` MD5 of all its streams as stored, copied out without decoding (`-map 0 -c copy -copy_unknown`).
BLD-fingerprint.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-fingerprint.title: How a fingerprint is computed

BLD-fingerprint_map.content:
A whole merge SHALL write `photos-35-fingerprint-map.json` — `artifact_type` `fingerprint_map`, its `artifact_name`,
`schema_version` 1, and under `photos`, keyed by its new value, each photo merged with an `engine_mapping`: that
mapping's `was` and `now`, its by-dest path as `from` and its `library_path` — empty where none was; geotag's records,
the log copied forward, are left keyed by the old value, and none is rewritten.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-fingerprint_map.title: Merge's package maps each changed fingerprint, old value to new

BLD-fingerprint_method.content:
Each fingerprint SHALL record its strategy — `image-content-hash-v2` for a photo, `video-md5-v2` for a video — and a
photo's the ImageMagick version that took it; a cached photo fingerprint is reused when both match the build's, a video's
when its strategy does. The handoff carries the method's version (`depends_on.cache.fingerprint_algorithm_version`); geotag's and merge's preflight stop on one that is not the build's.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-fingerprint_method.title: A fingerprint records its method

BLD-folder_fallback_cell.content:
Destinations SHALL be built parent first; each one's `folder_fallback` carries as `inherited_fallback` the
`fallback_lat`/`fallback_lon` written at its nearest ancestor that has them, as `lat`, `lon` and `from` (that ancestor),
else null. Its `user_decision` holds `fallback_lat` and `fallback_lon`. Its `effective_fallback` is the position written
there (`fallback_source: "own"`), else the inherited one (`fallback_source: "inherited"`, with `inherited_from`), else
null (`fallback_source: "none"`). Its `requires_user_input` is always false.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-folder_fallback_cell.title: The folder-fallback cell

BLD-folder_removals.content:
Prep's plan SHALL end with an `rmdir` for each folder it leaves holding no file — under `0-sources`,
`4-videos-by-date` and `5-photos-by-date`, and on the first run the dump's own top-level folders — found by replaying
its moves over the files on disk, hidden ones included, deepest folder first; execute removes one only if it is then
empty, journals a folder found not empty or not removable as skipped, and warns of it.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-folder_removals.title: Folder removals are `rmdir` operations

BLD-format_recorded.content:
The handoff SHALL record the format prep named the files in as `filename_timestamp_format`; prep compares it with the
configured format at plan once a file outside the inbox carries a timestamp name, and geotag and merge at their start.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-format_recorded.title: The format recorded in the handoff

BLD-geotag_auto_reprep.content:
When the only change prep has not recorded is one {need}`BLD-reprep_pending` names and the inbox is empty, `geotag
plan` SHALL run prep's `plan` and `execute` itself, inside its own lock, saying so, before it plans. Between the two it reads the plan prep saved and, where that holds a move, a rename or a quarantine of a media file, runs no execute: it stops, the plan left for the user to inspect and carry out.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_auto_reprep.title: Geotag runs prep itself when the inbox is empty

BLD-geotag_checks_decisions.content:
Geotag SHALL check the decisions in `photos-21`, `photos-22` and `photos-23` as it reads them: each blocker names the
artifact, the destination, the cell or the file, and the field, and an artifact holding one is left as
it is, its plan not written. A decision artifact that cannot be read, does not parse as JSON or is not a JSON object is
such a blocker, located to where parsing failed — never taken as absent. So is a `photos-23` review item's
`user_decision` holding a field other than `manual_lat` and `manual_lon` (`unknown_review_fields`), one blocker per
field, naming it; the decision editor shows such a `photos-23` as a record it cannot read, with those blockers.
BLD-geotag_checks_decisions.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_checks_decisions.title: Where geotag checks the decisions

BLD-geotag_dependencies.content:
`photos-24-executable-plan.json` SHALL record in `depends_on` the SHA-256 of `photos-21`, `photos-22` and `photos-23`;
the handoff's `content_fingerprint`; `config_fingerprint`, `code_fingerprint`, `camera_group_fingerprint`,
`camera_group_key_version`, `gpx_fingerprint` with the `gpx_window` it is of, `metadata_field_set_version`, `filename_format_fingerprint`,
`folders_fingerprint` and `media_extensions_fingerprint`; `resolved_utc_cache_fingerprint` and
`prep_cache_fingerprint`; each photo's `media_preconditions`; `planned_operation_fingerprint`; and `country_table`
({need}`BLD-country_table_dependency`). Execute recomputes
all but the two cache fingerprints — vouched for by the records and handoff they were derived from, checked where they
are made — before any change, and each photo's preconditions as it applies it. `photos-25-execution-summary.json` is
never checked as a dependency.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_dependencies.title: Geotag's dependencies, recorded and checked

BLD-geotag_destinations.content:
A photo's destination SHALL be the `dirname` of its path; the container destinations are every ancestor of a
destination within `6-photos-by-dest` that is not one, `6-photos-by-dest` included, each marked `file_less: true` in the
decision records, its fallback cell never requiring input, its timezone cell only as {need}`BLD-zone_asked_at_containers` says, and its `camera_group_time_decisions` empty;
destinations are processed parents first.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_destinations.title: Geotag's destinations

BLD-geotag_execution.content: `geotag execute` SHALL, under the workspace lock: revalidate every dependency of photos-24 — and, when it holds an operation, that the image engine is the handoff's `depends_on.cache.image_engine_version` — and stop before any change if one moved; take the snapshot labelled `geotag`, a required one that fails ending the run as `rejected`; keep photos-21, -22 and -23 in `executed/<plan id>/`; pin and move the own values, single-threaded; then, per photo and under `-j`, skip one whose operations the journal confirms; take one gone from its path with its rename target in place as applied before — its operations recorded, not redone — once the target has the planned fingerprint (or the accepted one) and holds the planned tags, else block; and for one whose size or modification time changed since the plan block if its decoded content differs and is not accepted, else read its tags back — holding the planned values it is counted applied, otherwise, or with only a rename planned, it blocks as edited since the plan. Otherwise it writes the photo's tags in one `exiftool` call ({need}`BLD-metadata_safe_write`), retakes its fingerprint — a changed one, not accepted, or one that cannot be taken, a mismatch that holds the photo's writes and rename back — and renames it, the target checked free. Anything a photo's application raises is that photo's failure and blocker. The results merge in path order into the journal, kept per plan id — each confirmed photo's final path, size and modification time under `media_after` — and photos-25.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_execution.title: How execution applies the plan

BLD-geotag_exiftool_needed.content:
Geotag's preflight SHALL stop `plan` and `execute`, exit 2, when `exiftool` is not on `PATH` — execution reads and
writes the photos' tags through it, and a plan is made to be executed — and leave `finalize`, which runs no tool on a
photo, to proceed without it.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_exiftool_needed.title: Where exiftool is needed

BLD-geotag_failed_write.content:
Geotag SHALL record a metadata write whose tool failed, or a rename that raised, as failed, confirming neither: a
failed write leaves the file as exiftool found it, a failed rename leaves it under its name.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_failed_write.title: Geotag's failed write

BLD-geotag_file_model.content:
Geotag's `build_file_model` SHALL take, from the handoff, only the records whose `folder_class` is `6-photos-by-dest`
and whose `media_class` is `image` or `raw`; every operation of `photos-24-executable-plan.json` names one of them, but
the renames of the JPEGs set aside beside them ({need}`BLD-set_aside_renamed_with_raw`,
{need}`BLD-set_aside_jpeg_catches_up`).
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_file_model.title: Geotag's file model

BLD-geotag_final_name.content:
Geotag SHALL compute the final name as resolved UTC → the destination's civil timezone → a local naive datetime → the
format. Two instants of the hour a zone repeats give one local time, and the name is that local time for both.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_final_name.title: Geotag's final name, step by step

BLD-geotag_log_steps.content:
Geotag's steps SHALL be `clock_offset_applied` (its `offset_seconds` with an `offset_description` in words, such as
"camera clock 1 h 55 min ahead of UTC"), `resolved_utc`, `timezone_resolved`, `time_written` (with its `writes`, the
`pre_state` it replaced — the value each field it writes held — the field `read_from` and the `rule`, from the plan),
`true_time_kept` (the time the user kept as the photo's true time, its `value`, from the plan's `true_times_kept`),
`date_fallback_applied` (the date fallback that gave a photo with no recorded time its time: its `value` as the user
wrote it, the day it was `filled` to and the cell it was written in as `because`, from the time write's provenance),
`gps_written` (with its
origin, method and, for a manual position or one written over a position the device wrote that is none of the photo's
own, the `pre_state` it replaced, from the plan), `gps_cleared` (a position geotag
wrote and no longer places, with that position, from the plan, and the method left), `gps_preserved` and `final_rename`,
each naming its `run`; finalize takes them from every executed pass — each superseded `photos-24` whose journal shows it
ran, oldest first, matched by fingerprint — before the current plan's, from the provenance each time write carries.

sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
