BLD-geotag_records_by_destination.content:
`photos-21`, `photos-22`, `photos-23` and `photos-24` SHALL each hold a `destinations` object keyed by the
destination's path under `6-photos-by-dest`, every decision of a destination inside its entry.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_records_by_destination.title: Geotag's records are grouped by destination

BLD-geotag_records_versioned.content:
`photos-25-execution-summary.json` SHALL be written as {need}`BLD-plan_backups` writes a plan — an existing one that
differs first copied whole to the next free `-NNN` — and `geotag finalize`, which may be run again, first copies each
file of an existing package so — `photos-26-complete-log.json`, `photos-26-finalized-media.json`,
`photos-26-geotag-ingest.db`, `photos-26-archive-manifest.json` and `photos-26-archive.tar.gz`, the last as
`photos-26-archive-NNN.tar.gz` — before it writes the new one; the copies are archived with the rest of the control
directory, an archive and its copies excepted.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_records_versioned.title: Summaries and packages set aside under `-NNN`

BLD-geotag_stage_order.content:
`geotag plan` SHALL recognise the camera groups — stopping on an unknown one before reading any track — then read the
tracks, then write `photos-21-time-decisions.json`; only once it is complete resolve each photo's true time and
write `photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json`; only once that is complete write `photos-23-gps-decisions.json`; and only
once all three are complete assemble `photos-24-executable-plan.json`, which refuses any photo without a valid
resolved time.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_stage_order.title: Geotag's planning stages, in order

BLD-geotag_untimed_gate.content:
Geotag's preflight SHALL pass a photo under `6-photos-by-dest` whose `metadata_status.has_timestamp` — or, failing it,
the `has_timestamp` of its `parsed_json` — is false; `geotag plan`, once it has written
`photos-21-time-decisions.json`, stops with exit status 2 before resolving any time where a destination's
`date_fallback` requires input ({need}`BLD-date_fallback_cell`), naming the photos it lists in `untimed_photos`, the
date fallback, and `2-missing-metadata`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_untimed_gate.title: Geotag stops at photos-21 on a photo with no recorded time and no date

BLD-gone_photo_entry.content:
An entry of the prior `photos-15-prep-log.json` whose fingerprint no database row holds, which this run's plan gives no
step and no quarantine record, and which no `fingerprint_retaken` claims ({need}`BLD-prep_log_build`), SHALL be written
into the new log unchanged, `prep_path` included.
BLD-gone_photo_entry.section_name: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-gone_photo_entry.title: A gone photo's entry is copied unchanged

BLD-gps_decisions_record.content:
Each destination's entry in `photos-23-gps-decisions.json` SHALL hold its `folder_fallback` cell and `gps_decisions`:
a `summary` counting `files_total`, `preserve_native_gps`, `automatic_gpx_interpolation`,
`automatic_gpx_extrapolation`, `automatic_folder_fallback`, `manual_locked`, `blocked` and `manual_review_required`; an
`automatic_decision_summary` naming the track files used; `review_items` — one per photo `blocked`
(`no_reliable_gps_source`, requiring input) or `manual_locked`, each with `manual_lat` and `manual_lon` — and one per
photo whose own position its camera's agreed offset contradicts ({need}`BLD-contradicted_position`); and, where there
are any, `placed_photos`, every other photo ({need}`BLD-placed_photos`). The executable plan reads no automatic position
from the record: it derives each again from its own inputs.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-gps_decisions_record.title: The GPS decisions record

BLD-gps_time_proposal.content: `build_file_model` SHALL give each photo holding its own position its fix's UTC as `gps_utc` — `GPSDateTime`, as exiftool's composite or XMP holds it, its zone `Z` or an offset, else `GPSDateStamp` with `GPSTimeStamp`; a fraction of a second dropped; a value that is no time, none — and `gps_time_proposal` reads, of a bucket's photos not yet corrected holding their own position, each `gps_utc` less the camera time, two photos with the same `gps_utc` and the same camera time being one reading. Where no track anchors the bucket, the readings, their `gps_utc` all different and their offsets within `gpx_anchor_offset_spread_max_seconds` of each other, propose the earliest one's offset as `proposal_source: "gps_time"` with `proposed_offset_seconds`, `proposed_real_utc`, `gps_time_count`, `acceptance_tolerance_seconds` and `gps_times` (the first `GPS_TIMES_SHOWN`: `source_file`, `camera_source_naive_time`, `gps_utc`, `offset_seconds`), ahead of the offset shared from the same day, `recorded_offset` and `timezone_naive`; otherwise the cell holds `gps_time_set_aside` — `reason` (`repeated_gps_time` or `offsets_disagree`), `gps_time_count`, an `example`, and for the second the lowest and highest offset. Two readings or more take effect as `gps_time_auto`, `decision_mode: "auto_resolved"`, under `multi_anchor_auto_apply`; one only once accepted, as `gps_time_accepted`, an acceptance holding within `gpx_anchor_decision_tolerance_seconds` as one of a GPX proposal does. No drift check follows either, and neither is passed to another destination.
BLD-gps_time_proposal.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-gps_time_proposal.title: The offset the fixes' own times give

BLD-gpx_fingerprint.content:
The GPX fingerprint SHALL be a SHA-256 over a version tag, the ranking of the tracks, and every point in the tracks'
window ({need}`BLD-track_window`), in time order, each with its time, position, file under `gpx_root`, index, track and
segment — so a track file's bytes outside the window, and the root's own path, enter it not at all. An empty
`gpx_root`, a `gpx_root` that is not a directory, and one with a folder that cannot be listed, each give a fixed value
of their own, the last two with a warning. It is recorded as `gpx_fingerprint` in the
`depends_on` of `photos-21-time-decisions.json`, `photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json`, `photos-23-gps-decisions.json`
and `photos-24-executable-plan.json`, and checked before each is used.
BLD-gpx_fingerprint.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-gpx_fingerprint.title: The GPX fingerprint

BLD-gpx_root.content:
The tracks' location SHALL be the configuration key `gpx_root`: a path, absolute or relative to the workspace, resolved
through links before use; empty means no tracks. It MAY be anywhere outside `0-sources` … `6-photos-by-dest` — on any
disk, or under the control directory, such as `.photos-ingest/gpx/`, which prep's skip of `.photos-ingest/` already keeps
out of the scan. Geotag catalogues every `*.gpx` file beneath it ({need}`BLD-track_catalogue`). The value and the matching thresholds are read by geotag;
their detail is {need}`BLD-track_points` and {need}`BLD-anchor_matching`.
BLD-gpx_root.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-gpx_root.title: `gpx_root`

BLD-gpx_root_checked.content:
Configuration validation, in every phase, SHALL resolve `gpx_root` against the workspace, through links, and refuse it
when it is a managed folder, lies inside one, or contains one — the workspace root among them.
BLD-gpx_root_checked.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-gpx_root_checked.title: `gpx_root` checked against the managed folders

BLD-gpx_root_missing.content: `geotag plan` SHALL stop before its first record, exit 2, when `gpx_root` is set and is not a directory — `geotag execute` then finds its plan stale; an empty `gpx_root`, or one holding no track, plans without tracks. The index keeps each file's points as a track of its own (`GPXIndex.tracks()`) and its SHA-256 (`file_sha`); placement and anchoring read the tracks one by one.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-gpx_root_missing.title: Tracks kept apart, and a root that is not there

BLD-group_in_both_lists.content: A `camera_group_key` listed in both `phones` and `fixed_clock_cameras` SHALL be classed `unknown`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-group_in_both_lists.title: A group in both lists

BLD-hand_change_is_work.content:
Prep's stop on an already-prepped workspace SHALL not apply while the run's check of the workspace
({need}`BLD-workspace_check`) named or accepted a change since the last execution, or no execution has recorded the
workspace's state yet ({need}`BLD-workspace_record`), so that prep's execute records it.
BLD-hand_change_is_work.section_name: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-hand_change_is_work.title: A change by hand is not "nothing to do"

BLD-handoff_content.content:
Prep's execute SHALL write `photos-11-handoff.json` last but for the database image and the mark, through a temporary
file renamed over it, holding: `schema_version`, `tool`, `run_metadata` (plan and execution ids), `cache_fingerprint`,
`folders_scanned` (the managed folders but `1-strays`, each with whether prep may change it), `files` (sorted, each with
its path, size, `mtime_ns`, `inode` — as the file's database row last recorded it — media class, fingerprint and its
status, folder and metadata),
`filename_timestamp_format`, `camera_groups`, `destination_folders` ({need}`BLD-handoff_grouping_facts`),
`diagnostics` (duplicates, the other files quarantined, blockers, warnings, quarantine footprint), `depends_on` (configuration, prep log, journal,
final inventory, metadata extractor, plan and database versions, image engine) and `content_fingerprint`.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-handoff_content.title: What the handoff holds

BLD-handoff_content_fingerprint.content:
`content_fingerprint` SHALL be the SHA-256 of the handoff serialized with sorted keys, without the keys `run_metadata`,
`diagnostics`, `execution_journal`, `prep_log`, `content_fingerprint`, `cache_freshness` and `conflicts_or_duplicates`
wherever they appear — the last two being each camera group's and destination folder's run-scoped counts and
duplicates. Each file's `inode` is in what it covers, as it is in `cache_fingerprint`: a file whose row is written again
at another inode changes both, though its size, time and fingerprint do not.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-handoff_content_fingerprint.title: The handoff's content fingerprint

sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-handoff_field_set_checked.title: The handoff's field set is this build's

BLD-handoff_grouping_facts.content:
The handoff SHALL carry `camera_groups` — each group's key, files and count, identity fields, earliest and latest
recorded time, native-GPS, missing-GPS and missing-time counts, cache freshness and the device class the configuration
gives it — and `destination_folders` — each folder's path, files scanned, camera groups, time range, native-GPS,
missing-GPS and `GPSProcessingMethod` counts, cache freshness, and the duplicates whose kept copy it holds.
BLD-handoff_grouping_facts.section_name: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-handoff_grouping_facts.title: The handoff's camera groups and destination folders

BLD-handoff_hashes.content:
The handoff SHALL be `photos-11-handoff.json` in `.photos-ingest/`, which geotag checks by its `content_fingerprint` —
the content-scoped staleness key prep stamps on it ({need}`BLD-handoff_content_fingerprint`) — recomputing it and comparing it with the value in
geotag's dependency block ({need}`BLD-geotag_dependencies`). Its whole-file SHA-256 is kept as an integrity and archival
hash ({need}`DEF-archival_package`), never the dependency check.

sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media

BLD-handoff_hashes.title: The handoff's two hashes

BLD-hash.content: A hash SHALL be a SHA-256 over the exact bytes of a numbered JSON record or the configuration.

sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed

BLD-hash.title: How a hash is computed

BLD-history_kept.content:
Each plan's journal SHALL be kept as its own `journal-<plan id>.json` — prep's, where the plan is executed again,
first copied to the next free `journal-<plan id>-NNN.json` (`backup_existing_artifact`) — each geotag execution keeping the decision records its
plan depended on, verified by hash, in `executed/<plan id>/`, which a step's `because_record` and
`because_record_sha256` name.

sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-history_kept.title: The journals and the decisions each execution used are kept

BLD-idempotency.content:
Each phase SHALL reuse what is still valid: prep, the cached fingerprint and metadata of a file whose size and
modification time are unchanged, carrying a moved file's identity forward without reading it ({need}`RUL-moved_file_carried`), a plan never executed leaving its fingerprints and metadata for the next plan to reuse
({need}`RUL-plan_memo_kept`); geotag reads no photo,
taking every photo's metadata from prep, works out its results again on each run — a result that comes out the same
leaving everything that depends on it as it is — keeps each decision whose target is unchanged
({need}`RUL-decision_kept`), and reads only a track file new or changed since the catalogue recorded it, or one the
tracks' window has grown into, taking the rest from the points the catalogue keeps ({need}`BLD-track_catalogue`); merge, a library file's fingerprint while its size and
modification time are unchanged ({need}`BLD-library_file_fingerprinted`). Fingerprinting (ImageMagick `identify`,
`ffmpeg`), metadata extraction (`exiftool`) and GPX parsing thus run only for new or changed inputs. Each phase's own
consequences are in its spec:
{need}`RUL-no_op_run`, {need}`RUL-geotag_execution_resumable` and {need}`RUL-merge_resumable`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-idempotency.title: What each phase reuses

BLD-identical_replan_writes_nothing.content: A re-plan whose content is byte-identical to the saved artifact SHALL write nothing and back up nothing.
BLD-identical_replan_writes_nothing.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-identical_replan_writes_nothing.title: A byte-identical re-plan writes nothing

BLD-identify_silence_limit.content:
Where `magick` is absent, each per-file `identify` attempt SHALL be killed once ten seconds pass with no output from it,
the attempt counting as failed — so a photo whose decode is slower than that fails both attempts and its fingerprint is
recorded as failed; the persistent `magick` worker has no such limit.
BLD-identify_silence_limit.section_name: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-identify_silence_limit.title: A silent `identify` is killed after ten seconds

BLD-init_library_cases.content:
`merge init-library [path]` SHALL resolve a given path to an absolute one and require an existing directory, then:
inside a workspace with a path, refuse a path `library_place_error` names and, under the lock, check the workspace's
filesystem and the seal, read the configuration through `load_config`, mark the directory and record it as
`merge.library_root`; inside a workspace without one, under the lock, read the configuration the same way and mark the
`library_root` it names, writing nothing in the workspace; outside any workspace with a path, mark the directory and
write nothing else; outside any workspace without one, stop with exit status 2. A configuration that cannot be read or
fails its checks stops it with exit status 2, nothing marked and nothing written.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-init_library_cases.title: `init-library`'s four cases

BLD-init_library_checks_seal.content:
`merge init-library` given a path from inside a workspace, which would record it as `library_root` in the configuration,
SHALL check the seal under the lock the same way, and stop with exit status 2 having blessed nothing; without a path, or
from outside any workspace, it writes nothing in the workspace and does not check.
BLD-init_library_checks_seal.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-init_library_checks_seal.title: `init-library` checks the seal before recording a library

BLD-init_library_writes_library_root.content:
The setup command `init-library` ({need}`BLD-init_library_cases`), run inside a workspace with an explicit library path,
MAY write the `library_root` key into the configuration, and only that key, writing the file again whole through
`write_json_artifact`: every other setting keeps its value, while the file's layout — the order of its keys, its
indentation, characters beyond ASCII written as escapes — becomes that of the control records. It is not part of
merge's data path.
BLD-init_library_writes_library_root.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-init_library_writes_library_root.title: `init-library` may write `library_root`

BLD-init_move_suffix.content:
The initializing run's move of a dump file SHALL go to `0-sources/<its path>`, and where that path, ignoring case, is
another file's current or planned path, to the same folder under `<name>-NNN.<ext>` with the first `NNN` from `001` so
free ({need}`BLD-name_suffix`), the extension kept as it was; the suffixed name is the one the later stages name the
file from.
BLD-init_move_suffix.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-init_move_suffix.title: A taken inbox path takes the next `-NNN`

BLD-interrupted_run_recognised.content:
Each execution SHALL note itself begun, before its first change, by adding `{phase, plan_id, record_id}` to the list
`meta.executions_unrecorded` of `photos-00-ingest.db` (`note_execution_begun`) — prep's execute before its operations,
geotag's `execute_plan` and merge's `execute_plan` before their photos — nothing noted where no record exists yet; and
`write_workspace_record` deletes the list in the transaction that writes the record. A note left with the current
record's id is therefore an execution begun since that record and never recorded — the interrupted run. The check
(`recognise_interrupted_work`, before `compare_workspace`) finds each such run's plan by its id — `photos-10`, `photos-24`
or `photos-30`, or the version a re-plan kept under `-NNN` — and its journal `journal-<plan id>.json`, and takes into
the record it compares with, over a copy of it: for prep, each file its move, rename and quarantine operations take,
followed through them in plan order, found at exactly one place they take it with the recorded file's size, time and
inode — or, from the inbox, the plan's preconditioned size and time — gone from where it was (an inbox path looked
for on disk, the inbox being in no record) and at a place no recorded file holds, and `<quarantine>/<plan id>/manifest.json` where it holds only entries of the plan's quarantine operations;
for geotag, each photo whose rename target (or own path) the journal's `media_after` notes, found there with exactly
that size and time, gone from its recorded path where renamed; for merge, each photo of the plan gone from photos by
destination that the journal confirms, or whose `library_target` has its recorded size and time. Each is returned as
`interrupted_run` with its `phase` and `plan_id`, printed by run and returned with the changes the run names
(BLD-workspace_changes_logged); `write_workspace_record` takes the same copy for the earlier record, so each file keeps
its fingerprint at the place it was taken to. A plan not found, or a plan or journal of another shape, recognises
nothing; whatever is not recognised is compared as any other change.
BLD-interrupted_run_recognised.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-interrupted_run_recognised.title: Recognising the work of an execution killed before its record

BLD-job_records_kept.content:
Each phase's job records — prep's handoff and summary, geotag's decision, plan and execution-summary records, merge's
summary — SHALL stay on disk, as do every pass's plan and journal and the decision records each execution kept
(`BLD-log_format`).
BLD-job_records_kept.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-job_records_kept.title: The job records stay on disk

BLD-jpeg_extensions.content:
A JPEG SHALL be a file of the `image` class ending `.jpg` or `.jpeg`, matched ignoring case; a raw file, one of the
`raw` class.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-jpeg_extensions.title: What counts as a JPEG and a raw file

BLD-known_camera_group.content:
A group SHALL be known when its key is listed under `camera_time_and_timezone_policy.device_groups` — `phones` (mobile)
or `fixed_clock_cameras` (fixed-clock).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-known_camera_group.title: A camera group is known when it is listed

BLD-library_file_fingerprinted.content:
Where a file is there, merge SHALL fingerprint it — from `library_fingerprint_cache` when its path, size and
modification time match a row taken by this build's photo method under the current, known ImageMagick version,
otherwise by decoding it and storing the row — and compare it with the incoming photo's fingerprint from prep. A file
whose name differs from the target's only in case is such a file: the same content is already present at its name.
Only planning writes these rows; execute fingerprints afresh and writes no row.
BLD-library_file_fingerprinted.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_file_fingerprinted.title: A library file in the way is fingerprinted, through a cache

BLD-library_folders_made.content: Merge SHALL create a missing destination directory under `library_root` with `os.makedirs` as it places a photo there.
BLD-library_folders_made.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_folders_made.title: Merge makes a destination's folder as it places a photo

BLD-library_lock.content:
The library lock SHALL be `LibraryLock`: an exclusive, non-blocking `flock` on `.photos-merge.lock` in `library_root`,
recording its holder's `pid`, `started_at` and `host` and nothing else, released by the kernel when its process dies,
the file never deleted; merge's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` take it after the workspace lock and after the
preflight's `validate_merge_config` and `is_library` checks, and hold it to their end, one that cannot take it stopping
with exit status 1.
BLD-library_lock.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_lock.title: The library lock

BLD-library_marker.content:
A library SHALL be marked by an empty `.photos-library` file in `library_root`, which `is_library` tests with
`os.path.isfile` and `merge init-library` alone creates, with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, leaving one already there as it is.
BLD-library_marker.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_marker.title: The library's mark

BLD-library_root_validated.content: `validate_merge_config` SHALL require `merge.library_root` to be non-empty and to resolve to an existing directory that is neither the workspace nor inside it; `library_workspace_error`, called by merge's preflight and by every `init-library` that blesses, refuses one that is a workspace, lies inside one — any folder above it holding a `.photos-ingest` directory, initialized or not — or holds one among its immediate folders.
BLD-library_root_validated.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_root_validated.title: `validate_merge_config` checks the library's place

BLD-library_space.content:
`_space_shortfalls` SHALL total the size of each photo of the plan placed new or renamed whose copy is still in
photos by destination and whose place is free, by the filesystem of the nearest existing folder of its place, leaving
out the workspace's own; and compare each total, raised by `merge.library_space_margin_percent` percent of it and
rounded up to a whole byte, with that filesystem's free space as `shutil.disk_usage` gives it,
naming the library where it lies there. Execute calls it after revalidating the plan and reading the journal, before
the snapshots, and a shortfall stops it with exit status 2, no summary written; the plan calls it once written,
warning of each.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-library_space.title: The library's free space against the photos still to move

BLD-library_trial.content:
Merge's plan, dry run and execute SHALL, after the preflight and the workspace's check and before `LibraryLock`, call
`library_filesystem_error`, which tries through `filesystem_lacks`, in `library_root`, the lock, the move that refuses a
taken name and the two syncs, and checks no filesystem type; one failing stops the run with exit status 2, naming it.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-library_trial.title: The library's filesystem, tried before its lock

BLD-local_filesystem_types.content:
`filesystem_type` SHALL read `/proc/self/mountinfo`, or else `/proc/mounts`, and take the type of the mount whose
point is the longest prefix of the workspace's real path, the later listed of two at one point; `local_filesystem_error`
accepts the types of `LOCAL_FILESYSTEM_TYPES` — `ext2`, `ext3`, `ext4`, `xfs`, `btrfs`, `zfs`, `f2fs`, `bcachefs`,
`jfs`, `reiserfs`, `nilfs2`, `tmpfs`, `ramfs` and `overlay` — and refuses any other, naming it, and a system with no
mount table to read. `workspace_filesystem_error` asks it, then tries the requirements ({need}`BLD-filesystem_trial`):
prep's and geotag's `run`, merge's plan, dry run, execution and in-workspace `init-library`, and the editor's start and
save, call it before they take the workspace's or the editor's lock — geotag, merge and the editor once they have found
the workspace — and on a refusal report it and exit 2, the editor's save refused.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-local_filesystem_types.title: The workspace's filesystem type, from the mount table

BLD-local_time_readings.content: Once its cells are built, `build_time_decisions` SHALL resolve each destination holding photos as `compute_resolved_utc` would, and give each photo left `local_time_skipped` or `local_time_repeated` an entry in the destination's `local_time_readings`, keyed by its path: `content_fingerprint`, `camera_time`, `timezone`, `case` (`repeated` or `skipped`), `offsets_seconds` (the zone's UTC offset before the change and after), `readings_utc` (the instant each gives), `user_decision.utc_offset_seconds` (`""` until answered), `effective_utc_offset_seconds`, `requires_user_input` and `stale_user_decision`. A photo's earlier answer is the entry of its destination's earlier record with its `content_fingerprint`, or with the fingerprint its own values are pinned under — never one by its path alone. An answer is a whole number of seconds within ±14 hours, else a blocker; for a `repeated` time one of `offsets_seconds`, else `stale_user_decision`, kept as written; for a `skipped` time any such. The record is not complete while an entry requires input; `compute_resolved_utc` reads the photo as its time less the answer.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-local_time_readings.title: A time the zone skips or repeats, answered per photo

BLD-lock_after_guard.content:
The lock SHALL be taken as soon as the run's workspace is known, before the guard, `photos-00-workspace-guard`, or
anything else in it is read.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-lock_after_guard.title: The lock is taken first

BLD-lock_owner_record.content:
The lock SHALL record the identity of the process that owns it and the time it started, so that a lock whose owner is
gone can be told from one whose owner is running.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-lock_owner_record.title: The lock records its owner

BLD-log_copy_checked.content:
Each copy SHALL carry the earlier log unchanged — every entry, every field and every step as it was, a phase only adding
— which finalize and merge check: a copy that would change the earlier record is not written, and merge refuses while
`photos-26-complete-log.json` no longer carries `photos-15-prep-log.json` so, or cannot be read.
BLD-log_copy_checked.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-log_copy_checked.title: A copied log carries the earlier one unchanged

BLD-log_format.content:
Each log SHALL be pretty-printed JSON with sorted keys, every step naming its `run`, its `photos` keyed by the content fingerprint
(`content_fingerprint`), each entry carrying where each phase left the photo — `prep_path`, written by prep and updated
by every prep run; `geotag_path`, by finalize, its by-dest folder under the name its last final rename gave it;
`library_path`, by merge — and a `journey` of steps, each step naming its `phase` and `action`, a move or rename its
`from` and `to` — the first step's `from` being the photo's path in the dump — and, where a decision caused it, a
`because` naming the decision exactly: a clock offset its `photos-21` cell, with its day where the camera's photos there
span days (`camera_group_time_decisions.<group>@<date>`), or the `photos-22` drift confirmation whose validated offset
replaced it; a time kept as the true time its entry of the destination's `changed_times`
(`changed_times[<path>]`); a time a date fallback gave the `date_fallback` cell of the destination it was written at;
a timezone its destination's cell; a manual position the photo's pin among `photos-23`'s review items or
the destination's folder fallback, with the destination it is inherited from where it is inherited.
BLD-log_format.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-log_format.title: The log's format

BLD-loop_commands.content:
The loop SHALL run as: `prep plan`, `dry-run`, `execute`; the sort, by hand; the prep commands again; `geotag plan`, the
decision editor (`edit`) for what it asks, and `geotag plan` again until `photos-24-executable-plan.json` is ready;
`geotag execute`, which writes `photos-25-execution-summary.json`; `geotag finalize`, which writes
`photos-26-complete-log.json` and the archival package; and `merge plan`, `dry-run`, `execute`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-loop_commands.title: The loop's commands

BLD-loop_gates.content:
The gates SHALL be checked as follows: `geotag plan` checks every gate; `geotag execute` and `finalize` check the
development gate and the workspace's shape, and validate against the plan's own dependencies instead of the scope and
re-prep gates ({need}`RUL-geotag_gates`, {need}`BLD-reprep_pending`); merge's preflight checks the inbox, the
development gate and that photos by destination holds only photos ({need}`BLD-merge_preflight`). A development subfolder
is one named in `destination_distribution_subfolders`. Geotag's preflight stops as well on a photo in `6-photos-by-dest` whose handoff record holds no fingerprint, named.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-loop_gates.title: Where the loop's gates are checked

BLD-lower_tracks_recorded.content: A position write of photos-24 whose placement has `lower_tracks` SHALL carry them in its `provenance`, beside `gpx_file`. photos-23's `lower_track_disagreements` lists, per lower-ranked track (`gpx_file`) and the track that placed the photos (`outranked_by`), the photos it put more than `gpx_tracks_agree_max_distance_meters` from their position, which `geotag plan` prints; nothing in it asks.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-lower_tracks_recorded.title: What a lower-ranked track said

BLD-marked_file_rerun.content:
On a re-run, a file with no pinned values carrying a position marker or the suffix SHALL be resolved from its own time
and offset tag with no clock offset, as no clock anchor and in no drift check, a camera group's offset cells being built
from its unmarked files alone. A file with a position marker counts as having no native GPS and is placed again; one now
placed nowhere has geotag's position and marker cleared and carries the suffix alone.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-marked_file_rerun.title: A re-run treats a marked file as geotag's work

BLD-merge_archive_manifest.content:
`photos-35-archive-manifest.json` SHALL hold `artifact_type` `archive_manifest`, its `artifact_name`, `schema_version`
1, the workspace's folder name as `workspace` and its identity as `workspace_id`, the merge plan's `plan_id`, the merge
run's id as both `execution_id` and `merge_run_id`, `supersedes` naming `photos-26-archive-manifest.json`, `contents` —
each file it lists keyed by its path in the control directory, with its path in the workspace (`path`) and its
`sha256` — and `run_metadata.generated_at`, the merge run's start.
BLD-merge_archive_manifest.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_archive_manifest.title: Merge's package manifest

BLD-merge_carry_forward.content:
Merge's `build_merge_plan` SHALL give a finalized photo no longer under `6-photos-by-dest` the record of the latest
plan — `photos-30-merge-plan.json`, then its `-NNN` backups newest first — holding a record for its content fingerprint
not blocked whose `library_target` holds it ({need}`BLD-placed_bytes_journalled`), adding `carried_from_plan`
(the plan that first placed it); no such record makes it a blocked record whose reason names the places tried, or that
no earlier plan placed it. A record's place counts only inside the configured `library_root`; a photo found at an earlier place outside it blocks, unless it is found at the same place under the configured library, where the user moved it.
One of those plans, or of their journals, that cannot be read, does not parse as a JSON object, holds no `plan_id` or is
not in the shape of {need}`BLD-merge_record_shape` stops the plan with exit status 2, naming it, no plan written.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_carry_forward.title: A fresh plan carries forward from the earlier plans

BLD-merge_collision.content:
Merge SHALL map each photo by destination to its place under `library_root`, and list only the folders its photos go to
— for the names taken there — and the library's top folder, for temporary copies a crash of its own left
({need}`BLD-temp_sweep`).
BLD-merge_collision.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_collision.title: Where merge looks in the library

BLD-merge_engine_recheck.content:
Merge's plan SHALL compare the ImageMagick version now in use with the handoff's `depends_on.cache.image_engine_version`
— a handoff recording none counting as another — and, where they differ and the current one is known, fingerprint each
by-dest photo it plans to place, one whose value is not the handoff's mapped or blocked ({need}`BLD-changed_fingerprint_mapped`);
the plan records the version in its `depends_on.image_engine_version`, and a plan made under another is stale, at dry
run and execute alike.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_engine_recheck.title: Merge checks prep's fingerprints against the handoff's ImageMagick

BLD-merge_execute.content:
Merge's execute SHALL, on its main thread, read the plan, revalidate its `depends_on` and read the journal an earlier
execute of the plan left — a plan or journal that cannot be read, does not parse as a JSON object, lacks its
`plan_id` or `operations` or is not in the shape of {need}`BLD-merge_record_shape` stopping it with exit status 2,
nothing changed, as such a plan stops the dry run — then
take the snapshots and sweep the temporaries a crash left; then move the photos on a pool of `jobs` workers, each touching only its own photo and
returning a result; the main thread alone writing the journal, as each result arrives, and sorting the results by path
before the summary is built.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_execute.title: Merge's execute, in order

BLD-merge_failed_placement.content: Merge SHALL record a placement that raised as blocked, its photo left in photos by destination.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_failed_placement.title: Merge's failed placement

BLD-merge_journal_resume.content:
The journal — one per plan, `journal-<plan id>.json`, a later execute of the same plan carrying the earlier's
confirmations into it and writing it again whole with each of its own, `updated_at` that execute's start — SHALL record
each confirmed photo, a re-run taking a place already holding the planned content, fingerprinted again, as done, and
removing the workspace copy if it remains; a photo whose workspace copy is gone counts as done only once its place is
checked again ({need}`BLD-placed_bytes_journalled`) and found to hold it, and is blocked otherwise — the journal is the record of what ran, never what
decides it.
BLD-merge_journal_resume.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_journal_resume.title: Merge's journal, and how a re-run resumes

BLD-merge_log_steps.content:
Merge SHALL append to the `journey` of each photo it placed or found already in the library one step: `phase`
`merge`; its `run`, the merge plan that placed it — the earlier one for a photo a re-plan carried forward
({need}`BLD-merge_carry_forward`); `action` `placed`, or `already_present`; `from`, its path in photos by destination;
`library_path`, its place in the library; and `renamed_for_library`, whether it took a name of its own there — setting
the entry's `library_path` to the same place.
BLD-merge_log_steps.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_log_steps.title: Merge's step in the log

BLD-merge_move.content:
Each photo SHALL move into its place without overwriting it: on the library's own filesystem by a single rename that
refuses an existing name; across filesystems by a copy to a temporary name beside its place, checked byte for byte against
the photo, renamed into the place only if it is still free, the rename made durable, and only then removed from photos
by destination.
A place found taken at execute holding the planned content makes the photo already present; holding other content, it
blocks the photo — the plan's alternative name used only where the plan recorded one.
BLD-merge_move.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_move.title: Merge's move: one rename, or copy, verify, rename and remove

BLD-merge_plan.content:
`photos-30-merge-plan.json` SHALL hold the plan id, schema version and `library_root`; per destination, each photo's
record — its path in the workspace, content fingerprint, library target and disposition (`placed_new`,
`renamed_incoming` with its new name, `already_present`, or `blocked` with why), and as preconditions its fingerprint
and its size and modification time as they stand at planning; the blockers and the totals; and `depends_on`: the
SHA-256 of `photos-24` and `photos-25`, the handoff's content fingerprint, the configuration's SHA-256, the code
fingerprint, the ImageMagick version, and the fingerprints of the folder names and media extensions.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_plan.title: Merge's plan

BLD-merge_preflight.content:
Merge's `preflight` SHALL run, under the workspace lock and before the library's, stopping at the first that fails:
the seal; the initialization mark; a link at the top level; a missing managed folder; a misplaced top-level entry; the
configuration, read and checked; the library's place and mark; the handoff, read; its filename format. It then gathers
the rest and reports them together: ImageMagick on the `PATH`, as `magick` or `identify`; the inbox empty; `photos-24-executable-plan.json` present with
`photos-25-execution-summary.json` at `success`; the handoff's content fingerprint the one `photos-24` pinned; prep's
log as the handoff vouches for it ({need}`BLD-prep_log_checked`); `photos-26-complete-log.json` and the archive
manifest present, the complete log carrying prep's; photos by date holding no photo; photos by destination holding
only `image` and `raw` files, no development subfolder and no link; every photo there one of the finalized set — the
handoff's photos by destination joined by fingerprint to `photos-24`'s renames, each under its final name; and each
photo of that set still there with the size and modification time `photos-26-finalized-media.json` recorded, and
holding a position ({need}`BLD-no_photo_unplaced`). Any
blocker ends the run with exit status 2 before the library lock, the plan or the summary. It stops, too, on a photo in `6-photos-by-dest` whose handoff record holds no fingerprint and on any hidden file or folder there, each named.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_preflight.title: Merge's preflight

BLD-merge_record_shape.content:
Merge SHALL read as unreadable a plan whose `destinations` is not an object of objects each holding a `files` list of
objects that name their `by_dest_source`, and any `library_target`, as text, or whose `depends_on` or `totals`, where
present, is not an object or `blockers` not a list; and a journal whose `operations`, or `placed_sha256` where present,
is not an object.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_record_shape.title: The shape of merge's plan and journal

BLD-merge_records.content:
Merge SHALL write `photos-31-merge-summary.json` when its execute ends — `success`, `partial` or `failed` — or refuses
for a required snapshot, and on no other outcome: not for a failed precondition, a plan missing, unreadable or stale,
a journal unreadable, or an interrupt, the file then left as it was. It holds, per photo,
grouped by destination, where it landed, whether it was renamed for the library or already present, whether it left
photos by destination, and, blocked, why — with no library path; in total, the photos placed new, renamed, already
present and blocked, the removed the sum of the first three; the status `success`, `partial`, `failed` (every photo
blocked) or `rejected` (a required snapshot not taken, nothing changed); the merge run and plan ids, `library_root`, the
geotag plan and execution ids, the photos it newly moved and those an earlier run had, and the SHA-256 of `photos-24-executable-plan.json`,
`photos-25-execution-summary.json` and `photos-11-handoff.json`; and, apart, the run's times and job count.
BLD-merge_records.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_records.title: The merge summary

BLD-merge_snapshots.content:
Merge's `_take_snapshots` SHALL snapshot the workspace's dataset and then, where the library's differs, the library's —
each pinned by `zfs.datasets.workspace` and `zfs.datasets.library` or detected from its path — taking the library's
only after the workspace's has succeeded, and recording both in `photos-31-merge-summary.json` under `snapshot`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_snapshots.title: Merge's two snapshots

BLD-merge_success_sequence.content:
Only on success — every photo placed or already present, none left, a plan of no photo among them — SHALL merge then,
in order, write `photos-35-merge-log.json`, `photos-35-fingerprint-map.json`, `photos-35-merge-ingest.db`, the package's
`photos-35-archive-manifest.json` and `photos-35-archive.tar.gz`, and last the seal.
BLD-merge_success_sequence.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_success_sequence.title: What a whole merge writes, and the seal last

BLD-merge_target.content:
Merge's `enumerate_finalized` SHALL take each photo of the handoff under `6-photos-by-dest` and give it, as its target,
`library_root` joined to its folder's path relative to `6-photos-by-dest` — empty for a photo directly in it — and its
final name: the target of `photos-24`'s `rename_no_clobber` whose `content_fingerprint` precondition is the photo's, or
its own name where geotag renamed nothing; the entries sorted by their path in the workspace.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_target.title: A photo's target in the library

BLD-metadata_extraction.content:
Prep SHALL read metadata with `exiftool -json -n -a -G0`, taking each field from the first group holding it in the
order `EXIF`, `XMP`, `MakerNotes`, `IPTC`, `QuickTime`, `File` — `Composite` first for the GPS position — and a time
field from the first group holding a valid time in it; it keeps the fields in `metadata_cache.parsed_json` with the
recorded time's field and group, stamped with `exiftool`, its version, the field-set version, the SHA-256 of the
options, the metadata-schema version and the camera-group-key version.
BLD-metadata_extraction.section_name: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-metadata_extraction.title: Metadata is read by exiftool, by group

BLD-metadata_failure_blocker.content:
A media file whose folder exiftool's batch failed on, or which is missing from its batch's result, SHALL have its
metadata recorded `extraction_failed`, and prep's plan records a blocker naming it, `6-photos-by-dest` included: for a
file whose folder's batch failed, always; for one missing from the result, unless the database holds a fresh record of
its metadata ({need}`BLD-metadata_extraction`), which is kept.
BLD-metadata_failure_blocker.section_name: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-metadata_failure_blocker.title: A metadata read that failed is a blocker

BLD-metadata_safe_write.content:
Geotag SHALL write metadata by having `exiftool -o` write the new file beside the photo as `<file>_exiftool_tmp` —
the photo itself untouched — then giving it the photo's permissions, syncing it to disk, renaming it over the photo
and syncing the folder, having first removed a `<file>_exiftool_tmp` an interrupted write left.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-metadata_safe_write.title: Geotag's metadata writes

BLD-modified_time_files.content:
`build_file_model` SHALL give a photo whose `source_time_tag` names `ModifyDate` — the pinned one, for a photo with
pinned values — the `camera_group_key` `NO_IDENTITY_KEY` in place of prep's, so that, as {need}`BLD-unidentified_files`
has it, it is classed `unidentified`, is in no group's offset cell or drift check, and is resolved by `OffsetTime`
(`unidentified_native_offset`), else its destination's timezone; prep's camera group and its report are left as derived.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-modified_time_files.title: Photos timed by their modification

BLD-move_match.content:
Prep's plan SHALL match, before laying the plan memo under the database, the rows of the workspace database whose path
is not in the inventory against the inventoried files under `6-photos-by-dest` that have no row, by size, `mtime_ns`
and exact basename; a triple held by more than one row or more than one file matches nothing.
BLD-move_match.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-move_match.title: The move is matched on size, time and name

BLD-move_row_effects.content:
Each move or rename in prep's plan SHALL carry its database effects — the row of its source removed and, but for a
quarantine move, the file's row with its fingerprint and metadata written at its destination — applied by execute once
the operation succeeds.
BLD-move_row_effects.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-move_row_effects.title: A planned move carries its row

BLD-name_check.content:
At plan, prep SHALL check the name of every media file in the dated, missing-metadata, redundant-JPG and by-destination
folders: without its extension and `-NNN` suffix, it is the file's recorded time ({need}`RUL-recorded_time_order`)
formatted by `filename_timestamp_format`, or starts with `UNKN_` for a file with no recorded time and for every file in
the missing-metadata folder. A dated file with no recorded time is moved to the missing-metadata folder instead, and the
strays folder is not checked. A JPEG in the redundant-JPG folder whose name without its extension is that of the raw
file its prep log names ({need}`BLD-set_aside_pair_recorded`), found by its fingerprint, is rightly named.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-name_check.title: What prep checks a name against

BLD-name_suffix.content:
The names SHALL be `<timestamp>.ext` for the first file with a free base name, `<timestamp>-001.ext` for the first
collision, `<timestamp>-002.ext` for the second, and so on.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-name_suffix.title: The `-NNN` suffix

BLD-names_case_folded.content:
Every phase SHALL take two names that differ only in case for one, on every filesystem, whether or not it tells them
apart: prep's execute refuses a move onto a name that differs only in case from one there or planned before it;
geotag's renames and merge's placements are planned with names compared ignoring case, merge settling a library file
under such a name by its content ({need}`BLD-library_file_fingerprinted`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-names_case_folded.title: Names that differ only in case are one name, on every filesystem

BLD-neighbour_day_proposal.content:
After the offsets shared within a day, `build_time_decisions` SHALL propose to each `camera` cell keyed
`<group>@<YYYY-MM-DD>` whose proposal is `recorded_offset`, `timezone_naive` or `manual_required` the effective offset of
the cell of the same group and destination keyed by the day before, else the day after — of a day split at a change of
the clock, its part next to this day — where that offset's source is `gpx_anchor_auto`, `gpx_anchor_accepted`,
`gpx_anchor_chosen`, `gps_time_auto` or `gps_time_accepted`: as `proposal_source: "neighbour_day"` with
`proposed_offset_seconds`, `neighbour_day` (`day`, `bucket`) and `confidence: "review_required"`, ahead of
`recorded_offset` and `timezone_naive`, whatever time lies between the two days' photos and with no setting of its
own. It never applies itself: where track points lie within `drift_check_track_window_seconds` of the cell's photos
— by the times the offset gives, else by the times the camera recorded — and no decision is given, it takes effect as
`neighbour_day_unconfirmed`, `decision_mode: "to_be_confirmed_against_tracks"`, asking nothing in photos-21 and always
asked in photos-22 ({need}`BLD-drift_validation`), as a `timezone_naive` proposal does; elsewhere only once accepted,
naming the offset, as `neighbour_day_accepted`, which the drift check follows as it does `timezone_accepted`. The
cell keeps its own key and decision.
BLD-neighbour_day_proposal.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-neighbour_day_proposal.title: The offset of the day next to it

BLD-no_clobber_rename.content:
Every move and rename that carries content SHALL go through `_move_no_clobber`: on one filesystem `renameat2` with
`RENAME_NOREPLACE`, one call that refuses an existing name, or where that is unavailable `os.link` then `os.unlink`;
across filesystems, for merge alone, `_move_cross_fs_no_clobber`. A refused name stops that operation: prep records it
failed and stops; geotag and merge record a blocker and leave the photo where it is. Merge also tests its target before
moving, and geotag compares names ignoring case ({need}`BLD-rename_planning`). The rename that completes an operation is
thus itself the check that its name is free ({need}`RUL-target_free_at_execute`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-no_clobber_rename.title: One rename that refuses a taken name

BLD-no_control_dir_stops.content:
Geotag and merge SHALL check that the control directory exists before they take the lock, and where it does not, stop
with exit status 2, having created nothing.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-no_control_dir_stops.title: Geotag and merge stop where there is no control directory

BLD-no_photo_unplaced.content:
`photos_utils.photos_without_position` SHALL name each photo under `6-photos-by-dest` that holds no position once the
plan is executed, by `has_own_position` ({need}`BLD-own_position_test`) of the position it holds: the one its
`metadata_gps_write` wrote, none where a `gps_marker_write` emptied `GPSLatitude`, else the `GPSLatitude` and
`GPSLongitude` its handoff record holds — a record joined to the plan's operations by its content fingerprint, by its
path only where it holds none or another record under `6-photos-by-dest` holds the same — so read without running a tool on a photo. `geotag finalize` refuses, writing nothing,
while it names any; merge's preflight, from the current handoff and `photos-24-executable-plan.json`, gathers a blocker
for them.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-no_photo_unplaced.title: No photo leaves geotag without a position

BLD-offset_acceptance.content: An offset cell's `user_decision` SHALL hold `accept_proposal`, `accepted_offset_seconds` — the `proposed_offset_seconds` that was accepted — and `manual_offset_seconds`. A `manual_offset_seconds` takes effect first. Else an acceptance takes effect while `accepted_offset_seconds` equals the offset now proposed, or lies within `gpx_anchor_decision_tolerance_seconds` of one proposed from GPS — its positions on the tracks or its fixes' times (the proposal carries that tolerance as `acceptance_tolerance_seconds`); and what takes effect is the offset accepted, not the one now proposed; naming another offset, or with nothing proposed, the cell is `stale_user_decision` and asks; naming none, or not a whole number, a blocker.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-offset_acceptance.title: How an offset is accepted

BLD-offset_buckets.content: Each destination's `camera_group_time_decisions` SHALL hold one cell per camera group present, keyed by its `camera_group_key`, or — when the group's photos there span more than one naive date — one per date, keyed `<camera_group_key>@<YYYY-MM-DD>` with a `date` field, the date taken from `source_naive_time`; every cell names the day its photos are of in `day`, whatever its key. A cell's earlier answer is the cell under its key when that names the same `day`, else the one under the key's other form whose `day` is the same; a drift cell's likewise. A cell's proposal is the GPX self-anchor of that group's photos holding their own position ({need}`BLD-own_position_test`) of that date there; else the offset their fixes' times give ({need}`BLD-gps_time_proposal`); else the offset shared from the same day elsewhere ({need}`BLD-offset_shared_within_day`); else the offset of the day next to it ({need}`BLD-neighbour_day_proposal`); else `recorded_offset` ({need}`BLD-recorded_offset_proposal`); else, with the destination's timezone resolved, `timezone_naive` at the cell's earliest naive time, DST-aware; else `manual_required`. A cell with photos not yet corrected names the earliest of them in `representative` (`source_file`, `camera_source_naive_time`). No cell reads the destination above it for an offset; the one case of a cell taking another destination's is {need}`BLD-offset_shared_within_day`. A day split at a change of the clock adds its parts beside its cell, keyed `<key>#1` and `<key>#2` ({need}`BLD-clock_change_split`).
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-offset_buckets.title: Offset buckets

BLD-offset_far_from_evidence.content: After the offsets shared within a day, `build_time_decisions` SHALL withdraw the effective offset of a cell whose proposal is `recorded_offset`, `timezone_naive` or `gps_time` and whose effective source is that proposal's (`recorded_offset_unconfirmed`, `recorded_offset_accepted`, `timezone_unconfirmed`, `timezone_accepted`, `gps_time_auto` or `gps_time_accepted`), the cell asking, where the destination holds a photo of another camera group whose resolved UTC is known — a smartphone's, resolved as `compute_resolved_utc` resolves it, or a camera's not yet corrected whose cell's effective source is `gpx_anchor_auto`, `gpx_anchor_accepted`, `gpx_anchor_chosen`, `gpx_anchor_imprecise`, `same_day_auto`, `same_day_accepted` or `manual` — and every photo of the cell not yet corrected, at the time the proposal gives, lies farther than `gpx_anchor_max_clock_error_seconds` from each such photo's resolved UTC and from every track point. Such a proposal, whatever the cell's decision, holds `far_from_evidence`: `max_clock_error_seconds`, `other_photos` (how many), `nearest_other_photo`, `nearest_other_photo_seconds` and `nearest_track_seconds` (empty with no track). The `gps_time` cells are judged first, in rounds, each round all against the resolved UTCs the rounds before left, until a round withdraws none; then the other cells, all against what the `gps_time` cells left.
BLD-offset_far_from_evidence.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-offset_far_from_evidence.title: A guessed offset far from all evidence

BLD-offset_shared_within_day.content: Over the cells of one camera group naming the same `day` in different destinations, `build_time_decisions` SHALL take as donors those whose effective source is `gpx_anchor_auto`, `gpx_anchor_accepted` or `gpx_anchor_chosen` — the last an offset the user wrote that a group of the camera's own GPS anchors supports; a `gpx_anchor_accepted` donor, its proposal accepted as it stood, is not written by hand, and is held as a `gpx_anchor_auto` one is. Donors not written by hand whose offsets differ by more than `clock_offset_same_day_max_difference_seconds`, or of which one differs by more than it from a `gpx_anchor_chosen` donor, are in conflict: those, with each `gpx_anchor_chosen` donor that differs by more than it from one of them, list the others in `conflicts_with` (`destination`, `bucket`, `offset_seconds`, and `chosen`: whether that one is `gpx_anchor_chosen`); each not written by hand loses its effective offset and asks, each `gpx_anchor_chosen` one keeps its own and does not ask; and nothing is shared. Two `gpx_anchor_chosen` donors are not held against each other. Otherwise a cell whose own proposal would be `recorded_offset`, `timezone_naive` or `manual_required` is proposed the donor's offset — a `gpx_anchor_auto` donor first, then by path — as `proposal_source: "same_day_elsewhere"` with `shared_from` (`destination`, `bucket`): taking effect as `same_day_auto` where the donor's source is `gpx_anchor_auto`, else once accepted, naming the offset, as `same_day_accepted`. An offset the cell keeps from its own earlier GPS comes first. Neither source is followed by a drift check.
BLD-offset_shared_within_day.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-offset_shared_within_day.title: A day's offset shared between destinations

BLD-one_library_file_compared.content:
Merge SHALL compare one library file with each photo: the one under the photo's own name where there is one, otherwise
the first, in sorted order, of those whose names differ from it only in case — so that a photo the library holds under
another of those names is not found there, and takes a name of its own beside it.
BLD-one_library_file_compared.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-one_library_file_compared.title: One library file is compared per photo

BLD-one_snapshot_mechanism.content:
The three phases SHALL take their snapshots through one mechanism — prep's execute, geotag's
({need}`BLD-geotag_execution`) and merge's ({need}`BLD-merge_execute`) invoke it, and none redefines it.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One snapshot mechanism for every phase

BLD-one_top_level_check.content:
Prep, geotag and merge SHALL find a workspace's misplaced top-level entries with the one function they share,
`photos_utils.misplaced_top_level_entries`, so the three cannot disagree on what belongs there.
BLD-one_top_level_check.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-one_top_level_check.title: One check of the top level for all three phases

BLD-operation_only_where_different.content:
A file's operation SHALL be planned only where the file does not already hold the target: prep does not move or rename a
file already in place, geotag plans no write a file already holds and recomputes an already-final name to itself
({need}`BLD-rename_planning`, {need}`BLD-rerun_writes_only_differences`), and merge records a photo already in the
library as already present ({need}`RUL-collision_same_content`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-operation_only_where_different.title: An operation only where the file differs

BLD-original_values_follow_fingerprint.content:
`build_file_model` SHALL find a photo's pinned values under its fingerprint or, failing it, under the value it was
taken again from, step by step back through the `fingerprint_retaken` steps of prep's log (`retaken_fingerprints`),
when the handoff vouches for the log; execution then moves the pin to the current value, unless one is held there. A
log holding two steps that give one value two predecessors, or one value two successors, is a blocker of geotag's
preflight, and so, for `geotag plan`, is a log the handoff does not vouch for (`prep_log_blocker`: missing,
unreadable, its SHA-256 other than `depends_on.prep_log`'s, or the handoff recording none); `geotag execute` stops on
such a log after its preflight, before the plan is read and before any snapshot, kept decision or write, with exit
status 2.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-original_values_follow_fingerprint.title: The pinned values follow a retaken fingerprint

BLD-original_values_pinned.content:
Before geotag's first write to a file, execution SHALL pin its own recorded time, its `DateTimeOriginal` and
`CreateDate` with their offset tags, its position and `GPSProcessingMethod` in an original-values ledger keyed by
fingerprint, once, unless it already carries geotag's mark; a later plan decides about a pinned file from those values
and plans only the writes that differ from what it holds ({need}`BLD-decided_from_own_values`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-original_values_pinned.title: A file's own values are pinned before geotag first writes it

BLD-other_time_fields_read.content:
Prep SHALL keep in `parsed_json`, each under its group-qualified name and from that group alone, `EXIF:CreateDate`,
`EXIF:OffsetTimeDigitized`, `XMP:DateCreated`, `IPTC:DateCreated` and `IPTC:TimeCreated`, so geotag knows which of the
time fields it rewrites a photo holds.
BLD-other_time_fields_read.section_name: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-other_time_fields_read.title: The other time fields are kept by their group

BLD-other_time_fields_written.content:
A time write SHALL carry as well, of the fields the photo holds, `EXIF:CreateDate` as `DateTimeOriginal` is written,
with `EXIF:OffsetTimeDigitized` as `OffsetTimeOriginal` when the photo holds it too; `XMP:DateCreated` as the local time
followed by any fraction of a second its value held and the offset, `YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS[.ff]+HH:MM` as `exiftool -n`
takes it; `IPTC:DateCreated` as the local date, `YYYY:MM:DD`; and `IPTC:TimeCreated` as the local time and offset,
`HH:MM:SS+HH:MM` — never a field the photo does not hold. `ModifyDate` and `OffsetTime`, the last edit's, and the
sub-second fields are left as they are, a clock offset being whole seconds.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-other_time_fields_written.title: The other time fields are written with the time

BLD-own_position_test.content:
A photo SHALL have a position of its own exactly when `photos_utils.has_own_position` holds of its `GPSLatitude` and
`GPSLongitude` as `exiftool -n` reads them: both present, and not both equal to 0 as numbers — `0`, `0.0` and `-0.0`,
never a value merely near it. Prep's `has_native_gps`, and geotag's file model — from the handoff's values and from the
pinned ones — take it from that test alone, so a photo at latitude 0 and longitude 0 is placed again, never
`preserve_native`, never an anchor frame and never counted in `preserve_native_gps`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-own_position_test.title: One test of a photo's own position

BLD-own_write_recognised.content:
`_holds_writes` SHALL take a photo for holding its planned tags when, of what `exiftool -n` reads back, each tag
planned empty is absent or empty, each planned number — a coordinate — equals the value read in magnitude to within
10⁻⁶ of a degree (about 0.1 m; the sign is in its reference tag), and each other equals it as text; a photo changed in
size or modification time since the plan that holds them so is geotag's own interrupted write, one that does not an
edit since the plan ({need}`BLD-geotag_execution`).
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-own_write_recognised.title: How geotag knows a photo holds what it planned

BLD-partial_log_marked.content:
A log whose kept history cannot rebuild a journey SHALL be marked partial: prep marks its log partial and warns when its
history cannot rebuild a journey ({need}`BLD-prep_log_build`); geotag's finalize marks `partial` the entry of a photo carrying geotag's
mark whose own values the workspace never pinned, with a `history_incomplete` step of its own saying why, and names in
the log's `warnings`, the log then `partial`, any pass whose journal is kept but whose plan is missing.
BLD-partial_log_marked.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-partial_log_marked.title: A log that cannot rebuild a journey is marked partial

BLD-phase_commands.content:
The phases SHALL be the commands `photos-cartographer prep`, `geotag` and `merge` — named in the specs, and in their
records, `photos-1-prep`, `photos-2-geotag` and `photos-3-merge`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phase_commands.title: The phases are three commands

BLD-phase_dependencies.content:
Each phase SHALL record a record's dependencies in its `depends_on` block and check them before use, as its own spec
states in full: prep in {need}`BLD-prep_dependencies`; geotag in {need}`BLD-geotag_dependencies`; merge in {need}`BLD-merge_plan`. The cascade consumes media by content fingerprints, records by byte
hashes, and the field-scoped configuration fingerprints ({need}`DEF-config_areas`) that keep staleness surgical.
BLD-phase_dependencies.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phase_dependencies.title: Each phase's dependencies, in full

BLD-phase_logs.content:
Each phase SHALL write its log: prep `photos-15-prep-log.json` at the end of every prep run ({need}`BLD-prep_log_build`); geotag's
finalize copies it to `photos-26-complete-log.json` and appends each photo's geotag steps
({need}`BLD-geotag_log_steps`); merge copies that to `photos-35-merge-log.json` and appends its own.
BLD-phase_logs.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phase_logs.title: The per-phase logs

BLD-phases_check_seal.content:
Prep's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute`, every geotag command, and merge's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` SHALL check
the seal under the workspace lock before reading anything else, and stop with exit status 2 if it is there, adding the
likely-new-dump warning when `likely_new_dump` finds an entry at the workspace's top level other than its managed
folders and hidden entries, or anything in the inbox.
BLD-phases_check_seal.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phases_check_seal.title: The phases check the seal first

BLD-phases_inside_lock.content:
Each phase's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` SHALL run with the lock taken at start already held, none taking it again
or scoping it on its own ({need}`RUL-lock_through_the_run`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phases_inside_lock.title: The phases run inside the run's lock

BLD-phone_offset_cell.content: For each `smartphone` group's photos not yet corrected of a destination and day, keyed as a camera's bucket is ({need}`BLD-offset_buckets`), `_phone_cell` SHALL take the GPX self-anchor of those holding their own position ({need}`BLD-anchor_matching`), else the offset their fixes' times give ({need}`BLD-gps_time_proposal`), and set it against `_read_offset` of each photo that gave it — of an anchor, those within `gpx_anchor_offset_spread_max_seconds` of the offset; of fix times, every reading — −(the offset recorded with its time), else −(the zone's at its time). One of them farther than `gpx_anchor_decision_tolerance_seconds` from it, or none read at all, the day has an offset cell in `camera_group_time_decisions`, `camera_group_class: "smartphone"`, holding `phone` — `applies_to: "every_photo"`, `photos` (how many), `read_by_offsets` (each distinct offset the photos giving it are read by) — built as a camera's is, but that one anchor never applies itself. Otherwise — the offset agreeing, or none found — the photos recording an offset are read by their own, and the day has no cell where none records none, or where those recording one all record the zone's at their time (as `_offsets_against_zone` reads them); else a cell with `applies_to: "untagged_photos"` over the photos recording none: an offset found applies itself to them, its count whatever; with none found its proposal is the `recorded_offset` of the photos recording one ({need}`BLD-recorded_offset_proposal`), else `timezone_naive` at the earliest of them, taking effect as a camera's guess does — `*_unconfirmed` to the drift check where track points lie by them, else once accepted — and checked as one against the destination's other devices ({need}`BLD-offset_far_from_evidence`). A `timezone_accepted` or `timezone_unconfirmed` offset, or a drift confirmation of it as it stood, reads each photo by the zone at its own time; any other, every photo by the one offset. In every cell `user_decision` holds `keep_as_recorded` too: `true` takes effect as `{"source": "as_recorded"}`, after `manual_offset_seconds` and before `accept_proposal`, while the proposal is `gpx_self_anchor` or `gps_time`, else is `stale_user_decision`; not a boolean, a blocker. A phone's cell gives no offset to, and takes none from, another destination's ({need}`BLD-offset_shared_within_day`).
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-phone_offset_cell.title: A phone's day checked against its own GPS

BLD-placed_bytes_journalled.content:
Merge's execute SHALL record in the journal, under `placed_sha256` keyed by the photo's path in the workspace, the
SHA-256 of the library file of each photo it confirms; a later plan carrying a photo forward gives its record, as
`placed_sha256`, the one the journal of the plan it is carried from holds, else that plan's record's own; and a place
whose file has the record's `placed_sha256` holds the photo, no fingerprint taken — one without it, or whose bytes
differ, holding it only where it fingerprints, through `_fingerprint_library_file`, to the value the photo was placed
under ({need}`BLD-changed_fingerprint_mapped`). Both the plan carrying it forward and the execute finding the photo's
workspace copy gone check the place so.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-placed_bytes_journalled.title: The bytes of each placed file are journalled, and confirm its place

BLD-placed_photos.content:
A destination's `gps_decisions.placed_photos` SHALL list, with its `relative_path` and `content_fingerprint`, each
photo no review item names, by what places it: its own position (`placed_by: "own_position"`), the tracks (`"tracks"`,
with the `method` of the placing track: `direct_match`, `interpolated` or `extrapolated`) or its destination's effective
fallback (`"folder_fallback"`, with `tracks`, why the tracks did not place it, as a review item carries it). Each of
them, and each review item, carries `camera_bucket` where its camera has an offset cell in the destination's photos-21
record and the photo a time its camera recorded: the key of the cell of its day, `<group>@<date>`, else `<group>`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-placed_photos.title: The placed photos, and each photo's camera day

BLD-placement_order.content:
`classify_gps` SHALL return, for each photo, the first of: `preserve_native` for a photo with its own position — but
`manual_locked` where its review item is `own_position_contradicted` ({need}`BLD-contradicted_position`) and holds
`manual_lat`/`manual_lon`; its
review item's `manual_lat`/`manual_lon` as `manual_locked`; the tracks at its resolved time as `gpx_interpolation` or
`gpx_extrapolation`, unless a date fallback times it ({need}`BLD-date_fallback_cell`); its destination's effective fallback as `manual_fallback`; else `blocked`, its review item
requiring input. A position from `manual_locked` or `manual_fallback` is written with that marker, and undone like any
manual position.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-placement_order.title: The placement order

BLD-plan_backups.content:
A differing re-plan SHALL first copy the existing artifact to the shared incremental `-NNN` suffix ({need}`BLD-name_suffix`) —
`photos-10-prep-plan-001.json`, say, the copy landing under that name only whole — then replace the artifact atomically,
and announce where. A plan carrying a fresh plan id differs every run, so
re-planning it always preserves the prior plan. The per-run journals keep their `journal-<run_id>.json` naming; this
convention governs the plan and decision artifacts.
BLD-plan_backups.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-plan_backups.title: A superseded plan goes aside under `-NNN`

BLD-plan_memo.content:
The plan memo SHALL be the SQLite file `photos-00-plan-memo.db` in `.photos-ingest/`, one row per path with its size,
`mtime_ns` and the file's row as read, replaced whole by each plan with its media files holding both a fingerprint and a
metadata record; read, its entries lie under the database's rows and pass the same reuse tests, and failing to open,
read or write it warns and goes on.
BLD-plan_memo.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-plan_memo.title: The plan memo is `photos-00-plan-memo.db`

BLD-planned_paths_tracked.content:
Each stage of prep's planning SHALL work from the path the stages before it gave each file, allocating every name
against the names on disk and those already planned.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-planned_paths_tracked.title: Each stage works from the paths the stages before it planned

BLD-planning_order.content:
Prep SHALL walk the workspace and take its files' sizes and times on one thread, sorted, before any parallel work, and
gather the workers' results by path; two plans of one workspace differ only in `plan_id`, `created_at` and the
operations' ids.
BLD-planning_order.section_name: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-planning_order.title: Planning in a fixed order

BLD-position_tags.content:
Every position geotag writes SHALL carry, in the same operation, `GPSLatitude`, `GPSLatitudeRef` (`N` or `S` by the
sign), `GPSLongitude` and `GPSLongitudeRef` (`E` or `W`); clearing one empties all four.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-position_tags.title: Position tags

BLD-prep_dependencies.content:
Prep's records SHALL carry their dependencies so:

- **The plan** records its schema version, the configuration's hash, its metadata dependencies — exiftool and its
  version, and the versions of the field set, the extraction options, the metadata schema and the camera-group
  derivation — and the size and mtime of every file it reads without changing, those in `6-photos-by-dest` among them.
  Execute recomputes each and refuses the plan when one differs or is absent.
