- **The journal**'s `depends_on` records the plan's schema version, the configuration's hash, and the cache's schema and
  fingerprint-algorithm versions.
- **The handoff**'s `depends_on` records the configuration's hash, the metadata dependencies, the plan's and the cache's
  schema versions, the fingerprint algorithm and the image engine with its version, the journal's hash, the prep log's
  hash ({need}`BLD-prep_log_vouched`), and the fingerprint of the final inventory.
- **The workspace database** records its schema and fingerprint-algorithm versions in its `meta` table.

A run's inventory and freshness maps are its own working state, recorded nowhere. No command option affects what prep
plans, so no record carries one.
BLD-prep_dependencies.section_name: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_dependencies.title: Prep's dependencies, in full

BLD-prep_execute_replays.content:
Prep's execute SHALL apply the operations of `photos-10-prep-plan.json` in their recorded order, to the destinations
recorded there, running no step of planning.
BLD-prep_execute_replays.section_name: 3. The plan, validated, then carried out
sections: 3. The plan, validated, then carried out
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_execute_replays.title: Prep's execute replays the saved plan

BLD-prep_fast_stop_checks_log.content:
Prep's stop on an already-prepped workspace SHALL not apply while the log's hash differs from what the handoff records,
so that prep's next execute rewrites both.
BLD-prep_fast_stop_checks_log.section_name: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_fast_stop_checks_log.title: A log not vouched for is not "nothing to do"

BLD-prep_guards_with_the_whole_hash.content:
Prep SHALL re-plan from the filesystem each run and guard execution with the whole-file hash, keeping no folder or
extension fingerprint of its own.
BLD-prep_guards_with_the_whole_hash.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-prep_guards_with_the_whole_hash.title: Prep guards execution with the whole-file hash

BLD-prep_journal.content:
Prep's execute SHALL append each operation's outcome to `journal-<plan-id>.json` as the operation ends, saving the
journal after each by replacing it whole — written to a temporary file in its folder, then renamed over it.
BLD-prep_journal.section_name: 3. The plan, validated, then carried out
sections: 3. The plan, validated, then carried out
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_journal.title: Prep journals each operation as it ends

BLD-prep_log_build.content:
Prep's execute SHALL build `photos-15-prep-log.json` from the plan's moves and renames replayed per file, the
quarantine evidence and the final database rows, merged onto the prior log by fingerprint: an entry whose old value is
nowhere in the workspace and whose `prep_path` holds a file of a new value that this run's plan gives no step moves to
it with a `fingerprint_retaken` step, the same file unchanged ({need}`BLD-retake_same_file`); an entry whose file is elsewhere with no step of this run gains a `user` step `moved_to_by_dest` — `moved_to_by_date` where the file is not in photos by destination; and a file in
a prep-organized folder with no recorded history gets an entry marked `partial`, with a warning.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_log_build.title: How prep's log is built

BLD-prep_log_checked.content:
Finalize and merge SHALL stop while `photos-15-prep-log.json` is not the log the handoff vouches for
({need}`BLD-prep_log_vouched`) — missing, unreadable, its SHA-256 other than `depends_on.prep_log`'s, or the handoff
recording none — through the shared `prep_log_blocker`, merge among its gathered preconditions.
BLD-prep_log_checked.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-prep_log_checked.title: Prep's log is checked against the handoff

BLD-prep_log_vouched.content:
Prep's execute SHALL write `photos-15-prep-log.json` before the handoff, and record the log's SHA-256 in the handoff's
`depends_on.prep_log`, outside its content fingerprint.
BLD-prep_log_vouched.section_name: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 4. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_log_vouched.title: The handoff vouches for prep's log

BLD-prep_operation_kinds.content:
Prep's execute SHALL carry out only folder creations, moves, renames, quarantine moves and database writes, refusing a
plan that holds any other operation — a metadata write among them.
BLD-prep_operation_kinds.section_name: 1. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
sections: 1. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_operation_kinds.title: Prep's operations hold no metadata write

BLD-prep_plan_contents.content:
`photos-10-prep-plan.json` SHALL record its id, its schema version, its command, the configuration's hash, the
fingerprint of the code that made it ({need}`BLD-code_fingerprint`), its operations in order, its blockers and warnings,
the size and modification time of each file it leaves as it is, its metadata dependencies, every path its scan found,
and a summary.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_plan_contents.title: What prep's plan records

BLD-prep_skip_set.content:
Prep SHALL skip `.photos-ingest/`, `.photos-ingest-quarantine/` and `.git` as whole subtrees, every dot-prefixed file,
and the strays folder `1-strays/` with all its `<plan-id>` subfolders ({need}`BLD-strays_per_run`), the strays of a run
going to `1-strays/<plan-id>/`. A hidden folder in a managed folder other than `0-sources` is not read, and one holding any file — a link counted — is a blocker naming it; a file named `<media name>_exiftool_tmp` is the one leftover of a write prep recognises, `<media name>_original` being a file of no media class like any other.
BLD-prep_skip_set.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-prep_skip_set.title: What prep skips

BLD-prep_stage_order.content:
Prep's planning SHALL run its stages in this order: initialization and inventory; duplicates; extension case; redundant
JPEGs; organization by class and time; database reconciliation.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_stage_order.title: The stages run in a fixed order

BLD-projection_without_heading.content:
A photo past a track's end SHALL be placed on the end itself, still `extrapolated`, when no other point of the end's
own segment lies within `gpx_extrapolation_heading_seconds` of it — a track of one point among them — or the farthest
that does is at the end's own time: with no stretch to take a heading over, no projection is made.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-projection_without_heading.title: A projection with no heading lands on the end

BLD-prune_command.content:
`prep prune-quarantine` SHALL remove whole `<plan-id>` folders of the quarantine, selected by `--plan-id` (repeatable)
or `--older-than-days` — a run's age taken from the time in its plan id, the two selecting the runs either names —
listing them with their files and bytes and deleting only with `--yes`, and with no selector only with `--all` too; the
plan's summary carries the quarantine's footprint. An age below one day is refused; a folder whose name gives no time is never selected by age, and is listed as such.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prune_command.title: `prune-quarantine` and its selectors

BLD-prune_ignores_seal.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-prune_ignores_seal.title: `prune-quarantine` does not check the seal

BLD-prune_record.content:
`prep prune-quarantine --yes` SHALL, before it removes anything and when it selects at least one run, write
`photos-16-prune-record.json` in `.photos-ingest/` through {need}`BLD-plan_backups`' set-aside: its time, its selectors,
and for each `<plan-id>` folder it removes, every file in it with its bytes and the folder's `manifest.json` as it
read it (null where it cannot be read). A listing prune writes none.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prune_record.title: The prune's record is `photos-16-prune-record.json`

BLD-quarantine_layout.content:
A quarantined file SHALL go to `.photos-ingest-quarantine/<plan-id>/` at its workspace path, its entry — original path,
quarantine path, the copy kept, the fingerprint and the plan id — appended to that folder's `manifest.json` before the
move; the manifest is replaced whole at each append, and one found unreadable is set aside as
`manifest.json.corrupt-<time>-<random>` and a new one begun — or, where it cannot be set aside, the quarantine move
fails before the file is moved, the manifest left as it was.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-quarantine_layout.title: The quarantine's layout and manifest

BLD-quarantine_reasons.content:
Each quarantine move SHALL carry its `kind` — `duplicate`, `exiftool_leftover`, `dump_dotfile` or `raw_culled`
({need}`BLD-culled_raw_found`) — into its manifest entry; the plan's report counts the moves by kind in
`quarantined_by_reason`, its duplicate counts taking only `duplicate`; the handoff's `diagnostics.duplicates_or_conflicts`
and each destination folder's duplicates hold the duplicates alone, the others listed under
`diagnostics.quarantined_not_duplicates` with their kind; and prep's log records the duplicates alone as duplicates.
BLD-quarantine_reasons.section_name: 10. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
sections: 10. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-quarantine_reasons.title: Each quarantine move names its kind

BLD-raw_jpeg_pair_by_exact_name.content:
A JPEG and a raw file SHALL be a pair only where, in one inbox folder, their names before the extension are the same
with case — `IMG_1.JPG` pairs with `IMG_1.cr2`, never with `img_1.cr2` — the extensions matched ignoring case
({need}`BLD-jpeg_extensions`).
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-raw_jpeg_pair_by_exact_name.title: A JPEG pairs with its RAW by its name, with case

BLD-record_ownership.content:
A phase SHALL write only records in its own number band of the numbering scheme: prep `photos-1X`, geotag `photos-2X`,
merge `photos-3X`, and on success the seal, `photos-00-sealed.json`, which merge alone writes. The configuration and
the database are phase-neutral, each with its own writers' rule: prep seeds
the configuration, which `init-library` may later extend by `library_root` alone
({need}`BLD-init_library_writes_library_root`) and the decision editor by a camera group's class alone
({need}`BLD-editor_writes_device_groups`), and prep writes the database's cache and identity rows while geotag and
merge write only their own regions of it ({need}`BLD-workspace_database`). Bundling copies of every phase's records into
the archival package reads them, and is no write.
BLD-record_ownership.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-record_ownership.title: Which phase writes which record

BLD-recorded_offset_proposal.content:
A camera group's bucket with no anchor, no reading of its fixes' times, no offset shared from the same day elsewhere,
whose photos not yet corrected record at least one offset with their times — each read as `_own_offset` reads it, the
offset recorded with the field its time was read from, a value that is no offset being none — and all the same one,
SHALL be proposed −(that offset) as `proposal_source: "recorded_offset"`, ahead of `timezone_naive` — a neighbouring
day's offering, where there is one, taking its place ({need}`BLD-neighbour_day_proposal`) — with
`proposed_offset_seconds`, `recorded_offset_seconds`, `recorded_by` (how many photos record it), an `example` of them
and `proposed_real_utc` at the bucket's earliest camera time. It takes effect as a `timezone_naive` proposal does
({need}`BLD-timezone_naive_offset`): as `recorded_offset_unconfirmed`, `decision_mode:
"to_be_confirmed_against_tracks"`, where track points lie by its photos and no decision is given, else only once
accepted, as `recorded_offset_accepted`. Photos recording more than one offset give no such proposal; the cell holds
`recorded_offsets_differ`, each offset recorded with how many photos record it and an `example`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-recorded_offset_proposal.title: The offset the photos record

BLD-rehash_summary.content:
The plan's `performance_and_cache.rehash_summary` SHALL count the media files fingerprinted this run by reason — `new`,
`moved-unmatched`, `size-changed`, `mtime-changed`, `metadata-stale`, `failed-before`, `engine-changed` — with a sample
of the unexpected ones, and the fingerprints reused from the plan memo.
BLD-rehash_summary.section_name: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-rehash_summary.title: The re-fingerprint summary

BLD-rename_planning.content:
For each destination, `plan_renames` SHALL count every current name of its photos as taken, case folded, and never
freed by a rename it plans — two photos that would trade names both take a suffix — then leave a photo whose name
already carries its timestamp, suffix and all, and ends with a lowercase extension, as it is; give one whose name
carries its timestamp but whose extension is not lowercase that name with its extension lowercased, unless another
photo there holds the name case folded; and give the others new names. Those that share a name, extension aside, and a
timestamp, and no two of one extension, are named as one. In order of their timestamp, their true time, the fraction of
a second they record (`sub_second`), a photo recording none after those that do, the suffix their name holds after the
timestamp prep named it by (`source_naive_time`), none first, and their path, each such photo or pair takes by
`allocate_stem` the first stem of its timestamp, bare or suffixed, that no name taken holds under any extension, each
member keeping its own extension. Every planned name ends with the photo's extension in lowercase. Execution applies
these renames, and those of {need}`BLD-set_aside_renamed_with_raw` and {need}`BLD-set_aside_jpeg_catches_up`, and no
other, each by a no-clobber move.
Photos a date fallback times record no fraction and were never named by a timestamp, so among themselves they take
their suffixes by path alone: in one destination, the file names they hold before the rename, compared as text,
character by character (`scan10.jpg` before `scan2.jpg`).
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-rename_planning.title: How renames are planned

BLD-repeated_write_failure.content:
`geotag execute` SHALL read, with the records of its earlier runs and before any change, the `failures` of the latest
of `photos-25-execution-summary.json` and its `-NNN` copies, newest first, that is not `rejected` — none when that one
is another plan's; one that cannot be read stops the run as {need}`BLD-unreadable_execution_records` does. Each photo
whose metadata write operations fail with the same set of operation types and errors as there is listed in
`repeated_failures` of the new summary — its path, `types`, `error` and `way_out` — and execute prints it with its way
out: move the photo from photos by destination into photos by date, a `moved_back` {need}`BLD-workspace_check` passes
with no acceptance, then run `prep plan`, `prep execute` and `geotag plan` again. The exit status is that of the run.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-repeated_write_failure.title: A write that failed the same way before

BLD-reprep_pending.content:
`by_dest_reprep_pending` SHALL name, from sizes and modification times alone, a photo in photos by destination the
handoff does not record at its path, one the handoff records in photos by date or by destination that is gone, or one
it records in photos by destination whose size or `mtime_ns` differs from its record: `geotag plan` stops on it with
the one re-prep blocker, and runs prep itself when {need}`BLD-geotag_auto_reprep` allows; prep's nothing-to-do guard
does not stop while it names one. It reads no hidden folder, as prep reads none; one holding a file it names itself, so that prep is run and stops on it ({need}`RUL-hidden_folder_among_photos_blocks`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-reprep_pending.title: What prep has yet to record

BLD-rerun_recognition.content:
Geotag SHALL record what it wrote in the file's `GPSProcessingMethod`: the bare value beside each position it writes —
`matched`, `interpolated` or `extrapolated` for one from the tracks, within the direct-match window of a track point,
between two or past a track's end, `manual_locked` or `manual_fallback` for one the user set — and, on a photo whose
time it writes — a `metadata_time_write` in the plan — or whose field already carries its mark from an earlier run, and
to which it writes no position, the suffix `+carto-time` appended once to whatever the field held, keeping the device's
own value. A photo whose time is resolved to what it holds, with no mark, gets no suffix; with no position written
either, no `gps_marker_write` is planned for it. Any other value is the device's own,
and the GPS beside it native.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-rerun_recognition.title: Geotag marks what it wrote

BLD-rerun_writes_only_differences.content:
A write SHALL be planned only where the file does not already hold its value, names being recomputed from the
destination's local time, a file already so named getting no rename ({need}`BLD-rename_planning`,
{need}`BLD-rerun_recognition`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-rerun_writes_only_differences.title: A re-run plans only the writes and renames that differ

BLD-resolved_utc.content:
`compute_resolved_utc` SHALL resolve each photo of photos by destination to UTC: a camera's photo by the offset of its
cell — `<group>@<date>` where the destination has one for its date, else `<group>`, and of that day split at a change
of the clock the part the split gives the photo ({need}`BLD-clock_change_split`) — a corrected offset from
`photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json` taking its place (`camera_group_offset`); a phone's, where its day there has a
cell whose `phone.applies_to` is `every_photo` — or `untagged_photos`, for a photo recording no offset — and whose
effective source is not `as_recorded`, by that cell, as {need}`BLD-phone_offset_cell` reads it; else a phone's by the offset recorded with
its time — one written within the time's own value, after the seconds and any fraction of them, else its field's:
`OffsetTimeOriginal` for `DateTimeOriginal`, `OffsetTimeDigitized` for `CreateDate`, `OffsetTime`
for `ModifyDate` (`smartphone_native_offset`) — else its destination's timezone (`destination_timezone`); and a time
geotag already corrected by its own offset, else the timezone (`geotag_corrected`); a time the user kept as the
photo's true time by the timezone (`kept_true_time`, {need}`BLD-changed_time_kept`); a photo with no recorded time by
its destination's date fallback, at midnight, through the timezone (`date_fallback`, {need}`BLD-date_fallback_cell`);
every other photo `unresolved` —
one whose time its offset carries past the calendar's first or last year as `time_out_of_range`. An offset is `Z`, or a
sign, two digits of hours up to 14 and two of minutes up to 59, with or without a colon between; anything else is none.
`geotag plan` writes the rows — `relative_path`, `destination_path`, `destination_timezone`, `camera_group`,
`time_decision_scope` (the cell, `<group>[@<date>]|<destination>`), `source_naive_time`, `source_time_provenance`,
`time_rule_used`, `utc_offset_used`, `resolved_utc`, `resolved_utc_status`, `resolved_utc_provenance` — into the
`resolved_utc_cache` table once photos-22 is complete, replacing the table whole. A time that must be read by the zone and which the zone skips or repeats is resolved by the UTC offset photos-21 holds in effect for the photo (`local_time_answered`, {need}`BLD-local_time_readings`), else left unresolved — rule `local_time_skipped` or `local_time_repeated`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-resolved_utc.title: How each photo's true time is resolved

BLD-resolved_utc_fingerprint.content:
`resolved_utc_cache_fingerprint` SHALL be the SHA-256 over the rows ordered by path — each its `relative_path`,
`resolved_utc`, `resolved_utc_status`, `time_rule_used`, `utc_offset_used` and `source_time_provenance` as text — and
the inputs, sorted by name: `camera_time_policy_fingerprint`, `camera_group_key_version`, the SHA-256 of photos-21 and
of photos-22, `prep_cache_fingerprint`, `metadata_field_set_version` and `gpx_fingerprint`, the last whether or not a
track decided anything.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-resolved_utc_fingerprint.title: The resolved-UTC fingerprint

BLD-retake_same_file.content:
A `fingerprint_retaken` step SHALL be given only where the record of the workspace's state ({need}`BLD-workspace_record`)
read as the execute begins has, at the path the entry was left at — or the path the user moved the file from — the size,
`mtime_ns` and inode of the file's new database row, and a fingerprint whose strategy or engine version is not the new
one's.
BLD-retake_same_file.section_name: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-retake_same_file.title: A retaken fingerprint is the same file's

BLD-review_item_identity.content: Each of photos-23's `review_items` SHALL carry its photo's `content_fingerprint`, and a photo's earlier decision is the item, among its own destination's earlier `review_items` alone, with its fingerprint, or with the fingerprint its own values are pinned under, else — for an item carrying none — the item at its path. An item of a photo the tracks did not place carries `tracks`: the `reason` (`no_tracks`, `outside_track`, `track_gap`, `track_jump`, `tracks_disagree`) with `seconds_from_track`, `gap_seconds`, `jump_meters` or the `gpx_files` and `apart_meters` that go with it. The record's `track_disagreements` lists each pair of tracks that placed photos apart and how many, which `geotag plan` also warns of.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-review_item_identity.title: A review item is its photo's

BLD-rewrite_synced_before_rename.content:
Every file cartographer rewrites in the control directory and the quarantine — the configuration's seed, the plans,
decisions and their backups, the journals, the handoff, the logs, the guard, the quarantine manifest, the database
images and the archival package — SHALL be written whole to a temporary file in its folder, synced to disk, renamed
over the earlier one, and the folder then synced.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-rewrite_synced_before_rename.title: A rewritten record is on disk before it replaces the earlier one

BLD-seal_marker.content:
The seal SHALL be `photos-00-sealed.json` in the control directory, its own file beside the workspace guard — which only
prep writes — recording `sealed`, the merge run id (`merged_run_id`) and `library_root`; its presence alone seals.
BLD-seal_marker.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-seal_marker.title: The seal

BLD-seed_before_fingerprints.content:
Prep SHALL seed the configuration at the start of its run, before any fingerprint of it is taken, so that every
fingerprint, the handoff's recorded hash among them, is of the file as it stands in the workspace.
BLD-seed_before_fingerprints.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-seed_before_fingerprints.title: The configuration is seeded before it is fingerprinted

BLD-set_aside_jpeg_catches_up.content:
For each photo holding geotag's mark (`GPSProcessingMethod` a position marker or ending in the time-fixed suffix) whose
`rename_no_clobber` the plan does not hold, `build_executable_plan` SHALL add the rename of
{need}`BLD-set_aside_renamed_with_raw` of each JPEG set aside beside it, to the name the photo holds, extension aside —
as there, but with no `follows`: execution applies it with the other files' operations, the photo's name being already
its own. None is added where the JPEG holds that name, or where another file in `3-redundant-jpgs` holds it or is given
it, case folded.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-set_aside_jpeg_catches_up.title: A set-aside JPEG catching up with its RAW

BLD-set_aside_pair_recorded.content:
Prep's move of a JPEG into `3-redundant-jpgs` SHALL carry, where its inbox folder holds one raw file of its name, that
raw file's fingerprint as `raw_fingerprint`: the JPEG's `redundant_jpeg_separated` step in the prep log keeps it, and
each prep execution writes the latest one of each JPEG into its record of the handoff. Beside two raw files of its name,
a JPEG names neither.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-set_aside_pair_recorded.title: The pair, recorded by prep

BLD-set_aside_renamed_with_raw.content:
For each photo whose `rename_no_clobber` the plan holds, `build_executable_plan` SHALL add a `rename_no_clobber` of each
handoff record in `3-redundant-jpgs` whose `raw_fingerprint` is the photo's fingerprint
({need}`BLD-set_aside_pair_recorded`) and which is on disk at its recorded size and time: to the photo's new name,
extension aside, with the JPEG's own extension in lowercase; `with_raw` naming the photo, `follows` its rename; its
preconditions among the plan's `media_preconditions`. None is added where the JPEG holds that name, or where another file in
`3-redundant-jpgs` holds it or is given it, case folded: the JPEG is left as it is. Execution applies such a rename
after every other photo's operations, and only where the rename it follows is confirmed; it writes no tag. Finalize
records it in the JPEG's own entry of `photos-26`, with the JPEG's `geotag_path`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-set_aside_renamed_with_raw.title: A set-aside JPEG renamed with its RAW

BLD-several_bodies_groups.content:
`camera_time_and_timezone_policy.several_bodies_groups`, beside `device_groups`, SHALL be a list of camera group keys,
each listed in `device_groups.fixed_clock_cameras` and each once — else the configuration is refused; `[]` by default,
every group one camera. `recognize_camera_groups` marks a `camera` group named there `several_bodies: true`, and
`_offset_cell` then applies none of its GPX self-anchor or GPS-time proposals by itself, nor keeps one from earlier
({need}`BLD-day_offset_kept`): each takes effect only accepted or written; a cell of such a group whose proposal is from
its GPS, or shared, holds `several_bodies: true`. Its cells take no part in the offsets shared within a day
({need}`BLD-offset_shared_within_day`): none is a donor, none is offered a donor's offset, none is held against another.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-several_bodies_groups.title: Camera groups that are several bodies

BLD-shape_guards_by_phase.content:
Links: prep across the tree it walks ({need}`RUL-who_checks_for_links`); geotag and merge at the workspace root and
throughout `6-photos-by-dest` at startup, by a walk that follows nothing and reads no file
({need}`RUL-geotag_merge_check_links`), and through the handoff for the rest. Missing managed folders: prep, geotag and merge alike ({need}`RUL-missing_folder_blocks`).
BLD-shape_guards_by_phase.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-shape_guards_by_phase.title: Where each phase applies the shape guards

BLD-sidecar_extensions.content:
The editing sidecars SHALL be the files ending `.xmp`, `.dop` or `.pp3`, matched ignoring case — a fixed list, not
configuration.
BLD-sidecar_extensions.section_name: 5. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 5. What prep refuses to work on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-sidecar_extensions.title: The sidecars prep refuses

BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.content:
The snapshot SHALL be a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block of the workspace configuration,
`photos-00-config.json`; with no `zfs` block, or one not enabled, none is taken. Its name carries the plan id.
`snapshots_required` decides what a failed snapshot means: true, the run aborts before its first change; false, or the
block not configured, it proceeds without one.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.title: The snapshot is a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block

BLD-staleness_by_field_fingerprints.content:
Staleness SHALL follow the dependencies each record carries ({need}`DEF-dependency_cascade`): a plan depends on the
whole configuration's hash, a costly result on the hash of the areas it reads.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-staleness_by_field_fingerprints.title: Staleness follows the field-scoped fingerprints

BLD-stray_media_probe.content:
Prep's plan SHALL ask exiftool the `MIMEType` of one file for each distinct extension among the inbox's files of no
media class, and warn for each whose type is `image/*` or `video/*`; with exiftool absent, it warns of none.
BLD-stray_media_probe.section_name: 5. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 5. What prep refuses to work on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-stray_media_probe.title: One probe per stray extension

BLD-stray_records.content:
A stray SHALL be named in `photos-10-prep-plan.json` alone — in its `inventory` and `metadata_plan_status`, and in the
move that sets it aside (on the first run, the move into `0-sources` too) with its size and `mtime_ns` — and in the
journal only by that move's id; it has no fingerprint, no row in `photos-00-ingest.db` or the plan memo, and no entry in
the handoff or `photos-15-prep-log.json`, the archival package holding it only within the plans it carries.
BLD-stray_records.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-stray_records.title: Where a stray is named

BLD-strays_per_run.content:
Prep SHALL move a run's strays into `1-strays/<plan-id>/`, each at its path under `0-sources/`, so that no two runs
share a folder there.
BLD-strays_per_run.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-strays_per_run.title: A run's strays go to `1-strays/<plan-id>/`

BLD-sub_second_read.content:
`build_file_model` SHALL take a photo's `sub_second` from its record in the handoff, by `recorded_sub_second`: the
fraction written in its recorded time itself, else the digits of the EXIF sub-second field prep reads beside it —
`SubSecTimeOriginal` beside `DateTimeOriginal`, `SubSecTimeDigitized` beside `CreateDate`, `SubSecTime` beside
`ModifyDate`; none where neither holds one.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-sub_second_read.title: The fraction of a second a photo records

BLD-summary_counts_reuse.content:
Each phase's report SHALL count the files already right, and the work it took from a cache: prep's summary its cache
hits, merge's plan the library fingerprints it reused — in what it prints, never in the plan, which an unchanged
re-plan leaves byte-identical. Geotag keeps no cache of results, so has none to count.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-summary_counts_reuse.title: A run's summary counts what it reused

BLD-temp_sweep.content:
Merge's `execute` SHALL, after revalidating its plan and taking its snapshot and before its first move, remove every
`.tmp-xdev-*.part` file directly in `library_root` and in each planned target's directory, and record how many in
`photos-31-merge-summary.json` as `run_metadata.orphan_temps_swept`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-temp_sweep.title: Merge's sweep of temporary copies

BLD-time_given_organized.content:
Prep's organization stage SHALL take each file in `2-missing-metadata` whose metadata gives a recorded time with the
inbox's files to be filed — one `move_no_clobber` of reason `Chronological Organization` into its day folder of
`5-photos-by-date` or `4-videos-by-date`, its name allocated against the names already planned — after the duplicates
stage has set aside any copy of it, and leave one with no recorded time where and as it lies. A JPEG set aside beside
its RAW in `3-redundant-jpgs` keeps its name when the RAW is so filed: the two cannot be paired there (the pairing
rests on their sharing a dump folder), and the set-aside copy is never used.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-time_given_organized.title: A timed file in missing metadata is organized with the inbox's

BLD-time_written_recorded.content:
Before it writes a time to a file whose own values are pinned, execution SHALL record the `DateTimeOriginal` and
`OffsetTimeOriginal` it writes beside the pin in the original-values ledger, keeping every one it has recorded there,
so a write interrupted after it landed is known as geotag's own.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-time_written_recorded.title: The times geotag writes are recorded beside the pin

BLD-timezone_cell.content:
Each destination's `destination_timezone` in `photos-21-time-decisions.json` SHALL hold `proposed_iana_timezone` with
its `proposal_source` — `inherited`, naming the ancestor in `inherited_from`, or `config_default`, or `country`
({need}`BLD-country_choice`), or `photos_in_country` ({need}`BLD-zone_from_photos_in_country`), or `none` —
`user_decision.manual_iana_timezone`, `effective_iana_timezone`, `requires_user_input`, `stale_user_decision` and, when
the proposal took effect without the user, `decision_mode: "auto_resolved"`. Destinations are built parent first, so
each takes the `effective_iana_timezone` of its nearest ancestor that has one; one with none is offered
`default_folder_timezone`, as `config_default`, which takes effect only once written as its `manual_iana_timezone`.
Where a photo of the destination that is no camera's, not yet corrected, records with its time an offset that is not the
zone's — the one written, else the one inherited — at that time, the zone does not take effect: the cell asks, holding
`contradicted_by` — `photos`, an `example`, `recorded_offset_seconds`, `recorded_offsets` (each distinct one),
`timezone` and `timezone_offset_seconds` — and a destination within it inherits nothing through it, until another zone
is written that the photos agree with or `user_decision.confirmed_despite_recorded_offsets` lists every one of
`recorded_offsets`; then the zone takes effect, `contradicted_by` kept with `confirmed: true`. A list that does not
cover them is `stale_user_decision`, kept as written; one that is not a list of whole seconds, a blocker — `null`, as an
absent list, being none.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-timezone_cell.title: The timezone cell

BLD-timezone_naive_offset.content:
A bucket with no anchor and a destination timezone SHALL be proposed the offset −(the timezone's UTC offset at the
bucket's earliest camera time), daylight saving included, one offset for every photo of the bucket, as `proposal_source: "timezone_naive"` with
`proposed_offset_seconds`, `proposed_real_utc` and `proposed_from_timezone`. Where track points lie within
`drift_check_track_window_seconds` of the bucket's photos — by the times the offset gives, else by the times the camera
recorded — and no decision is given, it takes effect as `timezone_unconfirmed`, `decision_mode:
"to_be_confirmed_against_tracks"`, asking nothing in photos-21 and always asked in photos-22; elsewhere it takes effect
only once accepted, as `timezone_accepted`. A camera time the zone skips or repeats gives no offset: the cell asks for one, its proposal carrying `timezone_ambiguous` — the time, the zone, which case, and the two offsets.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-timezone_naive_offset.title: The offset derived from the timezone

BLD-tool_workers.content:
Prep SHALL read metadata through persistent `exiftool -stay_open` workers and fingerprint photos through a persistent
`magick -script -` process per thread — each file read, given `-colorspace sRGB -depth 8`, its `%#` printed, then
`-delete 0--1`, a `{ready}` line closing its reply — falling back to `identify` per file where `magick` is absent; it
starts `ffmpeg` per video. Each tool gets two attempts per file, a dead worker restarted between them.
BLD-tool_workers.section_name: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-tool_workers.title: The tools' workers

BLD-top_level_entries.content:
The top level of an initialized workspace SHALL hold exactly the managed folders `0-sources`…`6-photos-by-dest` and
`.photos-ingest/`, `.photos-ingest-quarantine/`, `.git` and other dotfiles and dot-directories, the inbox being
`0-sources/`. Prep applies the guard, geotag at startup ({need}`RUL-shape_checked_first`), merge in its preflight
({need}`BLD-merge_preflight`).
BLD-top_level_entries.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-top_level_entries.title: The workspace's top level

BLD-track_catalogue.content: `GPXIndex` SHALL keep, in geotag's region of `photos-00-ingest.db`, a catalogue of every `*.gpx` file under `gpx_root` — `gpx_track_files`, one entry per file as it was read: its path under the root, the folder directly under the root it is filed in, the size, modification time and inode it was read at, the SHA-256 of its bytes, the parse version that read it, the first and last of its points' UTC times, the window its kept points cover, its warnings and why it could not be parsed, and whether it is withdrawn — and, in `gpx_track_points`, each entry's points within the window it covers, each with its UTC time, latitude, longitude, point index, track and segment. A file whose size, modification time and inode are its entry's is not read again unless the window has grown into the span from its first point to its last past what the entry covers; a new or changed file, or one the window has grown into, is read and parsed, and becomes the entry for its bytes, its kept points those of the window it covered grown by the new one. Once `geotag plan` has stopped — done, at a decision for the user or at a blocker, never interrupted — each current entry's points outside the window it reached are taken out of the record and what the entry covers narrowed to match, but for its points within the window of each executed plan `gpx_track_use` names it for; a withdrawn entry keeps every point, and the window's own points, and so the fingerprint, are as they were. `geotag plan` writes the catalogue and its points outside the plan's operations, as it writes the resolved-UTC cache: they are what the track files hold, read again while the files are there, and decide nothing by themselves; `geotag execute` and `finalize` leave them as they are but for the marks of use ({need}`BLD-withdrawn_track_points`). A file catalogued and no longer under `gpx_root`, or no longer readable, leaves the index; one gone is named in a warning. A file is judged readable only when it is read: one whose size, modification time and inode are its entry's is not opened again, its points being already recorded. A folder under `gpx_root` that cannot be listed stops `geotag plan`, exit 2, naming it, before anything is withdrawn, and makes the plan stale at `geotag execute`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-track_catalogue.title: The catalogue of the tracks, and the points kept

BLD-track_file.content:
A track file SHALL be a file named `*.gpx`, `*.kml`, `*.kmz`, `*.fit`, `*.tcx`, `*.nmea` or `*.igc`, in any case. Of
these geotag reads only the `*.gpx` files beneath `gpx_root`.
BLD-track_file.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-track_file.title: A track file

BLD-track_file_blocker.content:
Prep SHALL raise one blocker for each track file it inventories, naming it, and leave it out of the plan
({need}`RUL-track_files_block_prep`); execute raises the same blocker for one that appeared after planning
({need}`RUL-new_file_restales_plan`).
BLD-track_file_blocker.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-track_file_blocker.title: Prep's blocker for a track file

BLD-track_placement.content: `place_gps` SHALL place a photo on each track by itself, taking the first of: the nearer in time of the two points around its resolved time, within `gpx_direct_match_max_seconds` (`direct_match`); the place between those two, linear in time and the short way round in longitude, when they are at most `gpx_interpolation_max_gap_seconds`, `gpx_interpolation_max_distance_meters` and `gpx_interpolation_max_speed_kmh` apart (`interpolated`); past the nearer point when it is within `gpx_extrapolation_max_seconds` and is an end — the track's first or last point, or a side of a gap longer than `gpx_interpolation_max_gap_seconds` (`extrapolated`). The projection follows the heading from the farthest point of the track within `gpx_extrapolation_heading_seconds` of the end, and falls back to the end itself when it lands farther than `gpx_extrapolation_max_distance_meters` from it or the heading is faster than `gpx_extrapolation_max_speed_kmh`. Of the tracks that place the photo, those placing it by a point or between two count, and only where there is none the projections; of those, the tracks of the best rank (`BLD-track_precedence`), of which the best wins — by method in that order, then the nearest in time, then the file name; but when another of that rank lies more than `gpx_tracks_agree_max_distance_meters` from it, none places the photo, the reason `tracks_disagree` naming both files. Each counted track of a lower rank is kept with the placement in `lower_tracks`: its file — with the track's number where the file gives two — and `apart_meters` from the position. Two points either side of a `<trkseg>` break are never interpolated between — each is an end of its segment, the reason `track_gap` carrying `segment_break` — and a heading is taken from the end's own segment; two disagreeing tracks of one file are named by the file and the track's number.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-track_placement.title: How a track places a photo

BLD-track_points.content:
Geotag SHALL read every `<trkpt>` of each `*.gpx` file under `gpx_root`, its `<time>` as an `xsd:dateTime` — fractional
seconds optional, the zone `Z` or a numeric offset — normalised to UTC; a point lacking `lat` or `lon`, with one out of
range or not a number, lacking a `<time>`, or with a time unparseable or naive is skipped with a warning naming the
file and the point's index, as is a file that cannot be read or parsed. `geotag plan` prints the count of warnings and
the first `GPX_WARNINGS_SHOWN`, with the number of the rest. A point keeps the index of its `<trk>` and of its `<trkseg>`: the points of one `<trk>` of one file are one track. A file that cannot be opened, or is not well-formed, is unreadable; a folder holding track files all of them unreadable stops the plan, each named with why, and a linked folder under `gpx_root` is named in a warning and not followed.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-track_points.title: How track points are read

BLD-track_precedence.content: `gpx_track_precedence` SHALL be a list of folder names directly under `gpx_root`, best first, each once, a single path component not starting with `.` — else the configuration is refused; empty, every track ranks alike. `GPXIndex.rank` gives a track file the place of the first folder of its path under `gpx_root` in that list, and a file in no listed folder the list's length. A listed folder that is not a directory under `gpx_root`, or is a link, is the index's first warning. The list, as JSON, enters the tracks' `fingerprint`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-track_precedence.title: How tracks are ranked

BLD-track_time_parser.content:
A track point's `<time>` SHALL be parsed by the host Python's `datetime.fromisoformat`, a final `Z` or `z` first
written `+00:00`, and a time it takes with no offset skipped as naive ({need}`BLD-track_points`): on Python 3.11 and
later it takes, beside every `xsd:dateTime`, the other ISO 8601 forms it knows — a space for the `T`, the basic format,
a week date, a time without seconds; on 3.9 and 3.10 it refuses a fraction of a second of other than three or six
digits, whose point is skipped as unparseable. Which points a track gives therefore depends on the Python the
executable runs on.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-track_time_parser.title: Track times are read as the host's Python reads them

BLD-track_window.content:
The tracks' window SHALL be the union of what each reader of the tracks reaches, from the reader's own settings, never a setting of its own: each photo's camera time, read as UTC, give or take `gpx_anchor_max_clock_error_seconds` and the larger of `gpx_direct_match_max_seconds` and `gpx_interpolation_max_gap_seconds` — offset inference, the far-from-evidence check, and a higher-ranked track covering an anchor candidate's time; each camera's photos of one day in one destination, from the first camera time to the last, give or take `drift_check_track_window_seconds` — the drift check falling back on the camera's clock; once photos-21 is complete, each drift bucket's photos at their corrected times, from the first to the last, give or take `drift_check_track_window_seconds`; and once photos-22 is complete, each photo placement places, and each whose own position its offset contradicts
({need}`BLD-contradicted_position`), at its corrected time, give or take the largest of `gpx_direct_match_max_seconds`, `gpx_interpolation_max_gap_seconds`, and `gpx_extrapolation_max_seconds` with `gpx_extrapolation_heading_seconds`. A span is of whole seconds since the epoch, both ends in it. `geotag plan` indexes the first two before photos-21 and widens the index before photos-22 and again before photos-23, each record's `gpx_fingerprint` that of the window it was made in. `photos-24-executable-plan.json` records its window in `depends_on` as `gpx_window`, a list of `[start, end]`: `geotag execute` indexes the tracks under `gpx_root` over it, leaving the catalogue as it was, and `geotag finalize` the points the catalogue keeps, never reading `gpx_root`; merge builds no index of the tracks; a plan whose `gpx_window` is missing or not such a list is stale. Past the window a reader finds no track: the far-from-evidence check reports none within reach where one lies past it, the skipped-frame reason `outside_time_window` sees only the window's points, and an unplaced photo's reason measures to the window's points.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-track_window.title: The window of the tracks

BLD-two_step_case_rename.content:
A filed media file's extension SHALL be lowercased by two no-clobber renames in its folder, through a temporary name
free on disk and in the plan; an inbox file's, in the move that files it.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-two_step_case_rename.title: A filed file's extension is lowercased in two renames

BLD-unexecuted_kept_plan_passed.content:
`geotag finalize` SHALL pass over a kept plan `photos-24-executable-plan-NNN.json` that cannot be read when its
SHA-256 is the `summarizes` SHA-256 of photos-24 in neither `photos-25-execution-summary.json` nor any `-NNN` copy of
it, and every `journal-*.json` with a `confirmed` operation is that of the current plan or of a kept plan it can read;
otherwise the kept plan stops it as {need}`BLD-unreadable_execution_records` says, as does a summary it reads for this
that cannot be read.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unexecuted_kept_plan_passed.title: A kept plan no execution ran, passed over

BLD-unidentified_files.content:
A file whose `camera_group_key` is `NO_IDENTITY_KEY` (`unknown`), the key prep gives a file with no serial, make, model
or owner, SHALL be classed `unidentified` by `recognize_camera_groups` whatever the configuration lists, never among the
unknown groups, given no offset cell, and resolved by its own offset (`unidentified_native_offset`), else as
{need}`BLD-unidentified_files_question` says.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unidentified_files.title: Files naming no camera

BLD-unidentified_files_question.content: Each destination holding photos with files classed `unidentified`, not yet corrected, with a readable time and no offset recorded with it (`_own_offset`) SHALL hold `unidentified_files`: `files` (how many), `examples` (the first three paths), `proposed_iana_timezone` (the zone in effect, or `""`), `user_decision.accept_proposal` and `user_decision.accepted_timezone`, `effective_iana_timezone`, `requires_user_input` and `stale_user_decision`. An acceptance holds while `accepted_timezone` is the zone in effect — then `effective_iana_timezone` is that zone, whatever files have come since — else it is `stale_user_decision`, kept as written; `accept_proposal` not a boolean, or true with no `accepted_timezone`, or an `accepted_timezone` that is not text, is a blocker. Such a file resolves by the zone (`destination_timezone`) only while `effective_iana_timezone` is the destination's zone, else stays unresolved, `local_time_unconfirmed`; photos-21 is not complete while the question asks.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unidentified_files_question.title: The question of a destination's files naming no camera

BLD-unknown_group_snippet.content:
On an unknown camera group, `geotag plan` SHALL print the `device_groups` arrays `fixed_clock_cameras` and `phones`,
in the configuration's own key order, each the configured list with every unknown key appended, as JSON to paste over
the configuration's, and exit with status 2 having written no record and read no track.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unknown_group_snippet.title: The classification snippet

BLD-unreadable_execution_records.content:
`geotag execute` SHALL stop, exit 2, once its plan is revalidated and before it keeps a decision, takes a snapshot or
writes anything, when the plan's `journal-<plan id>.json` or `photos-25-execution-summary.json` is there and cannot be
opened or parsed as a JSON object; `geotag finalize` refuses likewise, writing nothing, on the summary, the plan's
journal, a kept plan `photos-24-executable-plan-NNN.json` — but one {need}`BLD-unexecuted_kept_plan_passed` passes
over — or any `journal-*.json` it reads to find the earlier passes.
Each names the file. A file that is not there is none.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unreadable_execution_records.title: Records of earlier executions that cannot be read

BLD-unreadable_offset_tags.content: For each photo not yet corrected whose offset field paired with the one its time was read from ({need}`BLD-resolved_utc`) holds a value that is not blank and is no offset, `build_time_decisions` SHALL list `{relative_path, field, value}` — the value as text — in its destination's `unreadable_offset_tags`, and `geotag plan` warns of each after writing photos-21, the first `UNREADABLE_TAGS_SHOWN` by name and the number of the rest; `_own_offset` reads it as none.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unreadable_offset_tags.title: Offset tags that hold no offset

BLD-unreadable_plan.content:
Where `photos-24-executable-plan.json` is there and cannot be opened or parsed as a JSON object, `geotag execute` and
`geotag finalize` SHALL stop, exit 2, before they read another record, take a snapshot or write anything, naming the
file and `geotag plan` as the way on; `merge plan` reports it as a blocker naming the same; and the console's summary
of the geotag plan shows it as a plan with that blocker, which no execution is offered for. The file is left as it is:
the next `geotag plan` sets it aside under `-NNN` as it sets aside any plan it replaces.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unreadable_plan.title: An executable plan that cannot be read

BLD-unreadable_prep_log.content:
Where `photos-15-prep-log.json` exists and is not readable JSON holding a `photos` object, prep's plan SHALL record a
blocker naming it, execute's preflight refuses on the same before any change, and the log's rebuild fails the run
rather than read it as empty; with no such file, the earlier log is empty.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-unreadable_prep_log.title: An unreadable `photos-15-prep-log.json` is a blocker

BLD-untimed_mark.content: The untimed name SHALL be `UNKN_<name it came with>`, with the `-NNN` suffix when that is taken.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-untimed_mark.title: The `UNKN_` mark

BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.content:
The whole-file fingerprint SHALL be carried in the `depends_on` of geotag's executable plan
({need}`BLD-geotag_dependencies`) and of merge's plan, `config_fingerprint`, each plan refused when it no longer matches
the file.
BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.title: The whole-file hash is in the executable plan's dependencies

BLD-withdrawn_track_points.content: `geotag execute` SHALL record in `gpx_track_use`, after revalidation and the snapshot check and before the first write — a run a required snapshot ends recording nothing — the plan's id and its `gpx_window` with each current catalogue entry by which the plan places or times photos: the track a GPS write's provenance names; for each cell of photos-21 whose offset the camera's own GPS gave, the tracks of its anchors within `gpx_anchor_offset_spread_max_seconds` of the offset — of every anchor where none is — and those of its `anchored_by`; and the `tracks` of each cell of photos-22 whose drift offset is in effect. An entry no longer its file's — the file gone, changed, or unreadable — is kept with its points, `withdrawn` 1, when `gpx_track_use` names it, and deleted with them when not. A withdrawn entry is not indexed; the file back with the same bytes makes it its file's again.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-withdrawn_track_points.title: The tracks an executed plan used, withdrawn and kept

BLD-workspace_changes_logged.content:
The check SHALL print the changes it passes, `sorted` aside, and those accepted, and return them — `kind`, `path`,
`from`, the `accepted` code, an interrupted run's `phase` and `plan_id` and, where the record holds one, the
`content_fingerprint` — for the execution's record:
prep's execute adds them, each with its `run`, to `workspace_changes` of `photos-15-prep-log.json`, after the earlier
runs' — an execute that ends short of writing its log adds them there, the rest of the log as it was, before it records
the state it leaves; geotag's execute writes them as `workspace_changes` of `photos-25-execution-summary.json`, merge's as
`workspace_changes` of `photos-31-merge-summary.json`. A plan, a dry run and finalize print them.
BLD-workspace_changes_logged.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_changes_logged.title: Where the changes by hand are named

BLD-workspace_check.content:
`check_workspace` SHALL compare `workspace_entries` — each file's `lstat`, no file opened — with the record through
`compare_workspace`, in this order: a file at its recorded path with its recorded size, time and inode is unchanged; one
at a new path with a recorded file's size, time and inode is that file moved; at its own path, the same size and time
under a new inode is `copied`, and a size or time changed is `time_given` in `2-missing-metadata`, `changed` elsewhere;
one of a recorded file's size, time and name under a new inode, the only such pair, is that file moved; a recorded file
left over is `deleted` in photos by date, photos by destination, videos by date and the redundant JPEGs, `removed`
elsewhere; any file left over `appeared`. A move from photos by date into photos by destination, or within the latter,
is `sorted` (`copied` under a new inode), one back from photos by destination into photos by date `moved_back`, any
other `moved`. `changed`, `appeared`, `removed` and `moved` stop the command, exit 2; the others pass. Prep calls it in
`_run_locked` for its plan, dry run and execute once its shape check has passed and the configuration loads, comparing
nothing where there is no record; geotag in `run` for its plan, execute and finalize, before the automatic re-prep,
where its preflight would find the workspace initialized and unsealed, the configuration readable, the top level as it
should be and no link in photos by destination; merge in `_run_locked_workflow` for its plan, dry run and execute,
before its preflight validates the library, the handoff or the photos, where the preflight's first steps find the
workspace initialized and unsealed, the configuration readable and the top level as it should be. Geotag and merge stop, exit 2, on a workspace with no record. `prune-quarantine`,
`init-library` and the editor never call it.
BLD-workspace_check.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_check.title: The check every checking command makes first

BLD-workspace_database.content:
The workspace database SHALL be SQLite, `photos-00-ingest.db` in `.photos-ingest/`, written by: prep, of the file and
metadata caches (`file_cache`, `metadata_cache`) and their version row (`meta`), through its single-writer path (execute's main
thread); geotag, of the resolved-UTC cache (`resolved_utc_cache`), the values each photo held before geotag first wrote
to it and the times geotag wrote to it (`original_values`, {need}`BLD-original_values_pinned`,
{need}`BLD-time_written_recorded`), and the catalogue of the tracks with the points kept and the tracks each executed plan
used (`gpx_track_files`, `gpx_track_points`, `gpx_track_use`, {need}`BLD-track_catalogue`); merge, of the library-file fingerprint cache
(`library_fingerprint_cache`, keyed by the library file's absolute path with its size and modification time); and every
execution, of the record of the state it leaves the workspace's files in (`workspace_record`, named by
`meta.workspace_record_id`, {need}`BLD-workspace_record`). Where each
photo landed is in merge's
JSON records, not the database. The other database is scratch, re-derivable and deletable at any time: prep's
plan memo, `photos-00-plan-memo.db` ({need}`BLD-plan_memo`).
BLD-workspace_database.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_database.title: The database: its file and its writers

BLD-workspace_guard.content:
The mark SHALL be the file `photos-00-workspace-guard` in `.photos-ingest/`, which the initializing run's execute writes
after every other operation has succeeded; the managed folders it creates are `0-sources` … `6-photos-by-dest`. It
holds `initialized`, `tool` and `initialized_by_run`, the initializing plan's id, which the archival package's manifest
records as the workspace's identity ({need}`BLD-archive_manifest`).
BLD-workspace_guard.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_guard.title: The mark is `photos-00-workspace-guard`, written last

BLD-workspace_one_filesystem.content:
`workspace_volume_breaks` SHALL walk every folder of the workspace without following links, comparing each one's device
with the workspace root's and not descending into a folder found on another; prep's and geotag's `run`, and merge's
plan, dry run, execution and in-workspace `init-library`, call it through `workspace_volume_error` once they hold the
workspace lock and have found the workspace not sealed against them ({need}`BLD-phases_check_seal`) and, on a folder
found elsewhere, report it and exit 2.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_one_filesystem.title: Each run checks the workspace's devices

BLD-workspace_record.content:
The record SHALL be the table `workspace_record` of `photos-00-ingest.db` — each file's `relative_path`, `size`,
`mtime_ns`, `inode` and `fingerprint` (prep's `file_cache.content_hash` where that row still has the file's size and
time, else the earlier record's for the same file: at the path a run of the tool's own moved or rewrote it from, at its
own path unchanged, or anywhere under the same size, time and inode) — named by `meta.workspace_record_id`, of every
file `workspace_entries` finds: in each managed folder but the inbox, hidden entries left out as prep leaves them, and
in `.photos-ingest-quarantine/` whole but the `.tmp-` files of a manifest's rewrite, a link an entry of its own.
`write_workspace_record` rewrites it whole, in one transaction, with a new id: prep's execute after its handoff and
before its database image, or in its `finally` once its operations have begun; geotag's `execute_plan` in a `finally`
once it begins applying photos, each written or renamed photo's fingerprint carried from the path it was planned under;
merge's `execute_plan` in a `finally` once its moves have begun, before its summary, database image and seal. A prune
that deletes takes out of the record every file under the run folders it removes that is no longer on disk
(`forget_in_workspace_record`), in a `finally`, so a removal cut short midway is taken out as far as it went, the
workspace not sealed. No plan, dry run or finalize writes it.
BLD-workspace_record.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_record.title: The record of the workspace's state

BLD-write_failure_reason.content:
`_exiftool_write` SHALL return `True` for a write it made and, for one it could not, the reason: exiftool's standard
error, else its standard output, its whitespace collapsed — else `exiftool exited with status <n>` — or, for an error
that stopped the write itself, its type and message. Each of the photo's write operations then fails with that text as
its `error` in `failures` of photos-25; a failed rename carries the error of the move, and a photo whose application
raised, the error raised.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-write_failure_reason.title: The reason a write failed

BLD-zone_asked_at_containers.content: A container destination's timezone cell with no `effective_iana_timezone`, where no `manual_iana_timezone` is written and no `country` is chosen, SHALL hold `asked_for` — each destination within it whose timezone cell requires input, where no folder below the container on the way down to it, it included, has a `manual_iana_timezone` written or a `country` chosen — and require input while that list is not empty; every other container's timezone cell requires none. Computed after every destination's cell is built, from the cells of that run.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-zone_asked_at_containers.title: A timezone asked at the folders above a destination waiting for one

BLD-zone_from_photos_in_country.content: A destination holding photos, in a country whose `country_zones` are several, with no zone reaching it from above within the country nor one of a country of one timezone, SHALL be proposed `_zone_from_photos`: the one of `country_zones` at which, for each photo `_recorded_readings` gives — not a fixed-clock camera's, not yet corrected, not a kept true time, with an offset recorded beside its time — the zone's offset at the instant that offset gives, to the minute, is the offset recorded; none where no photo is read, or where none or several zones fit them all. It is `proposal_source: "photos_in_country"`, ahead of `config_default`, and takes effect like an inherited zone, `decision_mode: "auto_resolved"`, a `manual_iana_timezone` overriding it; the destinations within it inherit it.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-zone_from_photos_in_country.title: The zone a country's photos fit

BLD-zone_table_download.content:
`fetch_zone_table` SHALL fetch `https://data.iana.org/time-zones/tzdata-latest.tar.gz` once, over HTTPS with the
standard library — a redirect followed only to another `https` address, any other refused as a failed fetch — within `ZONE_TABLE_TIMEOUT_S` (20 s) and `ZONE_TABLE_MAX_BYTES`, its one header beyond the
library's own the User-Agent `photos-cartographer`; open it in memory and take out `zone.tab`, `iso3166.tab` and
`version`, writing nothing of the archive to disk; and refuse it unless `check_zone_table_text` finds each table a row of
its form on every line not a comment and at least one row. The copy taken is recorded as `copy` (`source_url`,
`tzdata_version`, `fetched_at`, `zone_tab`, `iso3166_tab`) in `photos-02-zone-table.json`, which is archived and sealed
with the other control records. A fetch that fails or is refused warns, naming why: with a copy fetched earlier, that
copy and its record stand; else the answer is recorded with `failure` and the carried copy is in use.
BLD-zone_table_download.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-zone_table_download.title: The download of the table of countries

BLD-zone_table_question.content:
`prep plan` SHALL take its answer to whether to download the table of countries from `--download-zone-table yes|no`;
given none, while `zone_table_question_pending` — `host_has_zone_table` false (no `zone.tab` where this Python reads
its zones, `zoneinfo.TZPATH` then the `tzdata` package) and no answer recorded — it asks `zone_table_question`, which
names the carried copy's tzdata release and that refusing leaves it in use, possibly stale, as a y/N question before
its scan, where its standard input is a terminal and it reports to the terminal, not to the console; else it has no answer. Once the plan
is saved, `settle_zone_table` acts on it: where the host has its own table nothing is recorded or fetched; no answer
with none recorded warns how to give one and records nothing, the carried copy in use, the plan unaffected; `no`
records `{"download": "declined"}` and `yes` fetches ({need}`BLD-zone_table_download`) and records
`{"download": "accepted", "copy": …}`, both in `photos-02-zone-table.json` through `write_versioned_json`. A recorded
answer is not asked again; an answer given on a later `prep plan` is acted on as the first was. Where the host has no table of its own and
`photos-02-zone-table.json` exists and is not a JSON object whose `download` is `accepted` or `declined`
(`zone_table_record_error`), `prep plan` stops with status 2 before its question and scan, and each geotag command
after its workspace check, naming the file; the console's state then asks nothing. The console's prep Plan
asks the same question while its state's `zone_table` holds it, and sends the answer as `zone_table`, which it passes
to the run as `--download-zone-table`.
BLD-zone_table_question.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-zone_table_question.title: The question of the table of countries, asked by `prep plan`

CHC-ask_only_what_data_cannot_settle.content: Resolve everything derivable automatically; ask only real judgment questions, and make each one cheap to answer.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-ask_only_what_data_cannot_settle.title: Ask only what the data can't settle

CHC-local_folder_library.content:
The destination is a plain directory tree on disk (feeds digiKam or Immich), not a cloud service or proprietary
catalog.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-local_folder_library.title: A local, owned, folder-based library

CHC-photos_matter.content: Because they matter, no original may be lost or silently altered — correctness beats convenience.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-photos_matter.title: Photos matter; they are irreplaceable, so they deserve care

CHC-total_placement.content:
Every photo ends up on the map — precise where tracks allow, rough or manual where they don't — so the result is a
*map-complete* library, not just the frames that came with a location.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-total_placement.title: 100% placement, even under GPS scarcity

DEF-anchor.content:
An **anchor** is a photo holding its own position whose place on the tracks, at some offset of its camera's clock, gives
that offset; an offset its camera's anchors support is **anchored**.
DEF-anchor.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
DEF-anchor.title: An anchor

DEF-archival_package.content:
The **archival package** is one archive, kept with the control records, holding the complete record of a dump's journey
through the pipeline — what was done to its photos and why. It is what the user keeps when the workspace goes away.
DEF-archival_package.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-archival_package.title: The archival package

DEF-authored_value.content: An **authored value** is one the user writes by hand: a setting of the configuration, or a decision.
DEF-authored_value.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
DEF-authored_value.title: An authored value

DEF-camera_group.content:
A **camera group** is the photos one camera or device took, identified by a key derived from the device-identity
metadata the files carry.
DEF-camera_group.title: A camera group

DEF-clock_offset.content:
A camera's **clock offset** is the whole number of seconds added to its recorded time to give UTC: the timezone its
clock was set to and the clock's own error, together. A camera keeping exact Brussels summer time has −7200, not 0.
DEF-clock_offset.title: A clock offset

DEF-config_areas.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
DEF-config_areas.title: What the configuration sets

DEF-configuration.content:
A workspace's **configuration** is the one record of the settings its runs read. It is kept in the workspace, beside
what is processed under it, and it is an input the user authors.
DEF-configuration.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
DEF-configuration.title: The configuration

DEF-container_destination.content:
A **container destination** is a folder in photos by destination that holds destinations but no photo of its own —
photos by destination itself among them, when it holds no photo directly.
DEF-container_destination.title: A container destination

DEF-control_records.content:
A workspace's **control records** are everything cartographer keeps in it besides the media: the configuration, the
plans and the decisions, the journals, the end-of-phase records and the databases. The quarantine's manifests are not
control records: each belongs to the quarantine folder whose duplicates it describes.
DEF-control_records.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
DEF-control_records.title: The control records

DEF-corrected_time.content:
A photo's time is **corrected** when geotag writes its true time into the photo, the photo holding another, or none, and
stays corrected once written: a time geotag wrote on an earlier run is a corrected one. A true time the photo already
holds is resolved, not corrected.
DEF-corrected_time.title: A corrected time

DEF-database_image.content:
A phase's **database image** is a copy of the workspace database as it stood at the end of that phase's latest
successful run.
DEF-database_image.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-database_image.title: A phase's database image

DEF-date_fallback.content:
A **date fallback** is a date the user gives a destination — a year, a month of a year, or a day — for when its photos
that carry no recorded time were made.
DEF-date_fallback.title: A date fallback

DEF-decision.content:
A **decision** is a value the user records in one of geotag's records for the tool to act on — a destination's
timezone, an accepted time anchor, a clock offset, a confirmed drift check, a manual position, a folder fallback. The
tool *proposes*; the user *decides*.
DEF-decision.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
DEF-decision.title: A decision

DEF-dependency_cascade.content:
The **dependency cascade** is how the phases keep a record from being used once what it was made from has changed: each
record carries what it depends on — media by their fingerprints, other records by their hashes, and settings by a hash
of the configuration or of the areas the record reads — and each use checks them first. Its full name, the
*dependency-fingerprint/hash cascade*, says that it tracks both kinds of identity.
DEF-dependency_cascade.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-dependency_cascade.title: The dependency cascade

DEF-destination.content:
A **destination** is a folder in photos by destination that holds photos — directly, or only through the folders within
it, as a container destination ({need}`DEF-container_destination`) does; a folder within a destination that holds photos
is a destination of its own.
DEF-destination.title: A destination

DEF-development.content:
**Development** is the later processing of photos into distribution copies — the JPEG and TIFF breakout — kept in
subfolders of a destination.
DEF-development.title: Development

DEF-finalize.content:
**Finalize** is geotag's closing command, given once the user judges the workspace's media done: it assembles the
workspace's permanent record and its complete transformation log.
DEF-finalize.title: Finalize

DEF-fingerprint.content:
A media file's **fingerprint** is the identity of its content apart from its metadata — a photo's decoded pixels, a
video's streams. Unqualified, *fingerprint* means this.
DEF-fingerprint.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-fingerprint.title: A fingerprint

DEF-geotag.content:
**Geotag**, the second phase, resolves each photo to its true time, inferring and correcting each camera's clock
offset; places the photos that carry no position along the recorded tracks; and renames each by its corrected local
time.
DEF-geotag.title: Geotag

DEF-hash.content:
A record's **hash** is a digest of its exact bytes — of a numbered record, or of the configuration. Unqualified, *hash*
means this.
DEF-hash.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-hash.title: A hash

DEF-library.content:
The **library** is the permanent, curated collection the media ends in — outside every workspace, and written only by
merge.
DEF-library.title: The library

DEF-managed_folders.title: The managed folders

DEF-merge.content:
**Merge**, the third phase, runs after a workspace has been geotagged and finalized, and moves its finished photos,
sorted by destination, into the library.
DEF-merge.title: Merge

DEF-operator_loop.content:
The **operator loop** is how the user drives the three phases through one workspace's life: prep organizes a dump; the
user sorts photos into photos by destination; prep records the sort; geotag is re-run, the user deciding what it asks,
until its plan is ready, and executes it; more dumps may follow, each from prep again; finalize closes the workspace's
record; merge moves it into the library. Each phase's own loop is in its own spec; this is the sequence across them.
DEF-operator_loop.title: The operator loop

DEF-plan_memo.content:
The **plan memo** is the scratch database where prep's planning keeps what it read of each media file — its fingerprint
and metadata — with the path, size and modification time it read them at.
DEF-plan_memo.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
DEF-plan_memo.title: The plan memo

DEF-prep.content:
**Prep**, the first phase, takes an unorganized dump and makes it a clean working set: it consolidates the dump,
normalizes extensions, sets duplicates aside (recoverably, never deleting), organizes the media by date, and hands
geotag what it found.
DEF-prep.title: Prep

DEF-recorded_offset.content:
The **offset recorded with** a photo's time is the UTC offset written within the value of the time field that time was
read from, else in the offset field paired with it; a tag holding no offset records none.
DEF-recorded_offset.title: The offset recorded with a time

DEF-recorded_time.content:
A file's **recorded time** is the time of its making that its own metadata holds, as the camera's clock read it:
uncorrected, with no timezone.
DEF-recorded_time.title: A recorded time

DEF-sealed_workspace.content: A workspace is **sealed** once merge has succeeded in it: marked as finished, by a mark only merge writes.
DEF-sealed_workspace.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
DEF-sealed_workspace.title: A sealed workspace

DEF-strays_folder.content:
The **strays folder** is a media-tree folder at the workspace's top level. It holds the files that are not media which
prep moved out of the inbox, one subfolder for each run, their structure kept. It is neither a control record nor any
phase's output.
DEF-strays_folder.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
DEF-strays_folder.title: The strays folder

DEF-timestamp_name.content:
