written for it would put a record of nothing over the last execution's — and with it the acceptances finalize and the
next run read. An interrupted run reached no end to record: its journal holds what it confirmed, and the run that
finishes it writes the summary.
RAT-geotag_summary_records_an_execution.title: Geotag's summary, too, records an execution

RAT-gone_photo_history_kept.content:
A photo that is nowhere in the workspace any more was deleted by the user, or taken out for a while; prep did neither,
and cannot tell them apart. What it did do to the photo stays true, so its entry stays, its last place the one prep
left it at. A step saying it went would be one no record of prep's holds, a guess at why the file is missing; the
absence itself is what a reader of the log and the workspace together can see.
RAT-gone_photo_history_kept.title: Prep records what it did, not what became of a photo

RAT-gone_track_withdrawn.content:
The one reason a user takes a track file out of the tracks folder is that it is not this trip's: a companion's phone
recording the same afternoon elsewhere, which keeps photos from being placed. Taking the file out is the user's answer,
and geotag decides as if it never was; but a file that has merely vanished — a folder renamed, a sync gone wrong — would
change positions as silently, so each one gone is named.
RAT-gone_track_withdrawn.title: A track is taken out because it is someone else's

RAT-gps_time_measures_the_clock.content:
A camera with its own GPS writes, beside the position, the UTC its fix was taken at. Less the camera's own time, that is
the clock offset itself — measured, where the offset the camera records only states what its clock was set to and the
zone's guess assumes it. With no track by the photo's place it is all the photo says of its clock. A track anchor still
comes first: a fix's time can be stale, and a stale fix repeats its time while the camera's moves on — so readings count
only where their GPS times all differ and their offsets agree, and then, two or more, they apply themselves as several
anchors do; one is a single chance of a stale fix, and is offered. A camera writing local time into the GPS field shows
a whole-hour difference: a track catches it where there is one, and so does the check against the destination's other
devices that holds back a guess far from all of them.
RAT-gps_time_measures_the_clock.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RAT-gps_time_measures_the_clock.title: A fix's time is a measurement of the clock, unless the fix is stale

RAT-grouping_computed_once.content:
Two derivations of a camera's identity could disagree: a file grouped one way by prep and another way by geotag would
get another camera's clock offset. And the user classes groups by the key they see, so it must be the same key
everywhere it appears. One derivation, by prep, recorded with the file and reused by geotag, rules out both.
RAT-grouping_computed_once.title: Grouping computed once is never reinvented

RAT-growth_shown.content:
A quarantine that only grows costs space without a word. Reporting its size every run lets the user decide when to
prune, knowing what it holds.
RAT-growth_shown.title: A growing cost is shown

RAT-hand_changes_named.content:
A photo deleted, moved back or given a time by hand is gone or changed by no command, and the record of what was done
would not otherwise say so; a change accepted is one the user chose to keep. The log of the run that finds each names
it, so the account of the workspace stays whole.
RAT-hand_changes_named.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
RAT-hand_changes_named.title: What a person changed is part of the account

RAT-hand_written_fallible.content:
The user writes the configuration and the decisions by hand, so the tool cannot assume they are well formed. A
mistyped timezone or an unsafe path, reported early as a specific problem in a named place, is fixed at its source;
coerced, half applied or let through, it spoils a later operation, and the change it causes can no longer be
explained. Checking keeps every change explainable and the user its author. A field the tool does not read is
let through the same way: a name mistyped, or one from an answer the tool no longer takes, left in the record says
what the tool does not do — so a photo's position decision holding one is refused, the field named.
RAT-hand_written_fallible.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-hand_written_fallible.title: What is typed by hand can be mistyped

RAT-handoff_by_content.content:
Living in the skipped directory is independent of the handoff's role as a dependency: it is invisible to prep's media
scan yet fully verified as a dependency by geotag — verified by content, not by exact bytes, so a run-only refresh of
it does not restale downstream.
RAT-handoff_by_content.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-handoff_by_content.title: The handoff is invisible to the scan, yet verified

RAT-handoff_changes_with_workspace.content:
Geotag's work depends on the handoff and is made stale when it changes. A run that changed nothing must therefore leave
its content as it was; the run's own identity and diagnostics, which differ every time, are kept apart, so that only a
real change — a file filed, sorted or changed — restales geotag.
RAT-handoff_changes_with_workspace.title: The handoff changes when the workspace does

RAT-hash_is_for_change.content: A hash is chosen precisely so it changes on any byte change: detecting change is its whole purpose.
RAT-hash_is_for_change.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-hash_is_for_change.title: Detecting change is a hash's whole purpose

RAT-home_zone_offered.content:
The configured default is the zone the user usually lives in, and a trip is where they went. Applied by itself to a
trip abroad, it would name every photo in home time and turn the times of photos that record no offset by the hours
between the two zones — written into the originals, with no sign anything is off. Offered instead, it costs one answer
per place, at the folder of the country or region it holds for, everything beneath inheriting it; a place at home
takes it in one click.
RAT-home_zone_offered.title: The home zone is right for no trip in particular

RAT-idempotent_reruns.content: **Idempotent, diff-based** re-runs; a run over unchanged state is a no-op.
RAT-idempotent_reruns.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-idempotent_reruns.title: Re-runs must not redo settled work or cause churn

RAT-identical_kept_once.content:
Dumps overlap: the same card copied twice, a phone's backup next to its export. Two copies of one photo would be sorted,
geotagged and merged twice. The fingerprint is over the decoded content, so copies are found whatever their name or
metadata; the media class keeps a RAW and the JPEG from it apart, though they show one picture. The copies beyond the
first go to quarantine, recoverable, and photos by destination is never touched.
RAT-identical_kept_once.title: Identical media is kept once

RAT-identity_survives_edits.content:
A fingerprint is chosen precisely so it stays the same when the pipeline rewrites a photo's metadata or position or
renames the file: a media file's identity must survive those mutations, which is what makes it the identity spine the
transformation log and de-duplication rely on.
RAT-identity_survives_edits.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-identity_survives_edits.title: A file's identity outlives its edits

RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.content:
Never overwriting guards photos, which cannot be made again. An image can: it is a copy of the live database, and only
the latest end of each phase is worth keeping, so a phase's next successful run replaces its image — whole, so that a
capture interrupted leaves a usable image either way.
RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.title: An image is regenerable; a photo is not

RAT-init_taken_place_keeps_both.content:
The inbox can already hold a file at the place a dump file is bound for: an interrupted first run moved part of the
dump, or two of its files differ only by case. Moving over it would lose an original; leaving the file out of the
inbox would leave the top level unclean and the dump half taken in. Its folder is kept, for the folders are what a
dump says of itself, so only its name can change — by the suffix every phase uses, which the file then carries on.
RAT-init_taken_place_keeps_both.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
RAT-init_taken_place_keeps_both.title: A taken place keeps both files

RAT-interrupted_run_left_in_writing.content:
An execution records the state it leaves at its end, a failed one included — but a run killed outright, by a power
loss or a killed process, never reaches its end, and the next run would list its half-finished work as changes by
hand, to be accepted once by a user who made none of them. The run did leave its work in writing: its plan says where
each file goes, and its journal notes what it did and, for geotag, the state each photo was in after its write. A
change that is exactly what an operation of that run leaves is the tool's own work and passes unasked; the owner ruled
it so (*"both recommended"*). Exactly, because the check exists to catch what no command made: a file anywhere else, or
with another entry, is not that run's work however near it comes, and stops as any other change does. What a killed run
did after its last note — a photo written while the journal was not yet — is not in writing, so it is asked.
RAT-interrupted_run_left_in_writing.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
RAT-interrupted_run_left_in_writing.title: A run killed outright left its work in writing

RAT-invalid_decision_shown.content:
Erasing an invalid decision would take away the very thing the user must see to correct it. Kept and marked, it shows
what was written and what is wrong with it.
RAT-invalid_decision_shown.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-invalid_decision_shown.title: The user keeps what they wrote

RAT-jobs_buy_time.content:
Applying a plan in parallel only saves time, and how many jobs suit depends on the machine of the day. If the count
could change which name a photo got, or what a record says, the outcome would turn on how a run happened to be timed —
neither reproducible nor what the user reviewed. So every choice is made before the parallel work starts, each worker
touches only its own files, and the results are gathered in a fixed order.
RAT-jobs_buy_time.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-jobs_buy_time.title: Jobs buy time, not outcomes

RAT-journal_is_evidence.content:
After an interruption, the journal is the only record of what the run did. Rewritten in place, a crash mid-save would
leave it truncated — the evidence lost at the one moment it is needed, and the handoff unable to vouch for it.
RAT-journal_is_evidence.title: The journal is the evidence of an interrupted run

RAT-journal_is_the_account.content:
The journal is the history of a run: what it changed, in what order, and how each change ended. The logs are built from
it and the archival package keeps it, so a change missing from it is a change no record explains — the one thing the
record exists to prevent.
RAT-journal_is_the_account.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-journal_is_the_account.title: The journal is the run's own account

RAT-jpeg_goes_with_its_raw.content:
A JPEG set aside beside its RAW is that RAW's dependent: the same shot, kept only as a copy of it. Culling the RAW is
the user's verdict on the frame. Left behind, the JPEG is a frame the user threw out still in the workspace — and,
renamed by geotag with its RAW, under a name that is neither its own time nor its partner's, stopping the next plan for
a rename nobody wants. Taken into the quarantine it is out of the way and recoverable, purged only by the user's prune
like everything set aside. The RAW is known culled by its content, never its name: one sorted, renamed or copied
elsewhere in the workspace still holds its fingerprint; and only where a comparison saw it deleted by hand, for a
fingerprint taken again another way leaves the same absence with no frame culled. A RAW moved out of the workspace has
left it as surely as one deleted — wherever it is kept, it is no longer a frame of this ingest — and the comparison sees
it so: gone, its inode met by no file inside. The owner: "jpeg should also move to quarantine when the raw was not
deleted but moved outside the workspace (keeping its inode)." The log names the RAW, so the user sees why the JPEG
went; the move is prep's own, recorded as such, so the next run does not ask the user to accept it.
RAT-jpeg_goes_with_its_raw.title: A set-aside JPEG goes with its RAW

RAT-keep_further_along.content:
A copy in photos by destination carries the user's sort, and one already filed has been named and placed; keeping the
copy furthest along saves redoing that and never moves what the user arranged. The folders are taken as they are before
the plan moves anything, so a new dump never displaces a file already filed, and the order by path makes the choice the
same on every run.
RAT-keep_further_along.title: The copy kept is the one further along

RAT-kept_offset_needs_its_evidence.content: The offset is kept because it was read from the camera's own GPS against the tracks, and the photos that gave it can no longer give it again. But the user takes a track out of the folder for one reason — it was someone else's — and an offset read against it goes with it; and a photo arriving later with its own position is new evidence about the same clock. Kept past either, the offset would be the one decision in the record nobody could withdraw and nothing still supported.
RAT-kept_offset_needs_its_evidence.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RAT-kept_offset_needs_its_evidence.title: A kept offset is only as good as what it stood on

RAT-kept_points_are_the_windows.content:
The points are kept because decisions rest on them; a point no decision of the latest planning reaches is evidence of
nothing, and kept it would grow the record by every window a trip's planning ever passed through — a photo sorted
out, a setting tightened. So what lies outside the window the planning reached goes, and is read again from the track
file should a window reach it later. What an executed plan used is the exception: it is evidence of a value written
into an original, and stays, as a withdrawn track's points do. The owner's ruling: *"track points outside window - as
per recommended"*. The planning prunes only once it has stopped, at the window it last reached: mid-run the window
is still to widen, and pruning there would read the same files again on every run.
RAT-kept_points_are_the_windows.title: The record holds what the decisions rest on

RAT-library_across_network.content:
A library is often kept on a server, shared by the machines that read it; refusing one there would refuse the common
case. Its lock then may guard the merges of one machine only, on some network filesystems, and which ones cannot be
told reliably from a run. Running merges from two machines into one library at once is therefore the user's to avoid.
What it would cost is bounded: every placement is a move that fails where its target exists, so a photo the other
merge placed first under the same name is found there and settled by its content — the same photo already present,
another one blocked — and never overwritten. The worst is one photo failing and staying in the workspace — its place
taken by the other merge's photo, or its temporary copy cleared by the other merge as debris — or, where the two saw
the library differently, a photo placed under two names.
RAT-library_across_network.title: A library may lie across a network, and two machines merging at once is the user's to avoid

RAT-library_and_workspace_apart.content:
A library inside the workspace would be merged into itself, the tool walking its own output as input. A workspace
inside the library is no safer: the library's own tools, digiKam among them, watch the library's folders and would take
the workspace's working copies — not yet geotagged, not yet named — for photos of the library, each to appear twice once
merged; and a destination folder named as the workspace would place photos inside it. Kept apart, each is only what it
claims to be.
RAT-library_and_workspace_apart.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-library_and_workspace_apart.title: The library and the workspace lie apart

RAT-library_is_evidence_of_move.content:
The journal is written after a move, so a crash or a Ctrl-C can leave a photo in the library with no entry for it; and
the library is the user's, so a photo a journal entry vouches for may since have been moved or replaced there. Either
way the journal and the library disagree, and only the library says where the photo is. Trusting the journal would
block forever a photo safely placed, or seal a workspace whose merge log names a library file that no longer holds the
photo — a record the user would rely on to find it. Fingerprinting the place again settles it, and costs a read only on
a resume.
RAT-library_is_evidence_of_move.title: The library is the evidence of a move

RAT-library_is_ground_truth.content:
The library is the user's curated collection: its organisation and names are the ground truth, and other tools and
people rely on them. So merge adds to it and changes nothing in it. Where a name is taken, only the content tells a
copy already present from a different photo sharing a name — and where the content cannot be read, nothing does: a
guess either way is a duplicate placed or a photo lost from the workspace, so the photo waits.
RAT-library_is_ground_truth.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_is_ground_truth.title: The library is the user's, and already in order

RAT-library_mark.content:
The library is the user's: it has no structure of the tool's to inspect, so one mark, made once and on purpose, is
all that tells it from any other folder. Checking the mark before anything is written there — the lock included —
keeps the tool from writing into a folder that was never made a library.
RAT-library_mark.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_mark.title: A library has nothing of the tool's to inspect

RAT-library_outside_workspaces.content: A workspace's folders are scanned, moved from and sealed by the phases that run in it. A library that is one, or lies in one, would have its permanent photos taken for a dump by the next prep there.
RAT-library_outside_workspaces.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_outside_workspaces.title: A library inside a workspace would be prepped

RAT-library_reads_cost.content:
Fingerprinting a library file means reading and decoding it whole, and the library may sit across a network. Kept in
the workspace, a fingerprint already taken spares that read on the next run, and stays right while the file is
unchanged. Scanning the whole library to place one batch would cost far more than it saves, so merge trusts the library
to be in order and reads only the places its photos go.
RAT-library_reads_cost.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_reads_cost.title: A library file costs a full read

RAT-library_room_before_moving.content:
Into a library on another filesystem merge copies each photo before removing it from the workspace. A full disk is
safe — the photo it fails stays in the workspace and the run ends partial — but the shortage shows late, one photo at a
time, after part of the batch has moved. Comparing the free space with the batch first turns it into a refusal that
says how much room is needed, before anything moved; the plan says it as a warning, since room can be made before
execute. On the workspace's own filesystem a move is a rename and takes no room, so there is nothing to compare.

The comparison asks for more than the photos' own size: a filesystem filled to its last byte slows and fragments, and
the library is not merge's alone — digiKam writes its thumbnails and sidecars beside the photos. The owner, ruling it
(2026-11-16): *"I think a safety margin is needed. Configurable, too, default say 5% on top of by-dest size?"*
RAT-library_room_before_moving.title: A library short of room is found before the first photo moves

RAT-library_shared.content:
Many workspaces merge into one library, each under its own lock. Only a lock on the library itself keeps two of their
merges from writing it at once.
RAT-library_shared.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_shared.title: One library, many workspaces

RAT-library_snapshot_alone_loses.content:
Merge's changes land in two places: it adds each photo to the library and removes it from the workspace. Rolled back
alone, a snapshot of the library takes the merged photos out of the library while the workspace no longer holds them —
the rollback loses them, a rollback point that destroys what it should protect. A snapshot of the workspace alone is
safe: rolled back, it gives the photos back to the workspace while the library keeps them, a duplicate the next merge
finds already present. So merge snapshots the workspace always, the library beside it where it can, and never the
library alone; with no snapshot of the workspace it takes none at all, and says this merge has no rollback point.
RAT-library_snapshot_alone_loses.title: A snapshot of the library alone would lose what merge moved

RAT-linux_and_open_source_not_roots.content:
This is built and run on Linux, but Linux is not a root — the design is plain Python shelling out to `exiftool`,
ImageMagick, and `ffmpeg`, all cross-platform, so it would port with little structural change. Open-source is likewise
a downstream expression of the "local, owned" ethos (P1, P2), not a structural driver. Neither forces anything below.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-linux_and_open_source_not_roots.title: Linux and open-source are not roots

RAT-live_lock_never_taken.content:
Taking over a lock whose owner is still running would let two runs change the same originals at once — the very thing
the lock exists to stop. Leaving a stale lock alone costs a retry; taking a live one could cost photos. So a doubtful
owner counts as alive — and the lock's record of its owner, which a crash can leave saying anything, is never what
decides it: only the system's own account of who holds the lock is.
RAT-live_lock_never_taken.title: A live lock is never taken

RAT-lock_and_revalidation.content:
This whole-run lock is independent of, and stricter than, the dependency-revalidation discipline: revalidation guards
against *stale* inputs across separate runs, while the lock guarantees runs never overlap in the first place.
RAT-lock_and_revalidation.title: The lock and revalidation guard different things

RAT-log_adds_no_authority.content:
The log is for reading, not deciding: it gathers what prep's own records already say into one account per photo. Made
from them alone, it can be checked against them and never contradicts them; and a set-aside copy appears beside the
photo it copies, so the account of that photo is whole.
RAT-log_adds_no_authority.title: The log adds no authority

RAT-log_read_by_people.content:
The log outlives the tool that wrote it: it is read by a person, years on, perhaps without cartographer at hand. A
stable order lets two logs be compared line by line; names and values as people say them — a time with its timezone, an
offset in hours and minutes — need no program to decode.
RAT-log_read_by_people.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-log_read_by_people.title: The log is read by people, years on

RAT-longevity_is_free.content: *(zero-cost benefit)* Decade-longevity and "open one folder years later" come free — incidental, never the driver.
RAT-longevity_is_free.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-longevity_is_free.title: Built to survive a three-week gap, it survives a thirty-year one

RAT-loop_is_steady_state.content:
The loop is a steady state to return to, not a one-way pipeline: a batch can be imported, sorted, and followed by
another before anything is geotagged. A phase that judged by what ran before would have to forbid that; one that judges
the present state need not.
RAT-loop_is_steady_state.title: A steady state to return to

RAT-manifest_not_traded.content:
A quarantine record found unreadable may still be read by hand, so it is set aside, kept, and a new one begun. Where
it cannot even be set aside, a new one written in its place would be the end of it: the files already quarantined
would lie there with nothing saying why. Stopping keeps the record and the file not yet moved; the user mends the
folder, and the next run quarantines it again.
RAT-manifest_not_traded.title: The record of the set-aside files is not traded for a fresh one

RAT-mark_in_the_file.content:
What geotag did to a photo is marked in the photo itself rather than kept only in the workspace: the mark survives the
workspace, reaches the library, and is read back wherever the photo turns up again, so a photo corrected once is
recognised as corrected whichever workspace it is in.
RAT-mark_in_the_file.title: The file carries the record of what geotag did

RAT-mark_means_whole.content:
The mark says the workspace is whole. Written before the folders, a run that died halfway would leave a workspace marked
whole but missing a folder, and every later run would refuse it as disturbed; written last, a dead run leaves no mark,
and the next simply initializes again.
RAT-mark_means_whole.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
RAT-mark_means_whole.title: The mark means the workspace is whole

RAT-mark_once.content:
A file comes in already marked when the user sends it back from missing metadata: they gave it a time, or meant to. If
it still has none it returns to missing metadata, and the name it had there is the one the user knows it by; marking it
again would grow its name on every round and say nothing new.
RAT-mark_once.title: A file sent back keeps the name it had

RAT-memo_is_observation.content:
A memo entry says only that a file at a path read so; the database says what prep's executions left. So the database
wins where both speak, an entry is held to the database's tests, and an entry proves no move — a plan never executed
says nothing of where any file went. The memo saves reading and nothing else, so with it, without it, or with it
broken, prep plans the same.
RAT-memo_is_observation.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-memo_is_observation.title: The memo is an observation, not a record

RAT-merge_appends.content:
In the library a gap in the numbers is a photo the user deleted; giving its number to a new photo would hand it a name
a backup or an export may still use for the deleted one.
RAT-merge_appends.title: The library is append-only

RAT-merge_loses_no_photo.content:
The workspace's copy is removed last, once the library's is verified, so an interruption never loses a photo: running
merge again finishes the work. A photo merge cannot place stays where it is, so what stays behind is exactly what
still needs attention.
RAT-merge_loses_no_photo.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-merge_loses_no_photo.title: An interrupted or refused merge loses no photo

RAT-merge_needs_its_fingerprints.content:
A place merge finds taken is settled by fingerprinting the file there, and a photo gone from the workspace counts as
merged only once its place is fingerprinted again. Without ImageMagick no fingerprint can be taken: every collision
would block, no photo already moved could be confirmed, and a merge left half done could not be finished. Run so, it
would turn a merge that could be whole into a partial one; stopped, it changes nothing until the tool is back.
RAT-merge_needs_its_fingerprints.title: Without its fingerprints merge can settle nothing

RAT-merge_never_half_done.content:
Finalize is a point in time, and photos by destination can change after it. Merge checks the finalized set against the
present one rather than trusting finalize was last, so a half-geotagged set cannot reach the library.
RAT-merge_never_half_done.title: Never a half-geotagged set in the library

RAT-merge_outcome_decides_next.content:
What the user does after a merge turns on how it ended: nothing after a whole success, a fix and another run after a
partial one or a failed one, and after a refusal a fix with nothing to undo, the library untouched. Counts alone cannot
tell a refusal from a run that found nothing to do; a recorded outcome says which, long after the terminal has gone.
RAT-merge_outcome_decides_next.section_name: 6. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
sections: 6. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
RAT-merge_outcome_decides_next.title: The run's end decides what to do next

RAT-merge_report_at_the_end.content:
Merge is the step that puts photos where the user will look for them, and the one that ends the workspace. Its report
is the moment the user learns whether the batch is in, which photos are not and what to fix — without opening the
summary — and that the workspace is now finished, so the next dump belongs in a fresh one.
RAT-merge_report_at_the_end.section_name: 6. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
sections: 6. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
RAT-merge_report_at_the_end.title: Merge is the step the user watches

RAT-merge_unreadable_record_not_empty.content:
Merge's earlier plans say where its photos went, and its journal what it confirmed. Read as empty, an earlier plan
drops out and a photo it placed blocks for a reason that is not true — that no merge placed it; a journal read as
empty is written over by the run's first confirmation, and what it held is gone. Stopped, merge names the file to
repair or restore, and has lost nothing.
RAT-merge_unreadable_record_not_empty.title: A record that cannot be read is not an empty one

RAT-merged_means_in_this_library.content: The seal says the workspace's photos are in the library it names. A photo placed where the setting used to point is somewhere else, and counting it would seal the workspace over a library that does not hold it.
RAT-merged_means_in_this_library.title: Another library's photos are not in this one

RAT-metadata_failure_stops_everywhere.content:
A failed fingerprint in photos by destination decides nothing there, for prep never sets a file there aside. Its
metadata is another matter: geotag reads no photo, and takes each one's camera, times and position from what prep kept.
A photo of photos by destination handed on with none would reach geotag as one with no time and no camera — renamed,
grouped and placed on what is only a failed read. So prep stops and names it there as anywhere, and the next run reads
it again.
RAT-metadata_failure_stops_everywhere.section_name: 10. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
sections: 10. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
RAT-metadata_failure_stops_everywhere.title: Geotag has nothing else to read a photo's metadata from

RAT-method_in_the_photo.content: Completeness is bought with precision that varies: one photo sits on a track point, the next was projected five minutes past a track's end, a third shares its folder's one coordinate. In the library, years on, only the photo is there to say which — so the method is written into it — and the workspace's record adds what the photo cannot hold: which track, at what instant.
RAT-method_in_the_photo.title: The method travels with the photo

RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.content:
Such intricacy would be brutal to enter by hand, so P3 (ask only what the data can't settle) governs how it is
collected — and introduces the document's central trade.
RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.title: Minimal, cascading asks

RAT-misnamed_not_ignored.content:
Outside the inbox every name is one the pipeline gave. A name that is not means a file was renamed or put there by
hand, and nothing says which time or which photo it holds; passed over in silence, it would reach the library under a
name that looks trusted. Only the inbox takes files as they come.
RAT-misnamed_not_ignored.title: Outside the inbox, every name is the pipeline's

RAT-missing_tracks_are_not_no_tracks.content:
A library with no tracks at all is a supported case: every decision falls to its other sources. A tracks folder that is
named and not there is something else — a volume not mounted — and planning on as if there were none would place by
folder fallback every photo the tracks place precisely, and drop the confirmations given against them. Nothing in the
result would show it. Stopping costs one mount command. A folder of the tracks that cannot be listed is the same at
every step — at execute too, where the plan's tracks are checked again: what it holds cannot be seen, and taking it for
empty would withdraw every track in it. And a folder of tracks that cannot be read is not a trip without tracks — it is
one whose tracks are about to be ignored. A link within the folder leads out of it, to recordings the user did not file
there, and is not followed; its tracks, unread, are named as unread rather than taken silently for none.
RAT-missing_tracks_are_not_no_tracks.title: Missing is not the same as none

RAT-modified_time_is_another_clock.content:
A photo's `ModifyDate` is where its time is read from only when neither `DateTimeOriginal` nor `CreateDate` holds one —
an export whose capture time is gone. It is then the time the photo was last saved, by the editing computer's clock,
not the camera's; but the export keeps the camera's make and model, so it would join the camera's group, open a day of
its own on the edit's date — a question about a day the camera never shot — and have the camera's offset applied to a
computer's clock. Read alone, as a file naming no camera is, it asks nothing and borrows nothing. `CreateDate` is the
camera's clock still: a camera writes it as it writes the original. Treating such a photo as untimed instead would stop
geotag on a time that is, at worst, a poor guess the user can see and correct.
RAT-modified_time_is_another_clock.title: A modification time is another clock's

RAT-move_launders_nothing.content:
A move changes where a file is, not what it is, so what prep knows of it still holds — but only as far as it held before
the move. A row that would have been read again where it was is no better for being carried; carrying it unread would
keep under the new path what the old path would have refreshed. Yet it is still the same file: a new ImageMagick or
exiftool is a reason to check what the row says, never to forget whose it is. Forgotten, the user's sort would read as
a new file, and a fingerprint that changed with it would part the photo from its history.
RAT-move_launders_nothing.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-move_launders_nothing.title: A move launders no stale row

RAT-move_not_copy.content:
A copy left in the workspace of a photo already in the library is a duplicate that invites confusion and wastes space,
so merge moves rather than copies, and removes a copy whose content the library already holds.
RAT-move_not_copy.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-move_not_copy.title: The workspace keeps only what still needs attention

RAT-multi_session_job.content:
This is a **two-level chain**: a fact and a choice together force an intermediate consequence, and that consequence
forces the record machinery. It is the part most easily mistaken for an arbitrary choice.

Neither root does it alone. Scale (F1) without the 100%-coverage goal (P4) is fast: prep is automated, one keeps the
native-GPS frames, lets the track cover the easy matches, and stops — plausibly one sitting, because the long tail is
never chased. The goal without scale is also trivial: placing ten photos completely takes minutes. Only *total
coverage across a large, mixed batch* produces a long tail of per-(camera, destination, day) offset confirmations and
hand-placed remainder that cannot be finished in one sitting.

Note: not all of that elapsed time is P4's. The album **sort** into a destination tree is owed to **P2** — one would
drag photos into folders even with no geotagging at all — so P2 contributes session-spanning human time on its own.
What F1 + P4 *specifically* add is the **long tail of confirmations and manual placement** that has no automated
escape. Either way, the job likely spans multiple sessions.

**Intermediate consequence — a multi-session job.** The machine cannot hold one's decisions in its head between
sittings.
RAT-multi_session_job.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-multi_session_job.title: A multi-session job

RAT-name_in_local_time.content:
A name is read by a person looking for a photo, who remembers the time of day where it was taken. A camera's clock may
be off or still on home time, and UTC is nobody's time of day; the corrected time at the destination is the one that
matches the memory.
RAT-name_in_local_time.title: A name in the time of day where the photo was taken

RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.content:
A photo is renamed up to twice in the workspace — a provisional name, then its final one — and may be renamed again on
its way into the library, so no name identifies it across its journey. Its fingerprint does: it survives every rename,
move and metadata write the pipeline makes.
RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.title: A name cannot key the log

RAT-names_in_capture_order.content:
Within one second, the suffix is all a folder listing has to order a burst by. Given in path order, where `-` sorts
before `.`, `T`, `T-001` and `T-002` become `T'-002`, `T'` and `T'-001`: the burst rotates. The fraction of a second a
camera records is its own order of the frames, and the suffix prep gave is the order prep had them in; either keeps the
burst as it was shot. A RAW and its JPEG, a HEIC and the other file of its shot, are one shot: named apart, one half
lands beside another frame's other half, and the pair shows a shot that never was — as would a new name another photo
holds under another extension.
RAT-names_in_capture_order.title: A burst is read in the order of its names

RAT-names_local_in_repeated_hour.content:
A photo's name is the time its destination's clocks showed — the time of a ticket, a timetable, a diary. In the hour a
zone repeats as its clocks go back, those clocks run back, and names taken from them sort against the true order for
that hour. A name of true time — UTC, or an offset in every name — would mislabel every other hour to fix that one.
The true order is kept where it can be read: in the metadata, each time with its offset beside it.
RAT-names_local_in_repeated_hour.title: A name is the time the place showed

RAT-names_never_collide.content:
Photos taken in the same second — a burst, two cameras — get the same timestamp name, and a name given twice would
overwrite an original. The suffix keeps every one; counting the names already planned as taken stops two files of one
run from claiming the same name, and comparing without case keeps them apart on a filesystem that ignores case.
Allocated deterministically, a re-run gives each file the name it gave before.
RAT-names_never_collide.title: Two files never share a name

RAT-nearest_timezone.content:
The destination a place lies in is the most specific word on its timezone: Kyoto inside Japan is in Japan's zone. The
configured default is the user's usual zone, true of no trip in particular, so it is offered only where the tree says
nothing. And a zone the user sets on a place's folder — a country, a region — should hold for everything beneath it:
one answer for the place, not one per folder.
RAT-nearest_timezone.title: The nearest place says the most

RAT-neighbour_day_offered.content:
A day is a camera's day by its own clock, so a camera left on home time abroad, or a night shoot, has its midnight in
the middle of an outing: the outing becomes two days, and the half with no anchor asks for its offset and then for a
drift confirmation, though the other half settled the clock. The offset the camera's own GPS gave the day before or
after, in the same place, is a far better guess than the zone's — but it is another day's, and a clock may have been
set overnight. So it is offered, never applied. But asking for it twice — an acceptance, then a confirmation on the
tracks of the same offset — is the very cost the proposal was to spare, and the second answer is the better one: it is
asked once, as a timezone's guess is. Where tracks lie by the day's photos, it goes to the check against them as it
stands, and the confirmation there, made with the track before the user's eyes, is its acceptance; where none do,
there is nothing to check it against, and the user accepts it as proposed. Bounding the time between the two days
would need a new setting and guess at a night's length; the user's answer and the check are the bound. The day stays
the unit: its decision is its own, and taking the neighbour's offset joins nothing.
RAT-neighbour_day_offered.title: The day next door is the best evidence a day without its own can have

RAT-nested_place_same_timezone.content:
Destinations nest geographically — a city in a country, a museum in a city — so one inside a destination of known
timezone can scarcely lie in another. Asking the user to confirm it for every folder would be asking what the tree
already says. Where the tree says nothing — no ancestor and no default — there is nothing to propose, and the user must
answer.
RAT-nested_place_same_timezone.title: A nested place is in its parent's timezone

RAT-never_behind_prep.content:
Geotag depends on prep's handoff, and a photo prep has not recorded is not in it. Re-prepping after every sort, even
after geotag has run, keeps the handoff the whole truth about photos by destination.
RAT-never_behind_prep.title: New photos never reach geotag behind prep's back

RAT-new_fingerprint_same_photo.content:
The log follows a photo by its fingerprint. When the method that takes it changes — another ImageMagick — the same
pixels can come out under a new value. Left as it was, the old entry would point at a photo the workspace no longer
names, and the photo would start again with no history, marked partial. The file it was left at, now holding the new
value while the old one is nowhere, says it is the same photo.
RAT-new_fingerprint_same_photo.title: A new fingerprint is not a new photo

RAT-new_version_may_change_nothing.content:
A new ImageMagick usually decodes the same pixels to the same fingerprint, but nothing promises it. Trusted blindly, a
fingerprint from the old version compared with one from the new can call one photo two; discarded blindly, a photo
loses whatever is keyed by its fingerprint. Taking it again settles which: most often the value is the same and nothing
moves; where it is not, the photo is still the one it was, and what was recorded of it must follow, or wait.
RAT-new_version_may_change_nothing.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-new_version_may_change_nothing.title: A new version may change nothing

RAT-no_automatic_deletion.content: Duplicates are **quarantined**, never removed; pruning is an explicit, separate act.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-no_automatic_deletion.title: Deletion is never automatic

RAT-no_borrowed_offsets.content:
Folders nest by geography, which is why a timezone or a fallback position can pass down them; a clock's error does not
follow geography. A museum visited inside a city trip may be another day, the camera reset in between; a parent
folder's offset averaged from its children would be right for none of them. An offset borrowed would look measured
while it is not — so each is proposed from the camera's own positions that day, or from the timezone, and labelled as
such.
RAT-no_borrowed_offsets.title: One place's clock evidence says nothing of another's

RAT-no_chain_of_vouching.content:
The decision records are files the user edits between runs, in the editor or by hand. If the plan named only the last
of them and trusted it to name the rest, a change upstream of it — a track added, an earlier record edited after the
later one was written — would pass unseen whenever the later record happened not to be rewritten. Carried in the plan
itself, every input is checked against what it is now, at the one moment that matters: just before anything changes.
RAT-no_chain_of_vouching.title: A chain is only as fresh as its weakest link

RAT-no_hidden_litter.content: Hidden dotfiles are swept to the recoverable quarantine, not merely skipped, so a dump leaves no hidden litter.
RAT-no_hidden_litter.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-no_hidden_litter.title: A dump leaves no hidden litter

RAT-no_identity_no_change.content: A photo's own values are kept under its fingerprint before geotag first writes to it, and every later step finds the photo by it. One prep could not fingerprint cannot have its values kept, cannot be recognised after a write, and cannot be looked for in the library: writing to it or merging it is a change nothing can check or undo.
RAT-no_identity_no_change.title: No identity, no change

RAT-no_identity_no_group.content:
Screenshots, scans and photos a messaging app stripped name no camera, and share nothing but that. Taken for one camera,
they would be asked to be classed as one and, classed a camera, given one clock offset per destination and day — an
offset no camera of theirs had. Each carries what time it has; read alone, by its own offset, it asks nothing and
borrows nothing — and where it records none, the place's zone is a guess, asked once for the place.
RAT-no_identity_no_group.title: No camera, no clock to correct

RAT-no_migration.content:
A workspace lives from one dump to its merge, and the database is rebuilt from the files by any fresh workspace. A
migration would be code kept for databases that do not exist, run on the one record that cannot be checked against
anything else; a database of another schema read as this one would be read wrong. Stopping says so, and a fresh
workspace is the remedy.
RAT-no_migration.title: No old workspace to migrate

RAT-no_mutation_outside_plan.content: **plan → validate → execute**; the dry-run *is* the serialized plan; stale plans are rejected against current state.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-no_mutation_outside_plan.title: No mutation outside a validated plan

RAT-no_phase_invents_time.content:
A photo with no recorded time has nothing to correct and nothing to look up: its true time is unknown, and no
camera's offset or destination's timezone can supply one. Prep sets such a photo aside in missing metadata for the
user to deal with by hand. Sorted into a destination anyway, it would pass through geotag's decisions with nothing to
ask about it and stop only at the last plan, where nothing the user could decide would clear it. Stopping before any
time is resolved, naming it and the two ways out, makes the fix plain.

Letting such a photo through untimed, placed by hand or by its folder's fallback and left unrenamed, and giving it a
time by a decision for that photo alone, were weighed and set aside: the stop was ruled kept (2026-11-16). The one time
the user can give it is a date for its folder ({need}`RAT-date_fallback_for_scans`) — the user's word, never the
tool's guess; a photo no such date covers stops as before. The stop comes once the time decisions are written, not
before, so that the date can be asked there, in the editor or by hand, like any other question of time.
RAT-no_phase_invents_time.title: No phase invents a time

RAT-no_photo_unlocated.content:
The tool is for a map-complete library, and every photo has some place a person can name: where it was taken, or at
least the place its folder stands for. The owner: *"I explicitly want* no *unlocated photos. this is the role of the
folder fallback."* — and: *"This means that geolocation phase should not be able to close while photos that cannot be
geoplaced are in by-dest."* So a photo nothing places waits for that answer, and the folder's fallback is the one
answer that serves a whole folder of such photos at once. Waiting is not enough on its own: what reaches the library
is the photos as they are, and a photo can hold no position however its plan was decided — a write that never landed,
a device's latitude 0 and longitude 0 read again. So finalize, which signs for the photos, and merge, which takes them
into the library, look at what each photo holds, not at what was decided for it.
RAT-no_photo_unlocated.title: No photo leaves geotag without a position

RAT-no_redo_to_be_safe.content:
Settled work done again "to be safe" makes nothing safer: a file written with what it already holds gains nothing and
risks a failed write, and reading a library's content again can cost hours.
RAT-no_redo_to_be_safe.title: Redoing settled work buys no safety

RAT-non_destructive_core.content: plan / validate / execute; atomic no-clobber; quarantine, not delete; original-values ledger.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-non_destructive_core.title: Non-destructive core

RAT-null_island_no_fix.content:
A device that has no fix and writes a position anyway writes latitude 0 and longitude 0: a point in the Gulf of Guinea
no photo of a trip is taken at. Kept as the photo's own, it would never be placed, be counted as placed, and be matched
against the tracks as evidence of the camera's clock. It was measured nowhere, so it is no measurement to keep: the
photo is placed as one without a position, and asking about each would ask what the data settles. Only the exact
point counts — a position merely near it, or far from the others, may be real. The value the device wrote is replaced,
so the log keeps it, and the photo's history still shows what it carried.
RAT-null_island_no_fix.title: Latitude 0, longitude 0 is a device without a fix

RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.content:
Start with the fact. Because each camera's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes from day to day
(F2), there is no single offset to discover — the correct answer is **per (camera group, destination, day)**. *That*
granularity is the entire source of the decisions' "complexity": it is a consequence of real, time-varying drift, not a
premise.

A camera's clock drifts, and is set again — to local time, on a trip, often each morning. Destinations are where the
user went, not when: one offset per camera, or per destination over several days, would be wrong for every day but one.
A day in one place is the unit within which the error stays put, so it is the unit decided.

The offset is **inferred and applied per (camera group, destination, day)**; corrections fall *between* destinations
and between days, never within one destination's day — which is why **one destination = one coherent shoot**.
RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.title: Drift is per-camera and per-day, so no global offset is correct

RAT-one_editing_session.content:
Two editors open on one workspace would each show the decisions as they loaded them, and the first to save would make
the other's next save one over records it never showed — refused, with whatever the user had answered there since. One
editor at a time keeps the answers in one place. An editor cannot tell when its user is done: a page left open is still
the session, and a browser closed tells it nothing. Giving the workspace up between requests would let a second editor
in between two saves of the first, so it is kept until the editor itself is stopped.
RAT-one_editing_session.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-one_editing_session.title: One editing session answers the decisions

RAT-one_extension_spelling.content:
Cameras write `.JPG` and `.ARW`; tools and the library match names exactly on many filesystems. One spelling across the
workspace means a name is the same name in every folder and every phase, and two files differing only in an
extension's case are seen as the one name they are.
RAT-one_extension_spelling.title: One spelling of each extension

RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.content:
The mechanism is named for ZFS because that is the reference implementation, but it is deliberately the *only* part
of the pipeline that touches a feature of one particular filesystem, and it is optional; everything else asks only
what POSIX filesystems share, which is not nothing — locks, atomic renames, refusing moves and syncing are what the
safety of every change rests on.
RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.title: Why the snapshot alone may touch the filesystem

RAT-one_format_no_drift.content:
With one format key for the whole pipeline, the provisional names prep assigns and the final names geotag assigns are
guaranteed to share the same textual shape and can never drift apart; there is no format divergence to reconcile.
RAT-one_format_no_drift.title: One key, so the names cannot drift apart

RAT-one_number_one_question.content:
A timezone's offset, like the one a camera's photos record, is a guess that needs the user's word before it is written. Where tracks lie by the photos the
user gives that word at the check against the tracks, looking at where the offset puts a photo; asking them to accept
the same number first, in another file and another run, adds a question and no safety — the check is the stronger
act and names the offset itself. Where no track covers the photos there is no check, and acceptance is the word.
RAT-one_number_one_question.title: One number, one question

RAT-one_place_for_settings.content:
Settings read from more than one place — a phase's own file, an environment variable, the program's defaults — can
disagree, and a run's result would then depend on where it ran, not on the workspace. With one configuration in the
workspace, everything that governed a run is in one file, hashed, checked and archived with what it governed.
RAT-one_place_for_settings.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-one_place_for_settings.title: One place for every setting

RAT-one_place_per_plan.content:
A plan kept in one known place is the plan that runs: the dry run and the execution read exactly what the last planning
wrote, and the user always knows where to review it. An option naming another place would let a run carry out a plan
other than the last one made — an old copy, or another workspace's — and would ask the user to remember where they put
it, in a tool used a few times a year.
RAT-one_place_per_plan.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-one_place_per_plan.title: A plan in one known place is the plan that runs

RAT-one_read_serves_both.content:
Prep opens every file anyway, to fingerprint and file it; geotag needs the same files' times, cameras and positions.
Kept by prep, they are read once, and geotag reads no photo. Prep keeps them as recorded and decides nothing from them
({need}`RAT-prep_has_no_evidence`).
RAT-one_read_serves_both.section_name: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
RAT-one_read_serves_both.title: One read serves both phases

RAT-one_skipped_place.content:
Skipping the control directory wholesale means a control or artifact file can never be mistaken for a photo. There is
no per-file "ignore list" to maintain: whatever the control directory holds, now or later, is skipped with it.
RAT-one_skipped_place.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-one_skipped_place.title: One skipped place instead of a list of names

RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.content: Each phase that mutates uses the same mechanism so the phases behave identically and cannot diverge.
RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One mechanism, so the phases cannot diverge

RAT-one_source_per_fact.content:
The facts the dependencies are built from — the configuration, the control records, the camera-group derivation's
version, the filename format, the tracks, the snapshot mechanism — are each defined once, for every phase, so that a
single change has one authoritative source and a predictable staleness footprint everywhere.
RAT-one_source_per_fact.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-one_source_per_fact.title: One source for each shared fact

RAT-one_version_per_comparison.content:
Merge compares prep's fingerprint of a photo with one it takes now of the library file in its way. Taken by two
versions of ImageMagick, two fingerprints of the same pixels may differ: the photo would be called new and placed again,
renamed, beside itself — a duplicate in the library, which merge must never make. Taken again under the version now in
use, prep's fingerprint is confirmed and the comparison holds. A photo whose fingerprint did change is compared by its
new value, which is the one the library's files are fingerprinted under ({need}`RAT-changed_fingerprint_mapped`).
RAT-one_version_per_comparison.title: One version on both sides of a comparison

RAT-one_zone_can_be_checked.content:
A destination's photos are written and named in its timezone, so it can have only one. That is all the tree is asked
to be: a folder holding no photo may lie above destinations of any zones — a year, a country of several — because it
has no time of its own to get wrong; what it is given passes down only as far as the photos below agree. Whether a
folder is a place or a trip the tool cannot read off its name, and need not: the harm of a tree that is not one of
places is a zone applied where it is false, and that shows in the photos. So a zone, written or inherited, is set
against what the destination's own photos record; where they record another offset the user moves them, picks their
zone, or keeps it by a word that names the offsets it was given for — a phone left on another zone is real, and rare
enough to be said.
RAT-one_zone_can_be_checked.title: One timezone, because that is what can be checked

RAT-only_corrected_time_marked.content:
An original is touched only where it needs to be. A photo already holding its true time — a phone keeping the
network's local time, beside its own position — needs nothing from geotag; marking it would write to it for nothing,
and the mark would tell digiKam, and every reader after it, that a time was fixed which geotag never touched. So the
mark goes only on a photo whose time geotag writes, or wrote on an earlier run. Left unmarked, the other is decided
from its own values again on every re-run, and comes to the same: nothing to write.
RAT-only_corrected_time_marked.title: Only a time geotag wrote is marked as corrected

RAT-only_sorted_is_ready.content:
A photo's destination is what geotag corrects it by: the timezone of the place, the offset of that camera on that
day, the fallback position of the folder. A photo not yet sorted has none of these, and a file in the other folders is
not a photo to place — a stray, one missing metadata, a JPEG set aside beside its RAW. Videos stay where prep put them:
the pipeline does not place them, and a tag written into one would be a guess. Sorting a photo into a destination is
the user's statement that it is ready.
RAT-only_sorted_is_ready.title: Only what the user sorted is ready

RAT-only_what_geotag_treats.content:
Geotag corrects only photos: it reads and writes photo metadata and places photos on the map. A video or any other file
in photos by destination would reach the library beside photos geotag treated, itself untreated; refusing keeps the
destination's set one geotag has wholly treated.
RAT-only_what_geotag_treats.title: Only what geotag treats goes to the library

RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.content:
Geotag's and merge's plans locate the destination tree by name and classify the tree, and renaming a managed folder or
moving an extension between media and `other` changes which files exist where. Prep re-plans from the filesystem each
run and guards execution with the whole-file hash, so it needs no separate folder or extension fingerprint of its own.
RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.title: Folder names and media classes decide which files exist where

RAT-other_outside_inbox_is_the_users.content:
Prep sets files of no media class aside only from the inbox, where a dump arrives mixed. Outside it, such a file got
there another way: an extension the user has since taken off the lists, which turns organized photos into files of no
class, or a file the user put there by hand. Moving it would guess which; leaving it unsaid would keep among the media a
file nothing accounts for. Stopping names it, and the user decides — as for a misnamed file.
RAT-other_outside_inbox_is_the_users.section_name: 5. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 5. What prep refuses to work on
RAT-other_outside_inbox_is_the_users.title: A non-media file outside the inbox got there another way

RAT-outranked_distance_measured.content:
Where the better track wins, the other is not wrong evidence to discard but a second reading of the same walk: how far it
puts each photo is the measure of its error, which says how far it can be trusted where it alone recorded. Asking about
it would cost a question for something the ranking has settled; recording and counting it costs nothing.
RAT-outranked_distance_measured.title: The worse device's distance is a measure

RAT-own_position_best.content:
A position the camera wrote was measured where the photo was taken. Everything geotag can offer instead is derived —
from a track and a corrected time, from a folder — and so weaker evidence: replacing the measurement with it would make
the photo less right, not more.
RAT-own_position_best.title: The camera measured where it was

RAT-package_answers_later.content:
The workspace is transient; the package is what remains of it beside the library. It must answer later what the
workspace could: under which settings, by which decisions, from which plans each photo was changed, and what each phase
saw. Anything left out — a journal, a snapshot — is a question no one can answer once the workspace is gone.
RAT-package_answers_later.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-package_answers_later.title: The package answers what the workspace could

RAT-package_checks_itself.content:
A package moved to long-term storage is parted from the workspace that made it and may sit untouched for years. Naming
its workspace, plan and execution ties it to what it records; listing every item with its hash lets anyone confirm,
without the tool, that nothing in it has decayed or been altered.
RAT-package_checks_itself.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-package_checks_itself.title: The package can be checked without the tool

RAT-package_records_what_was_done.content:
The archival package is what outlives the workspace: the account of what geotag did to each photo and why. Made
from an execution that did not finish, it would record changes the photos lack; made after a decision was edited
and not executed, it would record a decision they never received. Either way the record would lie about the
library.
RAT-package_records_what_was_done.title: The package records what was done

RAT-pair_keeps_one_name.content:
A JPEG set aside beside its RAW is the same shot, named like it so that the two names show it. Once geotag corrects the
RAW's name, a JPEG left under the camera's time names another moment — eight hours away, for a camera left on home
time — and the pair no longer shows. Prep knows the pair when it sets the JPEG aside, so it records it, and the rename
rests on that record, never on a likeness of names, which a suffix given to one and not the other already breaks. A
rename is all: the JPEG is a copy nobody uses, no time or position is decided for it, and a tag written into it would be
a guess. Renamed so, its name is its RAW's and no longer its own recorded time, and prep takes it as given. A run that
renames the RAW and not its JPEG — the JPEG changed on disk, or its rename not reached — leaves the pair apart, and no
later run renames that RAW again; so the JPEG catches up with the name the RAW holds, or it stays apart for good.
RAT-pair_keeps_one_name.title: A pair keeps one name

RAT-partial_merge_no_dead_end.content:
A partial merge leaves the cause of its blockers for the user to fix — a library file that could not be read, a photo
changed — and some fixes change what the plan must say. Until the seal, nothing merge has done is final, and its
records describe what happened rather than gate what may happen next; refusing to re-plan would leave the user with a
plan that can no longer finish and no way to make one that can.
RAT-partial_merge_no_dead_end.title: A partial merge is never a dead end

RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.content:
The structural facts are shared by every phase because each relies on them when it scans, and a violation of any one
means the workspace was disturbed out-of-band. The guards compose with — but are distinct from — input validation, which
checks *authored values*, and the dependency cascade, which checks *change*: these check the *shape of the workspace
itself*.
RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.title: Every phase relies on the shape when it scans

RAT-phone_error_is_a_zone.content:
A phone takes its time from the network and was trusted with nothing checking it: a phone set to the wrong zone, a
photo whose tag is missing while the phone sat in another zone, a phone set by hand to the wrong hour, would each pass
unseen and misplace every such photo on the track. Where its photos hold their own position, the tracks — or the
fixes' own times — say what its clock was, exactly as they do for a camera, and by the same settings: no new setting,
for a phone's error is a whole zone, not drift (ruled as recommended, *"otherwise all as recommended"*). Agreeing with how the phone's photos are read,
there is nothing to ask. Several of them agreeing among themselves against it is the evidence a camera's several
anchors are, and applies itself for that phone and day, the cell showing it; one photo could be a coincidence, and is
offered. The user, who knows the track was someone else's, can keep the phone as it records itself (ruled *"all ok"*),
without typing an offset that a drift check would then ask about again.
RAT-phone_error_is_a_zone.title: A phone's error is a whole zone, and its own GPS shows it

RAT-phone_records_its_offset.content:
A phone's clock is set by its network and it records the offset it was at, beside each time it writes: better evidence
than any zone geotag could assume. But a photo holds several times, each with its offset — when it was taken, digitized,
modified — and an offset describes only the time it was written with; another would be right only by chance. Where the
photo records none for its time, the destination's zone is the best guess left. An offset written within the time's own
value is part of that value; one in a field beside it is paired by convention, and a tool may have written the two apart
— so the one within comes first.
RAT-phone_records_its_offset.title: A phone says its own offset

RAT-photo_answer_most_specific.content:
A position the user gives one photo is the most specific word there is on where it was, so it outranks a track and a
fallback — also for a photo they already place, where the user knows better: a track recorded on the way back, a
fallback that stands for the folder and not for this frame. Given, it is their decision, and a track or a fallback
coming later does not take it back; only the user does, by emptying it. An answer that names no photo it could place —
one not in that folder, or one keeping a position of its own — would be passed over in silence, so it stops the run.
RAT-photo_answer_most_specific.title: An answer given for one photo outranks the tracks and the fallback, and stays

RAT-photos_outrank_inheritance.content:
A place inside another is nearly always in its timezone; that is an assumption about folders. A phone's photo that
records +02:00 where the inherited zone was at +01:00 is evidence, in the photo, that the assumption fails here — a
country spanning zones, a border crossed, a folder that groups a trip instead of a place. Adopted unasked, the wrong
zone names and times every photo there an hour out, and proposes a camera's clock from the wrong hour. One photo is
enough to ask: a phone does not record another zone's offset by accident, and the answer costs one choice. A camera's
offset tag is not such evidence — it says what the clock was set to, and a camera left on home time would stop every
destination abroad.
RAT-photos_outrank_inheritance.title: What the photos record outranks what the folder assumes

RAT-photos_wait_by_date.content:
The user sorts photos into destinations from photos by date; ordered by their recorded time, the photos of one trip and
one day sit together, ready to be moved as a block. The timestamp name keeps that order however a folder is listed.
RAT-photos_wait_by_date.title: Photos wait by date for the user's sort

RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.content:
Timezone, clock offset, and GPS fallback are **piggybacked on the destination sort** one would do anyway for real albums
(P2).
RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.title: The unavoidable human act should pay for itself

RAT-placed_bytes_outlive_engine.content:
A merge left partial may be finished months later, and ImageMagick may be upgraded in between — the very case merge
takes prep's fingerprints again for. A photo already placed is then fingerprinted under the new version and compared
with the value the earlier plan recorded under the old; where the upgrade changed it, the photo would block as gone from
its place, a reason that is not true, and the workspace could never seal while that version is in use. Merge placed the
file itself, so it can know it by what no version reads differently: the digest of its bytes, taken as it lands. A
place still holding those bytes holds the photo. Where no digest was recorded — a move that finished without its
journal entry — or the library's copy has since been rewritten, the fingerprint is the evidence left, as before.
RAT-placed_bytes_outlive_engine.title: A placed file is known by its bytes, which no ImageMagick reads differently

RAT-placement_most_specific_first.content:
Each source speaks for fewer photos than the one after it: a position the user set speaks for that photo alone, a track
for the instant it was taken, a fallback for a whole folder. The first that applies is the most specific word on where
the photo was; a photo none of them places is one only the user can answer for — with a place for it, or one for its
folder.
RAT-placement_most_specific_first.title: Most specific first

RAT-plain_json_record.content: **Plain JSON** decision artifacts — the durable external record, read back at the start of each session.
RAT-plain_json_record.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-plain_json_record.title: Decisions can't live in the tool between sessions, so they must persist outside it

RAT-plan_before_run.content:
Execution carries out only a plan the user could review first. With none saved, there is nothing reviewed to carry out,
and planning on the spot would skip the review the plan exists for.
RAT-plan_before_run.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-plan_before_run.title: Nothing runs that the user could not review

RAT-plan_can_be_overtaken.content:
A plan is made from the filesystem at one moment, and the workspace or the library can change before it runs. The
plan's own collision check is the first defence; checking each name as it is written is a second, independent one,
which no plan, however careful, can stand in for.
RAT-plan_can_be_overtaken.title: A plan describes the workspace as it was

RAT-plan_is_its_codes.content:
A saved plan is the decisions of the code that made it: names, copies, places, a time and a position for each photo,
a target in the library. Carried out by another build, it would apply decisions the running code would not make — a
fault the upgrade fixed among them, and at merge into the library, the one place nothing is re-planned from. A version
number cannot tell builds apart while every local build carries the same one; the code's own fingerprint can. Planning
again is cheap: prep's memo keeps what it read, merge's cache the library's fingerprints, and geotag plans again from
its decision records.
RAT-plan_is_its_codes.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-plan_is_its_codes.title: A plan is the decisions of its code

RAT-plan_keeps_its_reading.content:
Decoding photos is most of a plan's cost — hours on a large library — and the user often plans again before executing:
a configuration edited, a folder corrected, a run interrupted. The database speaks only of the executed workspace, so
a plan's reading is kept apart from it, in scratch; kept only for what the latest plan saw, it stays the size of the
workspace.
RAT-plan_keeps_its_reading.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-plan_keeps_its_reading.title: A plan never executed loses nothing it read

RAT-plan_made_again.content:
The executable plan holds nothing of its own: geotag makes it from the decision records, the photos and the tracks, all
still there, so planning again makes it whole and nothing is lost — unlike a journal or a summary, which hold what only
a run saw. Read in part, a plan would be carried out in part, or summarised and merged on as if whole; stopped on, it
points the user to the one command that makes it anew. Planning again sets the torn plan aside, as it sets aside every
plan it replaces, and finalize reads the plans set aside for the passes they ran; a torn one there would stop it again,
a second step for a file that recorded nothing. A plan no execution ran is no record of an execution: when every summary
names the plan it ran by its content and every journal belongs to a plan that can be read — so not even a run cut off
before its summary can have been the torn one's — finalize passes it over, and it stays kept and archived. So a plan
made again for one torn before it ran ends in a finalize that needs no hand on the torn copy. Where an execution may
have run it, the torn copy is still a record finalize cannot read, and it stops.
RAT-plan_made_again.title: A plan is made again, not repaired

RAT-plan_on_current_record.content:
Geotag decides from what prep read in each photo — its time above all — and never reads the photo again. A photo
removed since would be planned for nothing; one changed since, its time set in another program say, would have that
change overwritten by a time worked out from values it no longer holds — and execution, which must accept a change to
a photo's metadata alone to resume its own writes, cannot tell the two apart. Its size and modification time, against
prep's record, show it without reading it.
RAT-plan_on_current_record.title: A plan on a reading the file no longer holds
