RAT-plan_read_before_anything_moves.content:
A plan is there to be read before anything happens — by the user, and by the dry run that checks it. Planning that
changed a file would leave the workspace neither as it was nor as the plan intends, before anyone agreed to either; and
planning again, which the user may do as often as they like, would change it again. So planning only reads, and writes
only what reading produced: the plan, the decisions it asks for, and what spares the next run reading it all again —
and once, the configuration the plan itself is made under.
RAT-plan_read_before_anything_moves.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-plan_read_before_anything_moves.title: A plan is read before anything moves

RAT-plan_saw_the_workspace.content:
A file that arrived after planning is one the plan never considered: a copy of something it files, or a name it gives
another. Carrying out the plan would leave the file unfiled, or file around it; planning again takes it in, reusing all
that is already known.
RAT-plan_saw_the_workspace.title: The plan is of the workspace it saw

RAT-planning_inside_lock.content:
Planning changes nothing but the fingerprints it keeps for later runs, but it must still not run concurrently: a plan
computed against a workspace another process is reading or changing is untrustworthy, so planning is inside the lock too.
RAT-planning_inside_lock.title: A plan made beside another run cannot be trusted

RAT-position_answered_for_its_destinatio.content:
A position typed for a photo is given looking at the photo where it lies: the place its folder names, the fallback
that folder has or lacks, the tracks that covered it there. Any of these may have been part of the answer — the owner:
*"it may have been decided partially because of the destination"*. Moved, the photo stands among another folder's
answers — a fallback that would place it now, a place it was not — and the old one, carried, could keep it pinned
where the folder says it was not. Asked again, it costs one answer.
RAT-position_answered_for_its_destinatio.title: A photo's position was answered where it lay

RAT-position_follows_time.content:
A photo with no position of its own is placed where the track was at the moment it was taken — its true time, after
the camera's clock is corrected. Placed before that time is settled, it would be placed at the wrong moment of the
track, possibly kilometres off, and every position would have to be planned again once the time changed. So the time
is settled for every photo first, and only then is any position planned.
RAT-position_follows_time.title: A position is looked up by time

RAT-position_whole.content:
EXIF stores a latitude and a longitude without their signs: the hemisphere is in a field of its own. A coordinate
written without it is read as no location at all, or put north and east of where it was — a photo from Sydney placed
in the Pacific off Japan. Left behind when the coordinate is cleared, the reference is half a position that some
reader will complete. Whole or not at all is the only safe write.
RAT-position_whole.title: Half a position is a wrong one

RAT-power_loss_is_an_interruption.content:
A rename can reach the disk before the bytes it names; after a power cut the file is then there and empty. A photo
lost that way is lost as surely as one overwritten, so the new file is made safe on disk before it takes the old
one's place, whatever that costs in speed: the archive outlives every run by decades.
RAT-power_loss_is_an_interruption.title: A power cut is an interruption like any other

RAT-prep_cannot_know_the_time.content:
Prep runs before anyone knows a photo's true time: the camera's clock offset comes from geotag, by matching against the
tracks or from the user, and the timezone from the destination the user sorts the photo into. All prep has is the time
the camera recorded — enough to put a day's photos in order, not enough for a name to keep.
RAT-prep_cannot_know_the_time.title: Prep cannot know a photo's true time

RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.content:
The destination tree is read-only for prep yet still scanned by it, so prep is also the gatekeeper for links that
appear there; and the mandatory re-prep after any change to it means geotag and merge only ever consume a handoff prep
built with no forbidden link present.
RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.title: Prep is the gatekeeper for links under the destination tree

RAT-prep_has_no_evidence.content:
A photo's true time and place need what prep does not have: the camera's clock offset, found by geotag against the
tracks or given by the user, and the timezone of the destination the user sorts the photo into. A correction made
before them would be a guess written into an original; prep leaves time and place whole for geotag.
RAT-prep_has_no_evidence.section_name: 1. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
sections: 1. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
RAT-prep_has_no_evidence.title: Prep has no evidence for a time or a place

RAT-prep_needs_no_answers.content:
Prep's work — sorting by type and date, setting duplicates aside, recording what is where — follows from the files and
the configuration with nothing left to judge. The questions only the user can answer are about time and place, which are
geotag's; a prep that asked would hold up the inbox on questions it does not need answered.
RAT-prep_needs_no_answers.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-prep_needs_no_answers.title: Prep has nothing to ask

RAT-projection_bounded.content: Squeezing the track means using it wherever it says something: at a point, between two, and a little past where a recording stops — each track's own stop, since a logger switched off at the car is an end whatever was recorded the month after. Past an end there is only a heading, and a heading read off the last two points is mostly receiver jitter: twenty metres in one second, carried five minutes, is six kilometres. So the heading is read over the track's last stretch, and a projection that still lands farther or faster than the configuration lets one go is dropped for the end itself — rough, marked as such, and wrong by no more than the user allowed.
RAT-projection_bounded.title: A projection is the roughest reading, so it is the most bounded

RAT-prune_age_is_real.content: Pruning is the only place cartographer deletes for good. An age of zero or less selects every run's quarantine, which is what `--all` exists to say out loud.
RAT-prune_age_is_real.title: The one command that deletes asks for a real age

RAT-prune_harms_nothing.content:
The quarantine holds only spare copies of duplicates, which a sealed workspace still keeps. Deleting them, with the
manifests that list them, touches no photo, library file, earlier control record or row of the database, adding
only its own record of what it removed; what each manifest said is kept in that record, and in the transformation log
and the package. It neither reprocesses the workspace nor adds a batch to it,
so the seal's reasons do not reach it, and the space can be reclaimed.
RAT-prune_harms_nothing.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-prune_harms_nothing.title: Pruning the quarantine changes nothing controlled

RAT-quarantine_manifest_beside_duplicate.content:
A quarantine manifest says why each file beside it was set aside. Kept in the quarantine folder it describes, it cannot
be parted from those files: whoever looks at a duplicate finds its reason next to it, and pruning a folder removes the
files and their manifest together, leaving no record of files that are gone. What each manifest said is kept in the
transformation log, so pruning loses nothing of the record.
RAT-quarantine_manifest_beside_duplicate.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-quarantine_manifest_beside_duplicate.title: A duplicate and its explanation are not separated

RAT-quarantine_outside_record.content:
A quarantined file is a copy set aside, not part of the workspace the later phases work on; its manifest records why it
was set aside. Kept in the database, it would be listed in the handoff among the photos, and reclaiming quarantine space
— which touches nothing of the record — would change the handoff at the next run and make geotag's work stale.
RAT-quarantine_outside_record.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-quarantine_outside_record.title: Quarantine is outside the record

RAT-raw_is_master.content:
A camera shooting RAW and JPEG together writes one name with two extensions in one folder. The RAW holds everything the
JPEG does and more, so the JPEG is redundant — kept, not deleted, but set apart from what the user sorts. Only that
evidence is trusted: a name shared within a folder, as the camera wrote it. Another image under the same name is not
the camera's JPEG, and a JPEG and a RAW in different folders, or matched only by time, may be two shots.
RAT-raw_is_master.title: The RAW is the master

RAT-reading_change_detectable.content:
Metadata kept is reused for every unchanged file, so what it depends on must be recorded with it: the file as it was,
and the way it was read. A new extractor, another field set or other options make each record detectably stale, without
being taken for a change in the file — and the record is read again whole ({need}`RAT-reread_on_purpose`).
RAT-reading_change_detectable.section_name: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 11. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
RAT-reading_change_detectable.title: A change in reading is told apart from a change in the file

RAT-reason_first.content:
The quarantine is never scanned, so a file moved there with no record of why would be invisible to every later run, its
reason lost. Written first, the record survives a crash before the move; the file is still at its source, and the next
run sets it aside again under a new record — the old one at worst a record of a move that did not happen.
RAT-reason_first.title: The reason is written down first

RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.content:
Since prep creates the structure once and never removes a folder, a missing one is evidence the structure was deleted
or moved out-of-band — not a state any phase produces. Silently rebuilding it could mask a real loss: a deleted folder
may have taken organized media with it. Recovering lost media — from an optional pre-mutation snapshot, say — is the
operator's task.
RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.title: A rebuilt structure could mask a loss

RAT-record_covers_broken_runs.content: The journal is what later says which run changed which photo. A run that falls over on one photo while others are in flight, or is killed between a write and its record, leaves photos changed and unrecorded; a next run that merely finds them done and moves on leaves them so for good, and the log built from the journals then shows a photo holding a position no pass ever gave it. So one photo's failure stays its own, and what is found done is checked and written down. The image engine is checked first for the same reason: with another one every write would be made and then held as changed, a whole plan of photos half applied.
RAT-record_covers_broken_runs.title: The record must cover what a broken run did

RAT-record_means_stage_reached.content:
The decision records are what the user, the editor and the next stage read. Written at every stage reached — even when
it holds nothing to decide — a record's presence says the stage ran and its status says what is left; its absence can
only mean the stage was not reached. Were an all-automatic stage to write nothing, an absent record would mean either
"nothing to decide" or "never got here", and a record written by a run that stopped at a gate would look like a decision
to act on when there was none. With no record written, the run's output is the one place left to say what stopped it.
RAT-record_means_stage_reached.title: A missing record should mean one thing

RAT-record_never_absent.content: The decision records are read back at the start of every run, and a record that is not there means nothing has been decided yet. Set aside by moving it, the record is gone from its path until the new one lands; a run killed in that instant leaves the next one starting every decision from nothing, silently, the answers surviving only under a numbered name nobody is told to look at.
RAT-record_never_absent.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-record_never_absent.title: Set aside by copy, so the record is never absent

RAT-record_of_a_finished_run.content:
The handoff tells geotag what prep left, and the log what prep did; written by a run that failed partway, either would
describe a workspace that does not exist. Written only at the end of a run that succeeded, and whole each time, they are
true of the workspace they stand beside, or absent.
RAT-record_of_a_finished_run.title: A record speaks for a finished run

RAT-record_outlives_workspace.content:
The decisions drive a run, but their lasting value is as the record of what was done to the archive and why — and the
workspace is transient: it is merged and set aside, or set aside at any phase boundary without ever advancing. Decisions
are kept for the future only if preserved beyond it, in one known place, rather than scattered in per-file sidecars or,
as with tools that change files and forget, not recorded at all. Since a workspace may stop at any phase, the record
must be whole at each.
RAT-record_outlives_workspace.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-record_outlives_workspace.title: The workspace is transient; the record must not be

RAT-records_attributable.content:
With each phase writing only its own records and carrying earlier ones forward by copy, every phase's output stays a
stable record attributable to it, which no later phase can silently change: complete at its boundary, and evident if
tampered with by what came after. That is why the log is three files, one per phase, not one changed in place. And a
phase that copies its predecessor's record, rather than deriving that history again from other sources, keeps one
account of each phase: a second, rebuilt account could disagree with the first.
RAT-records_attributable.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-records_attributable.title: A record no later phase can silently alter

RAT-recoverable_core.content:
Crash-recovery follows from P1 (an interrupted run must never strand an original half-changed); the diff-based
idempotency also answers F3 — because coverage is partial, one adds more tracks or photos later and re-runs, so a run
must act only on what actually changed.
RAT-recoverable_core.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-recoverable_core.title: Recoverable core

RAT-redundant_named_like_its_raw.content:
A redundant JPG is the same shot as the RAW kept in the dated folders: named from the same time, the two names show it,
and the JPG's name is checked like any other outside the inbox. With no time to name it from, it is named as any untimed
file is.
RAT-redundant_named_like_its_raw.title: The JPG named like its RAW

RAT-refusal_for_what_is_needed.content:
Finalize reads records and the photos' sizes and times, and writes only into the control folder; it reads and writes
no photo's metadata. Execution writes every photo's through that tool, and a plan is made to be executed, so those two
stop without it. Refusing it because the metadata tool is not installed — on a machine the workspace was moved to
for archiving, say — would stop the one step that packages work already done, for a tool nothing in it would run, and
send the user to install something they do not need.
RAT-refusal_for_what_is_needed.title: A command needs only the tools it runs

RAT-refused_merge_clean.content:
The library is the one place the pipeline cannot simply re-plan from: a photo half placed there, or a summary
claiming a merge that did not happen, would have to be found and undone by hand. Checking every precondition before
the first change makes a refusal free — fix the cause, run merge again — and keeps merge's records describing only
merges that ran.
RAT-refused_merge_clean.title: A refused merge leaves nothing to clean up

RAT-remainder_says_why.content: A photo the tracks did not place is one of a few cases with different cures: taken an hour after the logger stopped, taken across a gap the configuration will not bridge, or caught between two tracks that disagree. Listed bare, each sends the user to the map to work out which. Listed with the reason and the distance, most are settled at a glance — and the count of how every photo was placed is the one number that says whether the run did what the tool is for.
RAT-remainder_says_why.title: The remainder is a worklist only if it says why

RAT-remainder_worklist.content:
An explicit, short **remainder worklist** — what no evidence can locate is collected for a manual pin, not left off the
map.
RAT-remainder_worklist.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-remainder_worklist.title: The true unplaceable set must be surfaced, never silently dropped

RAT-removal_reads_the_library_again.content:
A kept fingerprint is trusted by size and modification time, and removing a photo because the library already holds
it cannot be undone: that one decision reads the library file again rather than trust what was kept.
RAT-removal_reads_the_library_again.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-removal_reads_the_library_again.title: An irreversible removal does not trust a kept fingerprint

RAT-required_means_condition.content:
An operator who requires snapshots has made a rollback point a condition of any change. Going on without one would break
that condition silently, so the run stops before its first change, when stopping costs nothing.
RAT-required_means_condition.title: Required means a condition of changing anything

RAT-reread_on_purpose.content:
The way metadata is read changes only on purpose: more of it is wanted, or what is read must change. Either way every
file is to be read again, and reading it whole — its fingerprint with its metadata — leaves nothing the database says
of it from before the change.
RAT-reread_on_purpose.title: A change in how metadata is read is made on purpose

RAT-rerun_is_safe.content:
Geotag can be re-run freely because a re-run redoes nothing settled: the user's decisions live in geotag's records and
survive their regeneration, what geotag wrote into a file is recognised there, so a corrected time is never corrected
twice and photos added later are corrected beside it, and a name computed from the destination's local time comes out
the same.
RAT-rerun_is_safe.title: Re-running is safe because nothing settled is redone

RAT-rerun_not_frictionless.content:
"Freely re-runnable" does not mean "always a no-op". Any change upstream — not only new media — restales exactly what
depends on it, and may raise new questions about the items it touches; a re-run does that work and no more.
RAT-rerun_not_frictionless.title: Safe is not frictionless

RAT-reseal_automatic.content:
Merge adds to the record finalize packaged, so the existing package no longer describes the whole journey. Since merge
is the workspace's last act, remaking the package once at its end is what the user always wants. Finalize stays its own
command because geotag is freely re-run, and re-packaging after every pass would be wasted.
RAT-reseal_automatic.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-reseal_automatic.title: Merge is the end, so the package is remade at once

RAT-reset_clock_not_accepted.content:
A camera whose battery ran out wakes at its factory date, years from the trip. Nothing of its own can anchor it, and
the zone's guess, or the offset it records, moves it a few hours: one acceptance — a click meant to say "the camera
kept local time" — would write that year into the originals as corrected. What the guess cannot see, the
destination's other photos can: a phone, or another camera whose offset is settled, says when the destination was
visited, and the tracks say when the user was out. An offset leaving every photo of a day farther from all of them
than any clock is allowed to be wrong is not a reading of that clock, and accepting it is not an answer; the user is
asked for the offset itself, which the true time of one photo gives. Where no other device's photo is there, nothing
tells a reset clock from a trip with no tracks, and asking every such day would cost an answer the user cannot
improve on; the guess is offered as before. The tracks alone are not that evidence: under a library's worth of them,
a trip with none of its own would be far from all of them too.
RAT-reset_clock_not_accepted.title: A guess that leaves the photos where nothing else was is no reading of the clock

RAT-restore_like_any_file.content:
Moving a file back is the user's way of saying it should not have been set aside. Handled as a new file it is checked
afresh — set aside again if it is still a copy, filed if its twin is gone — and no second path into the pipeline needs
keeping in step with the first ({need}`RAT-time_given_filed_where_it_lies`). The old record stays: it is history of what that run did.
RAT-restore_like_any_file.title: A restored file goes the way of any file

RAT-retake_needs_same_file.content:
The path alone does not say it is the same photo: prep's log once gave a different photo, put by hand where a removed
one had been, the removed photo's history under a "retaken fingerprint". Only the file prep left there, unchanged — its
size, modification time and inode those recorded — taken again by a changed method is the photo whose fingerprint was
retaken; a different file at the path is a new photo, and the removed one's entry stays a gone one.
RAT-retake_needs_same_file.title: A new value at the path is a retake only for the same file

RAT-retention_serves_the_log.content:
A journey spans many runs — prep, re-prep after moves, repeated geotag passes, merge — so a log rebuilt from the last
run alone would silently lose the rest. What is kept exists to serve the log, and resuming and auditing; it is not an
open-ended store of events.
RAT-retention_serves_the_log.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-retention_serves_the_log.title: Retention serves the log, nothing more

RAT-reverts_are_steps_too.content:
Withdrawing a manual position changes the photo as much as applying one: its position goes back to what it held, or to
none. Logged with what it replaced or restored, every position the photo ever carried can be traced; left out, the log
would show a position the photo no longer has.
RAT-reverts_are_steps_too.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-reverts_are_steps_too.title: Undoing a position is a step too

RAT-reviewer_sees_what_was_touched.content:
A run changes irreplaceable originals. Counted apart, what prep changed and what it only read let the user confirm the
run did what they meant and left alone what it must — at a glance, without reading the journal. A figure the code
fixes in advance is no such confirmation, so the summary reports only what the run counted.
RAT-reviewer_sees_what_was_touched.title: The reviewer sees what was touched

RAT-rollback_chosen_by_hand.content:
A rollback is done by hand, often long after the run. The snapshot must say which plan's changes it precedes, so the
operator can find the right one and tell the phases' snapshots apart.
RAT-rollback_chosen_by_hand.title: A rollback is chosen by hand, later

RAT-run_records_outlive_the_next.content:
An execution's summary is the one account of what that run did — what it applied, what failed, which pictures came
out changed — and a package is what was handed on for keeping. The next execution, or a finalize run again after a
further pass, would otherwise replace them, and with them a failure not yet looked at or the package already copied
to storage, which the workspace could then no longer show as it was. A prep journal is the same account of an attempt: a plan
executed again after a failed or interrupted attempt would otherwise replace the record of what that attempt did. Set
aside, as a superseded plan is, they cost a file each and lose nothing.
RAT-run_records_outlive_the_next.title: What a run reported stays on the record

RAT-safe_at_each_change.content:
That nothing is overwritten, and that an interrupted run is finished by running it again, hold only if each change is
safe when it happens. A half-done move, a half-written file, or a failure recorded as done would break both where no
plan can see it.
RAT-safe_at_each_change.title: Safety and resuming rest on the moment of each change

RAT-safety_net_stays.content:
De-duplication decides by fingerprint; the quarantine is what makes a wrong decision recoverable. Deleting on its own —
after some runs, or some age — would turn a recoverable decision into a loss nobody chose. So the quarantine grows,
visibly, until the user prunes it: by a command of its own, which shows what it would delete before it does.
RAT-safety_net_stays.title: The safety net stays until the user lifts it

RAT-safety_not_on_the_plan.content: No-clobber **re-verified atomically at the moment of each write**, not just at plan time.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-safety_not_on_the_plan.title: Safety cannot rest on the plan being correct

RAT-same_content_same_bytes.content:
A record is recognised as unchanged by the hash of its bytes. Were the same content written in another order of keys
or another spacing, every record depending on it would be taken for stale and remade, and the user asked again what
they had already answered.
RAT-same_content_same_bytes.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-same_content_same_bytes.title: A hash can stand for a record only if writing is repeatable

RAT-same_photo_new_fingerprint.content:
A new ImageMagick may decode a photo to a new fingerprint; the photo is the same, and so are its own time and
position. Lost with the old value, they would leave geotag taking the photo's corrected time for its own: a changed
offset would never reach it, a withdrawn one never undo. Prep's log says which old value became which new one; where
it does not say so one for one, no photo's values can be told apart, and geotag stops rather than guess. A log the
handoff does not vouch for says nothing that can be trusted of which became which: planned past it, as though no
fingerprint had changed, a photo would lose its pinned values without a word — so geotag stops on it as well, as
finalize and merge do. Execution builds the same model again from the log and moves each pin to its new value; the
log may have changed since the plan was made, so execution asks the same of it, before it changes anything.
RAT-same_photo_new_fingerprint.title: A new decoder does not make a new photo

RAT-same_picture_not_same_file.content: The fingerprint is of the pixels, and geotag's whole work is in the metadata beside them. A library file with the photo's pixels and other metadata may be the photo before its time and place were corrected — or one the user has since tagged and rated. Removing either copy loses something, and nothing in the files says which matters: the library is never overwritten, so the user settles it.
RAT-same_picture_not_same_file.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-same_picture_not_same_file.title: The same picture is not the same file

RAT-same_shape_different_value.content:
Both phases use the same format, but the **value** differs by phase and that difference is intentional. Because the
shape is identical, a file's name changes between phases only when its timestamp is genuinely corrected; an uncorrected
file's provisional and final names coincide, so geotag plans no needless rename for it.
RAT-same_shape_different_value.title: The same shape, a different value, on purpose

RAT-save_in_dependency_order.content:
A save of several records is several writes, and a power cut or a killed editor can fall between two of them. The
drift validation is proposed from the times the time decisions settle, and the GPS decisions from both; written in
that order, a save cut short leaves the earlier records with their new answers and the later ones as they were — no
answer stands on an earlier one left unsaved, and saving again finishes the rest. The summary's acceptances and a
camera group's class stand on none of the three, and come after them.
RAT-save_in_dependency_order.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-save_in_dependency_order.title: A save cut short leaves its earlier records, not its later ones

RAT-save_keeps_the_replaced.content:
The decision records hold the user's typed answers. A re-plan already keeps the earlier record; the save is their other
writer, and without a copy an answer lost to a mistaken save or a fault of the editor is gone, recoverable from
nowhere. Kept among the re-plan's copies, every earlier version of a record is in one series, in the order it was
replaced. The configuration is left out: nothing else that rewrites it keeps a copy, and the save's change to it is one
camera group's class, plain to see and to change back.
RAT-save_keeps_the_replaced.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-save_keeps_the_replaced.title: The editor's save, too, keeps what it replaces

RAT-save_what_was_seen.content: A decision is the user's answer to a proposal they were shown. A plan run since the editor loaded may have changed the proposal; a save laid over it would record an acceptance of something the user never saw, or drop an answer whose question is gone and report success.
RAT-save_what_was_seen.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-save_what_was_seen.title: A save answers what the user saw

RAT-seal_not_folder_state.content:
Photos by destination is empty both in a workspace just sorted and in one merged and finished, so its state cannot say
which a workspace is. A mark written only when merge succeeds whole can — and a merge that left a photo behind writes
none, so it can be finished by running it again.
RAT-seal_not_folder_state.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-seal_not_folder_state.title: An empty folder means two things; a mark means one

RAT-sealed_dump_moved_by_hand.content:
A dump dropped in a finished workspace is left untouched, for the user to move to a fresh workspace by hand — safer
than any automated move inside a finished workspace.
RAT-sealed_dump_moved_by_hand.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-sealed_dump_moved_by_hand.title: A dump in a finished workspace is the user's to move

RAT-sealed_is_final.content:
A second batch processed in a merged workspace would interleave with the first's database, logs and package, and its
record would no longer describe one dump. So nothing that could change it runs; the records stay readable; and a dump
dropped there is pointed out, so the user knows it was not processed.
RAT-sealed_is_final.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-sealed_is_final.title: A finished workspace is read, not reprocessed

RAT-set_aside_not_a_copy.content:
The quarantine takes more than copies: what an interrupted write left beside a photo, and the hidden files a dump
brings. These have no twin. Recorded as duplicates, they would read as copies whose kept file is missing, and a count of
duplicates would report copies never found — the reviewer checking the dedup against what they dumped would find it
wrong. Counted apart by why each went, each figure means what it says.
RAT-set_aside_not_a_copy.section_name: 10. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
sections: 10. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
RAT-set_aside_not_a_copy.title: A file set aside is not a copy unless it has a twin

RAT-setting_read_once.content:
A threshold is tuned against one judgement — how close a track must pass to anchor a photo, how far two points may be
joined across. Read for a second judgement as well, it cannot be moved for the first without moving the second unseen,
and the user who retunes it for a museum has also changed when two tracks are said to disagree. Each judgement has a
setting of its own, at the cost of more settings to read. Reading a setting to gather what its own judgement will
need — as the tracks' window reads each reader's reach ({need}`RAT-track_window_from_readers`) — is that judgement
still, not a second one.
RAT-setting_read_once.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-setting_read_once.title: A setting read twice cannot be tuned once

RAT-several_bodies_said_by_the_user.content:
Two bodies of one model that write no serial are one camera group: nothing in their photos tells them apart. With GPS
on both, their anchors disagree for good and no one offset is right; with GPS on one that day, its offset would apply
itself to the other's photos; and a day's offset found in one destination would be passed to, or held against, the other
body's in the next. Geotag cannot see this, and treating every group as perhaps two would cost every camera the offsets
that apply themselves. So the configuration says it, a group being one camera unless named — the owner's ruling: *"no,
this needs a workspace setting, default being that it's just one camera. If the setting says multiple cameras, then do
the recommended"*. For a group so named, an offset from its GPS is a proposal, said to be perhaps one body's; its photos
that disagree with it are another body's, their positions right, never offered for replacing; its days in
different destinations are decided apart; and the user tells the bodies apart by sorting one's photos into a folder of
their own — never by a split of the day, for two bodies shooting one after the other look like one clock set at the
change.
RAT-several_bodies_said_by_the_user.title: Only the user knows a group is two bodies

RAT-shutter_time_first.content:
`DateTimeOriginal` is the moment the shutter fired. `CreateDate` is when the file was written, the same moment for a
camera's own file but not for a scan or an export; `ModifyDate` is the last edit, a guess at the making when nothing
else is there. Taking them in that order dates a file as near its making as its metadata allows, and every phase reads
the same one. Some cameras fill a field they cannot set with a placeholder such as `0000:00:00 00:00:00`; that is no
time, and stopping at it would leave a file undated whose next field holds its time.
RAT-shutter_time_first.title: The shutter's time first

RAT-sidecar_orphaned.content:
A sidecar is tied to its photo by name. Prep renames and moves photos, so the sidecar would be left behind under the old
name, its development lost without a word. Development belongs in the library, after merge
({need}`RUL-development_after_merge`); a sidecar arriving with the dump is the user's to keep or discard before prep
goes on.
RAT-sidecar_orphaned.section_name: 5. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 5. What prep refuses to work on
RAT-sidecar_orphaned.title: A sidecar would be orphaned

RAT-size_time_sign_change.content:
Decoding a photo to fingerprint it is the costliest step prep takes, so it is done once per file and kept. Any write to
a file changes its size or its modification time, and both are read without opening it: an unchanged pair says the
fingerprint kept still describes the file, a changed one that it may not.
RAT-size_time_sign_change.title: Size and time are the cheap sign of change

RAT-snapshot_is_extra.content:
**Snapshots are an optional extra safety layer, not a requirement.** The pipeline operates fully and safely without
them: correctness and recoverability rest on the journal, recoverable quarantine, no-clobber operations, and
filesystem-as-truth reconciliation. Snapshots add a clean-slate rollback path on top of those for operators whose
filesystem supports it; they are not the basis of the safety model.
RAT-snapshot_is_extra.title: A snapshot is an extra layer, not the safety model

RAT-snapshot_just_before.title: A rollback point is the state just before the change

RAT-snapshot_name_early.content:
A snapshot's name the snapshot tool would refuse is found when the configuration is read, not when the snapshot is
taken, so a bad name never surprises an execution midway.
RAT-snapshot_name_early.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-snapshot_name_early.title: A snapshot fails before anything changes, not midway

RAT-sort_costs_no_reading.content:
Sorting photos into destinations is the user's own work, done between runs, and prep must plan again after it. Were each
moved photo read again, every sort would cost a decode of everything sorted. A move made by hand keeps a file's size,
time and name, so that triple, read without opening the file, says which file it was; where it fits more than one, prep
does not guess, and reads the file as new.
RAT-sort_costs_no_reading.section_name: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 9. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-sort_costs_no_reading.title: Sorting costs no reading

RAT-speed_is_the_machines.content:
Running fingerprints and metadata reads in parallel only saves time; how many at once depends on the machine, which may
change between runs of one workspace. A plan that differed with it would depend on where it was made; recorded, the
count would make two equal plans differ. So the work is listed and gathered in a fixed order, and the count is kept
nowhere.
RAT-speed_is_the_machines.section_name: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 15. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
RAT-speed_is_the_machines.title: Speed is the machine's, the plan is the workspace's

RAT-stage_cut_points.content:
**The exact decomposition into seven stages** rather than six or eight. The *principle* of discrete inspectable
checkpoints is forced (P1+F3); the specific cut points are judgment.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-stage_cut_points.title: The exact decomposition into stages

RAT-stay_tells_no_time.content: An anchor reads the time off the track where the photo's own position lies on it. That works while the track moves: it passes the place once, at one moment. Where it stood still — a museum, a lunch, a viewpoint — every minute of the stay is at that place, and the nearest point is whichever the receiver's jitter happened to put closest. Two photos taken there agree with each other perfectly and say nothing: the offset they yield can be wrong by the length of the stay, and would then slide every untagged photo of the day along the track by as much. Such evidence narrows the offset without fixing it, so it is offered, checked against the track, and never applied by itself.
RAT-stay_tells_no_time.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RAT-stay_tells_no_time.title: A place only tells the time while the track is moving

RAT-step_traced_to_run.content:
A photo's log outlives the workspace by decades. A step that names its run can be matched to that run's plan and
journal in the archival package; one that does not says what happened and not when, or under which decisions.
RAT-step_traced_to_run.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-step_traced_to_run.title: A step is traced to the run that made it

RAT-stray_as_it_came.content:
A file of no media class is not the pipeline's to process ({need}`RAT-strays_not_the_pipelines`); it leaves the inbox
so that the inbox ends empty, and goes where the user can find it as it was — at the place it had in the dump, under the
name it came with, in the run's own folder so no two runs' strays meet.
RAT-stray_as_it_came.title: A stray is the user's, untouched

RAT-strays_not_the_pipelines.content:
A stray is a file cartographer does not understand — a document, a sidecar it has no use for. Recorded beside the media,
it would make cartographer answer for what it cannot reason about; parked whole, it waits for the user to keep or clear
it, and clearing it costs the record nothing. Moving it is a change like any other, planned and journaled, so the plan
names it, where it was and where it goes, and that plan is kept with the workspace's records; it is named nowhere it
would be taken for a photo.
RAT-strays_not_the_pipelines.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
RAT-strays_not_the_pipelines.title: A stray is not the pipeline's to answer for

RAT-structure_from_the_tool.content:
The user edits these records a few times a year, by hand or in the editor. A field they had to add would need its exact
name and place remembered, and one mistyped would be a decision lost or misread; laid out by the tool, every decision is
one value to fill in, its place already right.
RAT-structure_from_the_tool.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-structure_from_the_tool.title: The tool lays out, the user fills in

RAT-structure_names_reserved.content:
A managed folder's name is reserved for the structure. Moving a folder of that name into the inbox would nest a managed
folder inside another, where nothing would look for it, and leave its place to be made again empty beside it.
RAT-structure_names_reserved.section_name: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 2. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
RAT-structure_names_reserved.title: The structure's names are reserved

RAT-summary_records_an_execution.content:
The summary is the record of an execution: what it placed, what it left and how it ended. A run stopped at the door
executed nothing, and the terminal has said why; a summary written for it would put a record of nothing over that of
the last merge that ran. An interrupted run reached no end to record: its journal holds what it confirmed, and the
run that finishes it writes the summary.
RAT-summary_records_an_execution.section_name: 6. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
sections: 6. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
RAT-summary_records_an_execution.title: The summary records an execution

RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.content:
Setting the prior artifact aside keeps a superseded plan and any authored decisions recoverable; writing nothing on an
unchanged re-run means the iterative decision-editing loop does not accumulate redundant backups.
RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.title: A superseded plan stays recoverable; an unchanged one adds nothing

RAT-surgical_staleness.content:
Collapsing all staleness to a single whole-file hash would needlessly restale unrelated artifacts on any edit, and is
explicitly not done.
RAT-surgical_staleness.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-surgical_staleness.title: Surgical staleness: one hash for everything would restale everything

RAT-temps_are_debris.content:
Merge holds the library's lock, so a temporary copy found in a folder it places into was left by an interrupted earlier
merge, never one being written now. It bears no photo's name, so it does no harm either way: clearing it keeps the
library free of litter — hygiene, not safety.
RAT-temps_are_debris.title: A temporary copy left behind is debris

RAT-time_given_filed_where_it_lies.content:
The user gives a file in missing metadata its time with their own tools, where it lies, whenever they choose; once it
has one it waits for nothing, and the next prep run files it as it files a file of a new dump — the same day folder,
the same name, the same check against the copies already filed. Filing has one way, whatever folder a file starts in,
so no second way needs keeping in step with the first; and the photo reaches photos by date, to be sorted with the rest
of its day. One still without a time stays where it is, waiting.
RAT-time_given_filed_where_it_lies.title: A time given is the fix done

RAT-time_name_recomputed.content:
A file's time and name are not rolled back when a decision is withdrawn but recomputed in place: reverting them would
un-position a file the user has already organized.
RAT-time_name_recomputed.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-time_name_recomputed.title: A time and a name are recomputed, not reverted

RAT-time_replaced_is_gone_from_the_photo.content:
Once geotag has written a time, the photo no longer says what its camera recorded: the log is the only place that can.
And two photos written alike may have been found differently — one by the offset its phone recorded, one by assuming
it was taken on the destination's local time. The second is a guess; a reader checking a photo that looks an hour out
must be able to see which it was, and what stood there before. The same holds of every other field the time is
written into — `CreateDate` and its offset, the dates of XMP and IPTC: rewritten, what each held is gone from the
photo too, and may not have been what `DateTimeOriginal` held.
RAT-time_replaced_is_gone_from_the_photo.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-time_replaced_is_gone_from_the_photo.title: The time replaced is the one thing the photo no longer holds

RAT-time_written_as_lived.content: Once a photo's true instant is known it could be written as UTC, as the camera's home time, or as the time where it was taken. A library is browsed by people: the morning market should read as morning. Written as the destination's local time with its offset beside it, the photo both reads as it was lived and still states its exact instant.
RAT-time_written_as_lived.title: The time a person would have read on the wall

RAT-tool_leaves_its_state.content:
The tool's own work changes the entries too: prep moves and renames, geotag writes an original through a file renamed
over it — a new inode, size and time, its fingerprint the same — and renames it, merge moves photos out. Unless each
execution records the state it leaves, a failed one included, every run after it would stop on the tool's own work. A
plan changes no file, so it leaves the record as it was. Prep can begin from the files alone, so a first run compares
nothing; geotag and merge build on what prep recorded, and without a record a change since could not be told. A prune
is the one way the quarantine changes, so what it removes is taken out of the record with it.
RAT-tool_leaves_its_state.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
RAT-tool_leaves_its_state.title: Each execution records the state it leaves

RAT-total_coverage_cascade.content:
This choice fights F3: tracks cover only *part* of the library, but the output must be *whole*. That gap is what forces
the fallback machinery to exist: without P4, tracks alone would be the entire story and everything below would be
unnecessary.
RAT-total_coverage_cascade.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-total_coverage_cascade.title: Total-coverage cascade

RAT-touched_since_geotag.content:
Geotag's gates held when geotag ran; merge runs later, often much later, and the user may have dropped a new dump into
the inbox, moved a photo back to photos by date, or put a video or a development folder among the photos by
destination in between. Merge is the step after which none of that can be undone cheaply: what it places is in the
library, beside photos it must never disturb. So it asks the workspace again, not geotag's record of it. The folders
the gates leave out are the residue the library never receives; they stay in the workspace, as they would for geotag.
RAT-touched_since_geotag.title: The workspace may have been touched since geotag

RAT-track_is_one_device.content:
Each track is one device's record, and the tracks folder — or one file of it — may hold several for the same hours: a
phone and a logger in the same pocket, or a companion who spent the afternoon elsewhere. Read as one line through all
the points in time order, two devices five kilometres apart become a zigzag between them, and a photo is placed at
whichever was logged a second nearer — or halfway. Kept apart, two tracks that agree are one party and either serves;
two of one rank that do not are a question only the user can answer, by filing their own track higher or taking out the
one that is not theirs.
RAT-track_is_one_device.title: A track is where one device was

RAT-track_points_read_exactly.content:
A track's points become positions and clock offsets; a time read an hour wrong, or in a zone guessed, would place
photos and correct cameras by that hour, and look like evidence. Recorders write the same instant in several valid
forms, so each is read as the instant it is; one stating no zone could be any of them and is not used. Skipping a
point silently would let a track whose every point was rejected pass for an empty one, and the user would never learn
why the photos it should have placed were not.
RAT-track_points_read_exactly.title: A track is evidence only where it can be read

RAT-track_squeezed.content:
**Direct match → interpolation between points → bounded extrapolation off the ends**, each used before falling back to
manual.
RAT-track_squeezed.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-track_squeezed.title: Every placeable point of the track must be squeezed out

RAT-track_window_from_readers.content:
The window bounds which points are read, and every point a reader of the tracks can reach must be in it — so it is
computed from each reader's own settings, never set by one of its own. The owner asked: *"aren't you reusing a config
value for a different purpose?"* — the window does read the matching, gap and drift settings. But it reads each as that
reader's reach, for that reader: the same judgement the setting is tuned for, not a second one beside it. Retuning
`gpx_interpolation_max_gap_seconds` for a museum widens the window with it, which is what it should do; no other
judgement moves unseen. A window setting of its own would be the second judgement: set smaller than a reader's reach,
it would starve that reader unseen — a photo the gap would bridge left unplaced, an anchor never found, with nothing in
the decisions to say the tracks were cut short — and set larger, it reads what nothing uses.
RAT-track_window_from_readers.title: The window is what the readers reach, not a setting of its own

RAT-tracks_are_geotags_evidence.content:
The tracks are evidence for a photo's time and place, and only geotag decides those: prep never plans a time or a
position, so it has no use for them. A phase that read them would also have to treat every change to them as a change
to its own records.
RAT-tracks_are_geotags_evidence.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_are_geotags_evidence.title: The tracks are geotag's evidence

RAT-tracks_change_the_answers.content:
The tracks are evidence for the clock offsets and positions geotag proposes, and a track added, corrected or removed can
change them. A decision made against the old tracks, or a plan built from them, could then be wrong while still looking
settled; the tracks' fingerprint in each record turns the change into staleness instead of letting it pass unseen.
RAT-tracks_change_the_answers.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_change_the_answers.title: Changed tracks can change the answers

RAT-tracks_kept_outside.content:
The shared rule that makes it safe for geotag alone to own the tracks is where they live. Kept outside the managed
folders, prep's normal scan never encounters them, so they can never be taken for files of no media class, or swept
into the inbox and organized.
RAT-tracks_kept_outside.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_kept_outside.title: Where the tracks live is what keeps them geotag's

RAT-tracks_kept_with_workspace.content:
A placement or a clock offset rests on track points, and the tracks folder is the user's, outside the workspace: it is
reorganised, pruned, moved to another disk. A sealed workspace that recorded only a track's fingerprint and name could no
longer show why a photo was put where it was once the folder had changed. The owner: *"I will have always the gps data
used during the process, in the form used during the decisioning, which would make the workspace truly
self-contained."* Kept in the database of record, the points are archived and sealed with every other record, and
sealing then needs nothing outside the workspace. A track taken out after its plan was executed takes nothing out of the
evidence of what was written into the photos: the points stay, withdrawn.
RAT-tracks_kept_with_workspace.title: The evidence stays with what it decided

RAT-tracks_never_strays.content:
Parked among the strays, a track could be deleted when the strays are cleared in bulk, and a lost track is evidence no
re-run can recover. Refusing to run leaves it where the user put it until they move it to the tracks' location.
RAT-tracks_never_strays.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_never_strays.title: A track among the strays could be deleted with them

RAT-tracks_read_where_reached.content:
A tracks folder holds years of recordings, and a workspace is one trip. Reading every track file whole on every run,
and fingerprinting it all, makes the whole folder a dependency of the trip: a walk recorded last week restales the
decisions of a holiday three years ago, and every decision asks again for no reason in its evidence. Only the points a
decision can reach change it; a track unchanged since it was last read need not be read again.
RAT-tracks_read_where_reached.title: The tracks are read where the photos reach them

RAT-trips_revisit.content:
A trip often comes back to its places: a town visited from the same hotel day after day, a square crossed morning and
evening, with a track for every one. Any of those visits passes where a photo was taken, and which passed closest is
chance. Matched to the wrong visit, a whole day's photos are corrected by a day, or by hours — written into the
originals, named by the wrong time, placed on the wrong walk — with no sign anything is off. When the photos cannot
say which visit is theirs, only the user, who remembers the day, can.
RAT-trips_revisit.section_name: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 11. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RAT-trips_revisit.title: A trip comes back to its places

RAT-two_readings_answered_in_the_record.content:
A time a daylight-saving change repeats or skips left a stop, could be mended only outside the tool: an offset written
into the original with exiftool, prep run again. The photo still says nothing of which reading is right, but the user
may know — the hour of the party, the flight — and so it is answered in the time decisions, per photo: which reading,
for a repeated time, or the offset, for a skipped one (ruled as recommended). A time shown twice is one of its two
readings and nothing else; a time never shown came from a clock that was not the zone's, so its offset is the user's to
say.
RAT-two_readings_answered_in_the_record.title: Two readings, answered where the other questions are

RAT-two_readings_no_guess.content: A local time that happened twice, or never, has two readings an hour apart, and the photo says nothing of which. Either is written into the original as its time and decides where on the track it falls. A guess here is wrong half the time and looks exactly like a right answer.
RAT-two_readings_no_guess.title: Two readings, and nothing to choose by

RAT-unknown_is_not_unchanged.content:
A dependency that cannot be checked gives no assurance either way. Counting it unchanged would let a failure to look
stand for proof that nothing moved: a file deleted since the plan, a record a crash left behind, a plan recording
nothing would all pass. Refusing costs a re-plan; trusting could cost a photo its place or its record.
RAT-unknown_is_not_unchanged.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-unknown_is_not_unchanged.title: Failing to look is no proof that nothing changed

RAT-unlisted_media_noticed.content:
The media lists are the user's configuration, and a camera may write a format they never listed. Its photos would be set
aside as strays, recoverably but without a word. Asking the files' content what they are catches that, and leaves the
choice — to list the extension and plan again — with the user; the warning blocks nothing and changes no list.
RAT-unlisted_media_noticed.section_name: 5. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 5. What prep refuses to work on
RAT-unlisted_media_noticed.title: A format the lists missed is noticed

RAT-unread_is_left_behind.content: Prep reads no hidden folder, so photos in one are never fingerprinted, never handed on, never merged — and the workspace is sealed around them as if it were empty. A hidden entry among the photos is something outside cartographer put there; saying so costs the user a moment, silence can cost the photos.
RAT-unread_is_left_behind.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-unread_is_left_behind.title: What is not read is left behind

RAT-unreadable_log_not_empty.content:
Each run's log is the earlier one with this run's steps added. Read as empty, the rewrite would drop every earlier
step: the photos already filed would start again marked partial, and those sorted into destinations would have no
entry at all — a log that looks whole and holds one run. Whatever made the file unreadable, a disk, a hand edit, the
history in it is not prep's to throw away; stopping before any change names it, and the user restores it, or removes it
knowing the history goes with it.
RAT-unreadable_log_not_empty.title: A log that cannot be read is not an empty one

RAT-unreadable_record_not_empty.content:
A journal says which of a plan's changes were made and how each photo was left; the execution summary holds the
user's acceptance of a changed picture; a kept plan and its journal are a pass the log must tell. Taken as empty, the
first is written over by the next confirmation, the second loses its acceptances, the third drops a pass from the
log without a word — each loss silent, and none recoverable from the photos. A damaged record is the user's to look
at; stopping and naming it keeps it as it is until they have.
RAT-unreadable_record_not_empty.title: An execution's record that cannot be read is not an empty one

RAT-unreadable_tag_said.content:
An offset tag reading `local`, or `+25:00`, is no offset; read loosely it would turn a photo's time by a guess.
Read as none, the photo falls to the next source of its time — and silently, the user would believe it read by the
offset its device recorded. So it is read as none, and said: named in the run's output and kept in the record, where
it can be seen later and mended.
RAT-unreadable_tag_said.title: A tag that cannot be read is said, not dropped

RAT-untimed_set_apart.content:
Prep cannot invent a time, and a file with none has no day to be filed under: it waits apart, flat, until the user
gives it one. Its untimed name keeps the name it came with, the user's only way to tell which file it was.
RAT-untimed_set_apart.title: A file with no time cannot be dated

RAT-unwritable_photo_taken_out.content:
A photo the metadata tool will not write — a damaged file, a format it reads and cannot write — fails every execution
the same way; the execution stays partial, and finalize waits on it with every other photo. The tool's own reason is
what tells such a photo from a passing trouble, so it is kept beside the failure. A failure seen twice the same way
will not mend by running again, and nothing else names the way out: take the photo out of what geotag works on — back
into photos by date, a move the workspace check lets pass — and plan again, the rest going on without it. Ruled
2026-11-16: no acceptance of such a photo as it is, and no sidecar. A photo must not reach the library holding a time
or a position other than the one the plan decided for it; and a sidecar is a second record of the photo that digiKam
reads only when set to, while the photo itself goes on holding the old values wherever it is taken.
RAT-unwritable_photo_taken_out.title: A photo that cannot be written is taken out, not let through

RAT-users_backup_is_theirs.content: A file named for a photo with `_original` after it is what the user's own tool left when they edited that photo: the photo as the camera made it. No write of cartographer's leaves one. Taken for debris it would go to the quarantine, which is the one place files are ever deleted from.
RAT-users_backup_is_theirs.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-users_backup_is_theirs.title: The user's backup is the user's

RAT-valid_is_not_unchanged.content:
A fingerprint tells whether a value changed, not whether it makes sense. A value can match its fingerprint and still be
meaningless or dangerous, or be freshly typed and wrong; and a value valid in one run can be edited before the next. So
both checks are needed, every time.
RAT-valid_is_not_unchanged.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-valid_is_not_unchanged.title: A current value can still be wrong

RAT-video_name_uncorrected.content:
A name is corrected to its destination's local time, and a video has no destination: videos are not sorted into
destinations, so there is no zone to read a corrected time in. A zone guessed from the photos of the camera's day goes
wrong on a day spread over two destinations of different zones — the video would be named in the wrong one, under a
name that looks corrected. Its camera's time, uncorrected, is at least what it says it is. Placing videos in
destinations, and then correcting their names, is another piece of work.
RAT-video_name_uncorrected.title: A video has no zone to correct its name by

RAT-videos_kept_not_corrected.content:
The pipeline's aim is photos placed in time and on the map. Videos arrive in the same dumps; prep organizes them by date
so they are neither lost nor scattered, not because the pipeline means to correct them — so they keep a folder of their
own, out of the sort.
RAT-videos_kept_not_corrected.section_name: 1. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
sections: 1. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
RAT-videos_kept_not_corrected.title: Videos are kept, not corrected

RAT-what_was_reviewed_happens.content:
What the user reviewed — the plan, its dry run — is what must happen. An execution that decided afresh would act on a
judgement nobody saw, and a difference between the plan and what was done could not be explained from the record.
Deciding again is planning's work: when the workspace has moved on, the plan is stale and refused, and the user plans
again.
RAT-what_was_reviewed_happens.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-what_was_reviewed_happens.title: What was reviewed is what happens

RAT-which_folder_library.content:
**The downstream library, not the tree.** A *hierarchical* destination tree is **forced**, not chosen: the timezone /
offset / GPS-fallback cascade rides on the folder nesting, so a flat or tag-based layout would make inheritance
impossible and drive the per-photo workload straight back up. What is actually free is only *which* folder-based
library consumes the result — digiKam, or any other — and the cosmetic naming of the levels.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-which_folder_library.title: The downstream library, not the tree

RAT-why_beside_what.content:
A step alone says what happened to a photo — its time moved by three hours — not why. Years later, the decision behind
it is what tells a right correction from a mistake; named beside the step, it is found without searching records that
may be long gone with the workspace.
RAT-why_beside_what.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-why_beside_what.title: The why beside the what

RAT-why_did_this_change.content:
For irreplaceable photos, a user who distrusts opaque, automatic change must always be able to answer *why did this
change happen?* — and to change the answer. So the tool proposes and the user decides, the decision stays in a durable
record that the change can be traced back to, and revising the record revises the result.
RAT-why_did_this_change.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-why_did_this_change.title: A user who distrusts opaque mutation can always ask why

RAT-workspace_as_last_left.content:
The owner: *"I wonder if before each run, as a rule, there should be a quick check to see if anything unexpected
happened. The only manual moves in a workspace should be the moves to by-dest. This should also make the processing
safer."* Each phase plans from the files as it finds them, and a scatter of particular checks — a time changed by hand,
a fingerprint changed after the plan, a hidden folder, a stale plan — catches only what one of them happens to look
at: a photo replaced, changed or put in by hand outside the inbox passes the rest, and is planned on as if the tool had
left it there. Once found, a different photo at the path a removed one freed took that photo's history. One comparison
with the state the last execution left closes the gap for every phase alike, before anything is built on what changed.
The inbox is where the user puts things, so it is never compared; the control records are compared by their own
checks, which know what each may hold.
RAT-workspace_as_last_left.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
RAT-workspace_as_last_left.title: The only hand changes are the expected ones

RAT-workspace_is_local.content:
The workspace is where the originals move, again and again, under one lock; on some network filesystems that lock
guards the runs of one machine only, and which ones cannot be told from inside a run. The workspace's database is no
safer there: its own locking is known to fail across a network. A workspace has no reason to be shared — it is one
place made for one ingest — so a local one costs nothing, and the question is settled for it rather than left to each
filesystem. The kinds known to be local are listed, not the network ones: a kind the list does not know is refused,
so no new network filesystem slips through, and a local one left off costs a refusal that names it. No setting turns
the check off: it would be the one switch that rests the safety of the originals on a filesystem's goodwill. Asked
before anything else, the lock included, it is never mistaken for a run in progress.
RAT-workspace_is_local.title: A workspace is local, by a list of the kinds known to be

RAT-workspace_keeps_its_settings.content:
A workspace's runs, spread over days or weeks, must all read the settings it was set up with, or a later run could
process the same files differently from an earlier one. The seed defaults belong to the installed program, which may be
upgraded or redeployed meanwhile; so they are copied once into the workspace, where they can be read, edited and
archived, and from then on the copy governs, not the program.
RAT-workspace_keeps_its_settings.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-workspace_keeps_its_settings.title: A workspace keeps the settings it started with

RAT-workspace_not_recycled.content:
Even with photos by destination empty, a merged workspace keeps its database, ledgers, caches, snapshots and sealed
record. Starting afresh keeps each workspace's record about one batch.
RAT-workspace_not_recycled.title: A merged workspace is not a clean slate

RAT-workspace_one_filesystem.content:
On one filesystem every move a workspace sees is a single rename: nothing to copy, nothing to verify, no temporary copy
to leave behind. A workspace is one place made for one ingest, so nothing needs it spread over volumes; one that is
would turn prep's ordinary moves into copies, slower and less safe. Only the library is a place apart, and only merge
crosses into it. Checking every run, not once, catches a volume mounted into the workspace since the last.
RAT-workspace_one_filesystem.title: Within a workspace, every move is one rename

RAT-write_leftover_is_debris.content:
A metadata write that was killed leaves a partial copy or a backup beside the photo, named after it. Taken for media
it would be fingerprinted, filed and perhaps kept over the photo it shadows; sent to the strays it would sit among
the user's own files as if they had put it there. It is debris of the pipeline's own making, and may still be the
only whole copy of something, so it goes where nothing is lost and nothing is mistaken: the quarantine.
RAT-write_leftover_is_debris.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-write_leftover_is_debris.title: A write's leftover is neither a photo nor a stray

RAT-zone_asked_at_every_level.content:
Asked only where photos lie, a country of three cities asks three times, unless the user knows to answer on the folder
that asks nothing. The tool cannot tell which folder is the place a zone holds for — a country, a region, a town — so it
asks at each folder above a destination that waits, and the user answers where it is true; the owner: *"the user should
be asked at every level and any choice should propagate to children, with the caveat of multiple timezone countries"*.
An answer passes down to everything below, so the questions it settles go with it: *"This should not multiply choices -
once a time zone is set, children destinations should not ask any longer"*. A folder whose answer would reach nothing —
one said to be in a country of several zones, or one above a zone written lower down — is not asked: its question would
be one no answer settles.
RAT-zone_asked_at_every_level.title: A timezone is asked wherever an answer would reach, and asked no more once given

RAT-zone_from_photos_in_country.content:
A country of several zones narrows the answer to a handful, and a phone's photo records the offset it was taken at.
Where exactly one of the country's zones had that offset at every such photo's time, the photos and the user's own
word on the country together settle it: asking would be asking what the data already says. It is the same evidence
that stops an inherited zone, read the other way — so it applies itself, as an inherited zone does, and passes down
as any zone in effect does. Where several zones fit (zones that share their offsets), or none, or no photo records an
offset, nothing tells them apart, and the destination asks. Positions would say more, but only through a database of
zone boundaries, a dependency the tool does not carry; the offsets need only the zone database it already reads.
RAT-zone_from_photos_in_country.title: The photos say which of the country's zones

RAT-zone_reading_is_an_assumption.content:
A camera's "clock was on local time" is a proposal the user accepts, and is then checked against the tracks. Read
silently by the zone, a phone's photo with no offset tag and a file naming no camera would be placed on the tracks by an
assumption. So, ruled as recommended, the phone's photo is read as the same phone's tagged photos that day show,
unasked, where those show the zone's offset; else its GPS time or a track settles it; with neither, it rides the drift
check where there are tracks, and is asked where there are none: the phone's own photos that day are the best word on
its clock, its own GPS the next, and only then is it the guess a camera's is, asked once. A file naming no camera has no
siblings to read it by; its question is one per destination — "N files name no camera and no offset: read them as local
time in <zone>?" — answered once and kept (the owner: *"I suppose that happens in the editor, right?"*): a screenshot is
made at the local time of wherever it was made, which the user knows for the folder as a whole, not file by file. The
answer names the zone it was given for, so a zone changed later asks again.
RAT-zone_reading_is_an_assumption.title: A time read by the zone is an assumption, asked like one

RAT-zone_table_where_host_lacks.content:
A country is picked from the zone database's own list, and some hosts' zone databases ship without it: there the
choice of a country would be refused. The owner asked: *"can we use OS one if available and some sort of master copy
from web if not, and a bundled version if master copy on web is not available?"* — then ruled: *"build including
download but get permission from user before downloading - this should be during the workspace init. And tell the user
that if he refuses it will use a potentially stale bundled copy"*. The host's own table comes first: it is the one its
zones are read from, and where it has one nothing is asked. Fetching is new for this tool, which otherwise never
reaches the network, so it is done only on the user's word, asked once when the workspace is made, carrying nothing
of the workspace or its user; the answer is kept so the question is not asked again, and the table fetched is kept
with the records — a choice of country rests on it, and a sealed workspace must show what it rested on, as it does the
track points. A kept answer that cannot be read is not no answer: taken for none, the question would come back, the
answer would be written over, and the table in use would change with no one told why — so the run stops on it, named,
as on the other records the workspace keeps. A table fetched is only taken whole and well formed; a failed fetch, a refusal or no one there to answer
leaves the carried copy in use, said aloud, for the question matters only to a choice of country and must never stop
prep. A zone the host cannot read is no country's, whichever table names it. And a choice made from one table may be
wrong by another, so the plan names the table it was made from: another one makes it stale, as a changed decision
does.
RAT-zone_table_where_host_lacks.title: The table of countries is found wherever the host lacks one, and fetched only when the user says so

RUL-acceptance_holds_for_its_proposal.content: An acceptance of a proposed clock offset SHALL hold only while the offset proposed is the one that was accepted.
RUL-acceptance_holds_for_its_proposal.title: An acceptance holds for the proposal it accepted

RUL-acceptance_recorded.content:
Each acceptance SHALL be kept in a record of the accepted changes that is never written over and goes into the
archival package with the workspace's other records.
RUL-acceptance_recorded.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
RUL-acceptance_recorded.title: An acceptance is recorded and kept

RUL-accepted_change_not_stopped_again.content: A change once accepted SHALL stop no later command.
RUL-accepted_change_not_stopped_again.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
RUL-accepted_change_not_stopped_again.title: An accepted change stops no later run

RUL-accepted_changes_logged.content: The changes a run accepts, and those accepted since the last execution, SHALL be named in its log.
RUL-accepted_changes_logged.section_name: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
sections: 17. The workspace as the last execution left it
RUL-accepted_changes_logged.title: The changes a run accepts are named in its log

RUL-accepted_offset_is_the_positions_own.content:
An offset the user accepted as the camera's own positions proposed it SHALL count, wherever offsets of one day in
different destinations are held against each other, as one those positions gave by themselves, not as one the user
chose.
RUL-accepted_offset_is_the_positions_own.title: An offset accepted as proposed is the positions' own

RUL-allowed_changes_named.content:
