TST-audit_backfill-other_class_moves_to_.title: test other class moves to strays

TST-by_date_subfolders-conforming_file_i.title: test conforming file is a noop

TST-by_date_subfolders-existing_flat_fil.title: test existing flat file is migrated into day folder

TST-by_date_subfolders-photo_lands_in_da.title: test photo lands in day subfolder

TST-by_date_subfolders-untimed_file_in_a.title: A file lying in photos by date or videos by date with no recorded time — in a day folder or flat under the band — is moved to missing metadata; a timed neighbour stays where it is.

TST-by_date_subfolders-untimestamped_sta.title: test untimestamped stays flat in missing metadata

TST-by_date_subfolders-video_lands_in_da.title: test video lands in day subfolder

TST-case_folded_names-geotag_never_plans.title: Geotag's rename planning asks nothing of the filesystem: a photo's name taken in another case by another's gives it a suffix, wherever the workspace lies.

TST-case_folded_names-prep_refuses_a_mov.title: On a filesystem that tells `x.jpg` from `X.JPG`, prep's execute still refuses a move onto `X.JPG` while `x.jpg` is there, before it changes anything.

TST-cli-dry_run_mutates_nothing_on_disk.title: Dry-run is validation, not simulation, and is strictly read-only: it loads the saved plan, validates it against an in-memory DB, and prints a summary. Snapshot the whole control dir + a seeded quarantine, run dry-run, assert every on-disk byte is identical (cache, plan, quarantine).

TST-cli-dry_run_summarizes_not_dumps.title: test dry run summarizes not dumps

TST-cli-every_command_waits_for_the_one_.nodeid: tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[prep plan] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[prep dry-run] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[prep execute] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[prep prune-quarantine] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[geotag plan] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[geotag execute] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[geotag finalize] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[merge init-library] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[merge init-library <path>] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[merge plan] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[merge dry-run] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[merge execute] tests/test_cli.py::test_every_command_waits_for_the_one_workspace_lock[edit save]
TST-cli-every_command_waits_for_the_one_.title: Every command of every phase, and the editor's save, takes the workspace's lock — the one lock, the same for all: while another run holds it, each command, run as the command line runs it, refuses with exit 1 and leaves the workspace and the library exactly as they were (the quarantine a prune would delete, the library init-library would bless, the decisions a save would rewrite).

TST-cli-execute_without_saved_plan_exits.title: test execute without saved plan exits nonzero

TST-cli-locked_workspace_failfast_produc.title: Lock contention is fail-fast and pre-mutation: a `plan` that can't take the workspace lock produces NO plan artifact and NO journal — the run never got past lock acquisition.

TST-cli-plan_saves_canonical_and_locks.title: test plan saves canonical and locks

TST-cli-prep_dry_run_validates_the_saved.title: Prep's dry run validates the plan saved for execute, as saved: it passes the saved plan and names it, refuses it once a dependency of it has changed since planning, and refuses it once the saved plan itself would be refused — as execute refuses it.

TST-cli-prep_plan_never_auto_deletes_qua.title: Quarantine is recoverable and is NEVER auto-purged: an ordinary prep `plan` leaves a populated quarantine completely intact (only the explicit `prune-quarantine` command may remove it).

TST-cli-prep_snapshot_is_taken_while_the.title: Prep's snapshot is taken while the workspace lock is held: probed, from a file descriptor of its own, at the moment the snapshot is asked for.

TST-cli-prep_stops_on_a_disturbed_shape_.title: An initialized workspace whose top level was disturbed: every prep command stops at once, naming what is wrong, having read no file, written no plan and no memo — even where there would otherwise be nothing to do.

TST-cli-prep_takes_no_snapshot_before_th.title: Prep's snapshot follows the plan's validation against its dependencies: a plan whose configuration changed after planning is refused with no snapshot taken at all, and a plan that passes is validated first.

TST-cli-prune_quarantine_is_the_sole_op_.title: The seal blocks ONLY plan/dry-run/execute; prune-quarantine is the sole maintenance op that still runs on a sealed (terminal) workspace — quarantine cleanup must survive the seal. Assert it is NOT refused with exit-2 SEALED, and that the --yes delete actually clears the quarantine.

TST-cli-prune_quarantine_preserves_manag.title: prune-quarantine removes only quarantine contents — the managed 0-6 tree (incl. 6-photos-by-dest) is never touched by a prune run.

TST-cli-replan_backs_up_previous_plan.title: test replan backs up previous plan

TST-cli-sealed_new_dump_is_left_exactly_.title: The sealed-workspace new-dump path only WARNS — it never relocates the dumped file. After the refusal the file is byte-identical at its original 0-sources path (the operator must move it to a fresh workspace themselves; prep touches nothing).

TST-cli-the_lock_and_the_seal_come_befor.title: Each phase takes the lock, then checks the seal, and only then the workspace's shape: on a sealed workspace whose shape is disturbed, a run that cannot take the lock stops on the lock (exit 1) and one that can stops on the seal (exit 2), saying the workspace is sealed and nothing of its shape — and neither changes anything but the lock's owner record. The shape check's own place, before everything else, is asserted per phase (TST-geotag_preflight-the_shape_is_checked_before_anything_else, TST-merge_preflight-the_shape_is_checked_before_anything_else).

TST-combined_cli-no_command_takes_a_sett.title: No phase's command takes a setting of the configuration on its command line — under the setting's name, its last part, dashed or not, before the command or after it.

TST-concurrency-exiftool_gets_two_attemp.title: exiftool gets two attempts at a folder's files, the dead worker restarted between them: one crash is retried and its result kept; only a second crash counts the folder's files failed.

TST-config-prep_reads_its_settings_from_.title: Prep, run on an initialized workspace, takes its settings from the workspace's configuration alone: another configuration in every other place — the seed defaults, beside the executable, above the workspace, in the home folder, an environment variable per setting — changes neither how it classifies a file nor how it names it.

TST-config_defaults-seed_defaults_holdin.title: test seed defaults holding jobs are refused

TST-config_validation-a_format_reading_a.title: A filename format holding a field that reads a timezone is refused as the configuration is read — by prep as it seeds and reads it, by geotag and merge as they load it — with what is wrong in plain words; the date and time fields alone pass.

TST-config_validation-field_fingerprints.title: test field fingerprints change with their area

TST-console_server-a_stop_on_changes_is_.title: The stop's list reaches the console as an event the late-joining page sees too, until the next run starts; the Accept button sends the code through the same command — `--accept-changes <code>` on its argv — and the server refuses a code for a command that does not check, or anything that is not such a code.

TST-console_server-accept_with_no_rememb.title: "Accept these" on a stopped execute this page never ran (reloaded, or another tab) sends nothing: it opens the execute gate on the saved plan, and only the confirmation given there sends the execute, with the reviewed plan id and the stop's code. A remembered execute, or a command that needs no confirmation, is sent again with the code at once (docs/design/decisions.md, BACKLOG 50). The page's code runs under Node, its DOM and requests stood in for.

TST-console_server-edit_tab_is_one_edito.title: test edit tab is one editor at a time

TST-console_server-edit_tab_refuses_a_se.title: test edit tab refuses a sealed workspace

TST-console_server-staleness_judged_by_t.title: A workspace whose configuration differs from the built-in defaults (folders renamed, extensions edited, a phone listed), planned on the command line, is fresh to a console that has run no phase — its CONFIG still the defaults — and its execute is offered, as the command line would run it. Judging reads the workspace's file and leaves the process's CONFIG as it was.

TST-console_server-unreadable_geotag_pla.title: A photos-24 that cannot be read — torn, or not an object — is summarised as a plan with a blocker sending the user to `geotag plan` again, never an error of the server; the gate refuses to execute it.

TST-console_server-unreadable_merge_plan.title: A photos-30 merge cannot read — torn, not an object, without its plan id, or in another shape than merge reads — is summarised as a plan with one blocker naming the file and the way on that merge itself gives: repair it or restore a `-NNN` copy, never `merge plan` again, which stops on it; never an error of the server, and the gate refuses to execute it.

TST-content_hash-byte_identical_images_d.title: test byte identical images dedup with real hasher

TST-content_hash-pixel_signature_is_exif.title: test pixel signature is exif invariant

TST-content_hash-raw_jpeg_pair_separates.title: test raw jpeg pair separates redundant jpeg

TST-content_hash-raw_signature_survives_.title: test raw signature survives geotag s writes

TST-content_hash-real_metadata_prefers_e.title: Read by the real exiftool: a time present in both EXIF and XMP is taken from EXIF; a shutter time present only in XMP is taken from there, ahead of EXIF's CreateDate.

TST-content_hash-unreadable_image_blocks.title: test unreadable image blocks with hash failure

TST-content_hasher-a_silent_identify_is_.title: Without `magick`, an `identify` that gives no output for ten seconds is killed; after its two attempts the fingerprint is failed, never valid. The wait is answered at once here, so the test takes no ten seconds.

TST-content_hasher-fingerprint_image_use.title: Default path: the per-thread persistent magick worker returns the signature.

TST-content_hasher-fingerprint_image_wor.title: A worker that keeps crashing is restarted, retried once, then reported failed (never confirmed).

TST-content_hasher-persistent_magick_wor.title: signature() sends the `-read ... -print %# ... {ready}` script and returns the line before the {ready} sentinel.

TST-control_dir-a_record_being_replaced_.title: The shared backup primitive (used by every phase's canonical plan/decision save) copies a pre-existing artifact aside under the `-NNN` suffix and never clobbers it — the artifact itself stays in place, so a run killed before the new version is written still finds the decisions at their path.

TST-control_dir-a_rewritten_record_is_on.title: A power cut: the new record is synced to disk whole before the rename that puts it in the earlier one's place, and the folder after.

TST-control_dir-an_interrupted_editor_sa.title: A decision file the editor rewrites, interrupted — while the new text is half written, or with it written but not yet in the file's place — holds its earlier content whole. The temp file such an interruption leaves is no record: the archival package does not carry it, and the next save writes over it and puts the new content down whole.

TST-control_dir-an_interrupted_record_re.title: A record rewritten in place and interrupted holds its old content whole — whether the interruption comes while the new text is half written or just before it takes the record's place — and the next write puts the new content down whole.

TST-control_dir-control_files_land_under.title: test control files land under control dir

TST-control_dir-journals_are_per_run_and.title: test journals are per run and retained

TST-control_dir-media_inside_control_dir.title: test media inside control dir is not inventoried

TST-control_dir-the_same_content_is_writ.title: A record's bytes follow from its content alone: built in another order, on another run, the same content is the same file — and so the same hash to whatever depends on it; another content is another file.

TST-control_dir-write_versioned_json_bac.title: test write versioned json backs up then writes

TST-culled_raw-a_cull_passed_by_a_failed.title: An execute whose check passed a cull, and whose quarantine move then fails, still logs the cull in prep's log before recording the state it leaves: the next check sees nothing, and the next plan quarantines the JPEG.

TST-culled_raw-a_cull_seen_by_an_earlier.title: A cull a geotag execution's check found, recorded since in its summary, still takes the JPEG at the next prep plan, when that plan's own check no longer sees it.

TST-culled_raw-a_raw_gone_unseen_by_a_ch.title: A RAW's fingerprint held by no file is not enough: without a check that found it deleted by hand — a fingerprint taken again another way leaves the same absence — the JPEG stays.

TST-culled_raw-a_raw_moved_and_renamed_t.title: A RAW sorted into photos by destination and renamed there, or copied there under a new name and the original deleted, is not culled: its fingerprint is still held, so its JPEG stays. Taken back into the inbox, it is held there too.

TST-culled_raw-a_raw_moved_out_of_the_wo.title: A RAW moved out of the workspace — kept whole elsewhere, under its own inode — is culled as surely as one deleted: the check finds it gone, no file prep scans holds it, and its set-aside JPEG goes to the quarantine.

TST-culled_raw-culled_in_photos_by_date_.title: A RAW deleted by hand from photos by date: the next plan quarantines its set-aside JPEG — recoverable, with its evidence — and nothing else; prep's log records the JPEG's step as its RAW culled, naming the RAW by path and fingerprint; the execution records the move as its own, so the next check finds no change. The RAW's video and a JPEG whose pair was never recorded stay where they are, their RAWs culled too.

TST-drift_validation-a_confirmation_hold.title: test a confirmation holds only for the offset it confirmed[zero scrub]

Confirmed by scrubbing the photo along trip.gpx; that track then changed or gone, the check asks again, the confirmation kept exactly as written and applied to nothing — the day is never placed on a track nobody looked at it against.

TST-drift_validation-a_confirmation_made.title: A check shown with no track by the photos (a timezone's guess, asked about whatever lies by it) can be confirmed naming no track; that holds only while still none lies by them — a track arriving later is one it never saw.

TST-drift_validation-a_confirmation_nami.title: test a confirmation naming no offset confirms nothing
A confirmation must name the tracks it was made against: saved without them, it is a blocker — never taken as made against whatever tracks are there now.

TST-drift_validation-a_correction_not_wh.title: test a correction not whole seconds blocks

TST-drift_validation-a_kept_confirmation.title: Every photo of the day corrected already, the confirmation is kept for photos arriving later — and rests there on the tracks it was made against all the same, though none is shown any more.

TST-drift_validation-a_track_put_in_besi.title: The confirmation rests on the tracks it was made against: another put in beside them leaves those there unchanged, and it holds.

TST-drift_validation-an_offset_against_t.title: An offset set against what the camera's own GPS shows is one its GPS does not support: it is confirmed against the tracks like any other, the anchored photo beside it vouching for nothing.

TST-drift_validation-an_offset_that_carr.title: A manual offset with a slipped digit puts the photos eight days from the tracks recorded the day they were taken. No track lies by the times it gives — because of it: the check asks, against the tracks by the times the camera recorded.

TST-drift_validation-an_offset_written_i.title: An offset written in a drift cell is checked as written: one that is no whole number of seconds is named while the cell is still unconfirmed, not only once a confirmation would make it count.

TST-drift_validation-e2e_a_changed_track.title: Confirmed as the editor does — naming the tracks the cell shows, by the SHA-256 of their bytes — the check passes; the track then replaced by another export of the day, the next plan asks again.

TST-drift_validation-e2e_drift_gate_bloc.title: test e2e drift gate blocks then resumes

TST-drift_validation-the_check_names_the.title: Each drift cell lists the track files its segment is drawn from, each with its SHA-256 — what the editor writes with a confirmation. Unconfirmed, the cell names none and nothing changed.

TST-drift_validation-the_track_window_is.title: Which track counts as covering a bucket's photos is the drift check's own setting, not the largest clock error an anchor may imply.

TST-drift_validation-zero_scrub_must_be_.title: test zero scrub must be explicit

TST-exif_metadata-a_database_of_another_.title: A workspace database recording a schema version not this build's stops prep's plan: it is never migrated.

TST-exif_metadata-a_field_is_taken_from_.title: Each field is taken from EXIF when EXIF holds it, else from XMP; a time field missing or holding no valid time in EXIF is taken from the same field in XMP before the next field is tried. The GPS position is taken signed, from exiftool's Composite group.

TST-exif_metadata-a_placeholder_time_doe.title: A field present but holding no valid time is passed over for the next that holds one; a file whose fields all hold none has no recorded time.

TST-exif_metadata-blank_identity_values_.title: Each identity field held enters the key as its text, the blanks around it stripped, in the fields' order: a blank one is an empty part, so a file holding only blank ones is a camera group of empty parts, never the key of a file naming no camera — which only a file holding none of them has, or one whose only field reads it.

TST-exif_metadata-metadata_cache_creatio.title: test metadata cache creation and staleness

TST-exif_metadata-parse_exiftool_item_ti.title: selected_source_naive_timestamp prefers DateTimeOriginal, then CreateDate, then ModifyDate, else None; its provenance names the group it came from.

TST-exif_metadata-the_other_time_fields_.title: The time fields geotag rewrites are kept each under its group's name, from that group alone — so a photo's IPTC date is never taken for an XMP one it does not hold — beside the field taken by the group order.

TST-exiftool_leftovers-bydest_leftover_l.title: test bydest leftover left untouched with warning

TST-exiftool_leftovers-inbox_user_backup.title: A `<photo>_original` in the inbox goes where any file of no media class goes — to the strays, never to the quarantine as a leftover; a `<photo>_exiftool_tmp` beside it still does.

TST-exiftool_leftovers-managed_folder_le.title: test managed folder leftover is quarantined

TST-exiftool_leftovers-organized_user_ba.title: Outside the inbox a `<photo>_original` is treated as a file of no media class there is: never quarantined as a leftover.

TST-exit_status-a_changed_photo_s_execut.title: An execution that found a photo's content changed when written ends partial, and says where its one question is answered: the decision editor, or the field of photos-25 by hand.

TST-exit_status-a_refused_prune_ends_as_.title: `prune-quarantine` refusing its selection — a delete naming nothing without `--all`, an age below one day — ends 2, a refusal, not 1, which says the workspace is locked; nothing in quarantine is removed.

TST-exit_status-each_end_of_a_geotag_exe.title: Geotag's execute ends 0 done, 1 with the workspace locked, 2 refused — by a precondition or a stale plan —, 3 partial or failed and 130 interrupted.

TST-exit_status-each_end_of_a_prep_execu.title: Prep's execute ends 0 done, 1 with the workspace locked, 2 refused with nothing changed — its plan stale or unreadable, or a required snapshot not taken —, 3 when an operation fails and 130 interrupted.

TST-exit_status-each_end_of_a_prep_plan_.title: Prep's plan ends 0 done, 1 with the workspace locked, 2 refused — exiftool absent, a blocker reported, a database of another schema — and 130 interrupted.

TST-fallbacks-a_cross_fs_move_stopped_at.title: Merge's move into a library on another filesystem — copy, check, sync, rename into place, sync the folder, remove the source — interrupted, or failing, at any of its steps or halfway through the copy, leaves the photo whole under its old name, its new name or both: at the moment it stops, and once the stop has unwound.

TST-fallbacks-a_hard_link_move_stopped_a.title: Where the filesystem has no rename that refuses a taken name, a move is a hard link under the new name and then the old name's removal: interrupted, or failing, at either, it leaves the photo whole under its old name, or both.

TST-fallbacks-cross_fs_move_makes_the_re.title: The source is removed only after the destination folder — holding the rename into place — is flushed to disk: a power cut cannot keep the removal and lose the rename.

TST-fallbacks-cross_fs_move_refuses_a_co.title: A copy of the right size but one byte off — damage a fingerprint of the decoded image would not see, in the metadata geotag wrote, say — is refused: the source kept, no destination, no temp.

TST-fallbacks-move_no_clobber_refuses_ex.title: Only merge crosses filesystems: for prep and geotag (no cross_fs) a move that would cross one is raised as a failure, never turned into a copy — the source stays and no temp is left.

TST-filename_format-format_change_after_.title: test format change after naming stops prep

TST-filename_format-format_free_while_no.title: test format free while nothing named

TST-filename_format-inbox_name_off_its_t.title: test inbox name off its time named from metadata

TST-filename_format-misnamed_file_given_.title: Each misnamed file is named together with the name it should carry: its recorded time in the format with its own extension, or — with no recorded time — its name behind the untimed mark.

TST-filename_format-misnamed_file_outsid.title: test misnamed file outside inbox stops prep

TST-filename_format-prep_and_geotag_name.title: Prep's provisional names and geotag's final names are in the one format the workspace's configuration sets — here not the built-in one: a photo whose time geotag corrects is renamed in it, and a photo whose time needs no correction keeps the name prep gave it.

TST-filename_format-prep_names_from_the_.title: Prep names a photo, and files it by day, from its time as the camera recorded it: not moved by the offset from UTC the camera recorded beside it, by its GPS time, by the workspace's default timezone or by the machine's own.

TST-filename_format-redundant_jpg_named_.title: test redundant jpg named from its time

TST-filename_format-suffix_allocation_is.title: Which file gets which differentiating suffix does not depend on the order the files are met in: the same files, listed by the filesystem in the opposite order, are given the same names.

TST-filename_format-wrong_day_file_moves.title: test wrong day file moves without blocker

TST-filesystem_checks-every_command_refu.title: Every command of every phase, and the editor's save, stops on a workspace on a network filesystem, naming its type, before anything else — the lock included: a free lock is not taken, and nothing changes.

TST-filesystem_checks-execute_counts_onl.title: A photo an earlier run moved, or whose place already holds a file, takes no room: with room for the one left, execute goes on and places it.

TST-filesystem_checks-execute_stops_shor.title: test execute stops with nothing moved when the library is short of room

TST-filesystem_checks-library_on_a_netwo.title: test a library on a network filesystem is merged into

TST-filesystem_checks-library_tried_befo.title: A library whose filesystem cannot refuse a move onto a taken name stops merge, naming it, before the library's lock is taken; the library, the workspace's photos and merge's records stay as they were.

TST-filesystem_checks-local_types.title: test only a filesystem known to be local holds a workspace[ext4-True]

TST-filesystem_checks-margin_is_a_number.title: test a margin not a number of zero or more is refused[-1]

TST-filesystem_checks-no_mount_table_ref.title: Where the filesystem's kind cannot be told — no mount table, not Linux — the workspace is not known to be local, and a run stops having made nothing.

TST-filesystem_checks-phases_stop_on_a_m.title: A filesystem without locks stops each phase naming them — never read as a run in progress — and leaves the workspace as it was; prep's first run tries them in the workspace itself, its control directory not yet made.

TST-filesystem_checks-plan_warns_short_o.title: test the plan warns of a library short of room and is written

TST-filesystem_checks-room_holds_the_mar.title: Room for the photos alone is short by the margin; the margin is the configuration's, 0 asking no more than the photos' size.

TST-filesystem_checks-same_filesystem_no.title: test on the workspaces own filesystem no room is asked

TST-filesystem_checks-trial_in_the_contr.title: test the workspace is tried in its control directory

TST-filesystem_checks-type_from_the_moun.title: The mount table is read as the system writes it — escapes and all — and the workspace's type is that of the mount whose point is the longest prefix of its real path, the later of two at one point.

TST-fingerprint_frames-both_paths_agree_.title: The worker and `identify` give one value for the same file, a 70-frame one too: no count of frames makes a legitimate file fail.

TST-fingerprint_frames-earlier_method_va.title: A fingerprint recorded by the method that hashed only the first frame, or only the default streams, is never reused — in prep's records or in merge's library cache — so it is never compared with one taken the way this build takes it.

TST-fingerprint_frames-frame_order_matte.title: The same frames in another order are another image.

TST-fingerprint_frames-later_frame_tells.title: Two 2-page TIFFs sharing their first page and differing in their second are different photos, on both paths.

TST-fingerprint_frames-prep_keeps_pages_.title: Prep does not quarantine one of two TIFFs as the other's duplicate because their first pages agree; two copies of one TIFF are still duplicates.

TST-fingerprint_frames-second_audio_stre.title: Two clips alike but for their second audio stream are different videos; one clip is itself.

TST-fingerprint_frames-single_frame_valu.title: A single-frame image's fingerprint is that frame's signature, as before, on both paths.

TST-fingerprint_frames-subtitle_and_time.title: A clip holding a subtitle stream and a timecode data stream fingerprints, and its subtitles count.

TST-fingerprint_frames-worker_reads_ever.title: However many frames a file has, every signature line is read and folded; an answer that is not a signature is a broken process, never a read without end.

TST-fingerprints-a_dependency_missing_or.title: A dependency that cannot be checked — its record gone, or the plan recording none — counts as changed: execution refuses the plan before its first change.

TST-fingerprints-a_failed_fingerprint_is.title: A failed fingerprint is offered for reuse neither by the plan memo nor by the database: once the machine is fixed, the next plan takes it, the file's size and time unchanged.

TST-fingerprints-a_file_whose_metadata_i.title: Metadata read by another way than the one in use is read again, and the file's fingerprint with it.

TST-fingerprints-a_fingerprint_is_reused.title: A cached fingerprint is reused only when taken by the method this build uses: the same strategy and, for a photo, the same ImageMagick version — one recording none is taken again; a video's is bound to its strategy alone.

TST-fingerprints-a_new_or_changed_file_i.title: A file the database holds no fingerprint for is fingerprinted; an unchanged one is not; one whose modification time changed is fingerprinted again.

TST-fingerprints-a_retaken_fingerprint_r.title: A file fingerprinted again only because the method changed keeps its fresh metadata, reported as reused — not as a failed extraction.

TST-fingerprints-execute_writes_the_data.title: Each execute writes the current versions into the database's version row, over what it held.

TST-fingerprints-handoff_vouches_for_the.title: Prep's execution records in its handoff the hash of the log it wrote — outside the handoff's content, so a pointer refreshed by a run that changed nothing makes nothing downstream stale.

TST-fingerprints-media_carries_fingerpri.title: test media carries fingerprint and no byte hash

TST-fingerprints-prep_records_hold_no_fi.title: Prep's plan records no `workspace_root` and its database effects no `absolute_path`; its journal records no `snapshots` and no tool or execution id among its dependencies; its handoff no `hash_algorithm`; and the database's `file_cache` no `absolute_path`.

TST-folders-dedup_priority_orders_by_des.title: test dedup priority orders by dest highest strays excluded

TST-folders-validate_config_rejects_bad_.title: test validate config rejects bad folders[bad0-missing role]

TST-front_end-a_drift_confirmation_names.title: A drift confirmation written in the editor names the offset it confirms and the tracks shown, and holds only while both stand.

TST-front_end-a_phone_a_reading_and_file.title: A phone's day kept as it records itself, accepted or set; a time at a daylight-saving change given a reading; files naming no camera read in the zone the answer names; an acceptance shown as the offset it accepted.

TST-front_end-a_position_chosen_for_a_ph.title: A photo nothing places is offered its folder's fallback, then a position; a placed photo is given one as a `chosen_by_user` item; a position the user set, emptied, is shown placed as before.

TST-front_end-a_split_day_is_accepted_an.title: A day split where its clock changed is accepted once, naming its offsets and each unsettled photo's part, on the day's cell; held stale with no change proposed, it is withdrawn there.

TST-front_end-an_answer_given_for_severa.title: Days answered together share what an answer writes: a day in a same-day conflict, kept as its phone records itself, or far from all evidence is a row of its own; a proposal taken in a conflict is the user's own offset; a group picked on a phone's kept day ends the keeping; an acceptance names its offset.

TST-front_end-the_editor_saves_answers_w.title: A save carries the hashes of the records as loaded; a changed content is accepted for that content, a changed time answered for the time it holds — kept only where it holds one geotag reads; a camera group classed, or named several bodies, in the configuration.

TST-front_end-the_editor_shows_settled_o.title: An acceptance in a same-day conflict, or of a guess far from all evidence, settles nothing; a country is chosen once at the top of its tree; the configured default zone is only proposed; a zone the photos contradict is not in effect without the user's word.

TST-geotag_clock_change-a_change_is_seen.title: The times the GPS fixes recorded show a change as the tracks do, where no track anchors the day; the photos alone — their recorded times, the offsets they record — show none.

TST-geotag_clock_change-a_clock_set_back.title: Four photos on a clock at UTC+9, then four after it was set back an hour: in camera time the two runs interleave — 18:00 and 18:30 each shown twice — and only by the true times the tracks give do they follow one another. A split is proposed; a photo without GPS in the repeated hour, which either part could have taken, is asked its part, one before or after it is not. Split so, every photo of each part agrees with its offset: no own position is doubted, and photos-23 raises no review item for any.

TST-geotag_clock_change-alternating_or_a.title: Photos whose offsets go back and forth in the order of their true times — three runs or more, as two bodies' photos taken in turn are — are no clock change; nor is a day whose photos agree.

TST-geotag_clock_change-an_acceptance_ho.title: Unaccepted, nothing splits; an acceptance naming other offsets than the runs now give splits nothing, is kept as written and asks; one naming none is a blocker.

TST-geotag_clock_change-an_accepted_spli.title: Accepted, with no word of the part of the photo the runs leave unsettled, the day still asks; told, the day's cell asks nothing and the day is two parts, each anchored by its own photos at the offset accepted for it, nothing asked of them. Each photo takes its part: a run's photo its run's, the one only the first part could have taken the first's, the unsettled one the part it was given. A part written other than 1 or 2 is a blocker.

TST-geotag_clock_change-photos_one_part_.title: With every photo without GPS one that only one part could have taken, nothing is asked of them: accepted, the day splits, each such photo in its part.

TST-geotag_clock_change-several_bodies_a.title: For a group the configuration names several bodies, two runs are two bodies as likely as one clock changed: no split is proposed — the bodies are told apart by their destinations.

TST-geotag_clock_change-the_split_follow.title: The split is answered on the day's cell: when another day's photos arrive and the day's key takes its dated form, the answer follows the day, its parts keyed after it.

TST-geotag_clock_change-two_places_to_cu.title: The walk passes one place twice, at 09:00 and at 17:00: a photo taken there agrees with the home-time run before it and with the local-time run after it alike. The day can be cut on either side of it, each cut leaving two runs that agree — not one place where the clock changed, so no split is proposed.

TST-geotag_clock_change-two_runs_propose.title: Three photos on home time, then three set to local time: two consecutive runs, each agreeing on its own offset. The day's cell proposes splitting at the change, naming each run's offset and its first and last photo in true time, and the photos without GPS whose part the runs leave unsettled; it asks, as a day whose anchors disagree always did.

TST-geotag_containers-a_zone_is_asked_at.title: Every folder with no zone above a destination waiting for one asks for it, naming the destinations an answer there would reach; answered at any of them, everything below takes it and nothing there asks again — answered at every destination, no folder above asks.

TST-geotag_containers-a_zone_is_asked_on.title: A folder where a country of several timezones is said is not asked — a zone there passes to nothing — nor is any folder above it for what lies inside; the asking goes on inside it. A destination below a zone written lower down, waiting on its own photos, is no question for the folders above that zone.

TST-geotag_containers-child_offset_decis.title: test child offset decision is not pooled upward

TST-geotag_containers-container_material.title: test container materialized with no offset cells

TST-geotag_containers-manual_timezone_re.title: test manual timezone reroots the chain

TST-geotag_containers-moved_photo_takes_.title: test moved photo takes its new destinations offset

TST-geotag_containers-the_default_zone_i.title: test the default zone is proposed and an answer cascades

TST-geotag_contradicted_position-a_posit.title: A photo whose own position lies far from every track — a side trip the walk never went near — matches no pass, so says nothing of the offset: only the stray one the tracks contradict is named, and offered their position.

TST-geotag_contradicted_position-a_scatt.title: The day's offset agreed by five photos, the stray one agreeing with none: photos-21 names it, and photos-23 makes it a review item proposing where the track was at its corrected time — about 1.4 km from its own position — asking nothing, its own position kept. The tracks' window reaches its corrected time.

TST-geotag_contradicted_position-several.title: For a group the configuration names several bodies, a photo disagreeing with the offset is the other body's: its position is never read as wrong.

TST-geotag_contradicted_position-the_use.title: The user takes the track's position: the photo is placed there by their answer, a position write planned with the position it replaces as its pre-state; unanswered, its own position is never written over.

TST-geotag_contradicted_position-with_no.title: Contradicted, at a corrected time no track covers: nothing to propose — the photo keeps its own position, and photos-23 notes it.

TST-geotag_date_fallback-a_bad_date_is_r.title: test a date that is no date is refused naming it[1985-02-30]

TST-geotag_date_fallback-a_midnight_its_.title: São Paulo's clocks went forward at midnight on 2 November 1985: that day has no 00:00. The scan is asked about as any time its zone skips, and resolves by the answer.

TST-geotag_date_fallback-a_written_scan_.title: Once written, the scan holds the filled time — but geotag decides it from the values pinned before its first write, which held none: the date fallback times it again, and the time it holds is geotag's, asked nothing.

TST-geotag_date_fallback-a_year_a_month_.title: test a date fallback is a year a month or a day the rest the first

TST-geotag_date_fallback-geotag_plan_ask.title: Two scans with no time beside a phone's photo: the first plan writes photos-21, asks for their folder's date and stops, naming them, nothing past photos-21 written. The date given by hand at the folder above, the plan goes on; their position given by the folder fallback, photos-24 writes each scan's filled time — local, with its offset — and names them by it in the order of their names, the date as given recorded with the write. The phone's photo keeps its own time.

TST-geotag_date_fallback-it_is_no_camera.title: A scan names its scanner as a camera group: having no time, it reads no clock — solved alone, never in a camera's offset cell, and its group is no class question.

TST-geotag_date_fallback-no_track_places.title: A track that covers the filled instant exactly places the timed photo, never the scan: the scan falls to its folder's fallback, else waits, saying why the tracks did not place it.

TST-geotag_date_fallback-suffixed_in_the.title: Three scans of one date take its name and suffixes in the order of the names they hold — compared as text, so `scan10` comes before `scan2`, as a listing shows them.

TST-geotag_date_fallback-the_log_records.title: test the log records the date fallback as given and where

TST-geotag_date_fallback-the_nearest_dat.title: Given at `Scans`, a container, the date covers `Scans/1985` inside it unasked; one given at `Scans/1985` itself wins over it. A folder holding a photo with no time and no date in effect asks; one holding none never does.

TST-geotag_date_fallback-the_untimed_pho.title: test a photo with no time takes its day at midnight local and a timed one keeps its own

TST-geotag_executable_plan-a_time_the_fi.title: test a time the file holds is not written again

TST-geotag_executable_plan-a_track_posit.title: test a track position says how it was derived[direct match-matched]

TST-geotag_executable_plan-automatic_gps.title: BLD-gps_decisions_record (anti): photos-24 re-derives every AUTOMATIC GPS decision from its own validated inputs — never by trusting what photos-23 records. A native frame's automatic decision is preserve_native (no GPS write). Inject a CONTRARY manual lock into photos-23 for that frame: if photos-24 parroted photos-23 it would emit a GPS write — instead it re-derives preserve_native from the file's own native-GPS input, so the ops are byte-identical and still carry zero GPS writes.

TST-geotag_executable_plan-gps_write_car.title: RUL-position_written_whole: EXIF coordinates are unsigned magnitudes — a write without GPSLatitudeRef/ GPSLongitudeRef reads as NO location to a conforming reader, and flips the hemisphere of a southern/western position for a lenient one. The refs ship in the same operation.

TST-geotag_executable_plan-plan_ready_wi.title: test plan ready with ops and full depends on

TST-geotag_executable_plan-the_other_tim.title: Each other field recording the making that the photo holds is written to the corrected local time, in its own format — XMP keeping the fraction of a second its value held — and the write records what each held. A field the photo does not hold is never added; ModifyDate, its offset and the sub-second fields are not written.

TST-geotag_executable_plan-time_write_ca.title: test time write carries its offset

TST-geotag_execution-a_change_of_case_al.title: `X.JPG` to `X.jpg`: on a filesystem that ignores case the new name is the photo's own, which a no-clobber move refuses. The rename goes by a free temporary name in two no-clobber moves; interrupted between them, the next run finds the photo under the temporary name and completes it, once it is seen to be that photo. A temporary name taken blocks the rename, nothing moved.

TST-geotag_execution-a_failed_write_keep.title: Each failure in photos-25 carries, beside the photo and the operation, the kind of operation and exiftool's own message — what tells a damaged file from a passing trouble.

TST-geotag_execution-a_plan_made_by_othe.title: Geotag's executable plan records the code that made it; another build, or a plan recording none, makes it stale before any change.

TST-geotag_execution-a_run_the_snapshot_.title: A required snapshot that fails ends the run before anything is executed: the tracks its plan rests on are not recorded as used, nor its decisions kept as executed. The same plan run once the snapshot is taken records both.

TST-geotag_execution-a_write_failing_aga.title: The same photo failing the same way on a second execution of the same plan will not mend by running again: the summary and execute's output say so for it, naming the way out — back into photos by date, a move the workspace check passes, then prep and `geotag plan` again. The exit status stays that of a partial run.

TST-geotag_execution-a_write_interrupted.title: Geotag itself stopped at the worst moment — the new file whole beside the photo, about to take its place: the photo is as it was, and the resumed write clears the leftover and puts the new one down.

TST-geotag_execution-an_acceptance_is_of.title: A changed picture is accepted as the fingerprint that was reported, under the plan that reported it: it stays there to be accepted through a run that finds the photo still held, and is no acceptance of another content, nor under another plan.

TST-geotag_execution-an_edit_made_since_.title: test an edit made since the plan is never overwritten

TST-geotag_execution-an_interrupted_meta.title: The real exiftool, killed while it writes the new file beside the photo, leaves the photo as it was, byte for byte; the write done again puts the new tags down whole, the photo keeping its permissions.

TST-geotag_execution-another_image_engin.title: Every write is checked by taking the photo's fingerprint again. With another image engine than the one prep took the fingerprints with, each would come out different: execute stops before writing anything.

TST-geotag_execution-another_table_of_co.title: The plan names the table of countries it was made from and where that came from; another one — the host's gone, a copy downloaded, another release — makes it stale, as a changed decision does.

TST-geotag_execution-apply_file_already_.title: A crashed prior run that already renamed the file (source gone, planned target present) is detected by state on resume — even with an empty/lost journal — rather than blocking on the missing source (BLD-geotag_execution): once the target is seen to be that photo holding the planned values, its operations are recorded as done (never redone), so the run that applied them is in the journal after all. A file merely of the target's name is not taken for the photo.

TST-geotag_execution-apply_file_precondi.title: test apply file precondition and resume branches

TST-geotag_execution-content_changed_wri.title: test content changed write flags mismatch

TST-geotag_execution-every_geotag_rename.title: Where the filesystem allows, each rename geotag makes is one rename — never a hard link and an unlink, or a copy and a removal, of the photo.

TST-geotag_execution-every_write_traces_.title: From the journal of what ran, each confirmed operation is found in the plan, and the plan names by hash the decision records it was made from, which hold the decision for that photo's destination.

TST-geotag_execution-exiftool_write_invo.title: exiftool is told to write the new file beside the photo, never over it; geotag puts it in the photo's place, with the permissions the photo had.

TST-geotag_execution-geotag_leaves_confi.title: Geotag never writes the workspace config (photos-00-config.json is hand-edited, authoritative). Snapshot its bytes, drive the full plan + execute, assert byte-for-byte identical (the geotag half of config-merge-readonly; the merge half is covered in test_merge_execute).

TST-geotag_execution-geotag_reads_its_se.title: Geotag takes its settings from the workspace's configuration alone: another configuration in every other place — the seed defaults, beside the executable, above the workspace, in the home folder, an environment variable per setting — naming other tracks, another format and another zone, changes neither the time it resolves nor the name it gives.

TST-geotag_execution-no_snapshot_before_.title: Geotag's snapshot follows the plan's validation against its dependencies: a plan whose time decisions were edited after planning is refused with no snapshot taken at all, and a plan that passes is validated first.

TST-geotag_execution-one_photo_s_failure.title: Applying one photo raises (the image engine cannot be started, a disk error): that photo fails, by name — and every other photo's result is still journalled and summarised, never applied behind a run that has already fallen over.

TST-geotag_execution-only_the_same_failu.title: A failure is told as repeated only against the previous execution of the same plan, with the same operations and the same reason: another reason, or another plan's summary, is no repetition; a run rejected before it tried the photos is passed over for the one before it, kept under -NNN.

TST-geotag_execution-planned_tags_held_b.title: The read-back test that tells geotag's own interrupted write from an edit: a coordinate equal in magnitude to within a millionth of a degree, its sign left to the reference tag; any other tag equal as text; a tag planned empty absent or empty.

TST-geotag_execution-reclassing_a_camera.title: Of a camera group the configuration sets only its class: the same group classed as a fixed-clock camera, then as a phone, then as a camera again, is treated as each — a clock offset decided for it as a camera, none as a phone — and is the same group in geotag's records every time, under the key prep derived.

TST-geotag_execution-rename_target_occup.title: test rename target occupied at execute blocks

TST-geotag_execution-resume_after_journa.title: Crash-resume (RUL-geotag_execution_resumable): a full execute renames + writes the files; deleting the journal (simulating a crash before its flush) and re-executing must detect the already-applied files at their targets and SKIP them — not block on the changed/missing source.

TST-geotag_execution-revalidate_detects_.title: test revalidate detects each stale input

TST-geotag_execution-snapshot_is_taken_w.title: Geotag's snapshot is taken while the workspace lock is held: probed, from a file descriptor of its own, at the moment the snapshot is asked for.

TST-geotag_execution-stale_plan_is_rejec.title: test stale plan is rejected without mutation

TST-geotag_execution-summary_written_onl.title: photos-25 is written by a run that applied the plan, or whose required snapshot failed — that one carrying the mismatches still open, acceptances and all. A preflight refusal, a stale plan or an interrupt writes none: the earlier summary stays as it was.

TST-geotag_execution-the_kept_tracks_are.title: The catalogue of the tracks planning keeps in the record is written outside the plan's operations and leaves no entry in the journal: the journal holds the plan's operations and nothing else; execute only checks the tracks.

TST-geotag_execution-the_new_photo_is_on.title: A power cut: the new file is synced to disk before the rename that puts it in the photo's place, and the folder after — a rename that reaches the disk ahead of its data is how a photo comes back empty.

TST-geotag_execution-what_a_killed_run_a.title: A run killed after applying photos and before recording them: the next run finds each at its planned name holding the planned values, redoes nothing, and records its operations — so the journal names every change made, and a later log has the pass. It also records each photo as the run left it.

TST-geotag_execution_real-a_burst_timed_.title: Against the real binary: two photos of one second recording no DateTimeOriginal, timed by CreateDate, the one whose name sorts first taken later by SubSecTimeDigitized. Prep reads the EXIF sub-second field beside CreateDate, and geotag gives the earlier photo the bare name, the later the first suffix — not their names' order.

TST-geotag_execution_real-a_photo_exifto.title: The real exiftool, given a file it cannot write: the write returns exiftool's own message, the file is left as it was and nothing is left beside it.

TST-geotag_execution_real-a_written_phot.title: Against the real binary: a photo geotag wrote reads back as holding every planned value — time, offset, position, references, marker — which is how execute tells its own interrupted write from an edit made since the plan; an edit to one tag no longer reads back as the plan.

TST-geotag_execution_real-exif_write_pre.title: The seam the executor relies on, against the real binaries: write EXIF, fingerprint is stable.

TST-geotag_execution_real-planned_gps_wr.title: RUL-position_written_whole against the real binary: the tags `plan_file_ops` plans must land a fix a conforming reader can use. Coordinate-only writes were readable to exiftool's lenient composite but carried no GPSLatitudeRef/GPSLongitudeRef, so exiv2/digiKam saw NO location — and `-n` stored a negative coordinate as its magnitude, flipping the hemisphere. Assert the raw ref tags AND the signed round-trip, since the composite alone would pass even with the refs missing.

TST-geotag_execution_real-the_other_time.title: Against the real binary, on a camera JPEG holding CreateDate, ModifyDate, their offsets and sub-seconds: one copy given an XMP and an IPTC date too. Prep's read tells which fields each holds; geotag's time write puts the corrected local time into exactly those, each in its own format, read back by prep as written — so a re-plan finds nothing to write, and execute recognises its own write. ModifyDate, its offset and the sub-second fields keep their values; the copy without XMP or IPTC is given neither.

TST-geotag_far_offset-a_recorded_offset_.title: The offset a reset camera records is held like the zone's: accepted, it does not take effect. And a guess bound for the check against the tracks, with tracks by its recorded times but none by the times it gives, is withdrawn too — the check is an acceptance, and acceptance is not enough here.

TST-geotag_far_offset-a_reset_clock_asks.title: The camera reads 2000-01-01; a phone's photo of Bruges says 2026. The zone's guess, accepted, does not take effect: the cell asks, its proposal still shown with why. An offset the user writes takes effect as ever.

TST-geotag_far_offset-a_withheld_fix_off.title: A phone's fixes put it on the reset camera's day, 2000-01-01; another camera, its offset the user's own, says 2026. The phone's fix offset is far from that and withdrawn first; the reset camera's guess, near only the withdrawn phone, is then far from everything left and asks too.

TST-geotag_far_offset-measures_the_neare.title: The pure check: nothing to tell by → None; anything within the bound → None; else how far the nearest lies.

TST-geotag_far_offset-near_any_evidence_.title: A phone's photo within the largest clock error, or a track point there, is enough: the accepted guess takes effect, the proposal unmarked.

TST-geotag_far_offset-no_evidence_nothin.title: No other device's photo of the destination whose time is known: a reset clock is not told from a trip with no tracks — tracks of other years lying far from both — and the guess is taken on acceptance, as before. A file naming no device, and another camera whose offset is only a guess, are no such photo; a camera whose offset the user wrote is.

TST-geotag_finalize-a_cleared_position_i.title: A position geotag wrote and no longer places is cleared, and the log says so with the position the photo held; a manual position records the one it replaced.

TST-geotag_finalize-a_copy_in_another_de.title: One photo copied into two destinations — two records of one fingerprint — the plan placing only one copy: the other holds no position, and is named. Each copy is joined to the plan by the path the plan was built on.

TST-geotag_finalize-a_decision_changed_s.title: test a decision changed since execution stops finalize

TST-geotag_finalize-a_photo_not_as_execu.title: Between execute and finalize a photo is edited in another program, deleted, or a new one dropped in. Finalize records the photos as geotag's finished work, which merge then trusts: it refuses, naming the photo, rather than record the changed state as its own.

TST-geotag_finalize-a_plan_made_again_af.title: The way on works: `geotag plan` makes the plan anew — the unreadable one set aside under -NNN, as a re-plan sets aside any plan — and execute then carries it out.

TST-geotag_finalize-a_position_the_plan_.title: A photo prep read with no position, or at latitude 0 and longitude 0, holds the one the executed plan wrote it; a photo whose position the plan cleared holds none; one the plan did not touch holds what prep read.

TST-geotag_finalize-a_time_written_is_lo.title: Two phone photos written alike: one read by the offset its phone recorded, one by assuming the destination's zone. The log tells them apart, and says what each held before.

TST-geotag_finalize-a_used_track_changed.title: The track the executed plan rests on is changed — a point of another year added — and catalogued again as a plan does: its earlier entry stays in the record, withdrawn, beside the current one, the window's points alike in both. Finalize indexes the current entry alone: the tracks are as the plan was made from, and it seals them once.

TST-geotag_finalize-an_offset_is_describ.title: test an offset is described in words

TST-geotag_finalize-an_unreadable_kept_p.title: A kept plan that cannot be read stops finalize unless no execution ran it: one a summary names by its SHA-256, or one that may be the plan of a journal with a confirmed operation and no plan finalize can read — a run cut off before its summary — still stops it, naming the copy; one neither can be is passed over, and the package written.

TST-geotag_finalize-complete_log_superse.title: test complete log superset and geotag steps

TST-geotag_finalize-each_step_names_its_.title: The offset names its exact cell — with its day when the camera's photos there span days — or the drift confirmation that replaced it; a manual position names the pin or the folder fallback.

TST-geotag_finalize-every_geotag_step_na.title: Every step geotag adds to a photo's log names the run that made it: the plan that was executed.

TST-geotag_finalize-execute_checks_the_t.title: The plan records the window its tracks' fingerprint is of; execute takes the tracks again over it: a track of another year added since stales nothing, a point moved inside it stales the plan.

TST-geotag_finalize-execute_marks_the_tr.title: The offset the camera's own GPS gave rests on t.gpx: execute records it as used, and when the file is taken out the tracks, catalogued again as a plan does, name it and keep its points, withdrawn.

TST-geotag_finalize-execute_sends_an_unr.title: A photos-24 that cannot be read — torn, not JSON, not an object — stops execute with exit 2 and the way on, `geotag plan`, never a traceback: nothing is written to a photo, no summary or journal is written, and the file is left as it is.

TST-geotag_finalize-execute_stops_on_an_.title: A journal or an execution summary of the plan that cannot be read is never taken for none: execute stops before it keeps, snapshots or writes anything, naming the file, and leaves the file as it is.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_archives_th.title: The package is the whole control directory but its transient files — the drift record and every journal among it — listed with their hashes in the manifest and archived, manifest included, into the control directory itself.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_assembles_p.title: test finalize assembles package and is nondestructive

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_only_reads_.title: Finalize reads the workspace's database — it images it — and writes nothing to it: once geotag has executed, the database is, byte for byte and row for row, what it was before finalize, and finalize leaves no journal of a write beside it; it has been read all the same, into finalize's own image of it.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_records_eac.title: Finalize records every by-dest photo as geotag left it — under its final, renamed path — by size and modification time, so merge can refuse one changed after.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_refuses_a_p.title: Finalize reads each photo's position from what it holds — prep's reading of it, and what the executed plan wrote it — not from the plan's decisions alone: a photo that holds none, or latitude 0 and longitude 0, stops it, named, and nothing is packaged.
Finalize copies prep's log only as the handoff records it, by hash: a log changed since — or gone, which cannot be checked — stops finalize, nothing written, and sends the user back to prep.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_reports_how.title: The measure of a run: every photo counted by how it came by its position — in the plan, in finalize's output, and in the package's manifest.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_runs_withou.title: Finalize runs no tool on a photo, so it packages an execution with exiftool not installed; plan and execute, whose plan is written through it, stop without it.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_seals_witho.title: Finalize seals what the workspace keeps: with the tracks folder gone after execute it packages all the same, and never builds the tracks from gpx_root.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_sends_an_un.title: The executed plan, unreadable at finalize, stops it with exit 2, sending the user to `geotag plan`; no part of the package is written.

TST-geotag_finalize-finalize_stops_on_an.title: The plan's journal, a kept plan or any journal finalize reads to find the earlier passes, unreadable, stops finalize writing nothing: no pass is left out of the log unsaid, no photo judged by a baseline it lacks.

TST-geotag_finalize-geotag_keeps_its_rec.title: Where geotag reads and writes its records does not follow the configuration: with the default folders, or with every folder renamed, geotag plans, executes and finalizes from the records prep left in `.photos-ingest/` and writes its own there, and nowhere else.

TST-geotag_finalize-geotag_leaves_preps_.title: Geotag — plan, execute and finalize — writes its own image of the database and leaves prep's, byte for byte, as prep left it.

TST-geotag_finalize-geotag_never_reads_a.title: No database image is read back as working data: with prep's image, and then geotag's own, holding no database at all, geotag plans, executes and finalizes — and finalizes again to the same record — opening neither.

TST-geotag_finalize-geotag_runs_whole_wi.title: With snapshots off, as they are by default, geotag never reaches for a ZFS feature: on a machine with no `zfs` at all it plans, executes and finalizes.

TST-geotag_finalize-prep_after_finalize_.title: Prep may still run once geotag has finalized, the workspace not yet merged: every command of it — plan, dry run, execute, the quarantine's prune — leaves geotag's image of the database, byte for byte, as geotag left it, while prep's own image is written anew.

TST-geotag_finalize-summary_and_package_.title: An execution run again sets the earlier summary aside under -NNN; finalize run again sets the whole earlier package aside so, the archive as photos-26-archive-NNN.tar.gz — kept, and never archived again.

TST-geotag_finalize-the_log_says_what_pl.title: A photo the tracks placed has in its log the track that placed it and the time it was placed at. And a photo recorded under its new name by a prep run since the plan keeps the time steps of the row planned under its old one.

TST-geotag_finalize-the_tracks_decided_b.title: The track points the plan was decided by are in the database of record from the plan on — no scratch memo beside it — and finalize archives them, in the database and in its image.

TST-geotag_finalize-tracks_that_cannot_b.title: A tracks folder that cannot be listed cannot be checked: the plan stops on it, naming it, and execute finds the plan stale, changing nothing.

TST-geotag_finalize-write_db_snapshot_is.title: test write db snapshot is a valid copy

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-a_chosen_positi.nodeid: tests/test_geotag_gps_decisions.py::test_a_chosen_position_naming_no_photo_to_place_is_refused[6-photos-by-dest/T/gone.arw-names no photo of this destination] tests/test_geotag_gps_decisions.py::test_a_chosen_position_naming_no_photo_to_place_is_refused[6-photos-by-dest/U/q.arw-names no photo of this destination] tests/test_geotag_gps_decisions.py::test_a_chosen_position_naming_no_photo_to_place_is_refused[6-photos-by-dest/T/n.arw-holds a position of its own]
TST-geotag_gps_decisions-a_chosen_positi.title: A position chosen for a photo names one of its destination's photos holding no position of its own — or the run stops on it, naming it: a photo not there, one of another destination, one whose own position geotag keeps.

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-a_destination_n.title: test a destination never waits on its fallback

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-a_moved_photo_s.title: A position typed for a photo was given for the folder it lay in: moved to another destination — or its folder renamed — the photo is asked again, though its fingerprint would find the old answer.

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-a_photo_s_decis.title: A position the user set for one photo is that photo's — found again by its fingerprint once geotag has renamed it, never lost with the old name (nor given to another photo that takes the name).

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-a_position_chos.title: An entry the user adds by hand — the photo's path, `chosen_by_user`, a position — for a photo the tracks or the fallback place is honoured: the photo is placed there as `manual_locked`, out of the placed list.

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-a_position_give.title: A position given for one photo stays its own while it holds one — after tracks, then a fallback, come to place the photo — and only once the user empties it do the tracks place it again, its item gone.

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-an_inherited_fa.title: test an inherited fallback follows the parent

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-an_unplaced_pho.title: Every photo no source places is listed by itself with why the tracks placed nothing — how far the nearest track point is in time — and tracks that cover its time in different places are named, even where a folder fallback then places the photo and would hide it.

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-fallback_placem.title: test fallback placements told per destination

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-leave_unlocated.title: A photo is never left without a position: `accept_unlocated`, in a photos-23 still holding it, is a field a position decision does not have — refused, named, the record left as it is — whatever its value.

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-photos_23_lists.title: photos-23 names, per destination, each photo no review item names and how it is placed: by its own position, by the tracks (with the track's method) or by the folder fallback (with why the tracks did not place it) — each with its camera's day as photos-21 keys its offset cell. A photo that waits is a review item, not among them.

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-summary_counts_.title: test summary counts and review items

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-what_photos_23_.title: photos-23's `depends_on`: the resolved-UTC fingerprint, the tracks', the nine placement settings' and the handoff's content fingerprint — and nothing else.

TST-geotag_gps_decisions-written_fallbac.title: test written fallback outranks the inherited

TST-geotag_gps_ledger-a_cleared_position.title: BLD-position_tags: a clear drops the refs with the coordinates — a ref left behind without its coordinate is a torn fix.

TST-geotag_gps_ledger-a_pin_executed_the.title: test a pin executed then withdrawn plans and executes again

TST-geotag_gps_ledger-a_withdrawal_never.title: Withdrawing a decision changes GPS only as any plan would: geotag has no revert operation at all (time writes and renames are forward-idempotent), and it never moves a photo across destinations.

TST-geotag_gps_ledger-a_withdrawn_pin_gi.title: A pin withdrawn from a photo that had no GPS, off every track: the plan, deciding from its own values, gives it its folder's fallback over geotag's old position, and records the position it replaces.

TST-geotag_gps_ledger-a_withdrawn_pin_is.title: Withdrawn, the pin gives way to the position the tracks give the photo's own time: recomputed, not rolled back to anything stored.

TST-geotag_gps_ledger-geotag_plan_tells_.title: `geotag plan` says, for the destination, how many photos its fallback placed and whose fallback it is; photos-23 lists the photo with why the tracks missed it and its camera's day, the camera-GPS photos beside it.

TST-geotag_gps_ledger-own_values_pinned_.title: BLD-original_values_pinned: a photo's own values are committed to the ledger BEFORE geotag's first write to it. Order-probe both seams during execute and assert the pin precedes the write.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-a_break_between.title: The recording broke for a minute — two <trkseg> of one track, 70 m apart, well within what points are joined across. A photo in the break is never placed between them: it is placed past the end nearer it, along that segment's own heading, while within the extrapolation window; beyond, nothing places it, the break the reason. The same points in one segment are interpolated, as before.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-a_heading_is_ne.title: A photo before a segment of one point is placed at that point: the next segment's points, half a minute later, give it no heading.
A photo past the end of a track is carried on along THAT track's heading: a point of another file lying within the heading stretch — before the end, or as the last point of all — gives it none.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-a_projection_ha.title: How far and how fast a projection past a track's end may go is not what bounds joining two points.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-a_projection_is.title: The heading at a track's end is read over its last stretch, never its last two points alone, and a projection farther or faster than points are joined across puts the photo at the end itself.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-a_projection_wi.title: Past an end whose nearest other point lies outside the heading stretch, there is nothing to take a heading over: the photo is placed on the end itself, still `extrapolated` — never projected from a point that far.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-a_track_s_end_i.title: A photo two minutes after the day's track stops is placed past that track's end — whether or not a track of another day, a thousand kilometres off, exists: a track's end is where ITS recording stops.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-across_the_anti.title: Two points 200 m apart either side of longitude 180: the photo between them is at 180, not at 0.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-coordinates_to_.title: A position placed between two points, or projected past an end, is rounded to six decimal places; a direct match is the track point as the track gives it; and a photo already holding a position to six places, under the marker the write would carry, is written no position.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-extrapolation_s.title: test extrapolation single point uses endpoint

TST-geotag_gps_placement-extrapolation_z.title: test extrapolation zero span vector uses endpoint

TST-geotag_gps_placement-how_far_apart_t.title: test how far apart tracks disagree is its own setting

TST-geotag_gps_placement-one_trk_of_many.title: The nearest safe case: one <trk> is one track however many <trkseg> it holds, and a photo within a segment is interpolated as before; two files are two tracks as before.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-the_heading_str.title: How far back a track's heading is read is one setting, and how close a point is the photo's place another: moving either leaves the other's answer where it was.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-track_times_are.title: A track point's time is what the host Python's `datetime.fromisoformat` reads, a final `Z` taken as `+00:00`: the xsd:dateTime forms on every Python, the other ISO 8601 forms where this one takes them, and a time with no offset never — its point skipped, never read as some zone's.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-tracks_in_two_p.title: Two tracks cover the photo's time five kilometres apart — two people, and nothing says which carried the camera: the tracks place nothing, and say which of them disagree.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-two_tracks_are_.title: Two loggers a few metres apart, their points interleaved in time: the photo is placed on one of them, between two of ITS points — never between a point of one and a point of the other.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-two_trk_of_one_.title: An export holding two devices' tracks for the same hours, as two <trk> of one file: the photo is placed on one of them, between two of ITS points, never zig-zagging between them; and two that put the instant 5 km apart place nothing, both named, each by its place in the file. The placement names the file.

TST-geotag_gps_placement-why_the_tracks_.title: test why the tracks placed nothing is said

TST-geotag_gps_time-a_repeated_fix_time_.title: A stale fix: the GPS says 00:59:30 for two photos an hour apart. Nothing is proposed from the fixes — the photos' recorded offset is — and the cell says why. A burst (same fix time, same camera time) is one reading.

TST-geotag_gps_time-a_track_anchor_comes.title: A track passes where both photos were taken, at 00:30 and 01:30 UTC: the track's −34200 is proposed, the fixes' times not read.

TST-geotag_gps_time-applies_only_as_conf.title: test two fixes apply themselves only as the setting for several anchors allows

TST-geotag_gps_time-disagreeing_fixes_co.title: test fixes whose offsets disagree count for nothing

TST-geotag_gps_time-far_from_evidence_wi.title: A camera writing its local time into the GPS field: its fixes say 10:00 UTC, three days from the phone's photo of the same visit. The offset is shown, and the cell asks for one of the user's own.

TST-geotag_gps_time-fix_time_read.title: The composite `GPSDateTime` (zone `Z`, or an offset, a fraction dropped), else the date stamp with the time stamp; anything that is no time is none.

TST-geotag_gps_time-no_drift_check.title: Tracks lie by the photos' times but not by their places: the fixes' offset is the camera's own GPS's, and no drift cell follows it.

TST-geotag_gps_time-one_fix_is_a_proposa.title: One photo with a fix time: proposed, never applied by itself — `single_anchor_auto_apply` set or not. An acceptance holds within the decision tolerance, as one of a GPS proposal does.

TST-geotag_gps_time-only_own_position_ha.title: test the file model reads a fix time only with the photos own position

TST-geotag_gps_time-two_fixes_apply_them.title: No track: the two fixes' times agree on −32430 — the earliest's — and apply themselves, where the photos' recorded +01:00 and the zone's +09:00 are only guesses.

TST-geotag_local_time_readings-a_cameras.title: A camera's photos of 25 October 2026 in Berlin, at 01:00 (summer time) and 05:00 (winter time): the zone's offset is proposed at the earliest, −7200, and once accepted every photo of the day takes it — a camera's clock does not change at the switch. No photo of the day is asked about as a phone's would be.

TST-geotag_local_time_readings-a_reading.title: test a reading answers a time shown twice and no other value does

TST-geotag_local_time_readings-an_offset.title: 02:30 on 29 March 2026 never happened in Berlin: the photo's offset answers it — either reading, or another.

TST-geotag_local_time_readings-asked_wit.title: 02:30 on 25 October 2026 happened twice in Berlin: photos-21 asks for the photo, naming both readings, and is not complete; the photo resolves to nothing until answered.

TST-geotag_local_time_readings-geotag_pl.title: Through `geotag plan`: the phone's photo at 02:30 on the night Berlin's clocks went back is asked about in photos-21, nothing past it written; answered there by hand, the plan goes on.

TST-geotag_local_time_readings-the_answe.title: Renamed, the photo keeps its answer (its fingerprint); another photo taking its name does not take it.

TST-geotag_model-a_group_classed_twice_i.title: The classification geotag offers lists a new group under both classes, for the user to keep one. Pasted as it is, the group is classed as neither — geotag stops and offers it again — never taken for a phone.

TST-geotag_model-a_linked_folder_of_trac.title: A folder under gpx_root that is a link to tracks elsewhere is not followed — its tracks are not read — and it is said, by name; the tracks beside it are read as before.

TST-geotag_model-a_track_of_untimed_poin.title: test a track of untimed points is reported not empty

TST-geotag_model-a_tracks_folder_none_of.title: A tracks folder that is there, holding track files not one of which can be read — one malformed, one that cannot be opened — is not "no tracks": `geotag plan` stops before any record, naming the folder and each file with why. One file read among them, it plans, the others warned of as before; a folder holding no track file at all plans as having none.

TST-geotag_model-a_tracks_folder_that_is.title: Tracks configured but not there — a volume not mounted — are not "no tracks": geotag stops before any record, rather than place by fallback what the tracks place and drop the answers given about them. With no tracks configured, it plans.

TST-geotag_model-file_model_carries_the_.title: The fraction of a second prep read beside a photo's recorded time reaches geotag through the handoff.

TST-geotag_model-file_model_excludes_non.title: test file model excludes non bydest and videos

TST-geotag_model-geotag_reuses_handoff_c.title: RUL-geotag_reuses_camera_group: geotag reuses prep's camera_group_key from the handoff and never recomputes camera identity. The handoff carries a SENTINEL group key that the identity fields (Make/Model/serial) could never compose — if geotag recomputed from CAMERA_IDENTITY_FIELDS it would land on a different key. build_file_model and recognize_camera_groups must use the handoff's key verbatim.

TST-geotag_model-gpx_parser_accepts_frac.title: test gpx parser accepts fractional and whole seconds

TST-geotag_model-gpx_parser_skips_bad_tr.title: test gpx parser skips bad trkpts

TST-geotag_model-run_unknown_group_print.title: test run unknown group prints snippet and exits

TST-geotag_model-the_editor_s_camera_gro.title: What the decision editor asks the class of, found from the handoff and the configuration, is what geotag stops on: a group listed in neither array, or in both; never one classed, nor files naming no camera.

TST-geotag_neighbour_day-a_day_with_no_a.title: The half after midnight is offered the offset the evening's anchors settled, in place of the zone's guess — its own cell still, with a decision of its own.

TST-geotag_neighbour_day-the_day_after_a.title: With no anchored day before, the day after is offered, however long lies between the two days' photos; a day two days away is no neighbour.

TST-geotag_neighbour_day-with_tracks_it_.title: Tracks lie by the day's photos: the neighbour's offset is asked about once, as a timezone's guess is — photos-21 asks nothing, the offset going to the drift check unconfirmed, and photos-22 asks it; confirmed there, nothing asks any more, in either record, and the photos resolve by it.

TST-geotag_neighbour_day-without_tracks_.title: No track at all — the evening's clock settled by its fixes' own times: the neighbour's offset is asked in photos-21 instead, taking no effect until accepted there; accepted, it takes effect, and with no track to set it against, the drift check asks nothing of it.

TST-geotag_null_island-file_model_holds_.title: test file model holds zero point as no own position

TST-geotag_null_island-own_position_is_n.title: test own position is not exactly zero[0-0-False]

TST-geotag_null_island-position_written_.title: test position written over zero point is logged with it

TST-geotag_null_island-prep_reads_zero_p.title: test prep reads zero point as no native gps

TST-geotag_null_island-zero_point_is_nev.title: test zero point is never an anchor[zero point]

TST-geotag_null_island-zero_point_is_pla.title: test zero point is placed never kept nor counted native

TST-geotag_null_island-zero_point_off_th.title: test zero point off the tracks is placed like any other

TST-geotag_offset_inference-a_kept_offse.title: An offset found from the camera's GPS is kept for later photos of the day only while the tracks it was found from are there unchanged and no photo that arrived since says otherwise.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-a_picked_gro.title: test a picked group counts as gps backed

TST-geotag_offset_inference-a_place_walk.title: test a place walked on two days takes the photos day

TST-geotag_offset_inference-a_stay_of_th.title: The tracks stood an hour at the place two photos were taken (a museum, a lunch): the place says the photos were taken some time in that hour, not when. The offset proposed is one that fits, marked as no reading — never applied by itself — and a third photo taken on the move fixes it.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-a_written_of.title: test a written offset outranks an acceptance

TST-geotag_offset_inference-an_acceptanc.title: The user accepted "the camera was on local time" (−2 h). Then the zone above changed, or photos with GPS arrived that say otherwise: what is proposed now was never accepted, so it asks — the answer kept as written, applied to nothing.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-an_anchor_is.title: Two people 220 m either side of a photo's place: no segment joins a point of one track to a point of the other, so the photo anchors on neither.
