TST-geotag_offset_inference-an_anchor_ne.title: Two <trk> of one export, 220 m either side of a photo's place: the photo anchors on neither — as for two files. One track whose recording broke there — its last point before the break 220 m one side, its first after 220 m the other: no segment joins them, and the photo anchors on nothing. Unbroken, it anchors there.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-anchor_searc.title: test anchor search by place finds what the whole walk finds

TST-geotag_offset_inference-cell_conflic.title: test cell conflict requires input even with autoapply

TST-geotag_offset_inference-cell_single_.title: test cell single anchor conservative then flag

TST-geotag_offset_inference-cell_timezon.title: test cell timezone derived when no anchor

TST-geotag_offset_inference-clock_error_.title: RUL-anchor_within_clock_error: the clock-error matching window reads the frame's naive time AS UTC; the destination timezone is never used to bound matching. The matcher takes no timezone, and decorating the frame + cfg with a destination timezone leaves the match identical. Discriminating: the window is tight (3h) so if the naive time were re-read through a destination tz (Tokyo +9 / Honolulu -10, hours off) the GPX point would fall outside the window and the match would vanish — it does not.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-consensus_ma.title: test consensus majority beats closer minority

TST-geotag_offset_inference-each_pass_by.title: test each pass by a place is a candidate

TST-geotag_offset_inference-how_far_a_pr.title: test how far a proposal may move under an acceptance is its own setting

TST-geotag_offset_inference-how_long_a_s.title: How long, and how near, a track must stay for its anchor to be imprecise are settings of their own.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-no_offset_pr.title: A camera's bucket whose earliest time is one its destination's zone skips or repeats gets no offset from the zone — the zone gives two there: the cell asks for the offset, saying why. An hour later, the zone proposes as before.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-offsets_clus.title: A cluster stays centred on its best-ranked candidate — 0, 100 and 200 s apart in turn are two clusters, never one chained across 200 s; a tie goes to the offset smaller in magnitude, whatever its sign or rank, then to the cluster started first; and `groups` lists equal magnitudes by signed offset.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-out_and_back.title: A path walked out and back within the half hour: each leg is a pass of its own, so a photo on the way back is not timed by the way out because that leg's track ran a metre closer.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-proposal_rec.title: One anchor per photo that matched a pass — the representative first, a photo of another cluster by its own best — each with its match; `anchor_count` counts them, a photo that matched nothing not among them.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-the_segment_.title: A frame beside a segment anchors on it while the segment's two points are no farther apart in time than the anchor's own gap setting — whatever gap a photo may be placed across.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-two_days_not.title: test two days nothing tells apart wait for review

TST-geotag_offset_inference-what_is_one_.title: How soon a track must be back to have passed a place once is not how close offsets must be to agree.

TST-geotag_offset_inference-window_rejec.title: test window rejects same place other year

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_camer.title: A camera's offset tag says what its clock was set to, not where it was — a camera left on home time would stop every destination abroad. A phone's that agrees, or a photo with no offset, says nothing against.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_chose.title: The camera's GPS fixes its clock at −2 h in the museum by itself; in the castle the user picked −1 h 50 min from the camera's own GPS groups. One clock, two readings: the museum's, which nobody was asked about, waits for the user; the user's pick keeps its effect. Both name the other, and neither is passed on to the third destination.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_confi.title: The timezone's guess, never accepted in photos-21, is confirmed at the check against the tracks: that confirmation is its acceptance. Nothing asks any more — neither file — and the photo resolves under it.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_confl.title: One clock read two ways the same day: both cells ask. Taking a cell's own proposal as an acceptance settles nothing — it counts as what the GPS gave by itself, and is withheld again; the same offset written as the user's own (`manual_offset_seconds`, what the editor writes there) keeps its effect, and the conflict is settled.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_count.title: The user says which country a folder is, whatever it is called. A country of one timezone gives that zone to everything inside. One of several gives none: each destination inside answers for itself, among that country's zones only — and nothing reaches past it to a zone given above.

Inside a country of several timezones, a destination nothing gives a zone is proposed the one zone of the country whose offset at each photo's time is the one the photo records — and it applies itself, passing down as any zone does. Where no photo records an offset, or several zones fit, or none does, it asks as before; a zone reaching it from a folder inside the country comes first, and is held to the photos as ever.
Whatever the user wrote for a destination's country — a code no country has, or a value that is no code at all — is named as a blocker at that destination; nothing is taken from it.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_desti.title: A zone the user writes is set against the destination's photos like one inherited. Photos that record another offset stop it: the user picks their zone, moves them to a folder of their own, or keeps the zone by an explicit word that names the offsets it is given for — a photo with yet another offset asks again.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_group.title: An offset the user picked from the camera's own GPS groups rests on the camera's own positions: the castle, with none of its own, is offered it like any offset the camera's GPS gave that day — for the user to accept, the pick not having applied itself. An offset no group supports is the user's alone, and is passed nowhere.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_null_.title: `confirmed_despite_recorded_offsets: null` reads as no answer, as `null` does in every other field: the zone the photos speak against still asks, and nothing blocks.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-a_timez.title: A camera with no GPS, in a destination whose zone is known. With tracks by its photos the timezone's guess goes to the check against the tracks as it stands — one question, the confirmation — and nothing is resolved for planning until it is answered. With no track to check it against, it is accepted here.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-an_acce.title: The museum's offset of −2 h, proposed from the camera's own GPS, the user accepted as proposed; in the castle the user picked −1 h 50 min from the camera's GPS groups. Accepting said the GPS read the clock right, not that the user chose −2 h: the museum's counts as the positions' own, and waits for the user, as an offset that applied itself would; the pick keeps its effect.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-an_inhe.title: Lisbon, Porto, Madrid under one folder answered Europe/Lisbon. A phone's photo in Madrid records +02:00, which Lisbon never has in July: Madrid does not take Lisbon's zone unasked — and nor does what lies inside Madrid. One photo is enough. The user writes the zone.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-child_d.title: test child does not inherit resolved parent offset

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-nothing.title: A country is chosen once, at the top of its tree. One chosen inside another is taken out of the decision — whichever was written first — and the run says so, and why.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-one_clo.title: The camera's GPS fixes its clock at −2 h in one destination and −1 h 50 min in another, the same day: one of the two is wrong, and neither is applied until the user says — a hand-written offset being their word.

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-sibling.title: test sibling offset does not leak

TST-geotag_offset_no_inheritance-the_day.title: Museum in the morning, castle in the afternoon, one camera, one day. The museum's photos have GPS and fix the clock; the castle's have none. The castle is not asked to guess from the timezone: it takes the offset the camera's own GPS gave that day — by itself where that applied itself, else for the user to accept — and says where it came from.

TST-geotag_offset_tags-named_in_the_outp.title: test geotag plan names the photo whose offset tag is no offset

TST-geotag_offset_tags-recorded_and_read.title: test an offset tag that is no offset is recorded and read as none

TST-geotag_orchestration-a_run_with_noth.title: Every photo has its own position and the camera's offset resolves from them: nothing needs the user. Each decision stage still writes its record, complete, and the executable plan follows.

TST-geotag_orchestration-broken_decision.title: test broken decision is a located blocker[21-flag]

TST-geotag_orchestration-drift_confirmat.title: test drift confirmation must be a real yes

TST-geotag_orchestration-no_plan_while_a.title: A photo nothing places waits in photos-23; a destination with no timezone waits in photos-21. Either way the run makes no executable plan.

TST-geotag_orchestration-plan_reports_gp.title: test plan reports gpx load warnings capped

TST-geotag_orchestration-sealed_workspac.title: test sealed workspace with dump warns and blocks

TST-geotag_orchestration-the_host_s_zone.title: `localtime` resolves to wherever the run happens: a decision resting on it would change with the host.

TST-geotag_orchestration-unknown_group_a.title: test unknown group aborts before gpx ingest

TST-geotag_orchestration-unknown_group_t.title: test unknown group template is valid full json

TST-geotag_orchestration-unparseable_dec.title: test unparseable decision artifact blocks and is kept[not json-21]

TST-geotag_per_date-an_answer_follows_it.title: A camera's only day in a destination is answered; then a photo of the next day arrives there, and the cells become one per day. The first day's answer is still its answer — and the drift confirmation beside it — and only the new day asks. Back to one day, the answer follows again.

TST-geotag_per_date-multi_date_splits_in.title: test multi date splits into per day buckets

TST-geotag_per_date-single_date_keeps_ba.title: test single date keeps bare group key

TST-geotag_phone_clock-agreeing_phone_as.title: The track has the phone where its tags say, a minute off — within `gpx_anchor_decision_tolerance_seconds`: no cell, and its photos are read by their tags as before.

TST-geotag_phone_clock-fix_times_check_a.title: No track: two fixes say 08:00Z and 09:00Z where the tags read 07:00Z and 08:00Z — the phone's day is read by the fixes' offset.

TST-geotag_phone_clock-kept_as_recorded.title: The track is someone else's: kept as recorded, the phone's photos are read by their tags, the cell resolved.

TST-geotag_phone_clock-not_shared.title: The phone's anchored offset in Bruges says nothing of its photos in Ghent, where they hold no position: Ghent has no phone cell, and its photos are read by their tags.

TST-geotag_phone_clock-one_photo_is_a_pr.title: One photo on the track: proposed, never applied by itself — even with `single_anchor_auto_apply` on; accepted, it takes effect.

TST-geotag_phone_clock-several_disagreei.title: The tags read the photos by −7200; the two on the track agree on −3600: the anchored offset applies itself to every photo of the phone's day there, the one with no position included, the cell showing it.

TST-geotag_preflight-a_handoff_of_anothe.title: A handoff whose fingerprints were taken by another method than this build's — or that records no method — cannot be compared with the fingerprints geotag takes: plan, execute and finalize each refuse, naming the mismatch and telling the user to run prep again, and write nothing.

TST-geotag_preflight-a_link_among_the_ph.title: A photo in photos by destination replaced, since prep, by a link to the same file moved outside the workspace — same size, same time, so the handoff's record of it still holds — or a folder of photos linked in: every geotag command stops, naming the link, having changed nothing inside the workspace or outside it.

TST-geotag_preflight-a_missing_setting_s.title: A setting missing from the workspace's configuration is never filled from the program's defaults: prep's load, geotag and merge each stop, naming the setting and the value to add.

TST-geotag_preflight-a_photo_removed_or_.title: A by-dest photo prep recorded that is now gone, or differs in size or modification time from its record (a time edited in another program, say), stops planning with the re-prep blocker: geotag never plans on prep's reading of a file that no longer holds it.

TST-geotag_preflight-a_photo_with_no_fin.title: A photo in photos by destination prep could not fingerprint — its record's fingerprint holds no value, or it has none — stops geotag at plan, execute and finalize alike, the photo named, with what to do; the photos that have one pass unnamed.

TST-geotag_preflight-an_empty_folder_put.title: An empty folder put back in a missing managed folder's place restores it: geotag's preflight passes.

TST-geotag_preflight-an_unknown_setting_.title: A setting cartographer does not know is never ignored: prep's load, geotag and merge each stop, naming it — the user would otherwise believe it took effect.

TST-geotag_preflight-auto_reprep_execute.title: The nearest safe case: a plan that records the sort and otherwise quarantines only a file that is no media (an orphaned exiftool intermediate) is executed as before; one prep saved no readable plan for is not.

TST-geotag_preflight-auto_reprep_never_e.title: Prep's plan for a clean sort that would also rename, quarantine or move a media file — work in the by-date folders the user was never shown — is not executed: geotag stops, naming what the plan would do and telling the user to review and execute it themselves; the saved plan is left as it is.

TST-geotag_preflight-auto_reprep_runs_in.title: Geotag takes the workspace lock before it reads anything, and runs prep's plan and execute for a clean sort inside that same lock — no read before it, no other run slipping in between.

TST-geotag_preflight-auto_reprep_runs_pr.title: A recorded by-dest photo changed since prep (0-sources empty) is brought up to date the same way: geotag plan runs prep's plan then execute.

TST-geotag_preflight-auto_reprep_with_re.title: With prep itself planning (its fingerprint and metadata reading stood in for): the user sorts a photo into a destination and goes straight to geotag — prep's plan only records it, and geotag executes it. The user sorts another and, by mistake, leaves a copy of a third in the by-date folder — prep's plan would quarantine it, and geotag executes nothing: the copy stays where it is, and prep's record is as it was.

TST-geotag_preflight-dev_subfolder_block.title: test dev subfolder blocks at execute

TST-geotag_preflight-dev_subfolder_of_an.title: test dev subfolder of any case blocks[JPG]

TST-geotag_preflight-directory_symlink_a.title: A symlink at the root is barred outright as a forbidden symlink (RUL-no_links), never followed — checked before the structural/misplaced-folder guards.

TST-geotag_preflight-every_misplaced_roo.title: Any other top-level entry blocks, whatever its kind — a named pipe too — and the block names every one, not only the first.

TST-geotag_preflight-filename_format_oth.title: test filename format other than prep s blocks

TST-geotag_preflight-fingerprinted_photo.title: The nearest safe case: every photo in photos by destination fingerprinted — geotag proceeds.

TST-geotag_preflight-geotag_and_merge_cr.title: Run in a folder that is not a workspace, geotag and merge stop without creating the control directory — not even for their lock file. Only prep creates it.

TST-geotag_preflight-geotag_classifies_b.title: Geotag reads the workspace's own configuration, extension lists included: a `.webp` the user listed as an image is a photo in photos by destination, not a file of no media class — whatever the built-in lists say.

TST-geotag_preflight-geotag_never_repair.title: test geotag never repairs a missing folder

TST-geotag_preflight-handoff_of_another_.title: test handoff of another derivation version blocks[camera group key version]

TST-geotag_preflight-missing_managed_fol.title: The block gives the remedy, not only the fault: restore the folders, then geotag.
An activated workspace missing a managed 0-6 folder is non-conforming — hard stop.

TST-geotag_preflight-no_auto_reprep_on_a.title: A move that would be re-prepped, in a workspace whose shape is disturbed: geotag runs no prep — nothing is scanned or planned before the shape is checked.

TST-geotag_preflight-other_file_in_by_de.title: test other file in by dest blocks

TST-geotag_preflight-photo_left_in_by_da.title: test photo left in by date blocks

TST-geotag_preflight-root_hidden_file_al.title: A hidden file at the top level (a file manager's `.directory`) is a hidden entry, not a misplaced dump: it blocks nothing (RUL-top_level_only_managed).

TST-geotag_preflight-the_shape_is_checke.title: Geotag checks the workspace's shape before anything else it checks or does: with its shape disturbed and the handoff it would read next missing too, every geotag command stops on the shape alone (exit 2), naming it and not the handoff, having written nothing. (That the lock and the seal come first is TST-cli-the_lock_and_the_seal_come_before_the_shape.)

TST-geotag_preflight-unfingerprinted_pho.title: Through the command itself: plan, execute and finalize each refuse, naming the photo, and write nothing.

TST-geotag_preflight-unrecorded_by_dest_.title: test unrecorded by dest photo demands reprep

TST-geotag_preflight-untimed_photo_passe.title: A photo sorted into a destination by hand with no recorded time passes the preflight: its folder's date fallback may time it, and where none does photos-21 asks for one and geotag stops there (test_geotag_date_fallback).

TST-geotag_preflight-video_in_by_dest_bl.title: test video in by dest blocks

TST-geotag_preflight-what_ran_before_doe.title: The gates read the workspace as it stands now. The records of any number of earlier prep and sort cycles, and of a geotag run carried through execute and finalize, change neither answer: a workspace that satisfies the gates passes with them, and one that does not is stopped with them, exactly as without.

TST-geotag_recorded_offset-an_offset_tha.title: A value in the offset tag that is no offset is read as none, never loosely: with it only, the zone proposes.

TST-geotag_recorded_offset-asked_once_ag.title: Tracks lie by the photos: the recorded offset goes to the drift check as it stands, photos-21 asking nothing; the confirmation there is its acceptance, and the photo resolves under it.

TST-geotag_recorded_offset-different_off.title: Photos of one day recording +01:00 and +09:00: no offset is proposed from either — the zone's guess is made as it would be with none recorded — and the cell names the offsets it saw, with a count and a photo of each.

TST-geotag_recorded_offset-proposed_ahea.title: A body left on home time in Kyoto: its photos record +01:00, the zone is at +09:00. The proposal is the clock the photos record — −3600, not the zone's −32400 — and, with no track to check it against, it waits for the user's acceptance; accepted, it takes effect as the recorded offset accepted.

TST-geotag_recorded_offset-the_camera_s_.title: The offset the camera's own positions give — here, or the same day in another destination — is proposed before the one its photos record: GPS measures the clock, the tag states a setting.

TST-geotag_rename_planning-a_pair_takes_.title: A RAW and its JPEG, a HEIC and another of its stem, take one name with one suffix, each its own extension — the first name no other photo holds under any extension, so a photo never lands beside another photo's RAW or JPEG. Two photos of one extension sharing a stem are two photos; members whose corrected times differ are each named by their own.

TST-geotag_rename_planning-already_corre.title: test already correctly named is no rename

TST-geotag_rename_planning-burst_keeps_i.title: A burst prep named T, T-001, T-002 keeps that order under its corrected time — never path order, where `-` sorts before `.` and the bare name would come last.

TST-geotag_rename_planning-every_planned.title: A photo put in photos by destination by hand keeps the `.JPG` its camera wrote, prep leaving that folder as it finds it: geotag lowercases it. One whose name already carries its timestamp is renamed for its extension alone — by a temporary name, the change being one of case only — and one whose lowercase name another photo there holds (two names differing in case, on a filesystem that tells them apart) takes the next free suffix.

TST-geotag_rename_planning-first_free_su.title: test first free suffix fills a gap

TST-geotag_rename_planning-local_basenam.title: test local basename custom format and ext preserved
test local basename dst and standard

TST-geotag_rename_planning-move_between_.title: Moving a photo to a new destination re-evaluates its name under the NEW dest's timezone — the old destination's local time is never carried. geotag re-derives every run from the handoff (it keeps no cross-run resolution cache), so the same resolved UTC under Brussels vs Tokyo yields different destination-local names.

TST-geotag_rename_planning-only_a_numeri.title: test only a numeric suffix counts

TST-geotag_rename_planning-repeated_hour.title: In the hour Brussels repeats as its clocks go back, names are its local time: a photo taken at 00:45 UTC (02:45 summer time) is named after one taken half an hour later at 01:15 UTC (02:15 winter time), and sorts after it. The true order is in the metadata.

TST-geotag_rename_planning-sub_second_or.title: Where the photos record a fraction of a second, it orders them before the suffix they hold; a photo recording none comes after those that do. Photos of one local second an hour apart — the hour a zone repeats — go by their true time first.

TST-geotag_rename_planning-sub_second_re.title: The fraction of a second is read from prep's record: written in the recorded time itself, else from the EXIF sub-second field beside it — its digits; none where neither holds one.

TST-geotag_rename_planning-suffixed_name.title: test suffixed name of the right time kept

TST-geotag_rename_planning-suffixes_do_n.title: Which photo of a destination gets which differentiating suffix does not depend on the order the photos are met in: the same photos, presented in every order, are given the same names.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_changed_time_.title: Answered `new`, the time the photo holds is its true local time: read by its destination's zone, the camera's ten minutes slow not applied to it again, the photo placed and named by it and its other time fields brought into line; execution records it beside the pin, its own values staying, so the next plan asks nothing and writes nothing — and goes on reading it as the true time.
Answered `geotag`, the photo is planned as any photo whose time is not the one geotag decides: geotag's time is written back over the one it holds, decided from its own time as before.
An answer names the time it was given for: the photo's time changed again, it is stale and asks again; a value that is no answer is a blocker naming the field, the record left as it is.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_copy_that_wou.title: Were finalize's copy to change prep's record, finalize writes nothing and says so.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_devices_own_m.title: A phone's own GPSProcessingMethod is not geotag's: its position is kept and its time is not taken as corrected. Its time standing as it is, geotag writes no mark of a corrected time into it — only its name changes — and read back the phone's GPS is still native, its own value unmarked.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_fingerprint_m.title: test a fingerprint mapping not one to one stops geotag

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_fingerprint_t.title: The image engine upgraded and then put back: a photo's fingerprint goes A → B → A. For a photo with no pin, the walk back through its earlier values comes round to where it started — and stops there, pinless, rather than going round for ever.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_history_too_t.title: Finalize never shows as whole what it cannot rebuild: a photo carrying geotag's mark that no pass here first corrected is marked partial, and a pass whose plan is gone is named in a warning.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_kept_time_is_.title: The log records a time kept as the photo's true time, naming the photos-21 entry that kept it, for the pass being finalized and for an earlier one alike — and no clock offset applied.

A camera with its own GPS, its clock found from its positions on the track. One photo's time set by hand to the true time and kept: its position, against the kept time, would read the clock two minutes otherwise — it is no reading of the camera's clock, so the cell's offset rests on the other photo alone, and is applied to it alone.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_kept_time_s_o.title: The time set by hand with an offset tag Brussels did not have then (+09:00): the question records the tag and the zone's offset and the plan says so, naming the photo. Kept, the time is read by the zone, not by the tag, and the tag is written to the zone's.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_kept_time_the.title: A time kept as the true local time that Brussels shows twice — 02:30 on the night the clocks go back — is asked which of its two readings it is, as any time the zone reads; answered, it is read by that one.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_marked_photo_.title: A photo geotag marked before (elsewhere) holds no original values: nothing is pinned, and its time is taken as fixed.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_phone_holding.title: A phone photo holding the right local time, its offset and its own position, under the name geotag would give it, needs nothing: no operation at all — no mark of a corrected time geotag never wrote — and a re-run decides it from its own values again, with the same result.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_photo_holding.title: The time geotag writes is recorded beside the pin before it is written; a re-plan of a photo holding it, or holding its own time put back, is not blocked — and a changed decision after execute still reaches it.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_photo_whose_f.title: test a photo whose fingerprint changed keeps its own values

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_time_changed_.title: A time kept and executed is the one geotag decides from: the photo's time changed by hand again, the question names the kept time as the photo's own, and taking back geotag's writes the kept time back — never the camera's own time corrected again.

A photo geotag corrected to 14:30 +02:00 from its own 14:20, then changed in another tool: photos-21 asks about it — naming the time it holds, the time geotag wrote and its own — and nothing is planned past it: geotag neither writes its time back nor decides from the new one unasked.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-a_time_read_fro.title: Geotag rewrites a photo's CreateDate and its offset with the corrected time, so both are pinned: a phone photo whose time was read from CreateDate is resolved again by the offset its phone recorded, never by the destination's offset geotag wrote — and the comparison side keeps what the photo holds now.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-an_interrupted_.title: A write that landed but was never confirmed — the photo's fingerprint could not be taken after it — leaves the photo holding geotag's time with no record in the journal. The time was recorded before the write, so the re-plan takes it as geotag's: not blocked, the time not written again, the rename still to do.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-an_unvouched_pr.title: A plan made on a vouched log, the log then changed under it: execution would carry the pinned values by a mapping nothing vouches for. It stops before any change — no snapshot, no decision kept, no write, no pin moved — exits 2, and sends the user to prep, then to plan again.

Prep's log says which photo's fingerprint was taken again from which; one the handoff does not vouch for says nothing to trust of it. The plan stops, writing nothing, and sends the user to prep — never planning as though no fingerprint had changed, which would lose a photo's pinned values.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-changed_offset_.title: A wrong offset, once executed, is fixed in the record: the re-run works from the photo's own camera time and corrects it once, under the new offset.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-finalize_carrie.title: Finalize's log carries prep's every field and step unchanged, a note of prep's among them, and adds only its own: geotag's note goes in a step of its own.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-geotag_position.title: A position geotag wrote is not the file's own: the re-run places the file from the track again and overwrites a fix that no longer agrees, and it is never a clock anchor.

A file geotag once placed, now off the track: geotag's old fix is not taken as its own — it waits for the user, no plan made, and once its folder has a fallback it is placed there, the old fix written over and kept for the log.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-geotag_writes_o.title: Geotag's plan, execution and finalize leave prep's part of the database exactly as it was, and merge's untouched.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-gps_derived_off.title: An offset found from the camera's own GPS stays the camera's offset for the day once those photos are corrected, so a later photo without GPS needs no answer.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-manual_offset_i.title: test manual offset is not applied twice

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-new_photo_joins.title: Same camera, same day: the earlier answer — offset and drift confirmation — is kept through a run where every photo was already corrected, and applied to the new photo alone.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-only_a_written_.title: The suffix goes on a photo whose time this plan writes, or whose field already carries geotag's mark; a photo whose time is resolved to what it holds gets none.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-originals_are_p.title: test originals are pinned once and complete

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-own_gps_camera_.title: With their own values pinned, a GPS camera's photos give the offset again on a re-run, as on the first: nothing is kept from earlier, and nothing is written.
A camera with its own GPS has its time corrected from that GPS, keeps the position, and is marked time-fixed; the re-run then neither corrects it again nor uses it as an anchor.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-the_log_keeps_e.title: Finalize logs what every executed pass did, in order and matched by fingerprint — not only the latest plan's operations: a photo corrected, then corrected again, then left alone shows all three.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-the_record_foll.title: Where every photo is marked and none has its own values pinned, the kept answer is derived from the decision, so the record never shows an effective value the decision no longer says.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-the_track_is_no.title: A photo the track placed is recorded with the track; what execute writes into the photo — its time, its position and how it was found — names no track.

TST-geotag_rerun_markers-withdrawn_offse.title: test withdrawn offset after execute asks again

A manual offset, five minutes off what the camera's own GPS photos give, is executed: the photo is corrected and named under it. Withdrawn, the offset gives way to the one the tool derives, and the photo's time and name are computed again from its own camera time — for the file where it now stands, under the name the withdrawn decision gave it, and within its destination.

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-a_phone_time_tak.title: test a phone time takes the offset recorded with it[EXIF:DateTimeOriginal-OffsetTimeOriginal]

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-a_photos_scope_n.title: test a photos scope names the cell its offset came from

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-a_time_at_the_ca.title: test a time at the calendar s edge is unresolved not a crash[0001:01:01 00:00:00-SONY|ILCE-6400|123]

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-a_time_the_zone_.title: A photo whose time is read through its destination's zone — a phone's or a file's naming no camera with no offset recorded, a corrected photo whose offset tag is gone — at a time the zone skips (Berlin, 29 March 2026, 02:30 never happened) or repeats (25 October 2026, 02:30 happened twice) is left unresolved, the case named: never resolved to one of its two readings. An hour away, the same photo resolves as before.

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-a_time_with_its_.title: The nearest safe cases: at the same skipped time, a phone's photo recording its offset, and a camera's photo resolved by its clock offset, resolve exactly as before — neither is read through the zone.

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-an_offset_within.title: A time whose own value states its zone (XMP writes `…+09:00`, `…Z`) is turned to UTC by that — never read as the destination's local time, which would move it by the difference.
A time whose value states its own offset, with an offset field beside it that says something else: the one within the value is the one the time is read by.

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-an_unclassified_.title: A group classed as neither phone nor camera — or not classed at all — is never solved as a phone would be, by the offset recorded with its time or the destination's timezone: its photos stay unresolved.

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-the_offset_writt.title: A zone's offset before it kept standard time has seconds (Amsterdam, 1935: +01:19:32). The offset field holds hours and minutes: it is written to the nearest minute, never as `+01:1932`, which reads back a day out.

TST-geotag_resolved_utc-unrelated_config.title: RUL-times_survive_unrelated_config_edits: a config edit OUTSIDE the time-policy subset re-plans but must NOT restale already-resolved UTC. The resolved-UTC cache fingerprint is built from time-relevant inputs only (photos-21 sha, the camera-time-policy fingerprint, GPX, prep cache, field-set/key versions) — not a whole-config hash. Here we edit `merge.library_root` (a merge-phase key, untouched by geotag) and re-run: photos-21 stays byte-identical and the resolved_utc_cache_fingerprint is unchanged.

TST-geotag_set_aside_jpegs-a_held_raw_ho.title: A RAW whose rename does not happen keeps its JPEG's name with it: the JPEG is renamed only once its RAW's rename is confirmed.

TST-geotag_set_aside_jpegs-a_jpeg_left_b.title: An earlier run renamed the RAW without its JPEG: the RAW holds its corrected time and name and geotag's mark, the JPEG is still under the camera's time. The plan renames nothing in photos by destination, and the JPEG to the name its RAW holds — a rename only, after no other — and the pair keeps one name.

TST-geotag_set_aside_jpegs-a_raw_culled_.title: A RAW culled from photos by destination after geotag renamed it and its JPEG: prep's next plan does not stop on the JPEG as misnamed — it quarantines it, its step naming the RAW by the path it was culled at and by fingerprint — and the execution leaves a workspace the next check finds unchanged.

TST-geotag_set_aside_jpegs-a_renamed_jpe.title: Finalize checks the JPEG the plan renamed with its RAW as it checks the photos: one changed since execution stops it, named under the folder it is in — not as a photo of photos by destination.

TST-geotag_set_aside_jpegs-a_video_keeps.title: A video keeps the name prep gave it from its camera's clock, uncorrected, while geotag corrects the names of the photos the same camera took in the same minutes.

TST-geotag_set_aside_jpegs-prep_after_ge.title: After geotag's execution the renamed JPEG is no change to the workspace check — the execution recorded it — and prep's next plan takes its name, its RAW's, as rightly given: no misnamed stop, and nothing moved or renamed. The same JPEG under a name of neither its time nor its RAW's still stops prep.

TST-geotag_set_aside_jpegs-renamed_with_.title: The JPEG set aside beside a RAW geotag renames takes the RAW's new name, its own extension kept: one rename, planned after the RAW's, and no tag written to it. One whose RAW is not in photos by destination, and one prep recorded no RAW for, are left as they are.

TST-geotag_several_bodies-an_offset_from.title: Two anchors agreeing would apply themselves for one camera; for a group named several bodies they are a proposal, noted as such — taking effect once accepted; so too two GPS fix times.

TST-geotag_several_bodies-its_days_in_tw.title: One body's photos sorted into A, the other's into B, the same day: for one camera the two offsets its GPS gives would be one clock read two ways, both withheld; for several bodies each is its destination's own proposal. And a destination where the group has no position of its own is offered no offset from the other.

TST-geotag_several_bodies-the_setting_na.title: By default no group is several bodies; the setting is a list of fixed-clock camera groups, each named once — a phone's group, an unclassed one, a key named twice or anything but a list is refused.

TST-geotag_time_decisions-a_file_naming_.title: test a file naming no camera is solved alone never asked

TST-geotag_time_decisions-a_photo_timed_.title: test a photo timed by its creation is the camera s
test a photo timed by its modification opens no day
test a photo timed by its modification takes no camera offset

TST-geotag_time_decisions-bad_timezone_b.title: test bad timezone blocks and leaves artifact

TST-geotag_time_decisions-classifying_a_.title: test classifying a camera again restales the time decisions

TST-geotag_time_decisions-determinism_un.title: test determinism unchanged rerun is byte identical

TST-geotag_time_decisions-new_destinatio.title: Media added to a new destination asks for that destination's decisions alone; every settled decision elsewhere stays as the user left it.

TST-geotag_time_decisions-rerun_after_su.title: A successful execution and a finalize leave geotag re-runnable; only merge's seal stops it.

TST-geotag_time_decisions-rerun_preserve.title: test rerun preserves decisions and completes

TST-geotag_time_decisions-timezone_propo.title: A destination's timezone proposal prefers the nearest RESOLVED ancestor's timezone over the generic global default; an inherited proposal auto-resolves without per-destination confirmation (nested geography), staying overridable; the configured default is only proposed.

TST-geotag_track_precedence-a_lower_trac.title: A camera photo taken where the receiver passed at 12:05 — when the phone, recording, was 5 km away: the receiver anchors nothing then. Where the phone recorded nothing — projecting past its end is no record — the receiver anchors.

The phone stopped at noon; the receiver ran on. A photo of the afternoon is placed by the receiver, with nothing to compare. A photo a minute past the phone's end, which the phone could only project to: the receiver covers the instant and places it — a projection is no witness against a track that recorded the time.

TST-geotag_track_precedence-a_ranked_fol.title: A ranked folder that is not under the tracks folder — misspelt, or not made yet — would rank nothing in silence: it is warned of, first, and the tracks are read as usual.

TST-geotag_track_precedence-a_track_rank.title: The first folder named ranks first; a track deeper inside it ranks as it; a track in no ranked folder, or at the top of the tracks, ranks below every ranked one, all such alike. Nothing ranked: all alike.

TST-geotag_track_precedence-lower_tracks.title: Three photos the phone placed: at two the receiver lay 5 km off, at one 20 m. The GPS decisions count the two, by track, and nothing asks about them.

TST-geotag_track_precedence-the_higher_r.title: Phone and receiver both cover the photo's time, five kilometres apart: unranked, that is two people and nothing is placed; ranked, the phone places it — even by a point between two, against the receiver's point at the very second — and the receiver's distance is kept with the position.

TST-geotag_track_precedence-the_position.title: The plan's position write keeps, beside the track that placed the photo, how far the receiver put it.

TST-geotag_track_precedence-the_ranking_.title: The same files ranked another way are other evidence: the tracks' fingerprint — which every record geotag derives from them depends on — changes with the ranking, and only with it.
The ranking names folders directly under the tracks folder, each once.

TST-geotag_track_precedence-tracks_of_on.title: A companion's track filed in no ranked folder, with another unranked one: two of one rank five kilometres apart are still two people, named, and the photo is not placed. A ranked track above both settles it.

TST-geotag_untagged_photos-asked_where_n.title: No tagged sibling, no position, no track: the zone's reading is proposed for the phone's untagged photos of the day and waits for acceptance; accepted, each photo is read by the zone at its own time — the phone's clock follows the daylight-saving change of 27 October 2024 (02:30 → +01:00 after, +02:00 before).

TST-geotag_untagged_photos-camera_less_a.title: test the answer holds for later files while the zone is the one answered

TST-geotag_untagged_photos-camera_less_f.title: test files naming no camera are one question for the destination

TST-geotag_untagged_photos-read_as_the_t.title: test an untagged photo is read by the zone where its tagged siblings show the zone

TST-geotag_untagged_photos-rides_the_dri.title: Tracks lie by the untagged photos' times: nothing is asked in photos-21, and the drift check holds the photos the cell offsets — the untagged ones alone.

TST-geotag_untagged_photos-settled_by_it.title: One untagged photo with its own position lies on the track where the zone reads it: that settles the day's untagged photos — the anchored offset applies itself to them, unasked.

TST-geotag_untagged_photos-tagged_siblin.title: The phone's tagged photos record +01:00 where Brussels is at +02:00 (kept despite them): its untagged photo is proposed the offset its siblings record, not the zone's.

TST-guards_quarantine-a_folder_not_empty.title: A planned removal finding its folder not empty leaves it, skipped in the journal and reported; the run still succeeds.

TST-guards_quarantine-a_hidden_top_level.title: Once the workspace is initialized, an empty hidden folder at the top level is the user's: no plan removes it.

TST-guards_quarantine-a_manifest_that_ca.title: A manifest that can be neither read nor set aside stops the quarantine move before the file is moved: the manifest keeps its bytes, the duplicate stays where it was, and the run fails.

TST-guards_quarantine-an_interrupted_man.title: The quarantine's manifest, rewritten whole for each entry and interrupted — while the new text is half written, or with it written but not yet in the manifest's place — holds its earlier entries whole, and the next entry goes down with them, whole.

TST-guards_quarantine-band_guard_blocks_.title: test band guard blocks raw under video band
test band guard blocks video under photo band

TST-guards_quarantine-folders_left_empty.title: The folders a plan leaves empty — emptied by its moves, or empty already — are planned removals, deepest first, journaled as they run; a folder holding a file the plan leaves is not.

TST-guards_quarantine-prune_by_age_reads.title: A run's age is the time in its plan id; --plan-id and --older-than-days together select the runs either names.

TST-guards_quarantine-prune_dry_run_dele.title: test prune dry run deletes nothing

TST-guards_quarantine-prune_yes_with_pla.title: test prune yes with plan id deletes only that

TST-guards_quarantine-prune_yes_without_.title: test prune yes without selector or all refuses

TST-handoff-a_files_inode_is_in_the_hand.title: Each file of the handoff carries its inode as its database row recorded it, and both the content fingerprint and the inventory's fingerprint cover it: another inode alone, size, time and fingerprint the same, changes both.

TST-handoff-camera_group_of_each_file_in.title: Prep keeps each file's camera group in its own records — the workspace database, against the path the file was organized to — not only in what it hands geotag.

TST-handoff-conflict_attributed_to_by_de.title: test conflict attributed to by dest folder

TST-handoff-grouping_facts_identity_and_.title: test grouping facts identity and device class

TST-handoff-handoff_content_fingerprint_.title: The content fingerprint is byte-stable across no-op reruns: it excludes run_metadata, diagnostics, the execution-journal pointer, itself, and the NESTED per-run audit (cache_freshness counts in camera_groups/destination_folders, and conflicts_or_duplicates); only real content moves it.

End-to-end (RUL-run_only_refresh_restales_nothing): a second prep run that changes nothing organized produces the SAME handoff content_fingerprint, even though run_metadata + cache-freshness counts differ run to run.

TST-handoff-handoff_is_rewritten_fresh_e.title: RUL-prep_records_written_whole: the handoff is written deterministically and NEVER edited in place — each successful run rewrites it wholesale. Inject a sentinel key into the on-disk handoff, then re-run prep: a non-editable rewrite drops the sentinel entirely (it is regenerated, not merged/appended), and the fresh write is reflected by a new run_metadata.execution_id.

TST-handoff-no_handoff_built_while_a_lin.title: Prep builds no handoff while a link is present anywhere it walks — the destination tree it never changes included — and leaves the earlier one as it was; with the link gone it builds one again. So the handoff geotag and merge find is always one built with no link present.

TST-handoff-roundtrip_assertion_catches_.title: If the just-written handoff would NOT re-read to the same content_fingerprint (a non-round-trip- stable field crept in), prep fails loudly rather than shipping a forever-stale handoff.

TST-handoff-the_configuration_classes_ca.title: Of camera grouping the configuration sets which groups are phones and which have fixed clocks, and nothing more: the same camera classed as a phone, as a fixed-clock camera or as neither is the same group, derived the same way, under the code's version of the derivation; a setting naming how a group is derived, or that derivation's version, is refused.

TST-handoff-unknown_device_class_when_no.title: test unknown device class when not configured

TST-hidden_folders-empty_hidden_folder_a.title: test empty hidden folder and hidden files left alone

TST-hidden_folders-hidden_folder_holding.title: test hidden folder holding a photo blocks[2-missing-metadata]
Any file counts, a hidden one or one of no media class too.

TST-hidden_folders-inbox_hidden_folder_g.title: In the inbox a hidden folder does not block: everything in it — a photo too — goes to the quarantine, recoverable, as today.

TST-hidden_folders-reprep_gate_agrees_wi.title: The re-prep gate names the hidden folder prep blocks on — never a photo inside it, which no re-prep could record — and says nothing of an empty one.

TST-idempotency_cache-a_failed_execute_l.title: An execute that fails on an operation after others were carried out commits none of its database effects: the database is as the earlier run left it.

TST-idempotency_cache-chronological_dest.title: RUL-suffix_no_clobber (anti): a 0-sources file whose computed chronological destination in 5-photos-by-date collides with an EXISTING path must not clobber. setup_workspace seeds 5-photos-by-date/2023-01-01/2023-01-01--12-00-00.jpg = "already_date" and a 0-sources file (new_img, "new_source") that resolves to the same date/name. Prep must (a) plan a move_no_clobber to a suffixed name, never the occupied target, and (b) on execute, land the incoming under the safe -001 name while the colliding original stays byte-unchanged.

TST-idempotency_cache-execute_applies_on.title: RUL-execution_only_the_plan (anti): execute applies ONLY the recorded plan operations; it never re-derives the organization from the filesystem. Drop the new_img move op from the saved plan before executing: if execute re-derived it would still move new_img to 2-missing-metadata. Instead new_img stays EXACTLY where it is (0-sources, untouched), while the operations that REMAIN in the plan (the dup_img quarantine) still apply — proving execute is plan-driven, not a fresh derivation.

TST-idempotency_cache-no_special_reimpor.title: A file in 2-missing-metadata still missing a date stays put (no op); one moved from there into 0-sources routes like any ordinary dump — here, to 5-photos-by-date by its (now present) date. (One given a time where it lies is filed on from there: test_time_given_filed_on.)

TST-idempotency_cache-prep_idempotency_a.title: test prep idempotency and by dest accounting

TST-idempotency_cache-prep_replans_from_.title: The prep journal is EVIDENCE, not a resume script: prep re-plans from the filesystem (+ cache) as truth. After a successful run, corrupting then deleting the journal must NOT change the re-plan — it still derives 0 operations from the on-disk state and never reads the journal to resume.

TST-idempotency_cache-quarantine_manifes.title: RUL-evidence_before_quarantine: the manifest evidence entry for a quarantined file is written BEFORE the file is moved into quarantine, so a crash never strands a file in quarantine with no record of why. Probe by wrapping both _append_quarantine_manifest and the move primitive _move_no_clobber to log a label in call order; setup_workspace's dup_img is the quarantined file. Assert the manifest append for the run precedes the quarantine move.

TST-idempotency_cache-quarantine_subtree.title: RUL-not_inventoried: the quarantine directory is excluded from the scan, so a rerun neither re-organizes nor re-quarantines its contents. A media file sitting under .photos-ingest-quarantine/<id>/ is never inventoried: no operation references it and it never enters the cache, while a real 0-sources photo is organized normally.

TST-idempotency_cache-restored_quarantin.title: No un-quarantine path: a file dragged back out of quarantine into 0-sources is re-evaluated as an ordinary fresh dump under a NEW plan_id — there is no special 'restore' handling that skips dedup. Here the restored file is still a duplicate of a by-dest photo, so it is quarantined AGAIN.

TST-idempotency_cache-stale_ghost_prune_.title: test stale ghost prune reappeared file aborts before cache remove

TST-kept_tracks-a_build_that_kept_nothin.title: Execute's check keeps nothing, and prunes nothing: the record is as planning left it.

TST-kept_tracks-a_changed_track_is_read_.title: A changed file is read and parsed again: its new points are decided by, and its earlier entry, which no executed plan used, leaves the record. A file touched without a change is read, and keeps its entry.

TST-kept_tracks-a_folder_that_cannot_be_.title: A folder of the tracks that cannot be listed is no folder of no tracks: the index says it cannot see them, and nothing it holds is taken for gone.

TST-kept_tracks-a_kept_point_keeps_its_t.title: A point read from the record is the point parsing gave: its <trk> and its <trkseg> with it.

TST-kept_tracks-a_narrower_window_prunes.title: A plan whose window narrows — a photo moved out, a setting tightened — leaves the record holding only its window's points: those outside it go, the fingerprint is the one the narrow window gives, and the file is read again if a later window reaches there.

TST-kept_tracks-a_new_track_is_read.title: test a new track is read

TST-kept_tracks-a_track_gone_is_told_and.title: A track file taken out is named, and decided by no longer; no executed plan used it, so its entry and points leave the record.

TST-kept_tracks-a_wider_window_reads_the.title: The window grown — a photo sorted in, a setting widened — reads again each file whose span from its first point to its last meets the new part, and only those: the points there are then kept and decided by.

TST-kept_tracks-an_unchanged_track_is_no.title: A track file whose size, modification time and inode are as the catalogue has them is not read again: its points, warnings and SHA-256 come from the record, exactly as reading it would give them.

TST-kept_tracks-execute_leaves_the_catal.title: Checking the tracks keeps nothing: a changed file is read, and the record is as planning left it.

TST-kept_tracks-geotag_plan_prunes_once_.title: `geotag plan` prunes the record to the window it reached once it has stopped — at a decision for the user, or at a blocker — never mid-run, where a window still to widen would read its files again, and never when interrupted.

TST-kept_tracks-points_an_executed_plan_.title: The points of a track an executed plan placed or timed photos by, in the window that plan was made in, stay when a later plan's window no longer reaches them: they are the evidence of what was written into the photos. A track it did not use is pruned.

TST-kept_tracks-the_catalogue_and_the_wi.title: Every track file is catalogued — path, its rank's folder, size, modification time, inode, SHA-256, first and last point time — and the points in the window are kept as decided on; points outside it are not.

TST-kept_tracks-the_drift_check_s_reach_.title: The drift check sets a bucket's photos, at their corrected times from the first to the last, against the tracks the drift window either side: the window holds all of it, the hours between two photos of the day included.

TST-kept_tracks-the_kept_points_are_read.title: The points the record keeps give the same index, fingerprint and all, with the tracks folder gone.

TST-kept_tracks-the_points_an_executed_p.title: A track an executed plan placed or timed photos by keeps its points in the record, withdrawn, when it is taken out or changed: the evidence of what was written into the photos survives. Back with the same bytes, it is the file's again.

TST-kept_tracks-the_window_grows_with_th.title: The window is each reader's own reach: a photo sorted in widens it to its camera time, a setting widened widens it by as much, the corrected times widen it for the drift check and for placement.

TST-kept_tracks-the_window_holds_every_p.title: Anchoring and placement decide the same over the window as over every point there is: a week of tracks from two ranked devices, broken and sparse, the photos' candidates and placements compared one by one.

TST-kept_tracks-tracks_of_another_time_l.title: Tracks added, or a track file grown, at times no photo reaches change nothing the tracks decide: the fingerprint is of the window's points. A point added inside the window changes it, as does the ranking.

TST-lifecycle-a_folder_left_in_the_inbox.title: A prepped workspace whose inbox holds only an empty folder is not "nothing to do": geotag counts any entry there, so prep plans the folder's removal and its execution carries it out, leaving the inbox empty.

TST-lifecycle-a_log_the_handoff_does_not.title: A prepped workspace whose log is not the one its handoff records — a crash between the two writes — is not "nothing to do": prep runs its execution again, which rewrites both.

TST-lifecycle-a_prep_only_workspace_has_.title: Prepped and never geotagged, the workspace still holds a whole record of prep: every photo's journey keyed by its fingerprint, ending where the photo now is, with prep's database snapshot beside it — and nothing of geotag's or merge's is needed for it.

TST-lifecycle-an_interrupted_guard_write.title: The workspace guard, written last by an init run and interrupted — while half written, or written but not yet in its place — is left as it was before, absent, never a damaged guard: the workspace is still uninitialized, and the next run puts the guard down whole.

TST-lifecycle-by_dest_reprep_pending_hel.title: test by dest reprep pending helper

TST-lifecycle-dry_run_on_prepped_workspa.title: test dry run on prepped workspace with empty sources is nothing to do

TST-lifecycle-execute_on_prepped_workspa.title: test execute on prepped workspace with empty sources is nothing to do

TST-lifecycle-execute_with_a_changed_by_.title: test execute with a changed by dest photo is not nothing to do

TST-lifecycle-guard_written_last_then_re.title: test guard written last then reentry is clean

TST-lifecycle-init_creates_structure_and.title: test init creates structure and moves dump structure preserved

TST-lifecycle-init_move_to_a_taken_inbox.title: test init move to a taken inbox path is suffixed

TST-lifecycle-loose_root_file_blocks_ini.title: test loose root file blocks initialized

TST-lifecycle-named_pipe_at_root_blocks_.title: A top-level entry of any other kind — a named pipe — is misplaced like a file or a folder.

TST-lifecycle-new_dump_after_successful_.title: A dump arriving after geotag executed and finalized is prep's again: the loop resumes from prep.

TST-lifecycle-no_flatten_organizes_subtr.title: test no flatten organizes subtree without consolidation

TST-lifecycle-no_flatten_same_name_disti.title: test no flatten same name distinct subtrees both survive

TST-lifecycle-prep_builds_the_structure_.title: test prep builds the structure once and never removes a folder

TST-lifecycle-prep_takes_no_decision.title: Prep asks nothing and carries no decision field: it organizes from the workspace and its config.

TST-lifecycle-renamed_folders_found_by_r.title: The user names the managed folders; prep finds each by its role. With the inbox and the photos band renamed in the seed defaults, init builds the renamed folders and organizes into them — no default name is created or written into.

TST-lifecycle-the_control_directory_is_t.title: Where a workspace keeps its records does not follow its configuration: seeded with the defaults, or with every folder renamed and the tracks and the library named elsewhere, prep keeps its configuration and its records in `.photos-ingest/`, and nowhere else; a setting naming another place for them is refused, and nothing is written there.

TST-lifecycle-the_guard_names_the_run_th.title: The guard holds the initializing plan's id, which is the workspace's identity in the archival package.

TST-lock-cross_process_exclusion_and_own.title: test cross process exclusion and owner report

TST-lock-only_a_dead_owners_lock_is_take.title: A lock is taken over only once its owner is provably gone — the kernel let its lock go when the process died — never on what the owner record says. While the owner runs, a record that would make it look gone (a pid that is dead, another host, a garbled or empty record) leaves the lock alone, record and all; once the owner is killed without releasing, the next run takes the lock over.

TST-merge_execute-a_byte_identical_libra.title: Only a library file that is the incoming photo byte for byte makes it already present: the plan says so, and its workspace copy is removed.

TST-merge_execute-a_carried_photos_merge.title: A photo placed under one plan and carried forward by the next: its merge step names the plan that placed it, not the one that only carried it; a photo the later plan placed names that one.

TST-merge_execute-a_copy_damaged_where_t.title: The content fingerprint reads the decoded image, blind to metadata by design. A cross-filesystem copy damaged only there — same size, same fingerprint, other bytes — is refused all the same: the photo stays in the workspace, nothing under its name in the library.

TST-merge_execute-a_file_without_a_finge.title: Only photos by destination are merged: a file the handoff records with no fingerprint in another folder — one geotag left out — does not stop merge.

TST-merge_execute-a_folder_dropped_into_.title: A dump copied in as a whole folder lands at the top level: every command refusing the sealed workspace says a new dump is likely there, and leaves the folder exactly as it was.

TST-merge_execute-a_hidden_entry_among_t.title: A hidden file — a photo named with a leading dot among them — or a hidden folder, even empty, under photos by destination is neither merged nor would it be reported, and the workspace sealed around it would keep it: merge stops, naming it, and places nothing.

TST-merge_execute-a_hidden_file_alone_is.title: A hidden file at the top level, such as one a file browser leaves, is not a dump: no command refusing the sealed workspace warns of one.

TST-merge_execute-a_mapped_photo_whose_p.title: A photo merged under its new value whose place is found taken at execute by the very same file is compared with it by that new value: already present, its workspace copy removed, the merge whole — never blocked as other content for a value the library's file was not fingerprinted under.

TST-merge_execute-a_merge_of_no_photos_s.title: A workspace whose finalized set holds no photo is merged whole: nothing is left to merge, so execute succeeds, writes its records and seals, the library untouched but for its lock.

TST-merge_execute-a_new_fingerprint_is_m.title: A photo whose fingerprint another ImageMagick changed, the file finalize recorded, is merged; merge's package maps its old value to its new, with both versions and where it was and is, beside the records keyed by the old — which, geotag's among them, are copied or read, never rewritten. A photo whose value held maps nothing.

TST-merge_execute-a_photo_already_presen.title: A photo planned as already present whose workspace copy is gone counts as done only while the library still holds it.

TST-merge_execute-a_photo_gone_from_the_.title: test a photo gone from the workspace that no merge moved blocks the plan

TST-merge_execute-a_photo_merged_under_a.title: A partial merge moved a photo under its new value; the re-plan finds it in the library — by the bytes the journal recorded placing, or, the move never journalled, by that new value — carries it forward, and the merge that finishes maps it.

TST-merge_execute-a_photo_moved_earlier_.title: test a photo moved earlier but gone from its place blocks the re plan

TST-merge_execute-a_photo_placed_before_.title: A partial merge placed a.jpg; ImageMagick is then upgraded, and the new version reads every photo to another value. The re-plan confirms a.jpg's place by the bytes the execute recorded placing there — not by a fingerprint the new version takes differently — carries it forward, and the merge that finishes seals.

TST-merge_execute-a_photo_placed_in_a_li.title: A partial merge placed a.jpg in one library; the setting is then pointed at another. a.jpg is not counted merged — the workspace would seal naming the new library while it sits in the old: the re-plan blocks it, naming the photo, where it is and the library now configured, and the two ways out.

TST-merge_execute-a_photo_touched_after_.title: The library already holds the photo's pixels, so merge would remove the workspace's copy — but that copy was written to since the plan (same pixels, as after a metadata write): it is refused and left where it is, the edit not lost.

A photo whose modification time changes once execute's preconditions have passed — its pixels, and so its fingerprint, the same, as after a metadata write — is refused and named, left where it is; the others are merged.

TST-merge_execute-a_photo_without_a_fing.title: A photo in photos by destination that the handoff records with no content fingerprint has no identity to merge by — none to find it in the library with, nor to carry it forward once moved: merge refuses to plan or execute, naming it, and nothing in the workspace or the library is changed.

TST-merge_execute-a_place_taken_by_the_p.title: The planned content appearing at the place while the photo moves makes it already present — as when it is found there just before the move.

TST-merge_execute-a_placement_on_one_fil.title: Where the library lies on the workspace's filesystem, each placement is one rename — never a hard link and an unlink, or a copy and a removal, of the photo.

TST-merge_execute-a_re_plan_after_a_part.title: A partial merge — a.jpg moved, b.jpg blocked — is re-planned once the blocker is cleared. The new plan carries a.jpg forward from the plan that moved it, and the merge that finishes logs both.

TST-merge_execute-a_re_plan_carries_a_ph.title: A move that finished without its journal entry — a crash just after it, or a Ctrl-C while it ran — is carried by the re-plan on the evidence: its earlier plan's place, fingerprinted again, holds it.
