TST-merge_execute-a_record_of_merges_own.title: A plan of merge's own — the saved one, or one a re-plan set aside — or its journal that cannot be read, or that parses in another shape than merge reads it in, stops the command reading it (exit 2), naming the file, which is left as it was: never taken for an empty one, nothing moved, no plan or summary written, no traceback.

TST-merge_execute-a_resumed_execute_chec.title: The journal says a.jpg was moved; its library place no longer holds it. Execute run again blocks it rather than counting it done, and the workspace is not sealed.

TST-merge_execute-a_run_that_never_execu.title: An execute stopped before it begins — by a precondition, a plan missing or stale, a journal it cannot read — or interrupted writes no summary: the one an earlier execute wrote stays as it was.

TST-merge_execute-an_error_placing_one_p.title: An error anywhere in one photo's placement — here its removal from by-dest after the library's copy is checked — blocks that photo alone: the others are placed and the run records how it ended.

TST-merge_execute-config_is_byte_identic.title: Merge never writes the workspace config (photos-00-config.json is hand-edited, authoritative). Snapshot its bytes, run the full plan -> dry-run -> execute cycle, assert byte-for-byte identical.

TST-merge_execute-each_end_of_a_merge_ha.title: Merge's execute ends with a status of its own for each way it can end: done 0, the workspace or the library locked 1, refused 2 (here a stale plan), partial 3, interrupted 130.

TST-merge_execute-either_way_out_of_a_li.title: Either way out the block names lets the merge finish: point library_root back at the library holding the photo, or move the photo by hand to its place in the new library — the re-plan carries it forward from there.

TST-merge_execute-execute_already_presen.title: test execute already present removes source no write

TST-merge_execute-execute_cross_fs_move_.title: test execute cross fs move verifies and completes

TST-merge_execute-execute_jobs_identical.title: Beyond the summary, the placed LIBRARY file tree is byte-identical under -j1 vs -j4 — the move pass has no concurrency-dependent semantics (relative paths + bytes match exactly).

TST-merge_execute-execute_occupied_by_di.title: TOCTOU clobber guard: target FREE at plan (placed_new), then a *different-content* file appears at the planned target before execute. The execute-time recheck must refuse — rc 3, source left in by-dest, the irreplaceable library byte UNCHANGED. (The identical-content sibling is covered above by ...renamed/already-present; this dangerous different-content path was previously unexercised.)

TST-merge_execute-execute_placed_new_mov.title: test execute placed new moves into library

TST-merge_execute-execute_renamed_incomi.title: test execute renamed incoming places under safe name

TST-merge_execute-execute_required_snaps.title: snapshots_required + the library pre-mutation snapshot fails -> abort BEFORE any move: status rejected (rc 2), nothing placed, source untouched in by-dest, library empty, workspace NOT sealed. The required-snapshot guard is the RUL-required_snapshot_or_nothing promise.

TST-merge_execute-execute_resume_after_c.title: test execute resume after crash before seal

TST-merge_execute-execute_resume_finishe.title: test execute resume finishes crash window

TST-merge_execute-execute_sweeps_crash_o.title: A prior interrupted run can leave a cross-fs copy temp (.tmp-xdev-*.part) in a library dir. Because merge holds the library lock (no concurrent merge), execute safely sweeps such orphans from the dirs it targets before placing — they never accumulate in the precious library tree.

TST-merge_execute-execute_torn_copy_bloc.title: test execute torn copy blocks and keeps source

TST-merge_execute-failed_placement_is_do.title: A placement that failed is never recorded as done: once its cause is gone, running execute again places the photo and the run succeeds.

TST-merge_execute-full_success_writes_te.title: test full success writes terminal artifacts and seals

TST-merge_execute-library_lock_held_thro.title: BLD-library_lock: the library lock is held for the WHOLE concurrent move pass — concurrency never relaxes cross-run exclusion. Probe by wrapping _move_file (the per-file placement that runs during the parallel pass): on its first invocation, a fresh LibraryLock on the same library_root must FAIL to acquire (rc False) because the running merge already holds it. Then call through to the original.

TST-merge_execute-library_takes_a_second.title: Merge ends its workspace — sealed, it refuses to merge again — and more media reaches the same library through a fresh workspace.

TST-merge_execute-merge_creates_in_the_l.title: Beyond its mark and its lock, a merge leaves in the library only the photos it placed and the folders they went into — no record, cache, temporary copy or database of its own.

TST-merge_execute-merge_journal_writes_o.title: Single-writer journal (BLD-merge_execute): under -j4 the merge confirmation journal is persisted ONLY by the main thread; worker threads move files but never touch the journal. Probe every journal write.

TST-merge_execute-merge_keeps_its_record.title: Where merge reads and writes its records does not follow the configuration: with the default folders, or with every folder renamed, merge plans and merges from the records geotag left in `.photos-ingest/` and writes its own there — the seal among them — and nowhere else, in the workspace or in the library.

TST-merge_execute-merge_leaves_the_other.title: A whole merge writes its own image of the database and leaves prep's and geotag's, byte for byte, as those phases left them.

TST-merge_execute-merge_log_copies_the_c.title: test merge log copies photos25 forward and appends

TST-merge_execute-merge_needs_no_tracks_.title: Merge seals what the workspace keeps: with the configured tracks folder not there, it plans and executes, and never builds the tracks.

TST-merge_execute-merge_never_reads_a_da.title: No database image is read back as working data: with prep's and geotag's images holding no database at all, merge plans, dry-runs and merges whole, opening neither — nor its own, once made, on the runs after.

TST-merge_execute-merge_only_inspects_sp.title: RUL-library_not_scanned (anti): merge never rescans the library wholesale — it fingerprints only each incoming file's specific collision target, never a library-wide index. Seed the library with the collision target PLUS unrelated files (same dir and another dir); probe the fingerprint seam and assert the unrelated files are NEVER fingerprinted, only the exact target the incoming would land on.

TST-merge_execute-merge_reads_its_settin.title: Merge takes its settings from the workspace's configuration alone: another configuration in every other place — the seed defaults, beside the executable, above the workspace, in the home folder, an environment variable per setting — naming another library, also set up as one, never draws a photo into it.

TST-merge_execute-merge_reads_the_librar.title: Merge lists only the folders its photos go to — and the library's top folder, for temporary copies a crash of its own left — never walks the library, and fingerprints a library file only where an incoming photo's place is taken.

TST-merge_execute-merge_runs_whole_with_.title: With snapshots off, as they are by default, merge never reaches for a ZFS feature: on a machine with no `zfs` at all it plans, dry-runs and merges whole, and seals the workspace.

TST-merge_execute-merge_snapshots_the_wo.title: Merge snapshots the workspace — it removes what it places from there — and the library beside it where the library can be snapshotted; a library that cannot be only narrows the snapshot, with a warning, and the merge proceeds.

TST-merge_execute-merge_takes_no_snapsho.title: Without the workspace's snapshot, merge takes none of the library either — rolled back alone it would lose the photos merge removed from the workspace. Not required, the merge warns that it has no rollback point, and proceeds.

TST-merge_execute-merge_writes_only_its_.title: Merge writes the library-file fingerprint cache and nothing else of the database: prep's and geotag's rows stand exactly as they were.

TST-merge_execute-merges_package_manifes.title: photos-35's manifest names the workspace and the merge run, supersedes geotag's, and lists every file it archives with its path and SHA-256.

TST-merge_execute-merges_step_says_how_e.title: Each photo merged gains one step — placed, placed under a name of its own, or already present — naming the plan, where it came from and where it is, its entry's library_path set to the same place.

TST-merge_execute-merging_a_merged_batch.title: A batch merged whole, then merged again — plan, dry-run and execute: every file of the workspace, its records among them, and every file of the library stands byte for byte as the first merge left it.

TST-merge_execute-no_snapshot_before_the.title: A snapshot follows the plan's validation against its dependencies: a plan that fails it is rejected with no snapshot taken at all, and a plan that passes is validated first.

TST-merge_execute-nothing_is_built_from_.title: Nothing is built from merge's records: after a merge that left a photo blocked, the next merge plans and merges the same — the same plan, the same outcome — whether merge's summary stands as written, is garbled or is gone.

TST-merge_execute-one_database_in_the_wo.title: After a whole merge the workspace holds one database of record, besides the phase images and prep's scratch memo, and the library holds no database at all.

TST-merge_execute-one_journal_per_plan_k.title: Merge's journal is its plan's, not its run's: a second execute of the same plan writes the same `journal-<plan id>.json`, carrying the first's confirmations into it with its own.

TST-merge_execute-partial_run_does_not_s.title: test partial run does not seal or finalize

TST-merge_execute-plan_blocks_when_bydes.title: Prep-consistency (RUL-merge_refuses_changed_since_finalize): a photo physically under 6-photos-by-dest but NOT in the finalized record (handoff predates the latest move into by-dest) -> 're-run prep' blocker at plan, rc 2, NO plan artifact written, nothing placed. Guards against merging an unrecorded file.

TST-merge_execute-plan_mutates_nothing_n.title: Planning never mutates: after `plan`, by-dest + library are byte-identical and NONE of the execute-only artifacts (photos-31 summary, photos-35 log/db/manifest, journal, seal) exist.

TST-merge_execute-precondition_failure_w.title: A preflight blocker stops merge before execute: no photos-31 summary, library byte-unchanged. Here the prep handoff is missing — a precondition the preflight gathers and refuses on.

TST-merge_execute-re_plan_after_failed_i.title: test re plan after failed is allowed

TST-merge_execute-reseal_archives_the_co.title: Merge's re-seal makes the package again: the whole control directory, merge's own records among it, listed in photos-35's manifest and archived with it.

TST-merge_execute-snapshot_and_revalidat.title: Sequencing (BLD-merge_execute): the move-set is fixed BEFORE any concurrent placement — dependency revalidation and the pre-mutation snapshot both complete before the FIRST per-file move runs, even under -j4. Probe the call order via wrappers.

TST-merge_execute-snapshot_is_taken_whil.title: Every snapshot of a merge is taken while the workspace lock is held: probed, from a file descriptor of its own, at the moment each snapshot is asked for.

TST-merge_execute-the_bytes_are_checked_.title: Wherever execute would remove a photo's workspace copy because the library holds it, it compares the two files' bytes again first: a library file that came to hold the same picture in other bytes after the plan — the planned copy rewritten, or one found at the place, or appearing there during the move — blocks the photo, and both files stay.

TST-merge_execute-the_library_file_is_re.title: The cache trusts size and modification time; removing the workspace's copy cannot be undone. A library file changed since the plan without either moving is still caught: the photo stays.

TST-merge_execute-the_run_reports_what_i.title: A partial run tells what it placed, what was already there, and each photo that stayed with its reason, and that nothing is sealed; the run that finishes tells that the workspace is sealed.

TST-merge_execute-the_same_picture_with_.title: The library holds the incoming photo's pixels in other bytes — the same picture without the time and position geotag wrote, say. Neither is removed: the photo is blocked, the block naming both files with their sizes and saying they hold the same picture with different metadata; the rest is merged.

TST-merge_execute-the_summary_says_where.title: Each entry of the summary: where the photo landed, renamed or already present, removed from the workspace — or, blocked, no place in the library and the reason.

TST-merge_plan-a_case_variant_in_the_lib.title: A library file whose name differs from the target's only in case takes the place on a case-insensitive library and may be the same photo on any: it is fingerprinted like a file at the target itself — the same content already present there, different content renamed around.

TST-merge_plan-a_log_edited_after_finali.title: Each log carries the one before it unchanged and only adds: an entry of prep's that photos-26 no longer carries whole — either edited after finalize — blocks merge; one carried whole does not.

TST-merge_plan-a_new_fingerprint_not_one.title: A new value merge maps from prep's must be one to one with it: where two photos' values now coincide, or a photo's new value is another's value under prep's ImageMagick, prep's duplicate decision would differ under the new one, and those photos stay in photos by destination, each with its reason; the others are merged.

TST-merge_plan-a_new_fingerprint_on_a_fi.title: A new value is mapped from prep's only for the very file finalize recorded — its path, size and modification time; a photo not so proven stays in photos by destination with its reason, the map built for none.

TST-merge_plan-a_plan_made_by_other_code.title: Merge's plan records the code that made it; dry run and execute refuse one made by another build, or recording none, before any change.

TST-merge_plan-a_plan_made_under_another.title: A merge plan records the ImageMagick it was made under; under another, its fingerprint comparisons no longer hold, and it is stale.

TST-merge_plan-a_plan_reporting_a_blocke.title: Merge's plan, and its dry run of that plan, end with a refusal's status, 2, while the plan holds a blocker — the plan saved all the same — and with 0 once the blocker is gone.

TST-merge_plan-another_imagemagick_has_p.title: Under an ImageMagick other than prep's, merge takes each photo's fingerprint again and compares that value with the library's, taken under the same version: the photo is found already in the library whether its value is prep's or a new one — a new value mapped from prep's, the photo the file finalize recorded — never called a different photo and placed again beside itself.

TST-merge_plan-any_config_edit_restales_.title: test any config edit restales the merge plan

TST-merge_plan-collision_suffixes_do_not.title: Which incoming photo gets which differentiating suffix around the library's photo does not depend on the order the photos are met in: the same photos, recorded in the opposite order and listed by the filesystem in the opposite order, are given the same names.

TST-merge_plan-dry_run_rejects_stale_pla.title: test dry run rejects stale plan

TST-merge_plan-dry_run_summarizes_valida.title: test dry run summarizes validated plan

TST-merge_plan-dry_run_without_plan_erro.title: test dry run without plan errors

TST-merge_plan-enumerate_joins_prerename.title: test enumerate joins prerename handoff to final name

TST-merge_plan-enumerate_unrenamed_file_.title: test enumerate unrenamed file keeps its name

TST-merge_plan-merge_plan_records_folder.title: test merge plan records folder and extension fingerprints

TST-merge_plan-one_library_file_is_compa.title: With no file at the photo's own name but two whose names differ from it only in case, merge compares the first of them in sorted order alone: the photo, held by the second, is not found there and takes a suffix.

TST-merge_plan-plan_rename_accounts_for_.title: test plan rename accounts for incoming suffix

TST-merge_plan-plan_renamed_incoming_app.title: test plan renamed incoming append at max plus one

TST-merge_plan-plan_reuses_handoff_finge.title: RUL-merge_rechecks_under_new_engine (anti): under the ImageMagick prep used, merge reuses prep's recorded content_fingerprint for each by-dest file and never re-fingerprints / re-organizes / re-dedups by-dest content. The handoff records fp "HANDOFF_ONLY" while the on-disk by-dest bytes are unrelated — if merge recomputed the by-dest fingerprint the plan's precondition would differ. Assert (a) the plan's per-file content_fingerprint is the handoff's recorded value verbatim, and (b) the by-dest file is NEVER passed to the (only) fingerprint seam — only library collision targets ever are, and here the library is empty.

TST-merge_plan-plan_two_incoming_case_va.title: Case-insensitive no-clobber (RUL-suffix_case_insensitive): two incoming photos whose final names differ ONLY in case target the same (empty) library dir. On a case-insensitive library they would collide; the plan resolves it now — one placed_new, the other suffix-renamed — instead of letting the second surface as an EEXIST blocker at execute.

TST-merge_plan-plan_unfingerprintable_li.title: test plan unfingerprintable library file blocks item

TST-merge_plan-replan_reports_library_fi.title: A re-plan says how many library fingerprints it took from the cache — and the plan it writes is the same file, the count kept out of it.

TST-merge_plan-the_library_mirrors_the_d.title: Each photo goes to the same path under the library as under photos by destination — nested folders as the user built them, the name geotag gave it, or its own where geotag renamed nothing.

TST-merge_plan-the_suffix_is_above_the_h.title: A photo whose name the library holds for another takes the suffix above the highest its name's root shows among the library folder's names and those of every photo bound for it — here an incoming `ts-007` — not the lowest free one.

TST-merge_preflight-a_configured_library.title: Merge checks the library it is configured with lies outside every workspace, even one blessed before the rule: one that is, lies in or holds another workspace stops it before the library is locked.

TST-merge_preflight-a_dead_merges_librar.title: A merge that dies holding the library's lock leaves it recognisable as stale — its record still names the dead merge, but no running process holds the lock — and the next merge takes it over and runs, with nothing to clear by hand; while that merge was alive, the same run was refused.

TST-merge_preflight-a_handoff_of_another.title: A handoff whose fingerprints were taken by another method than this build's — or that records no method — cannot be compared with the fingerprints merge takes of the library's files: plan and execute each refuse, naming the mismatch and telling the user to run prep again, and nothing in the workspace or the library is changed.

TST-merge_preflight-a_library_beside_wor.title: A library beside workspaces — siblings under one folder, as a library and its workspaces often are — is outside every one: blessed, from a workspace or from outside any.

TST-merge_preflight-a_library_holding_th.title: A library_root that holds the workspace is caught in the merge data path (validate_merge_config) and surfaces as a preflight blocker: rc 2, no plan, no photos-31 summary, no placement.

TST-merge_preflight-a_photo_holding_no_p.title: Finalize's refusal of a photo holding no position, checked again at merge's own start from what each photo holds: a finalized workspace one of whose photos holds none — or latitude 0 and longitude 0 — merges nothing.

TST-merge_preflight-a_prep_log_the_hando.title: Prep's log touched after finalize — edited, removed, or a handoff recording no hash of it — stops merge, as it stops finalize: photos-26 can no longer be shown to carry prep's record.

TST-merge_preflight-a_refresh_describing.title: Prep run again after finalize with nothing to do rewrites the handoff, changing only what describes the run itself — its ids and times, its diagnostics, its journal. The file's bytes differ; merge does not take that for a change since finalize, while a change to what the handoff says of the photos still is.

TST-merge_preflight-a_stale_finalized_re.title: Merge derives its plan from geotag's executed plan, and checks that plan's dependency — the handoff it was built against — before it writes anything: changed since, no merge plan is created at all.

TST-merge_preflight-an_empty_folder_put_.title: An empty folder put back in a missing managed folder's place restores it: merge's preflight passes.

TST-merge_preflight-bydest_symlink_block.title: A symlink anywhere under 6-photos-by-dest blocks the whole run (rc 2) and is NEVER followed: its external target is not inventoried/planned and stays untouched. (Preflight only detects the link via islink; this asserts the safety consequence end-to-end.)

TST-merge_preflight-dev_subfolder_of_any.title: test dev subfolder of any case blocks[JPG]

TST-merge_preflight-every_misplaced_root.title: Any other top-level entry blocks, whatever its kind — a named pipe too — and the block names every one, not only the first.

TST-merge_preflight-filename_format_othe.title: test filename format other than prep s blocks

TST-merge_preflight-imagemagick_absent_s.title: With neither `magick` nor the older `identify` on the PATH, merge's plan, dry run and execute stop (exit 2) as they start, naming ImageMagick, nothing written and the library not locked; either one of them is enough.

TST-merge_preflight-init_library_in_work.title: test init library in workspace with path blesses and writes config

TST-merge_preflight-init_library_keeps_e.title: `init-library <path>` in a workspace records the library and keeps every other setting as the user wrote it — a folder named beyond ASCII, a tuned value, the keys in the user's order — while the file's layout becomes the control records' own: keys sorted, characters beyond ASCII escaped.

TST-merge_preflight-init_library_reads_t.title: init-library reads the workspace's configuration whole and checked, as every command does: a setting cartographer does not know stops it before it blesses or writes anything.

TST-merge_preflight-init_library_refuses.title: Without a path, init-library blesses the library the configuration names — not when it lies in another workspace.
The library setup, run in a workspace whose shape was disturbed, blesses nothing and writes nothing.
test init library refuses a library holding the workspace

A library lies outside every workspace, not only the one merge runs in: init-library refuses a folder that is another workspace — initialized or not — lies inside one, or holds one among its folders, naming the workspace found, and blesses and writes nothing.

TST-merge_preflight-init_library_without.title: test init library without path refuses a locked workspace

TST-move_aware-a_recognized_move_counts_.title: A file whose move prep recognized counts, in the handoff's cache freshness, as metadata carried — not as metadata missing.

TST-move_aware-a_stale_row_follows_the_m.title: A moved file whose row would have been read again at its old path — its fingerprint taken by another ImageMagick, or its metadata read another way — is still recognized as moved, and read whole at its new path, the reason named; the old row is pruned.

TST-no_clobber-every_prep_move_is_one_re.title: Where the filesystem allows, each move prep makes is one rename: the dump into the inbox, a photo to its day folder, a duplicate into the quarantine — none a link and an unlink, or a copy and a removal.

TST-plan_memo-a_broken_memo_degrades_ins.title: The memo is an accelerator, never a dependency: a corrupt memo database costs the decode it was saving and nothing else — the plan still completes.

TST-plan_memo-changed_file_is_not_reused.title: A memo row faces the same freshness gate as a cache row: bump the mtime and it is rejected, the file is re-decoded, and the re-hash diagnostic names a reason rather than staying silent.

TST-plan_memo-engine_change_invalidates_.title: The memo stores the engine version bound to each pixel signature, so an ImageMagick bump restales memo rows exactly as it restales cache rows.

TST-plan_memo-executed_cache_wins_over_t.title: A cache row is the executed state and always outranks a memo row for the same path: after execute, reuse is attributed to the cache (memo_reused 0), not to the memo.

TST-plan_memo-memo_drops_paths_it_no_lon.title: The memo tracks the workspace instead of growing forever: a file that disappears loses its row.

TST-plan_memo-memo_skips_records_it_coul.title: Only complete observations are stored. A record without a metadata row could not satisfy the all-or-nothing freshness gate, so storing it would buy nothing and relabel its re-hash reason.

TST-plan_memo-plan_does_not_write_the_wo.title: The memo must not become a back door into the cache: planning still leaves file_cache empty, and the memo lives in its own database file.

TST-plan_memo-replan_without_execute_reu.title: The point of the memo: plan, do NOT execute, plan again — the second plan decodes nothing. Before the memo this re-hashed the whole workspace, because cache rows are written by execute.

TST-plan_memo-the_memo_is_not_journalled.title: Writing the memo is no operation of a plan and leaves no entry in a journal: planning writes it with no journal at all, and executing the plan journals the plan's operations and nothing else.

TST-plan_memo-the_memo_never_changes_the.title: The same workspace plans to the same operations with the memo empty, reused, or gone.

TST-plan_memo-the_memo_proves_no_move.title: A file read by a plan never executed and then moved into photos by destination is not recognized as moved: the memo's entry for its old path is no record of it, and it is read as new.

TST-plan_place-unchanged_replan_writes_n.title: test identical rewrite writes nothing and backs up nothing

TST-prep_log-a_different_file_at_a_freed.title: The user deletes a filed photo and puts a different one at the path it freed, while ImageMagick changes: the file there is not the one prep left — not its size, time or inode — so its fingerprint is no retake. It is a new photo; the gone one's entry stays as it was.

TST-prep_log-a_gone_photos_entry_is_carr.title: The user deletes a filed photo; the next run carries its entry exactly as it was — no step added, its prep_path the place prep left it — beside the new photo's, though the new photo is filed under the name it left free: a photo this run files is its own, never the gone one's under a retaken fingerprint.

TST-prep_log-a_log_unreadable_since_the_.title: A log that became unreadable after a clean plan is refused by execute's preflight, before any change.

TST-prep_log-a_photo_moved_under_a_new_i.title: A photo the user sorts into photos by destination while ImageMagick changes, its fingerprint's value changing with it, keeps its whole history: the entry moves to the new value and records the user's move — none left behind claiming the photo is still where prep put it.

TST-prep_log-a_retaken_fingerprint_keeps.title: A photo fingerprinted again by another method, its value changed, keeps its history: the entry moves to the new value, with a step saying so — no orphan under the old value, nothing partial.

TST-prep_log-an_earlier_runs_duplicates_.title: A later run that sets aside another duplicate of a photo adds it to the photo's record of duplicates; the earlier run's stay as they were.

TST-prep_log-an_interrupted_log_rewrite_.title: Prep's log, rewritten in place by a run and interrupted — while the new log is half written, or with it written but not yet in the earlier one's place — is the earlier log, whole; the next run puts the new one down whole.

TST-prep_log-an_unreadable_log_blocks_th.title: An earlier log that cannot be read is never taken for an empty one: the plan blocks, naming it, and execute refuses the plan before any change — the new photo stays in the inbox and the log as it was.

TST-prep_log-every_move_names_where_it_c.title: The journey keeps the chain of names and places: each move and rename records where the photo came from as well as where it went, so the first step holds its original path in the dump.

TST-prep_log-every_step_names_the_run_th.title: Each step prep adds names its run, the plan that made it — the user's own move, the run that found it; a later run's steps name that later run, the earlier ones keeping theirs.

TST-prep_log-log_is_deterministic_and_in.title: test log is deterministic and in control dir

TST-prep_log-media_journey_keyed_by_fing.title: test media journey keyed by fingerprint

TST-prep_log-missing_history_warns_and_m.title: test missing history warns and marks partial

TST-prep_log-prep_log_entries_are_derive.title: RUL-prep_log_derived: the prep log is DERIVED from the validated plan + journals and introduces no new authority — its facts trace back to plan operations. Assert the logged final destination equals a destination the plan actually planned, and the extension-normalization step's 'from' name matches the plan's rename source — the log records nothing the plan/journal did not establish.

TST-prep_log-recognized_move_appends_mov.title: test recognized move appends moved to by dest

TST-prep_log-set_aside_jpeg_names_its_ra.title: A JPEG set aside beside its RAW names that RAW by fingerprint, in its step of the log and in its record of the handoff — however the two were named. One set aside beside two RAWs of its name names neither.

TST-prep_log-strays_and_other_not_logged.title: test strays and other not logged

TST-prep_pipeline-a_duplicate_is_set_asi.title: A duplicate goes to quarantine from its dump path under its dump name — no rename first — and its record names that path.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_file_back_from_missi.title: A file sent back to the inbox with still no time returns to missing metadata under the name it had there: the untimed mark is not taken twice.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_file_sent_back_is_re.title: A filed file the user moves back into the inbox is filed again under the name it had; the row of that path is the move's, not a ghost to prune.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_jpeg_pairs_with_its_.title: The names before the extension must match with case: `IMG_1.JPG` beside `IMG_1.cr2` is set aside, `IMG_2.JPG` beside `img_2.cr2` is not — it is filed as a photo — while the extension's case never matters.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_quarantined_file_lea.title: A duplicate set aside has no row in the database and no entry in the handoff; reclaiming the quarantine leaves the next plan nothing to do.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_redumped_pair_settle.title: A RAW+JPEG pair dumped again is set aside as duplicates in the run that finds it — the JPEG too — keeping the copies already filed; the next run has nothing to do.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_restored_files_quara.title: Moving a quarantined file back into the inbox and running prep again — whether it is filed or quarantined once more — leaves the manifest that recorded its first quarantine byte for byte.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_stray_keeps_its_plac.title: test a stray keeps its place and name

TST-prep_pipeline-an_inbox_file_takes_it.title: An inbox file is filed in one move that lowercases its extension: no rename inside the inbox.

TST-prep_pipeline-an_untimed_redundant_j.title: A JPEG set aside beside its RAW with no recorded time takes its untimed name, flat — the mark once, however it came.

TST-prep_pipeline-copies_in_one_folder_k.title: test copies in one folder keep the first by path

TST-prep_pipeline-only_the_jpeg_beside_a.title: A RAW sets aside the JPEG of its name in its folder — `.jpg` or `.jpeg` — and no other image.

TST-prep_pipeline-the_quarantine_manifes.title: Each duplicate's record in the quarantine manifest names the copy prep kept instead of it.

TST-prune_age-folder_without_an_age_is_l.title: A quarantine folder whose name gives no age is never selected by age, and is listed as such.

TST-prune_age-function_refuses_an_age_be.title: The console reaches the prune without the command line's parsing: it refuses there too.

TST-prune_record-a_deleting_prune_record.title: The record is whole before the first folder goes: each removed run's files with their bytes, and what its manifest said; nothing else changes outside the quarantine.

TST-report-recognized_move_counted_in_re.title: test recognized move counted in report

TST-serve-a_class_is_not_saved_over_a_co.title: The configuration changed by hand since the editor loaded it — another setting, the camera group still unclassed, so the class asked for is still a question — refuses the save of a class, naming the configuration, and leaves the file as the hand left it; reloaded, the same class is saved over the configuration as it now stands.

TST-serve-a_photos_23_holding_leave_unlo.title: A photos-23 whose photo's decision still holds `accept_unlocated` — a field it does not have — is shown as a record that cannot be read, naming the field, as geotag refuses it; and nothing is saved into it.

TST-serve-a_position_chosen_for_a_placed.title: A position set in the editor for a photo the tracks place is written as the entry a hand would write — the photo's path, `chosen_by_user`, the position — into its destination's review items; saved again, that entry is changed, never doubled. TST-serve-a_save_cut_short_leaves_only_i.title: A save whose write of photos-22 fails has written photos-21 and left photos-22, photos-23 and the configuration as they were: what it leaves is a leading part of it.

TST-serve-a_save_keeps_the_record_it_rep.title: Each save that changes a record first keeps the one it replaces beside it under -NNN, numbered on from the copies a re-plan left: two saves leave two copies, in order. A save that changes nothing in the record sets nothing aside; the configuration keeps no copy.

TST-serve-a_save_writes_its_records_in_o.title: A save changing every record writes photos-21, photos-22, photos-23 and then the configuration, one after another.

TST-serve-classes_a_new_camera_group_int.title: The editor lists each camera group geotag would stop on — the photos' groups the configuration classes as neither phone nor fixed-clock camera — with a photo of it, and its save writes the class the user gives into `camera_time_and_timezone_policy.device_groups`, under the lock, over the configuration it loaded, every other setting kept.

TST-serve-names_a_camera_group_several_b.title: The editor lists each fixed-clock camera group of the photos with whether the configuration names it several bodies — never a question that waits — and its save puts the group into `several_bodies_groups`, or takes it out, under the lock, over the configuration it loaded, that setting and no other. A group that is no fixed-clock camera of the photos, or an answer that is not true or false, is refused.

TST-serve-save_hands_back_the_hashes_it_.title: A save made from the records as loaded goes through, a record absent then and now among them, and hands back the hashes of what it left, so the next save from the same page goes through too.

TST-serve-save_refused_when_a_record_cha.title: A geotag plan rewrote photos-23 after the editor loaded the records: a save of photos-21 edits is refused, telling the user to reload, and none of the records is written.

TST-serve-save_refused_when_an_edit_name.title: An edit naming a decision the record does not hold is refused — never dropped while the rest is written — and nothing is written.

TST-serve-save_refused_without_the_loade.title: A save that does not say which records it was made from cannot show it was made from these.

Once the run ends, the same save goes through, and leaves the lock free.

TST-serve-saves_a_changed_time_s_answer.title: A photo's time changed since geotag wrote it: the answer saved into its entry of photos-21's changed_times, by its photo's path, nothing else of the record touched.

TST-serve-saves_a_destination_s_date_fal.title: The date given a destination for its photos with no recorded time is written as its `date_fallback`'s `user_decision.date` in photos-21, nothing else of the cell touched.

TST-serve-saves_a_fingerprint_change_s_a.title: photos-25's fingerprint mismatches each ask whether the photo's changed content stands: the editor loads the summary with its hash, saves the answer into `user_decision.accept_fingerprint_change` of the mismatch named by its photo's path — nothing else of the summary touched — and refuses, like any record, when the summary changed since.

TST-serve-saves_a_phone_s_and_a_clock_ch.title: A phone's day kept as it records itself, and a photo's reading at a daylight-saving change: each saved into its own decision field of photos-21, nothing else of the record touched.

TST-serve-saves_the_camera_less_files_an.title: test apply edits saves the answer for a destination s files naming no camera

TST-serve-sealed_dump_check_goes_by_the_.title: test sealed dump check goes by the workspaces folder names

TST-serve-serve_points_out_a_dump_in_a_s.title: test serve points out a dump in a sealed workspace

TST-serve-serve_refuses_a_sealed_workspa.title: test serve refuses a sealed workspace

TST-serve-serve_refuses_a_second_editor_.title: test serve refuses a second editor without naming a workspace argument

TST-serve-the_editor_checks_zones_by_the.title: The editor checks a timezone against the zones geotag's plan accepts on this host, sent with the decisions — never the browser's own list — so a zone it lets be saved is one the plan takes. The host's own names (`localtime`, `Factory`, `posixrules`) are no place's zone, and are not among them.

TST-snapshot-failed_run_leaves_prior_sna.title: test failed run leaves prior snapshot intact

TST-snapshot-prep_never_reads_its_image_.title: Prep's image is never read back as working data: with it holding no database at all, the next prep run plans and organizes from the database of record, never opening the image, and makes it again.

TST-snapshot-snapshot_leaves_no_temp_and.title: test snapshot leaves no temp and refreshes on rerun

TST-snapshot-snapshot_written_and_matche.title: test snapshot written and matches live cache

TST-stale_plan-a_failed_journal_save_lea.title: The journal is replaced whole: a save that fails partway leaves the journal as the previous save wrote it.

TST-stale_plan-a_plan_executed_again_kee.title: A plan executed a second time, after an attempt that did not finish, sets the first attempt's journal aside under -NNN before it starts its own: the record of what that attempt did is kept.

TST-stale_plan-a_plan_made_by_other_code.title: A saved plan records the code that made it; execute refuses it once the code differs — or when it records none — before any change.

TST-stale_plan-config_change_rejects_pla.title: test config change rejects plan at execute

TST-stale_plan-new_file_since_planning_r.title: RUL-new_file_restales_plan: a file that appears anywhere prep scans between plan and execute is unplanned, so the plan is stale — refused before any mutation, the planned file and the newcomer left in place.

TST-stale_plan-replan_incorporates_new_f.title: After the refusal a new plan takes the newcomer in, fingerprinting only it: the refused plan's fingerprints are reused from the memo (RUL-plan_memo_kept). Metadata is read a folder at a time, so a file is re-read only when it shares a folder with one that needs reading; here they are apart.

TST-stale_plan-the_build_and_its_checkou.title: The code's fingerprint is the same whether the package runs from its checkout or from the zipapp built from it, and changes with any file the zipapp ships.

TST-stale_plan-track_file_since_planning.title: A track dropped in after planning is refused like at planning: the rescan blocks on it.

TST-strays-a_failed_metadata_read_never_.title: exiftool failing for a folder of the inbox blocks its media, never its files of no media class.

TST-strays-a_file_of_no_media_class_outs.title: Prep moves a file of no media class to the strays folder only from the inbox. Anywhere else — an extension taken off the lists, a file put there by hand — it stops the plan, naming the file, and the file stays where it is.

TST-strays-a_stray_is_named_only_in_the_.title: The plan names the stray — it moves it — and nothing else does: not the journal beyond the move's id, not the database, the plan memo, the handoff or the log.

TST-strays-every_track_format_blocks_pre.title: RUL-track_files_block_prep: a track in any format, not only the GPX geotag reads, is never media — it blocks the plan and stays in the dump, never parked in 1-strays.

TST-strays-prep_never_reads_the_tracks.title: Prep resolves gpx_root to check where it lies, and does nothing more with it: it never lists, walks or opens anything beneath it, and never builds geotag's GPX index.

TST-strays-stray_media_detection_silent_.title: test stray media detection silent when exiftool absent

TST-strays-stray_media_detection_warns_o.title: test stray media detection warns only for media mime

TST-strays-stray_media_hinted_on_the_run.title: On the run that initializes a workspace the dump is still where it was put, beside the folders prep makes; its files prep sets aside as strays are probed and hinted as the inbox's are.

TST-strays-stray_not_fingerprinted_and_n.title: test stray not fingerprinted and not cached

TST-strays-strays_are_never_processed_ag.title: Prep writes into the strays folder but never scans it: a stray set aside by one run — even once the configuration counts its extension as an image, and beside a photo dropped in the strays folder by hand — is never fingerprinted or read again by the runs after, enters no plan, no cache and no handoff (so geotag and merge, which read the handoff, never meet it), and stays where it was, byte for byte.

TST-strays-track_file_blocks_prep_and_st.title: RUL-track_files_block_prep: a track is never media. A `.gpx` anywhere prep inventories — the 0-sources dump or a managed folder — blocks the plan and is left where it is: no operation moves it (above all not into 1-strays, where clearing the strays would delete it), it is never fingerprinted, and the blocked plan cannot be executed.

TST-strays-what_prep_leaves_out_of_its_i.title: Prep leaves out of its inventory of media, each as a whole, the control directory, the quarantine, a `.git` directory and the strays folder with everything in it, and every hidden file: photos placed in each are never fingerprinted, never read for metadata, in no part of the plan, and never cached — while a photo in the inbox beside them is. A hidden file in the inbox is set aside to the quarantine (RUL-dump_hidden_files_quarantined), never taken as media.

TST-time_given_filed_on-a_copy_of_one_al.title: A file in missing metadata given a time, a copy of a photo already in photos by date — the same pixels — is set aside into the quarantine from where it lies, as a dump's copy would be, the photo already filed kept; and where its twin arrives in the inbox with the time given, it is the one kept and filed, the dump's copy set aside — the order of folders a copy is kept by, the same for both.

TST-time_given_filed_on-a_name_clash_is_.title: A file given the time of a photo already filed by date — another photo, of other pixels — is filed beside it under its timestamp name suffixed, never over it.

TST-time_given_filed_on-a_photo_given_a_.title: Two photos set apart for want of a time; one is given a time where it lies. The next prep run files it into its day's folder of photos by date under its timestamp name, its journey in prep's log gaining the steps a dump's photo takes, and names the change by hand; the other, still untimed, stays as it was. The next run's check finds the workspace as that execution left it, and plans nothing for either.

TST-time_given_filed_on-a_video_given_a_.title: Missing metadata holds videos too: one given a time is filed into its day's folder of videos by date.

TST-workspace_check-a_change_the_killed_.title: After a hard kill, a file not as the killed run's records say it left it — prep's photo with another modification time than the plan found it with, geotag's with another size than its journal notes — is no work of that run: the command stops, naming that file and only it, the rest of the run's work passing as its own.

TST-workspace_check-a_copy_with_new_inod.title: A photo restored where it was from a copy, and another sorted by copying it and removing the original: each has a new inode but its size and modification time, so each is the same file — the plan goes on, naming both.

TST-workspace_check-a_culled_photo_passe.title: Photos deleted by hand in photos by date and in photos by destination: the plan goes on, naming them; the execution writes them into prep's log, with the photos' fingerprints; the next run, the record rewritten, names them no more.

TST-workspace_check-a_deletion_is_cullin.title: A file gone from photos by date or by destination, videos by date or the redundant JPEGs is culling, allowed; gone from missing metadata, the strays or the quarantine it is a change no person is expected to make.

TST-workspace_check-a_file_still_in_the_.title: After a hard kill, a photo the killed run filed from the inbox that is in the inbox again — copied back with its size and time kept — is not gone from where it was: the file at the plan's place is no work of that run, and the command stops naming it.

TST-workspace_check-a_hard_killed_geotag.title: Geotag's execution killed outright once its photos are written — each a new inode, size and time — and renamed: nothing recorded, the photos are where and as its journal notes it left them, so the next command passes them unasked as the killed run's work; the execution that resumes the plan names them in its summary and records them, each keeping its fingerprint under its new name.

TST-workspace_check-a_hard_killed_merge_.title: Merge's execution killed outright after moving its photos into the library, before the record: the photos gone from photos by destination are its journaled moves, named as the killed run's work — not as photos culled.

TST-workspace_check-a_hard_killed_prep_e.title: Prep's execution killed outright after its moves — a photo filed from the inbox into photos by date, a duplicate set aside into the quarantine with its manifest, the last move not even journaled — records nothing. The next plan finds each where the killed run's plan put it, with the entry it had: its own work, passing unasked and named; the execution after it names it in prep's log and records the state, the note of the killed run cleared with it.

TST-workspace_check-a_photo_moved_back_p.title: A photo moved back from photos by destination to photos by date: the plan goes on, naming it; the execution names it in prep's log, and the photo's journey says where it went.

TST-workspace_check-a_prune_cut_short_is.title: A prune whose removal of a run folder stops midway — the duplicate gone, its manifest left — takes what it removed out of the record all the same: the next plan goes on.

TST-workspace_check-a_time_given_by_hand.title: A photo prep set aside for want of a time, given one by hand where it lies: the plan goes on, naming it, and the execution — a change by hand is work for it, never nothing to do — names it in prep's log.

TST-workspace_check-a_workspace_with_no_.title: A prepped workspace whose state no execution recorded — one begun under an earlier version — is not "nothing to do": prep's execute runs, and writes the first record.

TST-workspace_check-accepted_changes_are.title: Changes accepted once are recorded with their code, and stop no later command; a second acceptance keeps the first record under -001; the execution names every accepted change in prep's log, with its code; the record of acceptances goes into the archive with the rest of the control records.

TST-workspace_check-an_execution_records.title: Prep's execution records the state it leaves — and so does one that failed partway, so the next run does not take its own moves for changes by hand; a plan leaves the record as it was.

TST-workspace_check-an_unexpected_change.title: A photo changed in place, or another put at its path; a file appearing outside the inbox; one gone from missing metadata; anything in the strays or the quarantine changed; a photo moved where nobody sorts to: the plan stops, a refusal, naming the file, having planned nothing.

TST-workspace_check-every_checking_comma.title: Prep's plan, dry run and execute; geotag's plan, execute and finalize; merge's plan, dry run and execute — each stops on the same change before it does anything else.

TST-workspace_check-geotag_and_merge_ref.title: A workspace whose state no execution recorded: geotag and merge refuse it, a refusal, pointing to prep.

TST-workspace_check-geotags_own_writes_n.title: Geotag writes a photo through a temporary file renamed over it — a new inode, size and time — and renames it: its execution records the state it leaves, so the next command finds nothing changed, and each photo keeps its fingerprint in the record under its new name.

TST-workspace_check-maintenance_commands.title: Pruning the quarantine, setting up the library and the editor run whatever the files show; what a prune removes from the quarantine is no change to the next run.

TST-workspace_check-merge_checks_the_wor.title: Merge, like geotag, compares the workspace before its preflight validates anything past the workspace's shape: with a change by hand to stop on and a library its preflight would refuse, each command stops on the change, and the library is never judged.

TST-workspace_check-merges_own_moves_nev.title: Merge moves photos out of the workspace, one left behind blocked: its execution records the state it leaves, so the next merge finds nothing changed.

TST-workspace_check-prep_with_no_record_.title: Prep's first run — no record yet — compares nothing, whatever the folders hold; its execution writes the first record.

TST-workspace_check-the_code_accepts_onl.title: The stop prints the list and the command to run again with its code — a hash of the list as printed. One more change since, the old code no longer matches: the command stops again, listing them anew under a new code, which then accepts them.

TST-workspace_check-what_a_person_is_exp.title: A dump put into the inbox, photos sorted from photos by date into destinations and moved, a destination's folder renamed, the configuration and a decision record edited: the plan goes on, naming none of it.

TST-workspace_one_filesystem-breaks_foun.title: test breaks found anywhere without descending

TST-workspace_one_filesystem-geotag_refu.title: test geotag refuses a workspace on two volumes[plan]

TST-workspace_one_filesystem-geotag_seal.title: Under the lock, the seal is checked before anything else is read (BLD-phases_check_seal) — the walk over every folder for their devices included: a sealed workspace is refused as sealed, never walked.

TST-workspace_one_filesystem-init_librar.title: test init library in a workspace on two volumes refuses[False]

TST-workspace_one_filesystem-merge_refus.title: test merge refuses a workspace on two volumes[plan]

TST-workspace_one_filesystem-prep_refuse.title: test prep refuses a workspace on two volumes[plan]

TST-workspace_prep-a_blocker_is_reported.title: RUL-blockers_all_reported ('Blockers are reported textually; the workflow does not silently skip them'). With a forbidden sidecar present alongside a perfectly organizable photo, prep must (a) SURFACE the blocker as descriptive text in plan.blockers and (b) refuse the whole run at execute — it never silently drops the blocker and proceeds to organize the valid photo. Asserts the never-skip principle itself, not merely that some blocker string appears.

TST-workspace_prep-already_lowercase_ext.title: RUL-media_extension_lowercase: prep does not re-normalize an already-normalized extension. A file already named with a lowercase `.jpg` must produce NO extension-normalization rename op (no two-step temp rename, no rename_no_clobber on it) — distinct from the idempotency rerun, which asserts the whole plan is empty rather than isolating the extension non-renaming.

TST-workspace_prep-an_empty_folder_put_b.title: A missing managed folder blocks prep; an empty folder put back in its place restores it, and prep plans as on an intact workspace.

TST-workspace_prep-directory_symlink_at_.title: A directory symlink at the root of an UNINITIALIZED workspace must be flagged as a forbidden symlink at PLAN time, never followed. os.path.isdir() follows a directory symlink, so the old isdir-first order let os.walk(path) traverse the external target and inventory (and plan a move for) files outside the workspace — the pipeline escape the spec forbids.

TST-workspace_prep-empty_sources_is_stea.title: RUL-empty_inbox_normal: an EMPTY 0-sources is the normal steady end-state, NOT a missing-folder condition. On an initialized workspace whose 0-sources is present but empty (every managed folder intact), prep plans cleanly — zero operations, and crucially NO 'non-conforming'/'missing folder' blocker naming 0-sources. (Distinct from test_missing_managed_folder..., which DELETES folders; here 0-sources exists and is just empty.)

TST-workspace_prep-every_executed_operat.title: Execution records every operation it carries out in the run's journal — moves, renames and setting duplicates aside alike — each with its outcome, and no operation the plan does not hold.

TST-workspace_prep-gpx_root_inside_manag.title: RUL-tracks_outside_managed_folders: a gpx_root configured inside the managed tree is an invalid configuration — prep refuses to plan, naming the field, and nothing in the workspace moves.

TST-workspace_prep-init_does_not_move_a_.title: Reserved-name guard (RUL-dump_folder_named_as_managed): on an INIT run a base entry whose name collides with a managed folder (e.g. an as-arrived dump dir named `5-photos-by-date`) is treated AS that managed folder — NEVER inventoried as a dump and moved beneath itself into 0-sources/5-photos-by-date (a silent data-shuffling hazard). Assert no init-move op relocates it under 0-sources.

TST-workspace_prep-init_move_excludes_ma.title: RUL-init_moves_dump_to_inbox: init's base-dump consolidation moves genuine root dumps into 0-sources but EXCLUDES the managed 0-6 folders and the control/dot directories (.photos-ingest, .git). A real root dump file IS moved (proving the init move ran), while a pre-existing managed folder (with media already in it) and a .git dir are NEVER relocated beneath 0-sources. (The reserved-names test covers a dump dir NAMED like a managed folder; this covers actually-present managed + control dirs.)

TST-workspace_prep-initialized_root_dotf.title: The top level of an INITIALIZED workspace holds the managed folders and hidden entries (RUL-top_level_only_managed): a root dotfile (a file manager's `.directory` or `.DS_Store`) is not a misplaced dump — no block — and, the root being no dump area once initialized, no operation touches it.

TST-workspace_prep-missing_managed_folde.title: The block of a missing managed folder gives the remedy, not only the fault: restore the folders, then run.
An activated workspace (guard present) missing managed 0-6 folder(s) is non-conforming — prep hard-stops with a blocker rather than silently recreating them (which could mask lost media).

TST-workspace_prep-nested_directory_syml.title: os.walk does not descend into a subdirectory symlink (so it never escapes), but it must still be FLAGGED as forbidden rather than silently ignored.

TST-workspace_prep-plan_is_non_mutating.title: Planning changes nothing: with work to do, every file of a workspace past its first run — media and records, the workspace database among them — is byte-identical afterwards; the only file it adds is the fingerprint memo it keeps for later runs. (This writes no plan: the command saves it, not the planner.)

TST-workspace_prep-prep_blocks_a_link_un.title: Prep never changes 6-photos-by-dest, yet it is the gatekeeper for links there: a link under it blocks prep's plan, so no handoff is built while one is present.

TST-workspace_prep-prep_workflow_plan_an.title: test prep workflow plan and execute

TST-zfs-a_plans_existing_snapshot_counts.title: A snapshot names its plan, so executing the same plan again (a geotag resume, a merge re-run) asks for a name ZFS already holds: that snapshot precedes the plan's changes, so it counts as taken and says so — never a failure, which `snapshots_required` would turn into a refused resume. A failure with no such snapshot stays a failure.

TST-zfs-load_or_seed_config_rejects_ille.title: test load or seed config rejects illegal zfs

TST-zfs-prep_runs_whole_with_no_zfs.title: With snapshots off, as they are by default, prep never reaches for a ZFS feature: on a machine with no `zfs` at all it organizes a dump, and the next, whole.

TST-zfs-required_snapshot_with_no_datase.title: test required snapshot with no dataset aborts

TST-zfs-snapshot_taken_with_detected_dat.title: test snapshot taken with detected dataset and prefix

TST-zfs-take_zfs_snapshot_no_dataset.title: test take zfs snapshot no dataset

TST-zone_asking-an_answer_ends_the_askin.title: A zone answered in the editor settles, before any run, every destination it reaches and every folder asking for those alone; nothing it does not reach — past a country of several zones, or a zone the photos contradict.

TST-zone_table-a_bad_download_leaves_the.title: test a bad download leaves the table in use[offline]

TST-zone_table-a_permission_downloads_on.title: test a permission downloads once into the records

TST-zone_table-a_redirect_off_https_is_r.title: The download follows a redirect only to another HTTPS address: one to plain HTTP is refused, the plain address never opened; one to HTTPS is followed. An address not HTTPS is refused before anything is opened.

TST-zone_table-an_unreadable_record_stop.title: A record of the answer that is there and cannot be read is not no answer: `prep plan` and a geotag command stop on it, naming it, nothing planned, asked, downloaded or written over; the console asks nothing.

TST-zone_table-host_then_workspace_then_.title: test host then workspace then carried

TST-zone_table-nothing_asked_or_fetched_.title: test nothing asked or fetched where the host has it

TST-zone_table-prep_plan_takes_the_answe.title: The first `prep plan` of a workspace, given the answer or none, plans as it would anyway.

TST-zone_table-the_console_asks_the_same.title: The console's prep Plan asks what `prep plan` asks, and carries the answer into the same run as the flag.

TST-zone_table-the_question_says_what_re.title: test the question says what refusing leaves

TST-zone_table-the_request_names_only_th.title: test the request names only the tool

TST-zone_table-unanswered_downloads_noth.title: test unanswered downloads nothing and goes on

TST-zone_table-unknown_zone_is_no_countr.title: test unknown zone is no countrys

arch.description: Mapping of uml key to uml content.

constraints.description: List of constraint names, which are defined for this need.

constraints_error.description: An error message set if any constraint failed, and `error_message` field is set in config.

constraints_passed.description: True if all constraints passed, False if any failed, None if not yet checked.

constraints_results.description: Mapping of constraint name, to check name, to result, None if not yet checked.

content.description: The main content of the need.

docname.description: Name of the document where the need is defined (None if external).

doctype.description: The markup type of the content, denoted by the suffix of the source file, e.g. '.rst'.

external_css.description: CSS class name, added to the external reference.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

has_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list.

has_forbidden_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list, and the link type does not allow dead links.

is_external.description: If true, no node is created and need is referencing external url.

is_import.description: If true, the need was derived from an import.

is_modified.description: Whether the need was modified by needextend.

jinja_content.description: Whether the content was pre-processed by jinja.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

lineno.description: Line number where the need is defined (None if external).

parts.description: Mapping of parts, a.k.a. sub-needs, IDs to data that overrides the need's data

post_template.description: The template key, if the post_content was created from a jinja template.

pre_template.description: The template key, if the pre_content was created from a jinja template.

signature.description: Derived from a docutils desc_name node.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

template.description: The template key, if the content was created from a jinja template.
